On a baseline of one Aeron Chair (about $1,395 new), the Outlet / Open Box channel usually beats any sitewide sale, landing roughly $840–$1,185 depending on the specific listing, while a seasonal sale brings a current-config chair to about $1,046–$1,186. There is no military discount to stack on top of either: Outlet pricing is a channel rather than a code, seasonal sale prices generally exclude extra codes, and service status changes nothing at Herman Miller checkout. Always verify the specific listing and the 12-year warranty before buying.
allegiant-military-discount: The single most valuable part of Allegiant Honors is the checked-bag waiver. On a bags-heavy family trip — say three travelers each checking two bags each way — the waived fees frequently total hundreds of dollars, often more than a single-digit fare percentage would return on a ULCC ticket. The value scales with your bag count and family size, so the bigger the group and the more bags, the larger the win.

Verification happens in person at the airport. An Allegiant agent checks your CAC, Uniformed Services ID, DD Form (2, 214, or 2765), Veteran ID card, or veteran-designated driver’s license; spouses verify with DD Form 1173/1173-1 with the sponsor on the same reservation, and children under 10 need no ID. There is no online military account, code, or third-party verifier.

A note on the aggregators: several sites frame this as an "Allegiant Air military discount," which reads like a cheaper ticket. It is not. Allegiant publishes no percentage off airfare and no online military promo code — its own page states benefits are added at the airport by an agent after an ID check. The practical move is to book the lowest public fare, avoid prepaying for bags, and let the counter agent add the waivers.
polywood-military-discount: POLYWOOD routes its discount through SheerID. You create a free POLYWOOD account, verify your military eligibility once through SheerID, and receive a single-use 5% code (one per calendar year). There is no ID.me path on polywood.com — ID.me is Lowe’s verification partner, and there is no GovX or WeSalute program for POLYWOOD.

The 5% does not stack with a POLYWOOD sale: sale and promo items and other coupons are excluded, and discounted purchases are not eligible for future price adjustments. During a real sale — Memorial Day, July 4, Labor Day, or Black Friday — the public price often beats the 5%, and you cannot have both.

POLYWOOD and SheerID can re-verify eligibility and change or end the program at any time, so confirm the current terms in POLYWOOD’s Help Center before you buy. Free shipping applies to all polywood.com orders in the 48 contiguous states with no minimum.
disney-tickets-military-discount: The single best path for an eligible member is simply buying the Salute ticket itself. The price is fixed and the same across every channel — Disney directly, participating military base ticket offices (ITT/LTS), Shades of Green, and GovX — so the only real decision is which channel is most convenient, not which is cheapest. Buying through a base office or Shades of Green avoids any online handling fee and gets you in-person help; GovX is the online option when a base office is not convenient.

At Walt Disney World there is a mandatory activation step: the tickets are not valid until the member or spouse activates them at a theme-park ticket window with a valid military ID. Plan for the eligible person to be present on arrival. Advance park reservations are required at both resorts and are subject to availability, and the WDW offer carries 2026 blockout windows (March 29–April 11 and November 22–November 28). Disneyland has no 2026 blockout dates.

Choose the product that fits your trip length. For a single WDW trip, the 4-, 5-, or 6-Day Salute Park Hopper is cheapest up front; the $499 "Disney Celebrates America" year ticket wins only if you will do many park days across 2026. For a Disneyland trip, the 3- or 4-Day Park Hopper military ticket is the pick, with the Lightning Lane Multi Pass version costing more if you value skip-the-line access.

If you are not active-duty or a military retiree (for example, an ordinary veteran with only a DD-214, or a civilian), you do not qualify for the Salute ticket. Your real savings then come from standard public routes: buy tickets only for the days you need, watch for Disney’s public multi-day promotions, use authorized resellers and cashback portals on standard tickets, and consider Costco Travel packages. Disney’s separate military room discount can also stack with the ticket deal for a cheaper overall trip.
olukai-military-discount: OluKai routes its discount through GovX. You verify your eligibility (military, first responder, teacher, or government) once through GovX’s secure check; OluKai says it does not store or access your verification details, and GovX generates a unique code you enter at checkout. There is no confirmed ID.me, SheerID, or WeSalute path for OluKai — GovX is the named partner.

The GovX 10% combines only with shipping discounts and is otherwise non-combinable: OluKai allows one promotion per order, so a public sitewide code or sale blocks the GovX code and vice-versa. Because OluKai discounts publicly and often, a genuine 20%+ event beats the 10% — take whichever price is lower.
OluKai controls the program and can change it at any time, so confirm the current terms on OluKai’s Help Center article before you buy.
shinesty-military-discount: The military route is handled by GovX ID, a free GovX account — not ID.me or SheerID. You verify once to unlock a single-use code for shinesty.com, and each purchase generally requires logging back into GovX for a fresh code. Verification issues run through GovX; order issues run through Shinesty (customerservice@shinesty.com). GovX verifies current and former military alongside law enforcement, firefighters, healthcare workers, and government employees, so the same route serves several communities.

Two limits matter. First, the GovX discount covers new subscription and one-time orders only — recurring subscription renewals bill at the regular price, so GovX does not keep saving you money on an auto-renewing underwear subscription. Second, Shinesty checkout takes a single discount code per order, so a GovX code, a referral code, and a sitewide code are mutually exclusive — you pick one.

Because Shinesty runs constant public deals, the GovX discount is usually the floor, not the ceiling. On a first order, a $20 refer-a-friend credit is about 33% off a typical $60 cart. When a sitewide code is live, it usually beats the GovX rate and stays cashback-portal-safe, whereas a GovX single-use code runs through an identity-gated flow that typically breaks portal tracking. Reserve GovX for a full-price cart with no better public code available.
wiley-x-military-discount: Wiley X’s discount is powered by ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. You verify your eligible group once — military, first responder, nurse, or government — and the 30% then applies to your wileyx.com order. There is no standalone military coupon code to paste; the discount unlocks through verification, not a shared code.

Wiley X products are also sold on GovX, a separate marketplace for current and former military, first responders, and law enforcement. GovX lists 63-plus Wiley X models at member pricing (often roughly 15–25% off MSRP, model-dependent) and uses its own GovX ID verification. GovX is a substitute for the brand site, not a stack — you cannot combine it with the wileyx.com 30%. For a specific model, compare the GovX net price against wileyx.com-minus-30% before buying.

Coupon aggregators circulate scraped "Wiley X military codes" and vague percentages. The only verified official military path is 30% off through ID.me on wileyx.com. A public WX-15 code gives everyone 15% off for signing up for emails — it is not a military rate and does not combine with the 30%.
Because Wiley X controls the terms and can change them at any time, treat the numbers here as a starting point and confirm the current offer on Wiley X’s official ID.me discount page before you buy.
titleist-military-discount: Titleist’s "military verification" is part of a free Team Titleist account — it flags you as active-duty or veteran so you receive event and promotion information. It does not apply a discount at checkout. Titleist uses no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute military-discount program. Any "verify for a Titleist military discount" claim you see on a coupon site is inaccurate.

MAP is the through-line: new, current Titleist is priced the same nearly everywhere, so savings come from a different product (used/overrun/prior-generation) or a Titleist-authorized promo (Loyalty Rewarded), never from a service-member code. On the flagship Pro V1 dozen ($58 new), Loyalty Rewarded works out to about $43.50/dozen, Logo Overruns run roughly $30–40/dozen, and exchange refinished dozens are cheapest of all if you don’t mind a used ball.

Watch out for the specifics coupon sites get wrong: PGA Tour Superstore’s 10% military discount does not apply to Titleist; the ID.me "Titleist" listing is cashback (~3%) open to every member, not a military discount; and GovX does not carry Titleist. The genuinely cheaper paths are not military discounts — they’re promotions and channels anyone can use.
tonies-military-discount: Verification is handled entirely by ID.me at checkout: open the "Show order summary" dropdown, click the green ID.me button, and confirm your status once with a free ID.me account — the 20% then applies within the tonies.com checkout automatically. ID.me states it can detect fraudulent cross-account use and may revoke access for abuse, and support for verification issues runs through ID.me (help.id.me), not tonies directly.

A couple of corrections to what coupon sites say: this is not a military-only program — it’s a shared 20% "Everyday Heroes" offer that equally covers teachers, nurses, and healthcare workers. One aggregator claims SheerID is also used; the brand’s own page names ID.me only, so treat SheerID as unverified. And aggregator "30% off" code claims are generic promo scraping — the verified value is 20% via ID.me.

When might you skip the 20%? tonies runs recurring "buy 2 Tonies, get a free Creative Tonie" bundles — on a figure-heavy cart, one free ~$12–15 figure per two bought can beat a flat 20%. And Black Friday/seasonal sales have historically discounted Tonieboxes and select Tonies deeply. Since the checkout applies one order-level discount, price the bundle or sale against your 20% and take the lower. Not ID.me-eligible? A 10% first-order welcome code (email/SMS signup, US residents) is the public fallback.
ridge-military-discount: The Ridge verifies eligibility through GovX ID rather than ID.me or SheerID. You verify once, and GovX issues a single-use discount code for The Ridge; log back into GovX to get a fresh code on future orders. Ridge’s own X/Twitter account and the GovX brand storefront for The Ridge both confirm the 20% figure and the GovX channel.

One thing to watch: some coupon aggregators list Ridge Wallet at "15%." The current verified figure is 20% via GovX, per The Ridge’s own social confirmation and the GovX storefront. A separate "10%" figure you may encounter belongs to Ridge Footwear (ridgefootwear.com) — a different, unrelated boot company that runs its own GovX program. Don’t confuse the two.

The ridge.com military discount landing page itself renders through JavaScript and did not return scrapeable terms on this research pass, so the 20% and its exact mechanics are sourced to The Ridge’s own social post and the GovX storefront rather than a static ridge.com terms page. Re-verify the exact wording directly on ridge.com or GovX before treating every detail as fully confirmed.

Ridge also frequently discounts kits and outlet items 25–39% off outside of any military program. Assume the GovX 20% code does not stack with those sale prices — take whichever is deeper for a given item, and verify at checkout.
cozy-earth-military-discount: Cozy Earth’s military page routes through GovX ID: GovX confirms your status and issues access to the offer. The broader Cozy Cares program instead uses a self-attestation email form — you select your category and receive a code, with no document upload shown. There is no ID.me route.

On savings math, use the brand’s signature Bamboo Sheet Set (Queen) at $308 full price as a baseline. The verified 20% brings that to about $246.40 — the everyday floor when nothing else is running. But Cozy Earth’s Black Friday 2025 event ran 30-45% off sitewide with roughly 60% doorbusters, which beats 20% outright, and its public "buy 3+ = 20%" bundle matches the military rate with no verification.

A public sitewide sale is auto-applied (no code), so it’s portal-safe for cash back: routing through Rakuten added about 2% as of July 18, 2026. A GovX or Cozy Cares single-use code, by contrast, typically breaks portal tracking, so don’t assume "20% code + Rakuten" stacks. The combinable play is sale + about 2% Rakuten. Cash-back rates move weekly — re-check before relying on one.
cheddars-military-discount: s is a sit-down restaurant with no online-checkout promo-code field, and its official FAQ lists no military discount. Coupon aggregators claim a "10-15% year-round military discount at some locations" and list "20% / 30% off promo codes" — none are verified, and a public Tripadvisor review reports a diner being refused a discount in uniform. Treat any everyday percentage as location-manager discretion at best; call ahead and never assume.",
wilson-military-discount: Wilson’s discount is powered by SheerID, a third-party identity-verification service. You complete a one-time online check — name, service details, and sometimes a document upload if an instant match fails. After approval, the 15% is tied to your Wilson account and applies whenever you’re logged in, with no per-order code.

The military tier sits alongside parallel SheerID programs for first responders (fire, law enforcement, EMT) and healthcare workers, each also 15% off eligible merchandise. Students verify separately through UNiDAYS or Student Beans for the same 15%. No dedicated Wilson teacher program was found.

A word on providers: Wilson’s official pages name SheerID, so treat SheerID as the confirmed provider. ID.me Shop separately lists Wilson for cashback — that is a different program and is not the same as the 15% identity discount. Coupon aggregators advertising "20%–65% off" sitewide codes are scraped or expired public codes, not the military program, and they cannot be combined with the 15%.

Because the 15% cannot stack on coupons or sale prices, the genuinely cheapest path is situational. On a full-price item, the 15% is the simple win. During a deep public sale or in the Wilson outlet (up to 75% off), the marked-down price usually beats 15% — buy the sale. For a big, tax-heavy cart, the military Exchange (NEX/AAFES) stocks Wilson tax-free with price-matching, which can edge out 15%-plus-tax.
springfield-armory-military-discount: FIRSTLINE launched May 2, 2022 as a dealer-direct program “with immediate discounts… without rebates, vouchers or post-purchase steps.” You receive the FIRSTLINE price instead of the regular price at the counter — there is no separate code to enter and no third-party portal such as ID.me, SheerID, or GovX for the firearm itself.

Roughly 37–38 models across the Hellcat, 1911, XD, SAINT, Hellion, and M1A families are covered, and FIRSTLINE handguns ship with three magazines. A purchase limit of one of each firearm type per calendar year applies per participant.

Because Springfield publishes no percentage, treat any “X% off” figure with caution. One observed dealer example put a Hellcat Pro OSP at about $524 versus roughly $649 MSRP — near 19% off MSRP — but that is a single dealer price, not an official figure, and is often close to a good street sale that requires no credential at all.
vistaprint-military-discount: The Vistaprint military discount is verified through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers — not SheerID, and Vistaprint has no GovX storefront. You verify once, tied to your Vistaprint account, and the discount then applies automatically on future eligible orders with no code to enter.

The defining catch is stacking. Vistaprint states plainly that the military discount is "not combinable with coupons (offers with a promo code)," so you must remove any coupon from the cart to use it. Because Vistaprint’s biggest advertised deals — a 20% new-customer code, up to 25% "favorites" codes, up to 50% off invitations — are all promo-code offers, they are mutually exclusive with the military discount. You pick the larger; you don’t stack them.

What the military discount does combine with is automatic (no-code) sale pricing: the brand applies the sale first, then the 10% on top — a genuine, if modest, stack and the one advantage the military route has over a single code. The offer’s 20% off design and digital services is additive too, because most product promo codes explicitly exclude design services.

Because Vistaprint controls the terms and can change them at any time, treat the numbers here as a starting point and confirm the current offer on Vistaprint’s official military-discount page before you buy.
mt-olympus-military-discount: Verification is not applicable here: Mt. Olympus has no military verification program — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass integration exists for a military discount, because no such discount is offered. If a coupon site claims otherwise, it’s inaccurate.

About that "WELCOME" code: WorthEPenny correctly notes there is no Mt. Olympus military program, then claims the regular promo code "WELCOME" gives military members 35% off. That code is user-submitted and appears on no official Mt. Olympus page — don’t rely on it. The park’s actual savings pattern is public flash ticket deals (it has run $20 tickets and even $3 "today only" specials) and resort bundling, all open to everyone.

For the math, take a one-day visit for two people at the advertised ~$45 gate rate — about $90 before tax. A resort package turns that spend on its head: rooms are advertised from $59/night with park tickets and taxes included, so a night’s stay costs less than two gate tickets and covers admission for the whole registered party for the length of the stay. Free Water Park Pass holders can also take 20% off an overnight stay through Aug 31, 2026, and verified military members should check Vet Tix, which has distributed Mt. Olympus day passes in the past.
beis-military-discount: Because there is no Béis military program, there is nothing to verify and no military code to enter. The only ID.me connection is a cashback offer open to all ID.me members: you verify an ID.me account (any member), shop through the ID.me link, and receive a rebate after purchase. Nothing here is military-specific, and the rate is quoted "up to."

The practical playbook is simple. Everyday, download the Béis app and use its 20% exclusive — the biggest routine saving. On your first order without the app, use the 15% email/SMS offer instead. When a public sale is live, compare the sale price to the app 20% and take whichever total is lower, since codes usually do not stack on sale. Any order can then route through ID.me for a small cashback layer on top.

One correction to carry with you: the "20% for Active Military & Veterans" SheerID offer that appears in the same searches belongs to Osprey, and aggregator pages implying a "Béis military discount" or "15–30% for military" are describing a program that does not exist. What is real for a service member at Béis is exactly what is real for everyone.
yakima-military-discount: Yakima’s Offers page publishes public sales, not a military tier. The reliable one is a recurring 20%-off sitewide sale that rotates under names like "Haul-iday," "Out of Office," and the May "Hold My Gear" sale, usually paired with free shipping. A 25%-off bike-rack sale ("Wheelie Good Deals") runs in shorter windows. When no sitewide event is live, the close-out / "Deep Discount" clearance discounts last-chance stock up to about 40% — final sale, no returns. None of these is gated to military service; they are simply the best broadly-available Yakima prices.

Nothing stacks. Every Yakima offer states it "cannot be combined with other discounts," so you take one promotion per order. Sales also exclude parts, apparel, keys/cores, deep-discount items, pro sales, and prior purchases, so check that a rack qualifies before assuming the sale price applies. Free shipping at $499+ layers under a sale because it is a shipping benefit rather than a discount, but freight items such as cargo boxes and rooftop tents carry a higher threshold.

It is easy to confuse the Yakima Pro Program with a discount for service members, but they are different. The Pro Program gives exclusive pricing to outdoor and automotive industry professionals, partners, and influencers, and requires annual re-application — it verifies industry credentials, not military status. If you happen to qualify as an eligible industry pro, a pro-deal channel such as ExpertVoice can go deeper (often 30–50% off), but that is a trade benefit, not a military one, and ExpertVoice eligibility for Yakima is not something we can confirm for you here.

Be cautious of the "Yakima military discount" and "military code" listed by coupon aggregators. No such official discount exists — Knoji itself concedes Yakima does not offer military discounts, and GovX (which carries some rack competitors like Rhino-Rack) is not confirmed to list Yakima. Using a scraped "code" that is not a real Yakima promo can void cashback-portal tracking, so the honest move is to rely on the automatic public sale.
chuck-e-cheese-military-discount: Chuck E. Cheese has offered the Alpha and Bravo military bundles since 2016 (originally $26.99 and $44.99; prices have risen since). They’re valid for active-duty military and their dependents, National Guard and Reservists and their dependents, and retired service members, and they’re redeemed in person: "Valid military ID or proof of service is required" at the counter. There is no verified online-verification flow — the aggregator "10%–25% off" figures and "verify at chuckecheese.com" lines are fabricated boilerplate, not a Chuck E. Cheese source.

Because the bundles are fixed prices rather than a stackable percentage, treat them as non-combinable with coupons, Groupon, or Fun Pass food discounts — you pick one offer per order. That matters because Chuck E. Cheese’s public deals are strong: the $49.99 Ultimate Summer Family Deal packs more Play Points and extras, and a Fun Pass (from $7.99/mo) or the seasonal Summer Fun Pass ($54.99+) with unlimited visits out-values any single-visit bundle for repeat families.

Separately, Chuck E. Cheese has for years run a Veterans Day free personal 1-topping pizza on Nov 11 (documented in 2016 and 2022): active-duty, National Guard, retired service members, and veterans with a valid military ID or proof of service, limit one per person, no purchase required, in store only (not delivery). It’s recurring but not guaranteed — re-verify about two weeks before Nov 11 each year. E-commerce routes (GovX, cashback portals, the Exchange) don’t apply to an in-person entertainment venue.
sesame-place-military-discount: Verification is by ID.me on the park’s website before purchase. You click through from the park’s military tickets page to the active-duty or veteran offer, verify your status with ID.me, then claim the free tickets or buy the 50% tickets in the same online flow. There is no front-gate military discount — both offers are explicitly "not available at the front gate," so unverified walk-ups pay the full gate price. Bring valid military or dependent ID to the park; active-status offers require ID reflecting active status at the gate.

Know which tier you’re in. The free annual admission is limited to active duty, activated or drilling reservists, and National Guard — it explicitly excludes military retirees, inactive/standby reserve, Merchant Marine, and DoD civilians. Retirees aren’t left out entirely: Sesame Place defines veterans as "retired, honorably separated officers and enlisted personnel of the U.S. military," so retirees qualify for the 50% single-day offer instead. Each park also sets its own windows: Philadelphia’s free and 50% offers run through December 31, 2026, while San Diego’s current veteran window requires visiting by July 31, 2026.

A freshness warning: many blogs and military-family sites still promote free veteran admission at Sesame Place. That limited promo — free one-day admission for veterans plus up to six direct dependents, claimed by June 30 and used by July 5, 2026 — has expired. The standing veteran offer is 50% off, not free. And since that 50% is computed off the front-gate price (which is meaningfully higher than the everyday online price of $110.99 for a Philadelphia one-day ticket), price-check it against the day’s public online sale before buying: online flash sales have historically priced one-day tickets low enough to rival the gate-based 50% math.

Visiting more than once? The 2026 Military Season Pass (ID.me-gated; price not published — it appears in the ID.me flow) includes unlimited visits through January 3, 2027, two free guest tickets, free general parking, 10% off food and beverage, 15% off merchandise, and 20% off Abby’s Magic Queue. Unlike the ticket offers, the pass’s perks layer on every visit. Families with base access can also compare MWR/ITT ticket-office prices, which the San Diego park confirms sell discounted Sesame Place tickets year-round.
handr-block-military-discount: MilTax is the core military benefit. It is distributed through Military OneSource, not hrblock.com, and is free for active-duty service members, Guard and Reserve members (regardless of activation), eligible family members, survivors, and recent veterans up to 365 days from their separation or retirement date. It handles military-specific situations — PCS moves, combat pay, and multi-state returns — and includes free military-trained tax consultants. Eligibility is verified through DEERS and your Military OneSource login.

Separately, H&R Block at the Exchange gives all authorized Exchange shoppers — including honorably discharged veterans and DoD and Coast Guard civilians — 10% off in-office tax preparation at select Exchange locations, plus a free second-look review and a 100% accuracy guarantee. It is a seasonal, location-based benefit redeemed at H&R Block offices at the Exchange, not an online-software code.

Be cautious of coupon and "military discount" round-up sites claiming H&R Block gives "up to 10%–25%" off as a military or veteran discount on its online software. That is false — ID.me confirms no military discount exists on the DIY product, and those figures are general public promo codes available to anyone (and often expired), not a military benefit. We deliberately do not present any online percentage as a military discount here.

Bottom line: if you qualify for MilTax, use it — nothing H&R Block sells beats free. If you are past the 365-day window but want in-person help and have Exchange access, take the 10% Exchange discount. And if you are not MilTax-eligible with a simple return, H&R Block Free Online or IRS Free File is $0 too.
ace-hardware-military-discount: The defining fact is Ace’s structure: it is a retailer-owned cooperative of independently owned stores, and the corporation does not set a binding military discount percentage. Any "10% / up to 20%" figure you see is set — or not — by the individual owner, which is why no official Ace page states one.

The corporately documented benefit is the Military Double Points Program. Per Ace’s retailer instructions, the cashier asks for the customer’s service ID card to verify active, reserve, retired, or disabled status, scans the customer’s Ace Rewards account, and scans a Military Double Points barcode to add the points. There is no corporate online verification provider (no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX requirement) mandated by Ace for an in-store military benefit — verification is a physical ID shown at the register, and exact accepted IDs are at the store’s discretion.

For context on the rewards math: Ace Rewards earns 10 points per $1, and 2,500 points equals a $5 reward, so double points works out to about 20 points per $1. Ace Rewards is free, often includes a signup bonus, and offers free delivery on orders of $50 or more — the double-points benefit, where a store participates, effectively doubles your earn rate.
kroger-military-discount: The honest headline is that Kroger’s military benefit is a dated, holiday event, not an everyday rate. Multiple independent outlets quoting Kroger PR confirm the same mechanics for Veterans Day: 10% off eligible items for veterans, active military, and dependents, in-store and via Kroger Pickup, with a valid military ID or DD214 and a scanned loyalty card. Some divisions (for example the Dallas Division across North Texas, East Texas, and Louisiana) have run a one-day Memorial Day 10% event, but that is not confirmed chain-wide.

Because the discount is run division by division, availability genuinely varies. Kroger’s newsroom has framed Veterans Day as "in stores nationwide," yet the confirmations are division- and market-level, and cashier interpretation of what counts as "eligible" can differ. Treat it as a real but YMMV benefit: verify your local banner and ad each year, and don’t assume Delivery (as opposed to Pickup) is included.

There is no third-party verification and no online code for this offer — it is a manual military-ID check at the register plus your Kroger loyalty card. Kroger’s separate "Verified Savings" program is for government-assistance/SNAP shoppers, not a military path. So ignore any site telling you to "enter a Kroger military promo code" — none exists.

Every other day, the free loyalty wallet is the real saving. The Plus/Rewards card unlocks card and sale prices plus digital coupons and earns fuel points — 1 point per $1, with 100 points worth 10¢/gal (up to $1/gal on one big fill) or, new for 2026, $1 off groceries (up to $10/day). Frequent Kroger fuel/delivery shoppers can add the paid Boost membership (~$59–$99/yr as of July 2026) for 2X points and free delivery. And eligible service members and veterans should compare the on-base commissary, which sells groceries at or near cost with no sales tax and often beats any civilian grocery discount.
great-clips-military-discount: Thank a Veteran is the verified, nationwide benefit. On Nov 11, veterans and active service members get a free haircut or a free-haircut card at any U.S. salon, and non-military supporters can grab a card to pay it forward to a service member. The company reports more than 2.5 million free haircuts and $39M+ in value to date, and it has run the program for well over a decade — but it recurs annually rather than by contract, so confirm the current-year terms about two weeks before Veterans Day.

Everyday pricing is where the honesty matters. Because each Great Clips is independently owned, there is no national everyday military rate. Community reports commonly mention a small ~$2–$5 military or first-responder discount at many — but not all — salons, always at the manager or owner’s discretion. Some locations offer nothing everyday and point customers to the Veterans Day event. Treat any everyday figure as YMMV and ask your specific salon.

Verification is simple and in person. There is no online verifier — you confirm eligibility in the salon with a military ID or proof of service, at the salon’s discretion. For Veterans Day, staff honor the free-haircut program directly. In Canada, participating salons run the equivalent on Remembrance Day (Nov 11) — confirm with the local salon.
toro-military-discount: The 18% comes off MSRP (the manufacturer’s suggested retail price), not the lower "minimum advertised price" shown on toro.com. Before you buy, ask the dealer for the model’s MSRP and compare 18%-off-MSRP against the dealer’s normal out-the-door price — on a unit the dealer would already discount, the real savings can be smaller than a flat 18%.

American Hero is dealer-only and in person, so there is no code to enter online. It cannot be combined with a toro.com cart, a coupon-site code, or a cashback portal, and it does not automatically beat a dealer’s negotiated price or a seasonal financing or rebate promo. Treat it as one option to compare, not an automatic win.

Military and first-responder eligibility are equal here — both get the same 18%, and there is no larger separate "veteran" tier. Toro verifies status in person at the dealer with a valid military ID (or first-responder identification), not through ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute.
hyundai-military-discount: This is a flat manufacturer bonus, not a percentage discount, and it is applied on top of the price you negotiate. Hyundai’s terms are precise about where it lands: on a finance contract it must go toward the down payment; on a lease, toward the amount due at signing or capitalized-cost reduction. It is never paid out as cash, and the terms don’t say how an outright cash purchase is handled — ask the dealer before you assume. All new Hyundai models qualify, including the electrified line, SUVs, and sedans, but fleet, service-rental, and demo vehicles are excluded and the car must come from dealer stock.

Be careful with stacking claims. Hyundai’s official disclaimer names exactly two programs the bonus cannot combine with — the First Responders Program and Hyundai Circle plan sales — and says nothing either way about the national retail offers (APR specials, retail bonus cash) you see advertised. Several dealer sites claim the bonus "combines with most current offers," but that language is the dealers’, not Hyundai’s — get it confirmed in writing before you rely on it. One more correction worth knowing: ID.me’s own shop directory says it is "not aware" of a Hyundai military discount. That listing is stale — Hyundai’s official program page exists and uses ID.me itself as the verification partner. Trust hyundaiusa.com.

Because the $500 is flat and runs all year, the real lever is everything around it: negotiate your best price first, time the purchase to a strong retail-incentive month, and treat the bonus as the last line on the deal. If you also qualify for the First Responders Program or have Hyundai Circle access, compute each program’s total separately — they cannot combine with the military bonus — and take the single lowest.
dji-military-discount: GovX is an identity-verification marketplace that gives the military and first-responder communities access to member pricing from many brands. You create a free account, verify your status once with GovX ID, and then shop participating storefronts. DJI has a storefront on GovX, but because DJI enforces minimum advertised pricing (MAP), member prices on current-season models are frequently near retail — and GovX is a closed marketplace, so you cannot layer a DJI newsletter code, DJI Credit, or a cashback portal on top. Treat GovX as a route to price-check, not an automatic discount, and factor in GovX shipping before assuming it is cheaper.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites advertising a specific "DJI military discount" percentage or checkout code. DJI does not publish a brand-run military rate, so those figures are unverified and the codes generally do not work. We deliberately omit the circulating number here because repeating it would imply an offer DJI does not run.

The steady-state ways to actually save on DJI are public, not military-gated. DJI Official Refurbished lists last-generation models at up to ~20% off with full-functionality testing, a new box, and the same 1-year warranty and after-sales policy as new — usually the best evergreen deal. DJI’s seasonal sales go deeper still: Spring Sales run up to ~35% off and Summer Sales up to ~50% off select products, and they are the year’s cheapest new-unit prices for most buyers. Newsletter subscribers get early access to those events.

For smaller everyday orders, sign up for the DJI newsletter for 5% off a first order and earn 1% back in DJI Credit (a reward that layers on direct orders, though it is trivial next to a seasonal sale). Best Buy and other authorized US retailers also carry DJI and run their own sale events and price-matching; they offer no military discount, but they are competitive substitutes worth watching. Whether GovX, a sale, or refurb wins comes down to two questions: is a DJI Spring/Summer sale live right now, and are you open to a refurbished unit?
hyperice-military-discount: Hyperice uses ID.me at its own checkout and GovX ID on the GovX store. Both confirm your status — military, veteran, or first responder — through the provider, so you never send documents to Hyperice, and verification is free. The ID.me discount is tied to eligible full-price items only, and the amount appears after you verify.

The GovX side is a genuine dedicated storefront, not a code: it lists 13 Hyperice products, including the Normatec Elite, Hypervolt 3, 3 Pro, and Go 3, Normatec 3 Legs, Venom 2, Hyperice X, and the Hyperboot. GovX hides member pricing until you log in, so register (free) and check the price on your exact model before assuming either channel wins. ID.me and GovX are alternatives, not a stack — a Hyperice order goes through one or the other.

Because the military discount is full-price-only, Hyperice's public sale calendar matters more than the badge. Seasonal promos and bundle codes have run as deep as ~$250 off flagship devices — historically deepest around Black Friday/Cyber Monday, with Memorial Day, July 4, and Labor Day sales too — and during those windows the sale price usually beats the ID.me discount. Recovery-gear shoppers on deals forums report the same pattern: the ID.me discount is modest (around 10%, unverified) and doesn't apply during sales, so many simply wait for a Hypervolt or Normatec sale.

For a big-ticket Normatec system, also weigh the military Exchange (shopmyexchange.com / mynavyexchange.com) if Hyperice is stocked — tax-free checkout saves roughly the sales tax, which matters on an ~$800 item. Hyperice controls all of these terms and can change them at any time, so confirm the current offer before you buy.
tire-rack-military-discount: All the math below uses one baseline: a set of 4 mid-range all-season tires at roughly $800 installed-equivalent, a typical passenger-car replacement set (installation extra; Tire Rack ships to an installer). Effective costs include local sales tax except the exchange channel, which is tax-free.

The debunk matters here because the fabrications are specific. Pages like the "Ultimate Guide to Tire Rack Military Discount" invent a "5%/10% off with ID.me" or a "military code." None exists. Tire Rack has no military checkout, no verification partner, and no GovX store, and ID.me’s own page confirms it. Treat any "Tire Rack military promo code" as fabricated — the real 5% military tire discounts are at Discount Tire and Tire Agent, not Tire Rack.

The honest maximum-savings move is a two-step comparison. First, price your tire on Tire Rack with any live manufacturer rebate — that rebate (open to everyone) usually beats a 5% military line item on most sets, and Tire Rack’s selection and reviews are the reason to shop there. Then compare Discount Tire’s 5% military discount, which stacks with rebates and instant savings, and — if you’re exchange-eligible — the tax-free base tire center. Buy wherever the all-in cost is lowest.

One caveat we flag rather than assert: cashback-portal coverage of tirerack.com is unconfirmed as of this verification, so don’t count on a Rakuten/TopCashback layer at Tire Rack until you’ve checked it.
bogg-bag-military-discount: Verification runs through GovX ID, which confirms your eligibility online and issues a single-use code per verification. You can re-verify up to once per 30 days for a new code, and Bogg’s help center handles verification trouble. The code applies at checkout on the US site once your order reaches the $50 minimum.

Coupon aggregators (SimplyCodes "30% off," Groupon "up to $30 off") imply large stackable codes exist. Those are generic sitewide or affiliate promos, not a military benefit — and Bogg’s terms explicitly bar combining the military code with other discounts. The verified military benefit is 10% off $50+ via GovX, with digital e-gift cards excluded.

Because nothing stacks, the decision is simple: at or above $50 with no bigger public code in hand, take the GovX 10%. If a rare public sale beats 10%, take the sale instead (you can’t combine them). WeSalute lists a separate cashback offer for Bogg as an alternative path, but it’s not combinable with the code and the 10% usually wins. Bogg has no owned retail stores, so redemption is online only.
american-express-military-discount: The MLA benefit is the one that lets an eligible servicemember or spouse hold the flagship $895 Platinum Card (or the Gold, Delta SkyMiles Reserve, Hilton Aspire, and other premium cards) for $0 a year while keeping the full card benefits. It applies to any personal Amex card for covered borrowers — active duty, Guard/Reserve on orders of more than 30 days, and their spouses and dependents. It is automatic: Amex checks the application against Department of Defense records and applies the $0 fee as soon as the account is opened. No provider like ID.me or SheerID is involved.

SCRA is the mirror image for accounts you already held before going on active duty. It caps the interest rate on eligible pre-service accounts at 6%, and Amex’s definition of "interest" includes annual membership fees, late fees, and returned-payment fees — so those are effectively waived during the active-duty period. Unlike MLA, SCRA is not automatic: you must request it, provide documentation (active-duty orders, change-of-station orders, a DD-214, or a commanding-officer letter), and file while on active duty or within 180 days of leaving it. Servicemembers have reported meaningful historical fee refunds on long-held accounts, though amounts depend entirely on account history.

The make-or-break variable is the account-open date, and the two reliefs do not stack on one card. If you are active-duty or a military spouse applying for a new card now, MLA zeroes the fee automatically — do nothing extra. If you already had the card before serving, file an SCRA request with your orders. And if you are a veteran no longer on active duty and more than 180 days out, there is no ongoing benefit — the card is standard-priced. Other issuers (Chase, USAA, Navy Federal, Citi) also honor SCRA/MLA — though their fee treatment varies by issuer — and Amex is notable for applying the $0 fee to its most premium cards.
altra-military-discount: Altra’s on-site military route is ExpertVoice, the pro-deal platform. You verify your service status once at ExpertVoice account creation, then connect on altrarunning.com; when you’re logged in, your discount is applied at checkout with no code. Altra’s ExpertVoice group is literally named “Altra VIP (40% off MSRP),” which is where the “up to 40%” figure comes from — but the exact price you pay is gated behind verification, so treat 40% as the ceiling, not a guarantee.

The second route is GovX, which runs an “Altra” storefront and an “Altra Open Box” storefront for returned or like-new pairs. GovX verifies current and former military, first responders, healthcare, and government employees; its pricing is gated behind login and community reports put it around 25% off (unverified — confirm at login). Nothing stacks on a GovX order.

Watch the terms before you assume ExpertVoice is always the cheapest: it’s personal and immediate-family use only, capped at $2,000 per year, and every ExpertVoice order is final sale. It also can’t be combined with any other offer — and if a public sale price is lower, altrarunning.com charges you the sale price. On a $140 Lone Peak, up to 40% off MSRP lands near $84 if you qualify, but a live 30%+ public sale can beat it, and the two never combine.

One disambiguation to get right: the top “Altra military discount” search result promising an “exclusive 20% discount … partnered with GovX” is from Altra Arrows — an archery-arrow manufacturer (The Outdoor Group, LLC) — not Altra Running footwear. For the shoe brand, the verified routes are ExpertVoice and the GovX “Altra” / “Altra Open Box” storefronts.
rsvlts-military-discount: RSVLTS’s discount is a verified-community flat rate: a standing 25% off sitewide gated behind identity verification. RSVLTS uses VerifyPass — referred to on-site as the "ID system" or "ID Discount" — to confirm military or veteran status. You verify once through VerifyPass and receive a single-use code; because codes are valid for one purchase only, each order needs a fresh code pull (limit 1 per customer per 24 hours).

The military benefit is an always-on offer rather than a set of holiday spikes, so there is no distinct military-holiday calendar to chase — the 25% rate is available every day of the year. RSVLTS also runs public seasonal sales (for example a 4th of July sale) that are open to everyone; since only one code applies per order, you would use whichever single path nets the lower price.

Be cautious of coupon aggregators advertising RSVLTS "military" savings of 40%, 60%, or "up to 75% off." None of these is a verified RSVLTS military rate. The only official military figure is 25% off, and the only legitimate way to get the code is through RSVLTS’s VerifyPass verification flow — codes are unique, one-time, and non-shareable.
RSVLTS controls these terms and can change them at any time, so treat the numbers here as a starting point and confirm the current offer on RSVLTS’s official military discount page before you buy.
origin-military-discount: Origin uses GovX — its site loads GovX’s govx.js verification script. You verify military or government eligibility through GovX; re-verification cadence and code terms are set by GovX. Verification support runs through GovX, and order support through Origin.

The GovX discount is for regular-priced items only, so it does not apply to (or stack on) sale/20%-off items, and it does not stack with other promo codes. Free shipping over $75 is automatic and independent of the discount.

Aggregator "20% OFF Origin Maine" claims and the historical VETERAN2020 code are unverified — the verified military mechanic is GovX, applied to regular-priced items, with the exact percentage revealed after verification. When an item is in the 20% Off collection or a seasonal sale, take the sale (GovX will not stack on it).
verizon-fios-military-discount: Verizon verifies eligibility through ID.me, a third-party digital identity network also used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. During registration ID.me may ask you to upload a document validating your service, and it works in all major browsers except Internet Explorer. Importantly, your Fios ID.me verification and your mobile ID.me verification are registered separately — verifying for one does not apply the other.

The Fios military discount lasts as long as you keep a qualifying home internet plan and verified military status; there is no annual renewal, though Verizon may occasionally re-verify. You can hold only one "serve" discount per account (military, first responder, nurse, or teacher), and it cannot be combined with Deals at Work — but it does stack with Auto Pay + paper-free billing and with the Mobile + Home Discount.

A word on the actual dollars: Verizon confirms a Fios military discount exists but does not post a distinct military-only figure. On its /military/ page, the Fios "military" prices ($44.99 / $64.99 / $74.99 / $94.99 for 300 Mbps / 500 Mbps / 1 Gig / 2 Gig) mirror the standard Auto Pay + Mobile + Home bundle prices anyone who bundles can get, versus standard promo prices of $49.99 / $74.99 / $89.99 / $109.99. Third-party coupon sites that claim "10–17% off" or "$5–$15/mo" are restating that bundle discount, not a military-only cut. The clearly military-specific wins are the waived $99 setup fee (online) and the $5/mo Digital Voice / Home Device Advisor add-on — so verify the true monthly delta live at checkout after ID.me.
sling-tv-military-discount: Sling TV is a month-to-month live-TV subscription from DISH/EchoStar, and its checkout has no military gate of any kind — no ID.me wallet offer, no SheerID form, no GovX marketplace listing, and no support-ticket workaround. ID.me Shop’s own Sling TV military page says it is not aware of any Sling military discount, which is about as direct as a "no" gets: the company whose business is military verification has nothing to verify here. Sling’s promo calendar is sports- and season-driven (NFL, March Madness passes, device deals), not military-holiday-driven — no Veterans Day or Memorial Day military promo history was found.

Be cautious of coupon aggregators — beansid.com, worthepenny, valuecom, militarydisc.org and similar — that publish "Sling TV military discount" pages implying codes exist. No Sling military discount exists; ID.me itself says so, and Sling publishes none. Any "Sling military promo code" those pages list is a repackaged public intro offer or fabricated, and entering outside codes at checkout is exactly what tends to void a cashback-portal payout.

The honest savings math on a first quarter of Sling Orange & Blue (~$65.99/mo advertised, ~$198 at full price): the common 50%-off-first-month intro offer brings it to roughly $165, and signing up through a cashback portal adds a one-time bounty of up to about $15, landing near $150 — about $48 saved with zero eligibility requirements. Because Sling’s intro pricing applies automatically rather than via a code, it’s generally portal-safe. If you know you’ll keep the service for a quarter, price the prepay bundles (from $49.99 for 3 months on the entry tier, higher for Orange/Blue/combo) against intro-then-full-price for your exact plan — the two paths are mutually exclusive. Plan prices are July 2026 editorial-roundup figures; verify at signup.

Even without a military discount, service members have honest ways to watch for less. Sling Freestream is free, ad-supported, and needs no account gymnastics. Sling is contract-free, so pausing around seasons you don’t watch is a legitimate play, and sports day/month passes (when offered) beat a full subscription for single events. And if a military-discounted service is the actual goal, cross-shop YouTube TV: its ID.me-verified military offer ($67.99/mo for 12 months per its published terms) is the standout real military deal in live-TV streaming.
grand-hyatt-deer-valley-military-discoun: Salute to Service is run by the hotel itself, for eligible stays from November 20, 2024 onward. Booking goes through a dedicated online portal (with email support at SaluteToService@hyatt.com) that verifies eligibility before you get the discounted rate — there is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID step. The sources confirm discounted lodging but not a fixed room percentage, so treat the room rate as date-dependent and check your dates in the portal.

Keep the three discounts straight, because aggregators blur them: the 75% figure is the Grand Hyatt lodging-guest ticket benefit — it is not a room discount, and it is not Deer Valley Resort’s own ~25% ticket rate. The hotel program’s eligibility list is also broader than the resort’s, naming National Guard, 100% disabled veterans, and DoD civilians explicitly. And coupon-site "Grand Hyatt promo codes" aren’t real — the two genuine paths are the Salute to Service portal and the MILVET rate on hyatt.com.

The chain-wide Hyatt Veteran & Military Rate is the alternative worth pricing: Special Offer Code MILVET takes 10–15% off the Hyatt Standard Rate, is refundable, covers immediate family (parents, children and legal wards, spouses, domestic partners), and is verified with a Military/Veteran ID or DD-214 at check-in. It also earns World of Hyatt points and elite-night credit. Hyatt’s discounted rates are mutually exclusive, so compare the portal rate, MILVET, and any Member or Advance Purchase rate and book the lowest — your points and elite status still apply on eligible rates.

For a Deer Valley ski trip, the deepest total value for an eligible member is usually Salute to Service lodging plus the up-to-75%-off tickets bought at the property. Traveling on official government orders instead? Hyatt’s Government rate (a per-diem-style rate) may be deepest on the room. And if you’re not staying at the hotel at all, use Deer Valley Resort’s own ~25% military ticket rate — a separate offer covered in our Deer Valley Resort guide.
outer-banks-hotels-military-discount: The chain-hotel path is the classic travel/loyalty pattern: status stacks, rates don’t. The Hilton Garden Inn Outer Banks/Kitty Hawk offers page is the template — its "Military Family Rate" covers active and retired military, veterans, and their families at participating hotels, but the same page lists an Advance Purchase rate up to 17% off, AAA up to 10%, and Senior up to 6%. Those rates are mutually exclusive, so the winning move is to price every rate you qualify for and book the single lowest, direct, while signed into the loyalty program so points and status still apply. On official orders, the GSA per-diem rate is the tool instead: Dare County lodging caps for FY2026 are $133/night October–March and September, $190 April–May, and $254 June–August, with $74 meals & incidentals — a reimbursement ceiling for federal/DoD travelers, not a leisure discount.

Vacation rentals — the Outer Banks’ dominant lodging product — carry small, discretionary military discounts from individual property-management companies, and the terms differ company by company. Resort Realty publishes up to 5% with code MILITARY for active, retired, and reserve members ("not applicable to discharged personnel"), 7-night minimum, ID plus license at booking, participating homes only. Village Realty advertises up to 5% for "past and present" service members on week-plus stays, with ID validated at their office during your stay. Coastal Carolina (active & retired) and Sun Realty (military plus first responders and K-12/post-secondary educators, 2026 only) don’t publish an amount; Beach Realty (active duty & veterans) says it "varies per home" and is often off-season-only. All are full-week, non-combinable, new-reservation offers — so never assume a number or your eligibility; check that specific company’s page.

The third product is the one most military families miss: the Armed Forces Vacation Club, which sells 7-night condo weeks at the Outer Banks Beach Club in Kill Devil Hills from roughly $369–$569 total (some dates lower), plus a $10/night amenity fee, to the eligible military community — membership is free, "based on eligibility." On a per-night basis that undercuts almost any hotel-room total on the beach. It’s a closed program: no coupon, portal, or chain rate stacks on it.

One debunk worth carrying with you: Tripadvisor’s "Outer Banks Hotels with Military Discounts" list ranks Sea Ranch Resort third, yet Sea Ranch’s own specials page publishes no military discount at all — only "Stay More, Save More" and advance-purchase offers. Aggregator lists are unreliable at the property level, and no OBX property publishes a fixed destination-wide military percentage. Confirm the current rate with the specific hotel or rental company before you rely on it. Season matters more than holidays here: OBX pricing is driven by the tourism calendar, rates fall sharply November–March, and several rental military discounts only apply off-season.
vans-military-discount: The dedicated Vans military-discount program URL that previously existed now returns a 404, and the current US Current Offers page lists no military, veteran, or first-responder discount. Historically Vans did run a SheerID-verified military offer, but that cannot be verified on any Vans-owned source today, so we do not present it as active.

Every "Vans 10% military discount" figure found in research traces to third-party aggregators (ID.me Shop, WorthEPenny, UCMJ, dealhack) or mall and retail-directory listings — none of which are primary, and several of which appear stale. The generic SheerID "military-discount" slug those sites surface for Vans actually resolves to a NOBULL offer, not Vans — a clear example of aggregator mismatching. Treat all non-Vans "10%" figures as unverified.

The confirmed ways to save at Vans today are: join Vans Family (free) for 15% off your first order, opt into the SMS list for 15% off, take advantage of free shipping (Vans Family on $50+, guests on $99+), and watch for seasonal sitewide sales such as the 30%-off event running June 16–28, 2026 — often a bigger saving than a 10% military discount would be, and with no verification required.
nfl-shop-military-discount: NFL Shop verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. At checkout you click the Troop ID button (military) or the First Responder ID button, verify once with a free ID.me account, and the 15% is passed automatically to your cart. You’re not auto-subscribed to any newsletter by verifying, and ID.me support is available 24/7.

The single most important term is that the 15% "cannot be combined with any other promotional codes." That makes it an either/or against every other lever: the 10% newsletter code, any Outlet coupon, and — in practice — cashback, because an ID.me-gated checkout typically breaks portal tracking. So treat the 15% as a substitute for a sale, never an add-on.

Because it’s a substitute, the honest move is to price Outlet first. NFL Shop’s Outlet and Sale routinely run 30–60% off the public price, and on a marked-down jersey that public price beats 15% off full retail — and you can’t put the military code on top anyway. Use the 15% on new, full-price gear; take the public markdown on everything else.

A note on the noise: coupon aggregators inflate this offer, headlining "60% discounts" or implying stackable "military codes." The only verified military/first-responder discount is 15% via ID.me at checkout. Any "military + coupon stack" or flat greater-than-15% military claim is unverified, and the "up to 60%" figure is Outlet clearance depth on the public price, not a military rate.
jared-military-discount: Jared verifies eligibility through ID.me. Verification starts in your cart (or from Jared’s military discount page): sign in to a free ID.me account, confirm your military status, and ID.me issues a discount code you can enter at jared.com checkout or present at any Jared store. Because it is a code-based system discount, in-store redemption uses the exact same ID.me code — there is no separate register-discretion program.

The exclusions list is the real gatekeeper. Clearance, loose diamonds, custom items, previously owned merchandise, gift cards, warranties, repairs, trade-in purchases, and nearly every prestige watch brand Jared carries — Tacori, TAG Heuer, Movado, Breitling, Longines, Rado, Tissot, and more — never get the 10%. If your piece is on that list, the military discount simply does not apply, and your best move is Jared’s public sale calendar.

One thing to watch: some aggregator pages advertise a 20% or even 25% Jared military discount. Those figures are unsupported or tied to a dated seasonal promo — Jared’s own page says the military discount is 10%, with heavy exclusions. Treat anything higher as a public promotion to verify on Jared’s Coupons & Offers page, not as the standing military rate.

Because the 10% never combines with other offers, Jared’s frequent public promotions can beat it outright. A sitewide or category sale of 10% or more wins — and on a public-price order, Rakuten’s 2% cashback (rate as of July 14, 2026) may track on top, while applying the ID.me code is exactly the kind of non-portal coupon that typically reduces or voids cashback. Check the coupons page before you verify.
sixt-military-discount: Verification is handled by GoCertify, an independent verification service — not ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute. You verify your status before booking, on the GoCertify offer page. SIXT’s page does not state whether a SIXT account is required, nor a re-verification frequency, so don’t assume "verify once forever." Accepted IDs include a U.S. Armed Forces ID or an Army/Air National Guard Reserve ID; for veterans, a driver’s license with veteran designation, a state veterans ID card, or the VA VIC. If verification fails, GoCertify offers a Support request form; for questions about which IDs are accepted, SIXT advises contacting the specific branch before booking.

The most important caveat is that "up to 15%" is a ceiling, and the discount applies to the daily base rate only — taxes, fees, surcharges, and extras (protection packages, GPS, child seats) are excluded. Rentals must be 3–27 days, so very short 1–2 day trips won’t qualify. The offer can’t be combined with other promotions or corporate rates. SIXT’s own offer-terms page warns that an incorrect discount is occasionally applied due to a website issue, and tells renters to contact SIXT directly to fix it — so check that your confirmed rate reflects the discount.

A note on scope: SIXT’s First Responder campaign page shows country-tiered percentages (up to 15% in the US/UK/EU core, up to 10% elsewhere) and a US category restriction (Fullsize-or-higher, 3–4 day minimum). The military offer-terms page instead says "all vehicle categories" and defers full terms to post-verification, so we don’t assert those specifics for the military offer — confirm them after you verify. To save more, join SIXT ONE (free) for loyalty perks, compare the all-in total against Enterprise, Hertz, Avis/Budget, and National military rates (since SIXT’s 15% is off base rate only), and consolidate short trips into a 3+ day eligible rental.
black-rifle-coffee-military-discount: BRCC uses ID.me for its on-site identity discount and GovX for a separate discounted storefront. ID.me confirms your group (military, veteran, first responder, nurse, teacher, or government employee) by a document or account check; GovX requires a free account and its own verification for military and first responders/law enforcement. The two are different checkouts, so you pick one route per order rather than stacking them.

The single biggest win is the ID.me new-subscription discount. Because it currently shows about 50% off a first Coffee Club order, the effective price on a ~$50 first order lands near $25 — far better than the GovX route on the same cart. A common play is to take the discounted first box, then self-manage the subscription (skip or cancel before the next ships) if you do not want ongoing delivery.

For one-time bags or gear, the GovX storefront (~20%) or a live public promo code is the play, whichever is lower. Note the value here is volatile: editorial roundups still cite "25% off first subscription" and "up to 20%," while ID.me’s own store page currently displays 50% off new subscriptions — so confirm the live number at checkout. And the Veterans Day "deal" people search for is a charity donation drive, not a price cut: you pay full price and BRCC donates.
aldo-military-discount: ALDO uses SheerID to instantly confirm military status, and the offer is also surfaced through ID.me Shop. Online, verification yields a one-time code you enter at checkout; there is no permanent account discount, so you re-verify for future purchases as required. In store, an associate applies the discount when you present a valid military or veteran ID.

The key decision is 20%-off-full-price versus ALDO’s frequent public sales. The military code is non-combinable and excludes sale items, so on a just-dropped, full-price pair the 20% is the best available price, while on a style that’s already marked down the public sale stands alone and usually beats it. You can’t have both on the same item.

If you’re buying sale items, you can still layer a cashback portal (ID.me Shop or a Rakuten-style portal) on the transaction for a little extra back — but not alongside the exclusive military code. And remember the category exclusions: select limited-edition collaborations, shoe-care products, and gift cards don’t qualify.
rei-military-discount: REI’s membership is a flat $30 one-time, lifetime fee for everyone — there is no military tier or military price. Widely circulated claims of a "$20 military membership" appear only on aggregator sites; REI’s membership page lists a single $30 fee with no military discount, so we don’t present the $20 figure as fact.

The annual Co-op Member Reward is the main payoff. REI says it is typically around 10% back on eligible full-price purchases, but it is not guaranteed — it may be a Patronage Dividend, a Promotional Reward, or a combination, which REI determines each year and issues by March for the prior year. It is not earned on Outlet, sale, clearance, used gear, gift cards, classes/events, shipping, service fees, the membership fee, or tax.

Beyond the reward, members get periodic coupons and member offers, member sale pricing (the May Anniversary Sale is the headline event), free U.S. standard shipping, and Re/Supply — the year-round used-gear program that replaced REI’s in-store Garage Sales, where members buy gently used gear and trade in their own for an REI gift card.

One claim to ignore: aggregator sites also advertise a "10–20% military or bulk discount" through REI Corporate & Group Sales. REI’s Corporate & Group Sales page publishes no such terms, so we don’t assert it. Separately, veterans and Gold Star families can get a free federal America the Beautiful Military Lifetime Pass for national parks — useful for an outdoors audience, but a government program REI does not administer.
ynab-military-discount: Verification is not applicable here: YNAB runs no military verification (no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass gate) because it has no military discount to verify against. The only status YNAB verifies is college enrollment for its free-year student program — you submit a student ID, transcript, or tuition statement directly to YNAB.

On the "free year for active-duty military" rumor: the documented free-365-day offer applies to college students, not to military status. We found no YNAB primary source — pricing page, blog, support center, or referral page — offering a free year, or any discount, to active-duty military or veterans as such. Likewise, aggregator claims of limited-time military discounts on Armed Forces Day or Independence Day, and codes like "LX6SW5H" for "50% off," are unverified on any YNAB page; YNAB doesn’t publish general promo codes on its site.

For the math, take one year of YNAB as the baseline. Monthly billing costs $179.88 a year; the annual plan is $109 — about $70 less. A referral adds a free month (effectively 13 months for $109), YNAB Together spreads one subscription across up to 6 household members, and legacy YNAB 4 (classic) owners get a 10% lifetime discount on annual when they upgrade. The College Program tops everything at $0 for the first 365 days — but only with proof of current enrollment.
schlitterbahn-military-discount: The key thing to understand is that "Schlitterbahn" is no longer one program: New Braunfels resolves to sixflags.com and Galveston to enchantedparks.com, and each operator sets its own military offer. Aggregator sites still advertise "Schlitterbahn 70% off promo codes" and imply a single park-wide military deal — the verified reality is two parks, two operators, two different programs.

New Braunfels is the stronger offer: a military/veteran/first-responder ticket from about $35 (plus taxes and fees), gated by ID.me — the same identity-verification service used by the VA and the IRS — bought online only, with up to 6 tickets per verified member and free parking included. Galveston is a thinner, in-person deal: 10% off the online ticket price, applied at the ticket booth when you present a non-expired military ID, DD-214, veteran-designated driver’s license, or work ID/badge.

Because neither park lets the military discount combine with other offers or sales, always compare it against any live public advance-purchase promo and buy the cheaper path. For repeat visits, price a season pass — for two or more trips it usually beats repeat single-day military tickets. Reports of a Memorial Day free-military-admission weekend at New Braunfels circulate on aggregator sites, but we could not confirm one on the official 2026 page — treat that as unverified and re-check before planning around it.

Since the parks control pricing, verification, and combinability and can change them at any time, treat the numbers here as a starting point and verify the current offer on each park’s official page before you buy.
chase-military-discount: The MLA track is the one that matters if you’re applying now. Chase checks applicants against the Department of Defense MLA database at account opening, and for covered borrowers — active duty, Guard/Reserve on 30+ day orders, and their spouses and dependents — the annual fee on personal credit cards is reportedly adjusted to $0, including the $795 Sapphire Reserve and its co-brand lineup (Southwest, United, Marriott, Hyatt, IHG, and more; there is no published card list, but reporting is consistent that the policy is card-agnostic across the personal lineup, with authorized-user fees reportedly waived too). It’s automatic — Chase mails a benefits letter confirming the waiver, and that letter is your proof. It applies to credit-card accounts opened on or after October 3, 2017, when credit cards came under the MLA rule. Business cards are excluded. No ID.me, SheerID, or GovX is involved at any point.

The SCRA track is the mirror image for cards you held before going on active duty. Federal law caps interest on pre-service obligations at 6% with the excess forgiven; multiple military-finance outlets consistently report that Chase voluntarily goes further — 4% APR on eligible balances plus waived or credited fees, including annual fees, during active duty and for up to one year after it ends. Unlike MLA, SCRA relief is requested, not automatic: use the secure-message SCRA dropdown at chase.com/securemessages, mail Chase’s SCRA Request box in Columbus, or call Chase Military Services at 1-877-469-0110. Two conflations to avoid: the SCRA request route is for pre-service accounts only (the MLA waiver on newly opened cards needs no request), and none of the dollar figures appear on chase.com — pages quoting them, including this one, are citing Chase’s letters and editorial reporting.

The veteran-honest answer most pages skip: once you’re no longer a covered borrower, the card fee waiver goes away — separated members report Chase re-checking MLA status and reinstating fees, typically within roughly one to two years of leaving service, so never plan around a grace period. The benefit veterans do keep, and the one chase.com itself publishes, is banking: the $25 monthly service fee on Chase Premier Plus Checking ($300 a year) is waived for current servicemembers and veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces with qualifying proof (DD-214, VA ID, and similar), plus no Chase ATM fees worldwide and no fees on money orders or cashier’s checks. Other issuers — American Express, USAA, Navy Federal, Citi — also honor MLA and SCRA; Amex publishes its policy openly, while Chase’s is letter-confirmed. See the companion issuer guides to compare.
dodge-military-discount: Dodge, a Stellantis brand, runs its military program as a flat $500 factory incentive rather than a percentage off MSRP. It is verified through SheerID — not ID.me and not GovX. You submit basic information; if SheerID cannot instantly confirm you, you may be asked to upload documentation. Once confirmed, you receive an authorization number to hand the dealer.

Because the $500 stacks with most public Dodge Brand offers, the biggest savings come from timing. The incentive page notes you and the vehicle you’re interested in may also qualify for other offers, so the $500 layers on retail bonus cash and lease/APR programs. Heavy incentive months — Memorial Day, July 4, and year-end model-year closeouts — typically move far more than the $500 itself.

Separately, Stellantis Affiliate Rewards (preferred/employee-style pricing) is a distinct program that may itself apply to eligible affiliates; whether it stacks with the military bonus cash on a single deal depends on the current month’s program rules, so confirm in writing with the dealer. Personnel stationed outside the US are directed to Military AutoSource, a separate tax-advantaged overseas program.
titanic-museum-military-discount: Verification is ID-based. The museum processes military discounts at the box office when you present a valid military or veteran ID; there is no museum-issued online promo code for the everyday box-office discount. For an online purchase at Pigeon Forge, GOVX performs the military verification and issues the discounted tickets — bring physical ID even if you verified online, because the gate may ask to see it.

Ignore the aggregator noise. Coupon sites advertise a flat "40% off," a blanket "$5 adult / $3 child" military discount, and stackable "promo codes" — none of that is museum policy. The genuine, verified savings are the August and November free-admission programs plus a modest everyday box-office discount. An older Pigeon Forge "military discount" page that used an ID.me flow now redirects after the site consolidated to titanicattraction.com, so GOVX is the confirmed online path.

Terms differ by location. Both Pigeon Forge and Branson honor military and run recognition programs, but the exact everyday amounts and program dates can differ, and only Pigeon Forge is documented for the August "Celebrate Freedom" event and the GOVX online offer. Confirm the specifics with the location you plan to visit.
rothys-military-discount: s verifies military status through SheerID, an independent verification service — not ID.me. You confirm your status through SheerID
s offers Military discounts” — ID.me Shop only provides cashback via affiliate links. Rothy
hexclad-military-discount: Verification is handled by ID.me. You click "Verify with ID.me" from the HexClad Heroes page, sign in to (or create) an ID.me account, and confirm your military or first-responder status. On success, ID.me issues a unique 10% off code that auto-applies at checkout. ID.me accounts and their group verifications are managed by ID.me, which may periodically require re-verification per its own policies — HexClad does not state a HexClad-specific re-verification cadence. For verification problems, use ID.me’s help center; for order or discount questions, use HexClad’s Help Center.

The one-discount-per-order rule is the key thing to plan around. Because the Heroes 10% can’t stack with other promotions and isn’t valid during sitewide sales or Black Friday / Cyber Monday, the smart move is to compare your verified-member price against whatever sale is running and use whichever is lower for a given order. HexClad runs frequent sitewide sales with substantial markdowns, and set/bundle pricing on cookware and knife sets can already be 20–50% off MSRP independent of the Heroes program.

A couple of points HexClad’s own page leaves open: retirees aren’t separately named (they’re likely covered by ID.me’s Military/Veteran definitions), and free shipping appears on ID.me’s HexClad listing but not on HexClad’s Heroes page — so treat free shipping as ID.me-sourced until you see it confirmed at checkout. ID.me’s store page also lists other rotating HexClad offers; confirm current terms on ID.me before relying on them.
johnston-and-murphy-military-discount: Johnston & Murphy’s own site does not verify military status — there is simply no offer to unlock. That’s why the aggregator listings promising a military percentage don’t hold up: ID.me’s Johnston & Murphy page states it is "not aware that Johnston & Murphy offers Military discounts," and there is no verification flow on johnstonmurphy.com. Treat any "military code" for this brand as unverified.

The one genuine military channel is the GovX marketplace. Verified military, veterans, and other eligible members (per GovX’s rules) can buy select Johnston & Murphy footwear at member pricing on GovX’s own storefront, mirrored for VA and veteran shoppers on shopvcs.va.gov. Verification lives with GovX — a GovX ID — not with the brand. But GovX is a closed marketplace: no brand promo codes or cashback portals stack on top, returns follow GovX’s terms, and pricing must be checked per item. "GovX exists" doesn’t mean "GovX wins" — on current-season styles the public promo often beats it.

For most shoppers the bigger levers are public. Johnston & Murphy runs frequent sitewide promos — commonly 25–30% off, plus "$50 off $100"-style threshold codes — with the deepest windows historically around July 4, Labor Day, and Black Friday. Codes are one per order, so pick the larger of the percentage or the threshold code. The Sale/clearance section cuts deeper still when your size is in stock, and the free J&M Rewards program layers points and free-shipping perks onto sale prices. A cashback portal is only worth considering on a full-price, non-coupon order, where it returns a few percent.
zappos-military-discount: There is no active military verification at Zappos. Historically, Zappos verified eligibility through SheerID on a dedicated "Programs" page (create a Zappos login, verify status with SheerID, then receive a code applied for up to one year with annual re-verification). That program has been discontinued and the verification flow is no longer confirmable on Zappos.com. If Zappos relaunches a program, confirm the live provider and terms directly on Zappos.com.

The conclusion rests on primary and updated sources: ID.me states it is "not aware that Zappos offers Military discounts," Zappos’ former "truth about zappos coupons" policy page now returns a no-results state, and no military offer appears on Zappos’ live coupon or promotion pages. Stale editorial pages (and 2019 launch coverage) still describing a live 10% /c/programs discount could not be confirmed against a current Zappos source and are not treated as fact.

The real, everyone-eligible ways to save are Zappos VIP (1 point per $1, free expedited shipping), the new-subscriber 10%-off email code, clearance and seasonal sales, and occasional sitewide codes — all on top of free shipping and free 365-day returns. Service members who want a verified military discount may find one at competing footwear brands via SheerID or ID.me; verify each on its own site.
finish-line-military-discount: Verification happens in person at the register — there is no online account, no ID.me/SheerID/GovX flow, and no pre-enrollment. Because eligibility is checked on each visit, there is no “verify once” convenience; bring an accepted ID every time.
