becker-cpa-military-discount: Becker is a credentialed-education seller with employer- and government-sponsored pricing — closer to a certification / tuition vendor than a coupon-and-cashback consumer brand. That is why there is no flat "military code": military, government, and veteran eligibility is tied to your organization (via "Find Your Organization") or to your VA benefits (via the VA), not to a single military-ID verifier.

For a veteran with remaining GI Bill / VA benefits, VA direct billing is the best path by far. Becker markets itself as having a direct-billing relationship with the U.S. government, so when the VA approves and pays Becker directly for an approved review course, the out-of-pocket cost can be $0. Coverage of a prep course is conditional on VA approval, and it is separate from the GI Bill’s licensing-and-certification benefit, which reimburses the CPA exam itself up to $2,000 per test.

If you are active duty or a government worker, check "Find Your Organization" for a partner rate first — 200+ government agencies and many accounting employers sponsor Becker at reduced or no cost. Organizational pricing is already a negotiated rate, so it generally does not stack with public promo codes; take the better of the two.

If you have no affiliation and are paying yourself, the smartest move is the same one civilians use: buy the Pro package on a seasonal sale (Becker Pro is routinely ~30% off, with Black Friday / Cyber Monday historically the deepest) and route the purchase through a cashback portal like Rakuten (2.5% as of July 2026). A public promo code plus Rakuten cashback do stack — the code discounts the checkout price, and Rakuten pays cashback on the amount paid.
microcenter-military-discount: There is nothing to verify — Micro Center has no military program or verification partner. Member Pricing simply requires a free account, and in-store deals and price match are open to all shoppers. The military-, student-, and senior-discount claims on aggregator pages are inaccurate; the only profession-based discount Micro Center ever ran was a temporary pandemic-era first-responder discount that has since ended.

Micro Center’s real savings model is member pricing plus in-store deal-hunting. Member Pricing is the base layer and is free — always sign in, because it is the price rather than a coupon. On top of that, the deepest cuts live in-store: Manager’s Specials and open-box components frequently sell well below online, and a price-match guarantee lets you beat a competitor’s lower advertised price on the same item. New accounts also get a free-gift coupon (historically a flash drive).

Two community-reported claims deserve caution: shoppers cite about 5% off in-store on the Micro Center Insider Credit Card, and a forum thread references a law-enforcement discount. Neither is confirmed policy, so treat both as signal only and ask at your store. Micro Center’s deepest public sales cluster around Black Friday and Cyber Monday — open to everyone, not military-specific.
srixon-military-discount: Verification runs through SheerID, which checks your service status against its data sources at us.dunlopsports.com/dunlop/sheerID.html. If instant verification fails, SheerID requests documents (for example a DD-214 or military ID). Verification follows Dunlop Sports’ program terms — don’t assume it’s one-time-forever, as re-verification may be requested.

The discount is online-only and direct-only. Buying Srixon gear at Dick’s, Golf Galaxy, PGA Tour Superstore, or Worldwide Golf forfeits the 15% — those retailers run their own promos instead, so compare their net price against the discounted direct price (15% off a $500 full-priced club order is $425).

Because it’s full-price-only and non-combinable, the 15% is not always your best deal. Historically, Srixon’s spring Buy 3 Get 1 Free golf-ball promo (the 2024 edition is documented, roughly a February–April pattern) works out to 25% off — beating the military rate on balls. And prior-generation clubs in the sale/clearance section frequently drop 20–40%, which beats 15% off full price; the military discount wouldn’t apply to those sale items anyway.

One thing to watch: coupon sites advertise "25% off" and even "35% off" Srixon promo codes for us.dunlopsports.com — mostly expired or invented. The only verified identity-based offer is the 15% SheerID military discount; there is no ID.me route and no GovX storefront for Srixon.
eufy-military-discount: eufy’s military and first-responder discount is verified through GovX ID — a free account you create once and reuse, with real-time verification. Each purchase uses a single-use code, so you log back in to GovX to generate a fresh one for your next order. The separate student discount uses Student Beans instead.

There is no ID.me first-party checkout for eufy hardware and no separate GovX marketplace storefront — you always check out on eufy.com. eufy US does appear in ID.me’s shop directory, but that is a directory listing only; the official verification routes through GovX (and Student Beans for students), so ignore aggregator claims of an ID.me first-party eufy discount.

Because the 20% code is single-use and non-stacking, it rarely wins on price. eufy’s deepest public sales land around Prime Day (June) and Black Friday — historically up to about 60% off — and its products are frequently cheaper on Amazon with a clip-coupon. On eufy.com, a displayed sale price is a markdown, not a coupon, which is why it’s Rakuten-safe (4% cash back as of July 11, 2026), whereas applying a single-use code typically voids cashback. Reserve the 20% code for a brand-new release that isn’t discounted yet, or consider eufy Certified Refurbished (roughly 10–30% below new, with a 3-month warranty and 90-day risk-free trial).
eufy controls these terms and can change them at any time, so treat the figures here as a starting point and confirm the current offer on eufy’s official GovX discount page before you buy.
holiday-inn-military-discount: The Military Appreciation Rate is a bookable rate, not a coupon code: you select it at booking and prove eligibility at the front desk. IHG’s own terms state the discount "reflects a range of discounts off the Best Flexible Rate with a minimum discount of 5%," so anything above 5% is set by the individual hotel. It’s open to US and Canadian active duty, veterans, retired military, and family members with valid ID, is for leisure travel only, and requires a military or veteran ID at check-in. Dependents book in their own name and must check in themselves.

The separate Government Rate is for official government/military travel — federal, state, county, and local government employees, military personnel, Defense/Cost-Reimbursable Contractors, and state-funded higher-education and healthcare employees. It’s priced as a percentage off the Best Flex Rate at or under the GSA per-diem cap, and requires an official ID or work orders at check-in. Both the military and government rates earn IHG One Rewards points and neither can be combined with another offer.

This is the travel-loyalty pattern: status stacks, rates don’t. The military, government, AAA, senior, member, and advance-purchase rates are each mutually exclusive — you pick one per booking — but the booking still earns IHG One Rewards points and qualifying nights toward status when you book direct through IHG. Coupon aggregators that advertise a flat "Holiday Inn 15–20% military discount" or a "military promo code" are not stating verified IHG terms; the published floor is 5%, and the discount is a rate you select, not a code you paste.

The practical move: for a leisure stay, pull up the Military Appreciation Rate and the Best Flexible, AAA, senior, member, and Advance Purchase rates for your exact hotel and date, and book the lowest — the 10–15% Advance Purchase rate frequently beats the 5% military floor, though it’s prepaid and non-refundable. On official orders, book the Government Rate to stay within per diem. Keep a free IHG One Rewards account so every stay earns points on top of whatever rate you book.
tempur-pedic-military-discount: Verification is not applicable here: there is nothing to verify for a Tempur-Pedic discount, because the brand offers no military, veteran, or first-responder discount and uses no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX military program. The only military-specific channel is the military exchange, where eligibility is verified by the exchange itself (AAFES/NEX), not by Tempur-Pedic.

One thing to watch: military-discount listicles and coupon sites (OperationMilitaryKids, WorthEPenny, and others) repeat a "30% off via ID.me" claim for Tempur-Pedic. That is contradicted by both primary sources — Tempur-Pedic’s Help Center and ID.me’s own store pages — and appears to be a misread of a public 30%-off-Cloud sale. The "7%–50% off" coupon figures floating around are likewise public promo numbers, not military pricing.

For the math, take the entry flagship: a TEMPUR-Adapt Medium Queen at $2,299 MSRP, roughly $2,460 with an illustrative 7% sales tax. Buying through the exchange zeroes out that tax (~$161 on this cart) and ships free — the durable, repeatable win — while a typical public holiday sale plus 3% Rakuten cash back can be worth ~$370+ in combined value and keeps the 90-night trial. Tempur-Pedic’s deepest public events historically land around Memorial Day, July 4, Labor Day, and Black Friday.
hobby-lobby-military-discount: There is nothing to verify: Hobby Lobby runs no military-verification process and is not a partner of ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute for any shopper discount. No account, document upload, or re-verification exists because no military offer exists. Its customer-service FAQ has a dedicated "Sales, product pricing, & discounts" section that covers competitor price matching, bulk discounts, and rain checks — but no military discount.

Be skeptical of coupon-aggregator claims of a "10%" or "50%" Hobby Lobby military discount — none is confirmed by Hobby Lobby and they should be treated as false. In its place, Hobby Lobby uses always-on category pricing, so the "40% off" now lives in the shelf price of many departments rather than a one-item coupon.

huel-military-discount: Huel verifies eligibility through Beans iD, a free military identity-verification service — not ID.me, SheerID, or GovX (there is no Huel GovX storefront). windsor-military-discount: Windsor verifies eligibility the old-fashioned way: a physical military ID shown at the register. There is no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass step anywhere in Windsor’s official terms, and no online military-discount flow at all. Any coupon-site claim that you can "verify through ID.me" for a Windsor military discount is inaccurate — the ID.me storefront some sites point to belongs to Devon Windsor, an unrelated swimwear label, not this Windsor.

One aggregator worth debunking directly: WorthEPenny claims Windsor gives "up to 10% – 25%" to military "including active duty, veterans, and their immediate families" via ID.me. Every part of that beyond the 10% figure is false against Windsor’s own terms — the discount is a flat 10%, for active-duty members and spouses only, in store only, with a physical military ID. Treat any "Windsor military code" or "online military discount" claim from coupon sites as fabricated.

Because Windsor’s terms say the military offer "cannot be combined with any other code, offer, promotion, or discount" and excludes sale and clearance, the smart move is to compare paths, not stack them. An active-duty member or spouse buying a full-price dress in a store takes the 10%. Everyone else — including veterans — does better with the 15% sign-up offer on a regular-priced item, or a live public sale when one is running. Online, the military discount doesn’t apply at all, so use the welcome or sale price and optionally layer a cashback portal under it.
caraway-military-discount: The standout mechanic is stackability. Most brand military discounts can’t be combined with a sale, but MilitaryBridge describes the Caraway 10% as a "stackable offer … on top of most current Caraway sales." So the play is to time a purchase to a Caraway sale, shop through the MilitaryBridge link, and apply their code to take an extra 10% off the already-reduced price — that stack usually beats ID.me cashback or GOVX on its own.

Verification is light-touch because there is no native Caraway military page to gate. Two things to keep honest: the exact ID.me and GOVX military figures aren’t publicly posted (they’re gated behind login), so we don’t publish numbers for them, and the "up to 40–50% off for military" you may see on aggregators is a platform slogan, not a Caraway military rate. The verified reality is a 10% MilitaryBridge partner discount that stacks on sales, ID.me cashback for everyone, and gated GOVX pricing.
mazda-military-discount: The $500 is a factory (manufacturer) rebate, not dealer margin, which is why it stacks on top of the price you negotiate. tyr-military-discount: TYR verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. In its base terms the 20% is scoped to full-price items, but shoppers consistently report it applying on top of sitewide sale and clearance prices — with one code still enforced per order. Coupon-aggregator pages advertise vague "TYR 30–50% off" codes and an unspecified "essential worker" discount. The only verified TYR discount tied to military status is the 20% ID.me offer — treat aggregator percentages as public-sale echoes, not a military benefit. mizuno-military-discount: GOVX is an identity-verification marketplace that gives the military and first-responder communities access to member pricing from many brands. Mizuno has a storefront on GOVX, but it stocks only select footwear and per-item discounts vary — so treat GOVX as a price to check rather than a fixed, always-on military discount. For a verified service member, the smart move is to price-check GOVX against Mizuno’s current sale and take GOVX only when it is genuinely lower, which it frequently is not.
on-cloud-military-discount: On verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. chatgpt-military-discount: The benefit is a limited-window free year, not a recurring percentage. levis-military-discount: Levi’s verifies eligibility through SheerID. The stacking rule is what makes this offer unusually good. pizza-hut-military-discount: How verification works: it doesn’t — there is no Pizza Hut military verification. Pizza Hut has no storefront on ID.me Shop, GovX, or SheerID (checked July 7, 2026). bylt-military-discount: BYLT’s discount is powered by ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. vertx-military-discount: Vertx uses GovX ID to verify military and first-responder status. Vertx Rewards (1 point per $1) is likewise non-combinable — its discount codes can’t stack with any other offer, and only one reward redeems per order.

A debunk for the coupon-site claims: aggregator "promo codes" like "$115 off" or "25% off" are not the military discount and generally will not stack with it. The only verified Vertx military/first-responder offer is 15% off regular-price items via GovX ID. There is no verified ID.me, SheerID, WeSalute, or VerifyPass program for Vertx.
lexus-military-discount: This is a flat $1,000 reward, not a percentage off MSRP — on a $52,775 2026 RX it works out to roughly 1.9%. Because it is applied at signing inside the finance or lease paperwork, it comes on top of whatever price you negotiate: treat it as genuinely additive, and negotiate the vehicle price as if the rebate did not exist before you claim it.

Verification is a two-part process. Online, you verify your military status through ID.me from the official program page. At the dealership, you also present physical proof of service — a Leave and Earnings Statement, Military ID card, or DD Form 214. Even then, the rebate is contingent on credit approval and a qualifying salary from Lexus Financial Services, so verification alone does not guarantee it.

On stacking: the published terms name only three programs as non-combinable — the College Graduate Reward Program, the iFi Program, and the Lease-End Refi Program — with a limit of one rebate per transaction. Lexus does not publish whether the Military Rebate combines with its public APR and lease-cash offers, so do not assume either way: ask the dealer to price the deal with and without each offer. For eligible recent graduates who are not military-eligible, the separate $1,000 College Rebate delivers the same value through the same LFS mechanism.

Two comparisons worth knowing: the sibling Toyota Military Rebate is $500 through Toyota Financial Services — half the Lexus amount — and Military AutoSource, the overseas military car-buying program, carries Toyota but not Lexus, so there is no OCONUS purchase path for a new Lexus. Active-duty members financing with LFS can also ask about Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) benefits, which LFS administers separately from the rebate.
steve-madden-military-discount: Steve Madden verifies eligibility through SheerID, not ID.me — despite ID.me pages ranking for "Steve Madden military discount," ID.me does not verify this offer. Verification is per-offer and typically instant; if the instant check fails, SheerID may ask for a supporting document. The result is a single-use code rather than a reusable wallet, so you re-verify for future offers.

The 25% military code cannot be combined with any other offer, discount, promo code, price match, or the employee discount, and it excludes sale, clearance, and preorder items, gift cards, tax, and shipping. That makes it a full-price-only lever. Because the brand discounts heavily and often — reported Memorial Day and Black Friday sales up to roughly 50% off — the public sale usually beats the 25% code on anything already marked down, and the code is barred from sale items anyway.

The best total-savings logic is simple: for a brand-new, full-price style you want now, use the 25% SheerID code. For an item already on sale or clearance, skip the code and take the public sale price plus about 3% Rakuten cashback (as of July 13, 2026). A SheerID single-use code is not a Rakuten-listed code and may void cashback tracking, so don’t rely on stacking the two.
motosport-military-discount: MotoSport’s discount is powered by ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. You verify your military (or first-responder) status once, and ID.me issues a single-use 10% code for checkout. MotoSport references only ID.me — despite third-party listing sites that claim it also verifies through GovX or SheerID, MotoSport’s own military and first-responder pages mention neither.

The reason the discount is worth planning around is the stacking rule. Official language calls it "an additional 10% off … all year long," and it reduces the current listed price — sale items included. So the winning path is a clearance or seasonal-sale item plus your 10% code on top. On a roughly $300 riding-gear cart from a discount-eligible brand, a 40%-off clearance price of about $180 minus the 10% code lands near $162 — about 46% off — versus $270 (10% off) at full price.

The landmine is the MAP-restricted brand list. Manufacturers such as 100%, 6D, AFX, AGV, Alpinestars, Answer, and Asterisk do not allow MotoSport to extend any discount, so the 10% code is simply dead on those brands. When your item is a MAP-restricted brand, the levers that still work are MotoSport’s price match and 30-day best-deal guaranty, or Rakuten cashback on a no-code order.

Two more things worth knowing. Only one coupon code applies per order, so during a code-based promo you pick the better of the two, not both. And the 30-day best-deal guaranty is a post-purchase refund of the difference that layers separately from the code — you can buy with your 10% code and still claim a price-match refund within 30 days if an authorized US dealer is cheaper or the price drops.
guitar-center-military-discount: Guitar Center uses SheerID to confirm military status. You click to verify your military ID through a SheerID flow on Guitar Center’s offer page; on successful verification you get a unique promo code to apply at checkout. Account creation requirements and re-verification frequency are not stated on the official page — SheerID verifications are typically one-time per offer/code, but Guitar Center does not publish a re-verification cadence, so don’t assume "verify once forever." If automatic verification fails, the page directs shoppers to claim by phone at 866-498-7882.

The discount is a single-item offer: it applies to one qualifying item priced $199 or more, up to a $500 maximum discount, and it can’t be combined with other offers or used on past purchases. A broad exclusion list applies (discounted/clearance items, used gear, vintage equipment, gift cards, Pro Coverage, Rentals, Repairs, and Lessons).

Because the offer page frames the discount "Now thru Nov. 11," it may be a Veterans Day–window promotion rather than a standing year-round program. Confirm it’s live before relying on it, especially outside November. For deeper savings on excluded gear, compare Guitar Center’s seasonal sales, open-box/used inventory, and financing.
anthropologie-military-discount: Anthropologie uses ID.me for exactly one thing: its teacher discount. Current educators in the US and Canada — classroom and substitute teachers, principals, professors, and librarians — get 20% off full-price items after verifying their educator status through ID.me (online) or by showing documentation in store. There is no ID.me or SheerID verification path for military, veterans, first responders, students, nurses, or government employees, and no Anthropologie GovX storefront.

That teacher 20% is full-price only and "cannot be combined with other promotions," prior purchases, or gift cards, and it excludes sale, furniture and other home, bridal, Terrain, and select brands. Because Anthropologie’s public sales often reach 30–40%, a live sale usually beats the teacher discount outright — so even eligible teachers should compare.

For a service member who is not a teacher, the honest best path is Anthropologie’s near-constant sale events (30–40% off), stacked with roughly 2% Rakuten cashback on a no-code order. New shoppers should also join the free AnthroPerks loyalty program for a $20-off welcome offer, and can add Review & Reward coupons (20–25% off) and a 10% signup offer over time. These are one-per-order and non-combinable, so pick the single deepest discount per purchase.

Every "Anthropologie military discount" percentage and code circulating on coupon sites — the "10% military discount," the "ANTHROBSESSED 30% off" code — is contradicted by the primary source: ID.me, Anthropologie’s own verification partner, states it is not aware of any Anthropologie military discount. Treat all of them as invented, and save through the real sale-plus-cashback path instead.
motel-6-military-discount: There is no online verification provider on the official Motel 6 Military Rate — no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX. You self-select the rate at booking and the front desk validates a military ID at check-in (suggested proof: a military ID card or DD Form 214; reports indicate similar proof of service is accepted). For the enhanced 15% rate you must hold a paid WeSalute+ membership and show your WeSalute+ ID at check-in. Because most properties are franchised, confirm acceptance with the specific location before relying on the rate.

The Military Rate does not stack. Motel 6’s official terms say it “cannot be combined with other promotions or memberships” and carries “no cash value,” so only one rate applies per reservation. WeSalute+’s 15% replaces rather than adds to the 10% or a public sale, and My6 loyalty points are a separate mechanic, not a stackable discount. In practice, the prepaid or advance-purchase rate frequently undercuts the 10% Military Rate — so the honest advice is to compare every time and book the cheaper rate.

Motel 6 runs the Military Rate continuously rather than as dated Veterans Day or Memorial Day flash sales, and it’s reported to be valid only in a country the guest has served in or is currently serving (US/Canada properties). To save the most: compare the Military Rate against the prepaid/My6 rate, join My6 (free) for member rates and points, and consider WeSalute+ for 15% nationwide only if your stay volume offsets the membership fee.
rokform-military-discount: Rokform uses ID.me, a third-party identity service, to confirm military, first-responder, and nurse status; GovX ID is an alternate path through Rokform’s GovX storefront. You verify once, and your exclusive code is automatically applied at checkout — no percentage is shown on rokform.com until then. The discount is personal-use only, and ID.me monitors for misuse; re-verification cadence is set by ID.me, not stated by Rokform. ID.me support is available 24/7 at help.id.me.

Stacking is the key rule to understand: Rokform’s promo terms state offers "cannot be combined with other promotions, discounts or coupon codes." The ID.me discount arrives as a discount code, so it will not stack with a sitewide promo code — you pick the larger of the two. ID.me and GovX are alternate doors to the same kind of gated code, not two discounts to stack.

For the math: on a $69.99 Rugged Case for a current flagship phone, the 30% ID.me discount lands at $48.99 (saving $21.00), while the 20% public July 2026 code would have been $55.99. Aggregators cite deeper peak-season public sales (up to 40–50%), but those magnitudes are unverified — if a public sale in your cart genuinely beats 30%, take it instead. Third-party retailers (Amazon, Cycle Gear) occasionally mark specific SKUs below the 30% net price, so a quick comparison never hurts.
fox-nation-military-discount: Verification runs through SheerID — not ID.me, and no code is needed, despite the "Fox Nation military coupon codes" that aggregator sites list. SheerID first attempts an instant database check; if that fails, you upload supporting documents (a DD-214-type document showing name, branch, and discharge date or current affiliation — never a military ID photo, which SheerID legally can’t process). Fox’s eligibility wording is precise: anyone who "has served or is currently serving" in the U.S. Armed Forces. Spouse and dependent eligibility is not stated in the official source.

The renewal cliff is the part to plan for. After the free year, the subscription bills automatically at 50% off the then-current annual rate — about $35.94/year at today’s $71.88 list — for additional one-year periods, with Fox emailing a reminder before the charge. Set a calendar reminder: if you don’t want year two, cancel at least 24 hours before the renewal date in My Account. That ~$36/year renewal is already half the public price, but Fox’s public promo windows for new subscribers occasionally dip below it — the July 2026 America-250 promo hit $17.76 for year one (it ended July 5, 2026; historical, not a live offer) — so compare before letting it auto-renew.

The sibling offers cover most non-military readers: active first responders — firefighters, EMTs/paramedics, and law enforcement including federal LE — get their own free first year (not combinable with the military offer; pick one if you’re eligible for both), and enrolled students get Fox Nation free with a .edu email on a new account. Everyone else should grab a seasonal annual promo (Fox has historically run steep windows around July 4, Veterans Day, and Black Friday) — and annual always beats monthly: $71.88 versus $107.88 per year at standard pricing.

Ruled-out paths, so you don’t waste time: no cashback portal listed Fox Nation as of July 4, 2026; GovX lists Fox Nation but only refers members to this same offer; WeSalute members get the identical free year (the direct SheerID path is simpler); and there’s no gift-card, exchange, or pro-deal channel for this subscription. The free year also does not extend to FOX One or the FOX One + Fox Nation bundle — verified members pay public pricing there.
hotelscom-military-discount: Hotels.com verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used across hundreds of military offers. You verify once — service-record lookup, .mil email, or document upload, with most verifications clearing in minutes — and your ID.me login then unlocks this and the sibling Expedia offer. The coupon itself is issued per redemption: ID.me’s guidance is to click through and complete your booking at code-redemption time, so expect to re-click through ID.me for each new booking.

About the percentage: ID.me Shop’s Hotels.com page listed the military offer at "10% off" on July 14, 2026 — and listed the identical rate for nurses, first responders, teachers, government employees, medical providers, and students. But Military.com and prior coverage put the value at 8%, and the parallel Expedia coupon’s own terms page documented 8% with a $40 cap while marketing said 10% (June 2026). Treat "10%, no cap" as unconfirmed for Hotels.com: read the exact percentage and terms shown inside your verified flow before you count on the number.

The stacking rules decide what’s actually cheapest. The coupon and cashback don’t stack — Rakuten’s Hotels.com terms void cashback when a code not listed on Rakuten is used, and the ID.me military coupon is exactly that. One coupon per booking, and coupon vs. member/promo pricing is effectively either/or. One Key Member Prices, by contrast, are logged-in site pricing rather than codes, so Rakuten tracking (up to 3% as of July 14, 2026) survives them — that’s why member price + cashback often ties or beats the coupon. On a $450 three-night baseline stay: coupon ≈ $405 (or $414 if the live value is 8%), Member Price + Rakuten ≈ $392, and a mobile-app-exclusive deal of up to 25% ≈ $338 when your property carries one.

One more watch-out: aggregator sites advertise "60% off Hotels.com military discounts" or "10–25% military discounts." The verified military offer is a single ID.me-gated coupon — listed 10%, historically 8% — on select bookings; the 25–60% figures are public sale and mobile-app promos relabeled as military deals. And for chain hotels (Hilton, Marriott, IHG, Choice), price the chain’s own military rate booked direct before using any Hotels.com path — OTA bookings usually forfeit hotel points, elite credit, and chain military rates.
rail-explorers-military-discount: Verification is not applicable here: Rail Explorers operates no military verification program with any provider, so any site prompting you to "verify military status for a Rail Explorers code" is not an official Rail Explorers channel. In one case we traced, a SheerID "Unlock this Military-Only Offer" link surfacing in Rail Explorers searches resolves — per SheerID’s own program metadata — to Clinique Canada, a cosmetics brand, not Rail Explorers.

The discounts that do exist are structural, not identity-based. The 10% group rate requires 10 or more riders on a weekday, eligible tour, booked and paid in full by one representative — and because tickets are priced per railbike ("no discount for empty seats"), it only helps if you actually fill enough railbikes to hit 10 people. The 15% rebooking credit is an invitation to rebook after a cancel, late arrival, or no-show, not a public code.

For math, take the baseline one Tandem Explorer railbike (seats 2) at the Rhode Island Division, list price $99. A qualifying group booking brings each railbike to $89.10; a rebooked ride costs $84.15. Everyone else — including service members — pays the $99 list price, because there is simply no military rate to apply.
apple-music-military-discount: The honest core fact: Apple Music’s subscription has no military or veteran discount. Military.com puts it plainly — "Apple may not offer a military discount at this time." So the starting point for any service member is not a military code, but the Student plan (if you qualify), a carrier bundle, or Apple One.

Why the "4 free months" claim keeps circulating. In 2021 Apple ran a limited-time promotion offering up to four free months of Apple Music to US military and veterans, verified through ID.me. That promo expired on August 1, 2021. Dozens of "Apple Music military discount" pages still advertise it as current — it is not. Presenting the expired 2021 offer as live is inaccurate, and there is no ID.me military verification for Apple Music today.

Don’t confuse the hardware discount with streaming. Apple’s Veterans and Military Store runs the Veterans and Military Purchase Program, roughly 10% off eligible Macs and iPads for verified service members. It is a device program and has nothing to do with the Apple Music subscription. Buying a MacBook at the military rate saves you money on the laptop, not on your streaming.

Where the real subscription savings are. The genuine ongoing discount is the Student plan at $5.99/mo with Apple TV+ included (up to 48 months), verified via UNiDAYS/SheerID for enrolled degree-granting college students — a status many GI Bill users hold. Beyond that, several wireless carriers include Apple Music free on certain plans (often the best deal of all), Apple One bundles Music with TV+, iCloud+ and Arcade for less than buying them separately, and a free trial lets new subscribers start at $0. None of these is a military benefit, but each is a real, honest way to lower your price.
epic-pass-military-discount: The Epic Military Pass is itself the discount — it is not a code stacked on the regular pass. You buy a distinct military-priced product after SheerID verification, so you cannot also apply the young-adult 20% or other pass discounts on top. Two perks come bundled automatically: Epic Mountain Rewards (20% off on-mountain food, lodging, lessons, and rentals) and, new for 2026/27, 10 Epic Friend Tickets (up to 50% off lift tickets for friends and family). Those are perks, not stackable coupons.

Verification is powered by SheerID and runs inside the purchase flow. Depending on status it may confirm automatically before purchase, or route you to upload documents at verify.sheerid.com/vail-military-upload. Approval is per person and per season, so every spouse and dependent must be verified separately. Eligible groups include active duty, Guard/Reserve (Title 32), retired members, veterans, registered dependents, and Gold Star Families; Australian and Canadian forces also qualify for the Epic Military Pass.

On value, no other path is close. Active, Guard/Reserve, retired members and their dependents pay about $215 (spring) versus ~$1,089 retail; veterans pay about $620, still roughly 43% under retail. If you only ski Keystone, the Liberty Pass is the single-resort option. There is no GovX, exchange, or cashback route that sells this pass — the official military pass is the maximum-savings path. Buy in early spring before the ~May 25 price increase; spring buyers also get free summer lift access plus 20% off summer bike, golf, food, and lodging.
texas-de-brazil-military-discount: The Heroes’ Discount is verified in person, at the table, by restaurant staff — there is no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, WeSalute, or VerifyPass integration and no reusable online military code. Bring a physical military/veteran ID or badge each visit; acceptance is at the restaurant’s discretion.

A note on the percentage: some aggregators and a March 2025 post still cite 15%, but the brand’s own Heroes’ Discount page as of July 13, 2026 reads 10%. Treat 10% as the current, verified figure and confirm at the table.

For the biggest savings, time your visit to Veterans Day (November) or Memorial Day (May), when Texas de Brazil has historically discounted dinner 25–50% with guests included — far better than the everyday 10%. Frequent diners save most on the VIP Club ladder, where $50+ post-discount visits climb from 25% to 50% (3rd visit) to a free meal (5th visit).
sun-outdoors-military-discount: Sun Outdoors does not use an online verification provider — there is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID gate. You apply the SALUTE code yourself at booking and then show proof of military service at check-in (or at signing for a seasonal or annual stay). Eligibility is confirmed manually at the property, so bring a valid military or veteran ID.

The discount comes in two forms for two kinds of stay: 20% off select short-term RV sites, tent sites, and vacation rentals, or a flat $200 off a new seasonal or annual stay. They are separate offers for different stay types — you use whichever fits your booking, not both on one reservation. The $200 version is a one-time, non-refundable credit for new long-term guests only.

Because SALUTE can’t be combined with any other offer or with Sun’s weekly/monthly pricing, the smartest move is to price-check. For most short trips the 20% code wins, but on longer stays Sun’s own weekly or monthly rate can beat 20% off nightly, and a live public seasonal sale may occasionally net lower. You can only use one, so compare and take the single best. Confirm the current terms on Sun Outdoors’ official military-offer page before you book.
general-motors-military-discount: The GM Military Appreciation Program is verified through ID.me at gmmilitaryappreciation.com. You register once, validate your status, then request a time-limited Authorization Number — up to two per year, each valid 90 days. Present it to the dealer at the start of the deal along with a copy of your driver’s license. GM makes the final eligibility decision and may audit, requesting a military ID, a marriage license for a sponsored spouse, or title/registration.

The program’s most concrete, guaranteed wins are the $75 dealer documentation-fee cap and protection from being talked up above a set price. Because GM publishes no dollar figure and no combinable list, whether current Customer, Bonus, or Loyalty Cash stacks on top is model-specific — make the dealer show every national incentive that applies to your VIN. On heavily-incentivized or slow-moving models, a well-negotiated street price with those same public incentives can match or even beat the program figure, so treat the program price as your ceiling and take the lower of the two quotes.

A few claims that circulate on aggregator and dealer pages are not supported by GM’s own materials: a "$500 additional bonus cash" figure, guaranteed Corvette eligibility, and automatic stacking with Customer/Loyalty/financing offers. GM publishes no dollar figure, no combinable list, and no model guarantee — only "not available with some other offers." Also note that gmmilitarydiscount.com is now a parked/defunct domain; the live program is gmmilitaryappreciation.com, so ignore any page telling you to print a "Go Code" from the old domain. There is no online-checkout or promo-code path — this is an in-dealership vehicle purchase.
daniel-defense-military-discount: The MILE 20% is a customer-group price applied automatically once VerifyPass clears — it is not a stackable promo code. Coupon aggregators headline "20% off Daniel Defense" as if it were a public code, but that figure tracks the MILE group discount, not anything you can paste at checkout.

MILE and Brownells VALOR are separate ecosystems with different verifiers (VerifyPass for MILE, ID.me for VALOR) and different stores. You pick one per purchase; they do not combine. VALOR’s advantage is spouse and surviving-spouse eligibility plus one verified cart across 1,200+ brands, but its member price is not published until you verify.

On a baseline DDM4 V7 listed at $2,099, the MILE 20% lands around $1,679 — about $420 off — with the transfer fee waived if you pick a Preferred Dealer. Because Daniel Defense controls the terms and the 20% came from a dated June 2026 post, confirm the current rate on the live program page before you buy.
feetures-military-discount: Feetures verifies the military discount manually by email — you contact hello@feetures.com and they assist. There is no third-party verification portal (ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or VerifyPass) for this discount. You never need to send photos of a military ID or CAC; a simple email request is all Feetures asks for.

Because Feetures allows only one coupon per order, the 10% military code, the 15% welcome code for first orders, and any other code are mutually exclusive — you pick the biggest single one. On a first-ever Feetures order the 15% welcome code beats the 10% military code; on repeat orders, email for the 10% code unless a live bundle or sale runs deeper.

Feetures’ Perfect Pair Rewards loyalty program accrues points on every order regardless of the code you use, so it is the one layer that effectively adds up over time. Eligible ExpertVoice pros can access far deeper pro pricing through the Feetures ExpertVoice store, though that is not a military benefit and eligibility is not automatic.
public-storage-military-discount: Aggregators (WorthEPenny, DontPayFull, TenereTeam, and others) headline a "Public Storage military discount — up to 50% off." There is no verified first-party military discount. The "up to 50%" is Public Storage’s public first-month promo, available to anyone booking online — not a military rate. The WeSalute "up to 50% off monthly rent" listing sits behind a paid WeSalute+ membership and repackages that same public promo; paying ~$9.99/mo to unlock a discount you can get free at publicstorage.com is usually a net loss.

The one thing that is genuinely and uniquely military here is statutory, not promotional. Under 50 U.S.C. § 3958, a self-storage operator may not enforce a storage lien — no auction or foreclosure of your stored property — without a court order during your period of military service and for 90 days after; a knowing violation is a criminal offense. Under 50 U.S.C. § 3955, you can terminate a term lease with no penalty using PCS orders or deployment orders of 90 or more days, by delivering written notice and a copy of your orders; the lease ends 30 days after the next rent due date. You can’t use orders you already held when you signed. These rights are statutory and cannot be waived away by lease fine print.

On price, every path leads back to the public online promo. On a 10×10 unit at roughly $150/mo standard rent, the public $1-first-month deal brings the first month to about $30 (the ~$29 admin fee still applies), and the up-to-50%-off alternative brings it to about $104 — both open to anyone. The walk-in rate (~$179) is the one to avoid; always book the web price online. Promos cover rent only, never the admin fee or the lock, on any path.

If a real military storage discount matters to you, some competitors do publish one — CubeSmart, and some Extra Space and Storage Rentals of America locations advertise military offers (verify locally). And if you’re deploying long-term, weigh terminating and re-renting later (using your SCRA lease-termination right) against paying to hold an empty unit.
bj-military-discount: s uses ID.me to confirm military/veteran eligibility. You create or sign in to a free ID.me account, verify your service once, and ID.me passes an eligibility token to BJ
t confirm you automatically. Verification is per-person and tied to your ID.me identity; BJ
s a first-year rate that renews at full price.",
vivid-seats-military-discount: Vivid Seats verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. You authenticate once, ID.me confirms your military (or other eligible) status, and the discount applies at checkout. Re-verification may be requested periodically per ID.me’s policy, and verification issues route through ID.me’s help center.

The most important number is the cap, not the percentage. Ten percent capped at $30 means the discount maxes at a $300 ticket subtotal; on a $600 order the effective rate is about 5%. And it never touches Vivid Seats’ service fees, which are a large share of the total — so the real out-the-door savings are smaller than “10% off the order” implies. Any claim of “10% off everything including fees” is inaccurate.

Because the ID.me code is non-combinable, treat it as one lever among several. On orders around $300 or less it usually wins outright. On larger orders, compare a live public promo code to the flat $30 cap and take the bigger; a cashback portal can layer on a public code (not on the ID.me code). Vivid Seats Rewards (buy-10-get-1) accrues regardless. For military-priced event tickets outside Vivid Seats entirely, GovX Tickets is a separate channel.
omaha-zoo-military-discount: Military pricing is a discrete ticket type — you select military tickets at purchase and should expect to show a valid military ID at the gate. It does not stack with other coupons. The zoo publishes seasonal prices: summer military adult is $30.55 (vs $33.95 standard) and military child $23.35 (vs $25.95), with lower absolute prices in spring/fall and winter.

In person, a valid military ID at the gate is the practical proof. Online, the zoo is an ID.me Shop participant, so ID.me may handle verification for online ticket purchases. Immediate-family free entry on Veterans Day is tied to the service member’s status.

The Veterans Day free-admission day is a long-running annual tradition (a prior announcement noted a 12th consecutive year), and there is a separate Veteran’s Recognition Day event. Aggregator "30%/35% off" coupons are unverified — the zoo’s published military pricing is roughly 10% off.
specialized-military-discount: Specialized routes its military discount through ID.me. You create a free ID.me account and verify your eligibility once; ID.me confirms your status and unlocks the Hero Pro portal. There is no confirmed GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute path for Specialized — ID.me is the named partner. (GovX carries competitor e-bike brands, not Specialized.)

The Hero Pro Program is separate from the Specialized Pro Program on ExpertVoice, which is an industry-only channel for cycling and outdoor-industry professionals, partners, and ambassadors — that is not a military discount and should not be confused with Hero Pro.
Specialized and ID.me can re-verify eligibility and change or end the program at any time, so confirm the current terms on Specialized’s official Hero Pro page before you buy.
mdt-military-discount: There’s no automated verification. MDT’s support team issues codes by email; the published policy — one sentence, last updated March 4, 2026 — states no documentation requirements, so expect them to specify what proof (if any) they need when you write. Nothing in the policy states how often you can request a code or whether it’s single-use, so ask in the same email.

Ignore the coupon-site noise. Aggregators advertise "up to 30% off MDT coupons," "70% OFF promo codes," and embellished military terms — 10–25% off, immediate-family eligibility, in-store use, third-party verification. None of that appears in MDT’s own help center. What MDT itself publishes is exactly this: a 10% code for military and law enforcement, issued by emailing support. Treat every other number and condition as fabricated until MDT confirms it.

The one thing that can beat the code is MDT’s own calendar. Black Friday is, in MDT’s words, "the one sale we have every year" — everything on the site goes on sale at varying discounts, and factory seconds and overstock are listed for the deepest cuts. The sale is announced through MDT’s newsletter, and the item list isn’t published until it starts. On a $449.99 ORYX Chassis System, the 10% code takes you to about $405 — sale pricing or a factory second can go lower, so late-November buyers should compare before burning the code.

No GovX storefront for MDT was found as of July 14, 2026, and no cashback portal was verified for mdttac.com — this is a two-path brand: the emailed code or the annual sale. If neither works for you, Brownells and OpticsPlanet carry deep MDT catalogs and run their own promos (Brownells has advertised up to 43% off MDT items) that can beat 10%-off-list on your exact SKU — those are the retailers’ own deals, separate from MDT’s code.
2nd-swing-military-discount: The PING Military Rebate is the centerpiece of 2nd Swing’s military-discount page, but it is a PING manufacturer program, not a 2nd Swing store discount. It pays $10–$30 per eligible PING club — Drivers $30, Fairway woods $20, Hybrids $15, Irons $10, Wedges $10, Putters $15 — on specific new PING models bought within the rebate window (Jan 30–Aug 1, 2026), with submissions due by September 1, 2026. It is open to active duty, active reserves, and military retirees, and it is not combinable with other offers.

Separately, 2nd Swing runs seasonal, form-gated “extra 10% off used clubs” promos around military holidays. Its Memorial Day 2026 offer began May 21 and gave veterans and active military an extra 10% off used clubs after completing a sign-up form; it excludes all new and custom-order clubs. A Veterans Day promo recurs each November. These are holiday-gated, so never assume the 10% code is currently live — verify before you rely on it.

Be cautious of coupon and aggregator sites (WorthEPenny, ValueCom, SimplyCodes) that advertise a 2nd Swing “10–25% military discount” and imply an ID.me service tier. That storewide military discount does not exist — ID.me itself confirms it is unaware of one. The verified realities are narrower: a models-specific PING manufacturer rebate, seasonal 10%-off-used-clubs holiday promos, and ID.me-portal cashback that is open to everyone, not just military.

The real, year-round savings engine at 2nd Swing is not a military badge at all — it is the used/pre-owned inventory (routinely 30–70% off retail) plus the trade-in program, which credits your old clubs toward a purchase and usually dwarfs any 10% promo. For a service member, the honest playbook is: shop pre-owned and trade in for the biggest savings, file the PING rebate on eligible new PING clubs, and grab the 10% used-club code if a military-holiday promo is live. ID.me Shop portal cashback (new up to 5%, other up to 2.5%) is a small extra for any member.
four-seasons-military-discount: Four Seasons is an ultra-luxury hotel brand, and like most of that tier it does not run a service-based room discount. Its booking widget holds senior, government, corporate, AAA, and friends-and-family rate types, but there is no published "military" rate code. A government rate may exist for official or qualified travel, but that is not a leisure veteran discount — it carries its own eligibility and rules.

The one genuinely "military" lever connected to the Four Seasons name is a third-party offer: 10% off vacation packages booked through American Airlines Vacations, with eligibility checked by WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage). That discount applies to bundled air+hotel packages, not a standalone Four Seasons room booking, so it cannot be added to a room-only fourseasons.com reservation. If you are booking a package, compare the package total against booking flights plus a perked hotel rate separately.

Be careful not to confuse Four Seasons Hotels & Resorts with the "Lodge of Four Seasons" in Lake Ozark, Missouri (4seasonsresort.com). That golf resort advertises its own "Exclusive Military Discount" with military ID at arrival, but it is a completely separate, unaffiliated company. Aggregators frequently scrape its "military ID at arrival" copy and mislabel it as a Four Seasons chain benefit — it is not.

For a real Four Seasons stay, the honest best value comes from perk programs rather than a discount percentage. Booking the Best Available Rate through Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts (with an Amex Platinum or Centurion card) or a Virtuoso / Four Seasons Preferred Partner travel advisor gets you the same nightly rate plus a property credit (often around $100), free breakfast, room upgrades, and a free 4th night on stays of four or more nights — a package that typically beats a hypothetical flat 10% off. Military-only portals like American Forces Travel are also worth checking for a member rate, along with the public seasonal offers at fourseasons.com/offers.
cinemark-military-discount: In person, verification is a visual check of a valid U.S. Government-issued military ID at the box office — no account required. Online, GovX requires a free account and a one-time military/government status verification before you can buy discounted tickets; GovX (not Cinemark) controls that verification and may re-verify per its own policy. ID.me lists Cinemark but does not state any verified terms, so don’t rely on it as the rate source. If a local theatre says it doesn’t participate, the discount is unavailable there — there’s no corporate override.

The defining feature here is that there is no published rate. Cinemark sets the military price per theatre and repeatedly directs guests to check locally, so no honest page can promise a percentage — treat any "10%" or "25%" on coupon sites as unverified. One eligibility nuance worth flagging: Cinemark’s prose honors "veterans," but its ID list and box-office mechanic assume a current government military ID, which separated (non-retired) veterans often don’t carry. If that’s you, ask your local theatre whether a VA card or DD-214 is accepted before counting on the discount.

To save more, everyone can use Cinemark’s Discount Tuesdays (discounted tickets all day Tuesday at participating theatres) and matinee pricing (up to $6 off at earlier showtimes). The free Movie Fan tier includes Discount Tuesday savings, and paid Movie Club adds a monthly 2D ticket, 20% off concessions, and waived online fees. Separate student and senior discounts exist too. And it’s worth comparing: AMC and Regal also offer box-office military pricing with ID, with amounts varying by location at all three chains.
enterprise-car-rental-military-discount: The honest headline: there is no flashy "20% off" veteran discount at Enterprise. There is a modest, verified 5% off leisure base rates for the whole military and government community, plus a separate official-travel contract rate for those on orders. Veterans qualify through the 5% Government Leisure rate — there is no larger veteran-only percentage.

Government Leisure vs. Official Travel. Leisure is off-duty, personal travel and gets 5% off base rates (you must be 21+ to book). Official is on-duty/TDY travel under the U.S. Government Car Rental Agreement; it requires official orders or a government-issued credit card and bundles unlimited CONUS/Canada mileage, damage and liability protection, and a full tank of gas. The two are mutually exclusive per trip.

Why the "up to 20–25%" claims keep circulating. Coupon aggregators and military-discount listicles advertise larger Enterprise "military discounts," but Enterprise’s own pages publish only the 5% government leisure figure plus the contracted official rate. Treat any percentage above 5% as a generic public promo or a third-party portal rate, not a military rate — the exception is the official-travel contract price you see live on orders.

Where the real savings are. Because the leisure discount is small in isolation, the smart move is to treat the 5% as a floor, not a ceiling: on the same dates, compare a USAA member rate (if you are a member), your Enterprise Plus member rate, and any live public or weekend sale, then book the lowest. Using a credit card that includes rental damage coverage can also let you decline Enterprise’s coverage on leisure rentals — a real saving that is independent of the rate.
cricut-military-discount: Cricut’s military offer is really two parallel programs in one order. The four featured machines carry a set "everyday special discounted price," and materials and accessories get an additional 15% off with free shipping. Because the 15% excludes machines, you benefit from both in a single order, but you are not stacking one percentage on top of the other.

Verification runs through gocertify, which certifies your U.S. military or veteran status and emails a code you apply in cart. Multiple aggregators mislabel this as an "ID.me" deal — it is not. Cricut does not run its military offer through ID.me, SheerID, or GovX; the ID.me Shop lists no Cricut military offer.

One honest caveat worth weighing: during Cricut’s big seasonal sales (Black Friday, Prime-style events), the public machine price sometimes dips to or below the military "everyday" price, and public materials markdowns can exceed 15%. Since the military code is not combinable, compare the live public price against the military price during a major sale and take the lower.
safariland-military-discount: Verification runs through GovX ID (not ID.me — some coupon sites get this wrong). Registration is free and typically real-time, using DoD databases, an approved email address, or a document upload depending on your group. If you already have a GovX ID account, log in to pull a fresh single-use code. Access is per-code and per-day — it is not a permanent account-level discount, and re-verification may be required per GovX terms.

The GovX 15% is one discount, not a stack: Safariland promo codes cannot be combined with other promotions or codes and are not valid on clearance or sale items, so you take whichever single discount is larger. Loyalty points also cannot be combined with other discounts.

For the deepest legitimate pricing, verified LE, military, and industry pros can apply for ExpertVoice (Bianchi/Safariland), which often runs 30%+ off eligible items, though many products are excluded. The GovX marketplace, third-party dealers, and the tax-free Exchange are separate channels from the Safariland.com code.
otterbox-military-discount: OtterBox does not run its own verification. There is no ID.me or SheerID discount on otterbox.com — the FAQ and help pages name no military checkout, and ID.me’s own OtterBox pages confirm no military or first-responder discount exists. The ID.me Shop listing for OtterBox is an Amazon-affiliate cashback page, not a verified discount.

The identity-verified routes live off OtterBox’s site. GovX runs an OtterBox storefront (up to 25% off) behind a free account, but its stock skews to older iPhone and iPad Defender cases. ExpertVoice runs an OtterBox pro store for approved members — military, veterans, and first responders — at gated pricing that can be the deepest of all, within personal-use caps.

The cleanest genuine edge on a current-model case is the tax-free Exchange: shopmyexchange.com and mynavyexchange.com stock current OtterBox cases, and eligible shoppers pay no sales tax. For everyone else, OtterBox’s public 20% welcome code or its buy-2 "35%" multi-buy usually wins on a new-model case.
xfinity-military-discount: On its official offer page, Xfinity lists three core perks for verified military members and families: one free Xfinity Mobile "Mobile Select" line for 2 years (included with Xfinity Internet), an instant upgrade to Diamond — the top Xfinity membership tier, which includes Peacock Premium at no extra cost — and NOW TV free for 1 year with 125+ live channels. Because these are tied to Xfinity Internet, the value is in stacking them onto Internet service you may already pay for.

You verify by signing in at xfinity.com/military with your Xfinity ID. Per Xfinity’s support documentation, verification is processed through SheerID, which accepts military documentation showing your name and a clear military affiliation. The offer page itself does not name SheerID — it directs status questions to 1-833-231-6446 — and it does not state how often you must re-verify.

One thing to watch: many aggregator and editorial pages still advertise a "$50 Visa prepaid card" as the Xfinity military discount. That framing is outdated. Xfinity’s current official military page describes the perks bundle above, not a prepaid card or a flat discount, as of June 23, 2026.
greyhound-military-discount: WeSalute verifies your service status once at enrollment and issues a secure WeSalute+ ID Card with a personal Travel Code; family members can be added at 50% off with their own cards and codes. Because WeSalute+ carries an annual fee, the 10% only pays off once your yearly base-fare spend times 10% clears the membership cost — a math that favors frequent riders and riding families over one-or-two-trip-a-year travelers.

Watch the coupon sites. Aggregators advertise generic Greyhound codes ("25% off," "15% off," "35% off," "10% off") as if they were a military discount. They are not — the only verified military mechanic is the WeSalute+ Card, and its terms expressly forbid combining it with other Greyhound promotions. A scraped percentage code is not a military offer, and you can’t stack it on the WeSalute rate.

A note on GovX: it has been referenced historically as a Greyhound verification route, but the current live fare flow on greyhound.com exposes the WeSalute passenger type, so WeSalute is what we document as the mechanic today.
sig-sauer-military-discount: SIG’s online discount is powered by VerifyPass — not ID.me, SheerID, or GovX. You confirm your eligibility once and receive a one-time coupon code to use at checkout on qualifying, non-sale, non-firearm gear. The offer names military and veterans, first responders, and government employees.

Firearm savings work differently. The OFF-DUTY program (launched January 2025) sets special per-model prices on select SIG firearms, redeemed in person at a participating dealer with approved purchaser ID. It is not a percentage and not a stackable coupon — it is the dealer’s program price, completed with a background check and FFL transfer.

A separate note for shoppers who qualify: GovX sells SIG accessories and optics to verified members, but it does not sell SIG firearms and does not verify SIG’s direct discount. And if you are Exchange-eligible, buying a SIG pistol tax-free at shopmyexchange.com can rival a small discount on a big-ticket firearm. Always confirm the current terms on SIG’s official pages before you buy.
red-wing-military-discount: The verified online benefit is a flat $15 off per pair, not a percentage — the exception is students, who get 15%. That matters for the math: on a $300 boot, $15 is only about 5%, but the same $15 is worth more as a percentage on a cheaper pair, and the student 15% ($45 on a $300 boot) usually beats the flat rate. The discount runs entirely through ID.me: you verify your community once at checkout, and it applies automatically to eligible footwear. It does not stack — Red Wing’s own page states it cannot be combined with other offers, and sale items and collaborations are excluded.

The single biggest savings path is not the coupon at all. If your job requires safety-rated footwear, Red Wing For Business — the company’s B2B program of employer-funded digital vouchers — can put you in approved Red Wing PPE at little or no personal cost. It is employer-gated (there is no military-specific angle), so ask your employer before paying anything out of pocket.

The often-repeated "10% in-store military discount" is real at some locations but is store-dependent, not a published brand-wide policy — many Red Wing stores are independently operated, so call your local store first and confirm the rate and the proof they need. Coupon aggregators advertising "20% off Red Wing" or generic military promo codes are not a verified standing rate; the flat $15 via ID.me is the reliable online lever, and no Red Wing/Irish Setter presence on GovX or at the military Exchange was confirmed this session.
graco-military-discount: Two authoritative sources put the "Graco military discount" question to rest. Graco’s Help Center article "Does Graco Offer a Military Discount?" states plainly that Graco does not offer a specific military discount at this time, and ID.me’s Graco page says it is not aware that Graco offers military discounts. There is no Graco storefront on GovX and no SheerID program either. So there is no percentage to claim and nothing to verify with Graco.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites that advertise a Graco "military discount" of "up to 38%," "40%," or a "HONEY10" code for 20% off. None of these trace to Graco. HONEY10 is a generic public promo code (associated with the Honey browser extension), open to anyone — not a military benefit. We deliberately omit those figures here because repeating them would imply an offer Graco does not run.

The real military-tied advantage is the exchange channel. AAFES and the Navy Exchange carry many Graco car seats, strollers, and travel systems, sold tax-free with free shipping to eligible shoppers. Because it is a closed channel, no gracobaby.com code or cashback portal layers on top — its value is the ~7–10% sales tax you do not pay plus free shipping and MILITARY STAR perks. On big-ticket items like a $300+ car seat, that tax saving alone can beat a public code.

Even without a brand-run military discount, there are honest ways to lower what you pay. Graco runs recurring ~20% off car-seat sales (the 4Ever line especially) that need no code, so a cashback portal still tracks. New subscribers get 15% off a car seat or 20% off other categories on a first full-price order. Buying three eligible items together unlocks BUNDLE3 for 25% off (not valid on toddler car seats or sale items). And retailers like Amazon, Costco, Target (RedCard 5%), Albee Baby, and Walmart carry Graco, often below MSRP — cross-shop the exact model number before you buy.
field-museum-military-discount: Verification is a simple in-person ID check at the counter — a military status ID, or an Illinois State ID with Gold Star Family status. Because it’s an in-person benefit, it cannot be applied to a pre-purchased online ticket, so active-duty members and veterans should redeem at the counter rather than buying military tickets online. There is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID gate for a museum admission.

The benefits stack up well for families. Year-round, the eligible service member or veteran gets free general admission, and up to six family members get a discounted rate. In summer, the Field Museum’s participation in the National Endowment for the Arts’ Blue Star Museums program gets the active-duty member plus up to five family members in free from May 16 through September 7, 2026 — for that, bring a DoD-issued ID such as a CAC or DD Form 1173.

One thing to note: "free general admission" covers the base ticket, but special exhibitions and All-Access packages may still carry a fee unless the day’s offer says otherwise. Illinois residents also have separate free-resident days that any resident can use, which is a handy alternative for non-eligible companions. The cheapest path for an active-duty family is a summer visit under Blue Star Museums; outside summer, the service member or veteran is free and family members pay the discounted rate.
citi-military-discount: The MLA side is what makes this valuable. The MLA caps the cost of consumer credit to covered borrowers at a 36% MAPR — and because that math must include annual fees, issuers refund them. At Citi the fee posts on the statement, then an "MLA FEE/INT CREDIT" for the full amount appears. On the new Strata Elite, military-finance editors report the credit is automatic — $595 refunded, $75 authorized-user fee waived, no documentation. On older cards (Strata Premier at $95, AAdvantage Platinum Select at $0 intro then $99, AAdvantage Executive at $595), cardholders who don’t see the credit email militaryorders@citi.com with their MLA-database certificate, with roughly 2-week processing reported. One hard federal cutoff: the MLA’s credit-card provisions took effect October 3, 2017, so card accounts opened before that date can never get MLA relief — no ranking page explains that regulatory why, but it decides real cases.

SCRA is the mirror image for cards you held before activating. Citi’s official page promises "reduced interest rates and more" for eligible servicemembers — it publishes no rate number, but editors and cardholders consistently report Citi applies 0% APR and waives fees on eligible pre-service accounts, well beyond the 6% statutory cap (under which fees count as interest and excess interest is forgiven, not deferred). Citi’s request window is also more generous than the law’s 180-day floor: file any time during active duty or within one year of release. Enroll online, or through the Military Response Unit at 877-804-1082, by fax, or by mail; benefits apply within 2–3 monthly billing cycles and protections run from your active-duty start date. Citi’s SCRA eligibility list is broad: active duty, Guard on 30+ day federal orders, PHS and NOAA commissioned officers, and spouses and dependents.

Two clarifications save readers real confusion. First, the high-volume "citibank military login" and "citi gov card" searches are about the DoD Government Travel Charge Card (GTCC) — a separate government travel-card program Citi administers, not a military benefit on personal Citi cards. Second, the lounge angle: American Airlines already gives U.S. military in uniform on same-day AA flights complimentary Admirals Club access, while the fee-waived Citi AAdvantage Executive carries full Admirals Club membership (up to $850 value) out of uniform — reported MLA-waivable if opened while covered. Other issuers (Amex, Chase, USAA, Navy Federal) also honor MLA/SCRA; Citi’s distinctive edges are the reported 0% SCRA rate and the 1-year filing window (Amex’s window is 180 days), while Amex has the longer track record of frictionless automatic waivers.
goruck-military-discount: GORUCK verifies eligibility exclusively through GovX ID — not ID.me or SheerID. You create a free GovX ID account once, verify your status (military, first responder, teacher, or government), and GovX may re-verify periodically. At checkout the GOVXID button unlocks a code that applies the 15% to full-priced items.

The Earned Service Discount was reduced from 25% off gear to 15% effective February 17, 2020, and stacking was removed at the same time. Aggregator sites still advertising “25%–50% off” GORUCK military codes are citing the pre-2020 rate or stale/generic sale codes — the current, real offer is 15% off full-priced gear via GovX ID.

Because the ESD excludes sale items and cannot stack, the smartest play is timing. GORUCK’s public sale calendar — Veterans Day (historically up to ~35% off), Memorial Day, Black Friday/Cyber Monday, “Christmas in July,” and Labor Day — is open to everyone and typically beats the 15%. Flagship packs like the GR1 rarely go on deep sale, so the 15% ESD is often their best available cut.
tecovas-military-discount: Verification is handled by ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many retailers. You verify your military status once; ID.me lets you reuse it across participating retailers, though it may re-verify or require re-authentication at its discretion, so don’t assume it’s permanent. If verification stalls, Tecovas directs customers to ID.me support and, if issues persist, to email howdy@tecovas.com.

Tecovas names only active duty, retirees, and veterans for the military discount. It does not list Reserve/National Guard, spouses, or dependents — ID.me’s standard military community often includes those groups, but because Tecovas doesn’t name them, the honest answer for any of those is "confirm it during ID.me verification." There is also no standing first responder, nurse, teacher, or government discount; enrolled students get a separate 10% via ID.me.

Two timing notes. The everyday rate is 10% and can’t be stacked, so when an item is in Tecovas’s Last Call markdown section, compare the Last Call price against 10% off full price and take the lower. And around Veterans Day, Tecovas has historically raised the military discount to 20% for a single day (it did so on Nov 11, 2024) — that was a separate, expired promotion, not the everyday rate, so watch tecovas.com/p/veterans-day in early November for any renewed offer.
amsoil-military-discount: The Preferred Customer program is AMSOIL’s membership for direct buyers. You pay a small fee — $10 for a six-month trial the first time, or $20 a year thereafter — and AMSOIL applies wholesale pricing, roughly 25% below suggested retail, automatically at checkout. It is not a coupon and not a military benefit: it is open to anyone, and AMSOIL states there are no excluded products and no minimum quantity. On a typical DIY oil-change order, that membership pays for itself on roughly the first $80–$100 you spend.

Membership adds a few real perks that stack with the wholesale price: orders of $100 or more ship free, you earn a $5 Back reward per $100 spent that you can redeem on future orders, and if you spend $500 or more in a membership year your next renewal is free. AMSOIL also runs public seasonal promotions (free shipping, free gifts, occasional percentage events) that members can use — but these are open to all customers and are never a dated, military-only percentage, so don’t count on a specific Veterans Day deal.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites advertising "AMSOIL military discount codes" or "35–50% off" promo codes — AMSOIL publishes no such code, and those figures are fabricated or stale. The often-repeated "up to 4% cash back via Rakuten" claim is also wrong: Rakuten does not carry amsoil.com directly (it lists resellers like Advance Auto Parts instead), and there is no AMSOIL storefront on GovX. Because there is no marketplace or cashback layer to add, the Preferred Customer wholesale price essentially is the savings path.

One legitimate wrinkle: some independent, veteran-owned AMSOIL dealers advertise their own military or first-responder offers — for example, sponsoring a free six-month Preferred Customer membership that waives the $10 trial fee. These are genuine but unofficial and vary dealer by dealer; AMSOIL corporate does not run them. If you find a veteran-owned dealer near you offering one, it’s a fine place to start, because you end up on the same ~25% wholesale pricing without paying the trial fee. A separate AMSOIL Dealer account gives the same wholesale price but carries business setup and commitments, so it’s only worth it if you also plan to resell.
vw-military-discount: The $500 is explicitly offered in addition to other current VW discounts/programs (restrictions may apply) — treat it as additive, not exclusive. It is one bonus per VIN, and an eligible customer can use it on up to two VW vehicles per year.

Verification is handled at the dealership via the signed Military & First Responder Claim Form plus your documentation — there is no third-party (ID.me/GovX/SheerID) portal. Keep your LES or Military ID (or department ID) and proof of household residency (if applicable) on hand.

The bonus is not redeemable for cash and is not valid on Fleet or Dealership Sale vehicles; certain performance models such as the Golf R are excluded. The program is renewed in a rolling annual window (the last published cycle ran Jan 3, 2025 – Jan 5, 2026), so confirm the current dated program with a dealer.
golds-gym-military-discount: s Gym exited Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2020, RSG Group acquired the brand and closed the U.S. corporate-owned clubs. Nearly every U.S. Gold
hawaiian-airlines-military-discount: Hawaiian’s bag waiver is verified in person by a check-in or gate agent who checks your military ID (and orders for the 5-bag on-orders allowance). Nothing is verified online, and no everyday fare percentage is gated by ID.me, GovX, or SheerID. Because the waiver is a benefit rather than a fare code, it layers on any fare — the ticket price you pay does not change what bags are covered; whether you are on orders or on personal travel sets the bag count.

The WeSalute VetRewards 5% is a different animal: it reduces the fare itself but is gated by a paid third-party membership, not by Hawaiian. Its true value is 5% minus the annual membership fee, so it only pencils out for frequent Alaska/Hawaiian flyers. Atmos Rewards status and points always stack on top of whatever fare or benefit you use, and a live public fare sale frequently beats a 5% membership discount outright.

Aggregator and AI-generated pages claiming a flat "Hawaiian Airlines military discount" percentage off fares overstate what Hawaiian publishes. Hawaiian’s own military benefit is the baggage-fee waiver; the only fare percentage is the 5% VetRewards discount through the paid WeSalute membership. Don’t confuse the two, and re-verify before each trip during the Alaska cutover.
sperry-military-discount: Sperry verifies eligibility through ID.me. You verify once with ID.me (documents or records checks, as ID.me requires), then the 20% unlocks at your online checkout. ID.me credentials are reusable across brands; how often this offer re-checks your status is set by ID.me and Sperry and isn’t published, so expect periodic re-verification. ID.me’s military community generally includes veterans and eligible family members, but Sperry doesn’t publish the sub-group list for this offer — start the ID.me flow to confirm your status qualifies.

The stacking rules are strict and worth internalizing: the 20% does not combine with anything. Sperry’s own terms say it "cannot be combined with any other promotions, coupons," and it applies only to select full-price items. So there’s no stacking it on sale prices, no adding a welcome code, and no reliable cashback on an ID.me-verified checkout. The public sale, by contrast, is prices-as-shown (no code), which normally keeps cashback-portal tracking intact — Rakuten listed roughly 2% for Sperry as of July 14, 2026, but rates move weekly, so check the live rate.

Two more routes are worth a price check. Sperry maintains a GovX storefront with member pricing (the Authentic Original 2-Eye is listed there); GovX is a closed marketplace where nothing stacks, so treat it as a substitute for sperry.com and compare its net price directly. And retailers like DSW, Famous Footwear, and Amazon frequently clear last-season Sperry colorways below the 20%-off price if you’re flexible on colorway.

One thing to watch: coupon aggregators advertise "20% off every order for military" at Sperry — and some promise "85% off Sperry coupons" or claim the military code stacks on sale items. Sperry’s own page contradicts those terms. The real offer is narrower: 20% off select items at full price, online only, non-combinable, with unstated exclusions.
us-cellular-military-discount: Here’s what changed. T-Mobile’s roughly $4.3–4.4 billion acquisition of UScellular’s wireless business closed on August 1, 2025, after the FCC approved it on July 11, 2025. UScellular’s corporate remainder was renamed Array Digital Infrastructure and kept the towers and spectrum, not the retail wireless business. The practical result: uscellular.com/military returns a 404, uscellular.com/deals/discounts points new shoppers to T-Mobile, and there is no UScellular primary source confirming an active military discount for new customers.

If you are already a UScellular subscriber, nothing forces a change immediately — you keep your current plan for now. But the transition notice is specific: self-serve account changes (adding a line, plan changes, upgrades, accessories) end May 1, 2026, UScellular Lifeline support ends March 31, 2026, and accounts migrate to T-Mobile through summer 2026.
