Whether T-Mobile will auto-map migrated customers onto a Military Savings plan or require fresh verification is not stated in official sources, so re-check after your line moves.

The live military path today is T-Mobile’s. Its Experience plans with Military Savings run about $70/month for one line with AutoPay ($75 without), scaling to roughly $720/year in savings at four lines. Eligible groups are Active Duty, Reserve, National Guard, Veterans, and Retirees across all branches, plus Gold Star family members — but not spouses of living service members or DoD civilians (unless Gold Star). Crucially, T-Mobile verifies in-house through the T-Life app, your my.t-mobile.com profile, in-store, or by phone — it does NOT use ID.me, SheerID, or GovX. You must verify within 45 days of activation or the plan reverts to Magenta at up to $20/line more per month. Our full write-up is at /discount/t-mobile-military-discount/.

Because carrier plan discounts don’t stack across carriers, this is really a "which carrier" decision. AT&T advertises 25% off (about $37.50/month for a single line, dropping to roughly $22.50/line at four lines) and is the deepest single-line percentage; Verizon’s Unlimited Welcome military pricing is about $55/month for one line. T-Mobile Military Savings is the natural path for migrating UScellular customers who value that footprint. Compare all three on coverage where you actually live, then time any device or trade-in promo separately — those run independently of the plan discount.
universal-studios-military-discount: The Orlando 2026 Military Freedom Pass functions like an annual pass: unlimited admission except on blockout dates. The 2-Park version ($220) covers Universal Studios Florida and Islands of Adventure; the 3-Park version ($255) adds Volcano Bay. It is sold only at participating base ITT/MWR ticket offices — Universal’s press release states the offer cannot be purchased at the Universal Orlando front gate — and you can buy up to 6 passes per valid military ID.

You receive vouchers rather than active tickets. At the park you activate them at a ticket booth or resort-hotel counter, with the military member or spouse present and a DEERS ID in hand; one ticket must be used by the member or spouse, and the DEERS ID is shown again at first entry. After activation, each pass is tied to its assigned person by facial recognition. An activated pass also unlocks specially priced 1-Day Epic Universe add-on tickets (Epic Universe is not part of the base pass), and Orlando offers 40% off Universal’s Cabana Bay Beach Resort plus military vacation packages booked at 1-877-801-9720.

Universal Studios Hollywood runs a separate program with none of those Orlando terms. There is no Freedom Pass; instead, military shoppers get pricing on day tickets and select passes either at a base MWR/ITT office or online by verifying their Military community through ID.me. Universal does not publish the exact Hollywood discount on its official site, and the figure varies by where you buy — base ticket offices typically offer deeper pricing than the gate — so we don’t assert a specific number.
puma-military-discount: Verification is handled by ID.me. You sign in or create a free ID.me account and confirm your eligible group; ID.me may ask for documentation (e.g., proof of military service). After verification, PUMA issues a discount code to apply at checkout. PUMA’s official page does not state the re-verification frequency or code expiration, so we don’t promise "verify once" permanence — ID.me-gated retail offers commonly require periodic re-verification.

Because PUMA groups all eligible shoppers under "military personnel" and defers the granular military categories to ID.me, the specific coverage for veterans, retirees, Reserve/Guard, spouses, and dependents is governed by ID.me’s military verification rather than stated on PUMA’s page. Confirm your status in the ID.me flow before assuming eligibility.

Students are not part of this Service Discount — PUMA runs a separate Student Discount (10% off via Student Beans). And note that PUMA’s own page states 20%, so ignore coupon-site claims of a different figure.
home-goods-military-discount: There is no military verification partner for HomeGoods — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute military offer. HomeGoods is absent from ID.me’s military partner list, and ID.me confirms it is not aware of a TJX-family military discount. Any site telling you to "verify your military status for a HomeGoods discount" is describing a program that does not exist.

Two false patterns circulate on coupon and Q&A sites. First, a "10% HomeGoods military discount — register on the site and verify as active-duty/veteran/family" claim: no such program or verification exists. Second, inflated "25%–50% off HomeGoods military" codes: fabricated; WorthEPenny confirms there is no official HomeGoods military program. Don’t present either as a military discount.

The real levers are the same for a service member as for anyone. The TJX Rewards Credit Card earns 5% back in Rewards (a $10 certificate per 1,000 points) across HomeGoods, T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, Homesense, and Sierra, with 10% off your first purchase and no annual fee; the open-loop TJX Rewards Platinum Mastercard adds 2% back on gas, grocery, and restaurants elsewhere. On a single cart, the one-time 10%-off welcome offer beats the ongoing 5%. Beyond the card, timing the yellow-sticker markdowns is the biggest lever — final clearance beats any 1.5%–5% — and SHIP119 gets free shipping on online orders of $119 or more.

If an actual military home discount matters to you, price-check retailers that verify one — Home Depot and Lowe’s run a 10% military discount via ID.me/SheerID (as of July 15, 2026) — against HomeGoods’ markdowns before you buy.
att-military-discount: AT&T verifies eligibility through its own military verification form at att.com/verification/military (or in store). You enter your service details and, if not auto-approved, upload a supporting document — a current pay stub (under 90 days), a DD214 or NGB 22/22A, or a veteran-designated driver’s license. AT&T’s pages do not name a third-party verification vendor for this program, so we don’t assert a provider. For help, AT&T lists 855-830-7190 to speak to an expert.

The discount only applies to AT&T’s newer 2.0 unlimited plans (Premium, Extra, or Value) or an older qualifying unlimited plan — not to every AT&T plan, and not to non-unlimited or prepaid plans. The percentage is tiered by plan: 20% on Premium 2.0, 15% on Extra 2.0, and 10% on Value 2.0, per line. The military discount stacks on top of AT&T’s standard AutoPay and paperless-billing discounts, which the plan estimator already reflects.

One thing to watch: many coupon and aggregator pages still advertise a 25% AT&T military discount. That figure is outdated — AT&T’s official military-discount page and support article state "up to 20%", with the per-plan 20% / 15% / 10% breakdown. Use 20% as the headline maximum, never 25%.

Military wireless customers can additionally get 20% off AT&T Fiber when bundling with an eligible unlimited wireless plan (applied within two bills; limited availability and areas). Active first responders and healthcare workers are served by AT&T’s separate FirstNet and Family program rather than this one.
bed-bath-and-beyond-military-discount: The evidence for "no discount" is the checkout verifier itself. ID.me is wired into bedbathandbeyond.com for community verification generally, but its Bed Bath & Beyond military page returns no offer — and its page for the sister brand Overstock says the same. A generic ID.me store banner advertising "up to 40% off for Military, Veterans, Nurses, Teachers, and more" is marketing over ordinary public sales, not a status-gated, verified military rate. Coupon boards still circulate a "Military ID = 25% off everything" claim, but that echoes the defunct chain’s old in-store deal and is not verifiable on the current site.

The brand transition explains the confusion. The original roughly 360-store chain filed Chapter 11 in April 2023 and closed all stores; Overstock.com’s parent bought the intellectual property for $21.5M in June 2023 and relaunched the site online that August; the company renamed itself Beyond, Inc., then reclaimed the Bed Bath & Beyond, Inc. name and the BBBY ticker in August 2025. In 2026 it is acquiring The Brand House Collective (formerly Kirkland’s) and converting Kirkland’s Home locations into Bed Bath & Beyond Home stores — a new physical footprint separate from the defunct chain, with no announced military discount.

For actual savings, the math favors loyalty over hunting a non-existent code. welcome rewards+ costs $24.95 a year and returns 5% in rewards plus free shipping with no minimum, so it pays back for anyone ordering more than roughly $500 a year; the Bed Bath & Beyond Credit Card includes that membership free plus 5% back, so holding the card and paying the fee would be redundant — use one path. One-off buyers should skip the membership and stack a new-customer sign-up offer on a live sitewide sale, then price-check the same item on Overstock.com.
atom-tickets-military-discount: Atom Tickets is an online ticketing marketplace (a Fandango competitor) that resells tickets set by individual theaters. Because Atom does not set ticket prices, it has no company-wide military discount to offer, and it runs no military verification on its checkout. When a "military" ticket type shows up on an Atom showtime, that price was set and is honored by the theater, and a valid military ID is typically checked at the theater — whether that ticket type appears at all depends entirely on the specific cinema.

The genuine military savings are off Atom. At the box office, AMC, Regal, and Cinemark all run everyday military pricing for anyone with a valid military ID; amounts and eligibility vary by location. For AMC specifically, you can verify on GOVX and buy discounted AMC military e-tickets, then redeem them at the theater — often the best real saving for a service member who sees AMC films regularly. Neither path stacks with Atom promos, because you are not transacting on Atom.

On Atom itself, the honest wins are open to everyone. Periodic new-user codes take $5–$7 off (or 50% off) a first ticket; Atom’s own rule caps any promo at $10 off and allows one code per transaction, one-time use per user, with fan events, double features, marathons, and Fathom special events excluded. Amazon Prime members get a free child’s ticket with an adult ticket when signed in with Amazon, and Atom Rewards gives a free standard-format ticket after four movies in a year. Linking AMC Stubs or Regal Crown Club (or using a fee-waiver promo like T-Mobile Tuesdays) removes Atom’s per-ticket convenience fee.

Be cautious of coupon sites listing "military" codes for Atom such as TUNERDOLBY, SPYDER5, or GIFTY50. These are generic or new-user codes, single-use, and consistent with Atom’s one-time-use rule they usually fail after a first purchase. No verified Atom code grants a standing military discount, and the "up to 25%" ID.me figure that circulates belongs to a generic ID.me Shop movie-tickets store, not to Atom Tickets.
rogue-fitness-military-discount: Per Rogue’s help center, you verify your military status in your account on roguefitness.com; once verified you "will be notified and eligible for any future sales of this nature." Rogue does not publicly name a third-party verification provider — GovX and ID.me aren’t referenced in its policy copy, and SheerID appears only as an internal account field, not stated as policy. Re-verification frequency, accepted documents, and the failure/support path are not stated; for help, use Rogue’s customer support.

Be skeptical of coupon-aggregator claims. Several sites assert a standing "10%–25% Rogue military discount via GovX/SheerID with a unique checkout code" — this is unverified and directly contradicted by Rogue’s own sources, which say there is no standing discount. So don’t expect a flat percentage; the real benefit is account-gated exclusive pricing during promo windows, and Rogue publishes no number for it.

The practical moves are Rogue’s own recommendations: verify your account now so you’re notified of future military/veteran-exclusive sales, and watch Veterans Day, Rogue’s historical window. For deployed service members, the APO store (rogueapo.com) makes it possible to ship equipment to APO/FPO/DPO addresses — a shipping capability, not a discount. Some fitness-equipment competitors do publish standing military discounts via GovX/ID.me/SheerID worth comparing; Rogue’s value proposition is everyday low pricing rather than an identity-gated percentage.
cava-military-discount: There’s no CAVA military verification to complete — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass — because there’s no brand-run military offer behind it. The only “account” involved is free CAVA Rewards, which requires no military status. CAVA is also absent from every major verified Veterans Day free-meal list for 2024 and 2025 (Military.com, Veteran.com, VA News, American Legion), so there’s no observed military-holiday promotion either.

The real, repeatable savings is CAVA Rewards. It’s a free points-based program: you earn on paid orders and redeem points as credit toward a bowl or pita, banking roughly $8 for about every $88 spent — effectively around 9% back over time, though CAVA sets the thresholds and can change them. Members also get a birthday reward: a free drink, pita chips, or dessert at the entry “SEA” tier, or a half-off bowl or pita at the top “Sun” tier, with the credit typically expiring about 30 days after it’s applied.

Be skeptical of coupon and affiliate pages advertising a fixed “10%” or “20% CAVA military discount.” Those numbers are fabricated and self-contradicting — the same pages often state elsewhere that CAVA has no specific military discount — and cite no CAVA source. What’s real: CAVA Rewards, the birthday reward, occasional public promo days (like National Pita Day giveaways, open to all), and whatever a local store manager chooses to honor at their discretion. If a guaranteed military discount matters to you, other fast-casual chains do run Veterans Day free-meal programs.
lyft-military-discount: There is nothing to verify — Lyft has no rider military program or verification partner. The coupon-aggregator “Lyft military discount code” is invented, and the “$5 off first ride” seen on discount portals is simply Lyft’s standard new-rider credit, which anyone can use. A WeSalute “Lyft” listing reflects that same first-ride credit rather than a military-specific benefit.

The real recurring saving is card-linked credits. USAA — the card most tied to the military community — along with American Express and Chase have at various points bundled a monthly Lyft credit that applies automatically to a fare. These rotate, so check your card’s current benefits. New riders should also apply a first-ride promo code, and everyone can use fare tools: Wait & Save trades a little wait time for a lower fare, Price Lock caps a routine commute fare against surge, and Lyft Pink adds perks for frequent riders.

Lyft’s veteran offerings are genuine but are programs, not fare discounts. The Jobs Access program (with Hire Heroes USA and the Call of Duty Endowment) provides rides to interviews and work for eligible job-seekers, and Lyft Healthcare partners with the VA on non-emergency medical transport for veterans. Both require eligibility and are arranged through partner organizations — a service member cannot simply apply them to a personal ride.
keen-military-discount: KEEN’s discount is powered by ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. You verify your military, first-responder, government, medical, teacher, or student status once, and eligible items are discounted at checkout while you’re logged into your ID.me Wallet. GovX and ExpertVoice each run their own separate membership/affiliation verification for their gated storefronts.

The key strategic point is that the 15% is one order-level discount that cannot be combined with any other promotion — KEEN’s Pro terms say Pro/ID.me orders are “not eligible for the promotions on the regular site.” Since KEEN is a chronic deep discounter running near-constant up-to-50% markdowns, on any style that’s already 30–50% off, the public sale price beats the 15% and the two don’t stack. Buy whichever is lower on the day.

Watch the debunk: military listicles headline a “KEEN 50% military discount.” That 50% is KEEN’s public sale/clearance depth, not the military discount — the verified military figure is 15% via ID.me. Aggregators also cite a stale “10%” and scatter promo codes; there is no separate hidden military code, and scraped “KEEN military codes” should be treated as unverified.

If you qualify as a verified outdoor or industry pro, ExpertVoice pricing often goes deeper than 15% (personal-use only), and there’s a GovX KEEN storefront for verified military and first responders — price-check both against the public sale before buying.
red-lobster-military-discount: The everyday 10% is verified in person, not online. There is no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX checkout code for it — you show a valid military ID or proof of service to restaurant staff, and acceptance and exactly which documents count are handled at the restaurant’s discretion, so it can vary by location. Aggregators frame the discount as "Military Mondays" (Monday-only), but the brand’s own current language says "everyday" — the brand statement governs. Ignore any "Red Lobster military promo code" for online ordering; the discount is applied at the table.

For many diners the bigger lever is My Red Lobster Rewards, a free loyalty program. New members get a 20% off reward on a $30+ dine-in or to-go order (plus 12 free Cheddar Bay Biscuits with the first app download on a $15+ to-go order), and everyone earns 1 point per $1 with a reward at every 125 points. Restaurants apply one promotional offer per check, so the new-member 20% generally won’t combine with the military 10% — use whichever is larger. On a first visit, the 20% usually wins.

Separately, Red Lobster runs an annual Veterans Day free meal. In 2024 and 2025 it was a free Veteran’s Shrimp & Chips on November 11, dine-in, one per customer, with proof of service (a free appetizer or dessert in 2018). It excludes beverage, tax, and gratuity, allows no substitutions, and is not guaranteed for a future year — confirm the exact offer each late October or early November.
vivobarefoot-military-discount: Vivobarefoot verifies eligibility through Gocertify, a UK-based verification service — you’ll see "This verification service is run by gocertify.me" on the offer page. It confirms your status via a payslip or work-ID upload, or by verifying a work email, and issues a discount code for vivobarefoot.com checkout. One quirk worth knowing: the offer’s FAQ lists UK-flavored eligible IDs ("R.A.F, Army, Navy or Armed Forces Dependents"), even on the US offer — that’s shared program copy, and the same document/email flow handles US service. Veterans without current "work" documents should use Gocertify’s support path.

The math on a $160 pair (a Primus Lite-class everyday shoe): the 15% military discount brings it to $136. But a typical seasonal sale of 20–30% plus ~4.8% portal cashback lands around $107–$122, and a ReVivo refurbished pair at up to ~40% off retail runs roughly $96–$112. Because the military discount doesn’t combine with anything, the honest play is to check the sale and ReVivo prices first — the 15% is the default for full-priced, current-line shoes.

Watch out for coupon pages advertising a "20% Vivobarefoot military discount" or generic "50% off Vivobarefoot codes." The verified military offer is 15% via Gocertify; the 50% figures are recycled from ReVivo refurb pricing or expired sale events, not live codes.

Vivobarefoot runs no dedicated Veterans Day or Memorial Day military promo that we could find — the 15% key-worker offer is evergreen, and public sales follow the normal retail calendar. ReVivo and "last chance" clearance markdowns run year-round.
bucked-up-military-discount: The make-or-break fact is Bucked Up’s own policy: only one discount code is allowed per order. That means a GovX code, a welcome code, and a public sale code are mutually exclusive — you cannot combine the military/GovX route with a public sale or welcome code. Ambassador codes require being logged into an account and still count as the one allowed code.

For the GovX route, verification is handled by GovX ID (free, one-time, reused across GovX partners). Bucked Up itself does not run an on-site ID.me or SheerID military flow, and Bucked Up was not surfaced in ID.me Shop’s supplements/military listing. GovX issues a single-use code after verification, and the offer and support are governed by GovX, not Bucked Up — its member price is not shown until you verify, so no public percentage can be honestly quoted.

Because Bucked Up’s deepest discounts are public sitewide sales (its "BF50" code has hit 50% off storewide, and warehouse/anniversary/summer sales recur), the honest verdict is to check for a live sale first: it’s typically the biggest markdown and needs no verification. If no sale is live and you qualify via GovX, verify and compare the member price to the current on-site price. For repeat orders of the same product, Subscribe & Save gives a standing discount — confirm the current rate. Coupon aggregators that headline a "50% off military" rate are really pointing at the public sale, not a military benefit.
dunkin-donuts-military-discount: The “Dunkin’ military discount” that content-farm pages present as a blanket 10%–15% everyday rate is not a Dunkin’ corporate discount. Any percentage is a per-franchise, unadvertised courtesy at participating locations only — never assume it and never quote a fixed rate. There’s also no Dunkin’ military promo code and no app military discount. The likeliest place to find an informal everyday courtesy is a store near a base, but treat it as YMMV, not policy.

The one dependable corporate offer is the Veterans Day free donut. Dunkin’ has run it consistently (2023, 2024, 2025) with identical language: a free donut (donut only — not coffee, a common misstatement) for all active and retired military, no ID required, in-store only, limit one per guest while supplies last, at participating locations nationwide. Expect a repeat on Nov 11, 2026, but confirm participation and exact terms in late October.

For everyday spend, Dunkin’ Rewards beats an informal 10% and it’s guaranteed nationwide: earn 10 points per $1, redeem from 150 points, reach Boosted Status (12 points per $1 for three months after 12 visits in a month), and get 3× points on your birthday. Clip the live app coupons before ordering — those frequent $1–$3-off and combo deals are usually the everyday winner. Note that a register-level courtesy generally does not stack with app/coupon pricing, and the free Veterans Day donut can’t be redeemed through the app at all.
taco-bell-military-discount: Because over 90% of Taco Bell restaurants are independently owned and operated, store-level promos — including any military discount — are not mandated by corporate. That’s why the company’s official language is that such discounts “vary,” which is another way of saying there is no program.

There is nothing to verify online: Taco Bell does not use ID.me, GovX, SheerID, WeSalute, or VerifyPass for a military offer. If an individual franchise chooses to give a discount, verification is simply a staff member checking your physical military ID at the register.

The real, repeatable savings live in the free app. Rewards points, the welcome reward, the Luxe Value Menu, and Tuesday Drops are open to everyone and beat a coin-flip register discount for almost every order.
urban-air-military-discount: Because Urban Air is franchised, each park sets its own prices, tickets, and whether it even honors a military rate. Multiple individual-park social accounts (e.g. Aurora, Appleton, St. Charles) state that "military receives a 10% discount every day" and instruct you to "bring your Military ID to purchase tickets," and a 2021 corporate tweet echoed a "10% military discount for veterans year-round." None of this appears on urbanair.com’s national offers page, which lists only promo, party, and membership deals and warns that "coupon codes may not be valid at all locations." Treat the ~10% as a common but location-specific courtesy, not a guaranteed chain-wide policy.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites. WorthEPenny claims you "prove your status through SheerID" and get "a unique discount code for 10% off at checkout on urbanair.com" — no such SheerID offer or online military code exists on Urban Air’s site; the real mechanism is showing a physical Military ID in the park. ValueCom’s "up to 85% off" and various "up to 25%" military headlines are fabricated or are generic public promo codes mislabeled as a military rate. Urban Air is also not on GovX and is not an ID.me merchant.

Individual parks occasionally run deeper, time-boxed military-appreciation events. St. Charles ran 50% off Platinum tickets from June 23–27, 2025 for military and first responders who showed ID in person. These are location-specific and vary year to year, so watch late May through June (Military Appreciation Month / Memorial Day) and Veterans Day — though on Veterans Day many parks simply restate the everyday 10% rather than add an extra percentage.

For repeat visitors, a membership beats every per-visit discount. Urban Air lists memberships from roughly $16.99/mo (Deluxe) to about $20.99–$24.99/mo (Platinum) per person, with higher tiers adding café/pizza perks; pricing varies by location. If you visit twice a month or more, the subscription math wins over paying per visit — but the military 10% does not apply to a membership, so it is an either/or choice.
espn-military-discount: ESPN launched its standalone direct-to-consumer app in August 2025, keeping the name "ESPN." The former ESPN+ content was folded into ESPN Select (roughly $11.99/mo or $119.99/yr), and a larger ESPN Unlimited tier ($29.99/mo or $299.99/yr) carries the full ESPN experience, including linear networks, and is available inside the Disney Bundle. Neither tier has a military discount — the app’s only savings levers are annual billing versus monthly and the Disney Bundle.

ESPN took over MLB.TV distribution in 2026 under a three-year deal, so new MLB.TV subscribers now register through the ESPN app (existing subscribers renew automatically). MLB.TV carries an official military discount of up to 35% off — about $49 off the all-teams annual package, whose regular 2026 price is $149.99. The discount is verified through GovX or SheerID against the regular price; the exact percent varies by package, so treat "up to 35%" as the ceiling and check the live price in the flow.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites advertising a "50% off ESPN+ military" code (ESPNHALF) or a "40% off military" line. There is no ESPN military discount — ID.me, ESPN’s listed verification provider, explicitly says so, and no GovX/SheerID/WeSalute ESPN offer exists. Where "ESPNHALF" works at all, it is a general (non-military) promo, not a service-member benefit.

One important nuance: MLB runs periodic public in-season price drops open to everyone (in 2026 the all-teams season pass dropped to $94.99), and those can undercut the verified military price. The military discount does not stack with a public promo — you simply take whichever is lower. If you already pay for ESPN Unlimited, its MLB.TV add-on ($134.99, about $15 less) may beat re-buying MLB.TV separately, but that is a subscriber perk, not a military discount.
directv-military-discount: There is no military verification for a DIRECTV discount because there is no discount to verify — DIRECTV uses no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID military program. The separate WeSalute new-customer offer verifies eligibility through a paid WeSalute+ membership, but since that offer matches or trails the free public promo, verification buys you little.

The math is the whole story. On the CHOICE package, DIRECTV’s public new-customer promo gives $10/mo off for free, while the WeSalute "military" offer gives only $5/mo — and charges ~$60/year for the WeSalute+ membership on top. On ULTIMATE and PREMIER the WeSalute amounts merely match the public promo. So paying to unlock the military offer can cost an eligible shopper money rather than save it. Verify at a live checkout whether it stacks on the public promo before relying on it.

For deployment, do not chase a discount — use your rights. You can suspend DIRECTV for 30 days to 9 months (call 800.531.5000 with your orders), or cancel penalty-free under the SCRA as amended by the Veterans Benefits and Transition Act of 2018, with deployment or relocation orders of 90+ days. Return your equipment and keep a paper trail of your orders and correspondence.
brooks-military-discount: Brooks verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. You sign in or create a free ID.me account and confirm your status in one of the eligible categories — Military, Nurse, or First responder. The Military community covers active duty, veterans, retirees, Guard, and Reserve.

After verification, ID.me issues a single-use promo code that you enter at checkout on brooksrunning.com. Members receive up to three of these codes per rolling 12-month period, starting from the issue date of the first code — not a calendar-year reset. For verification problems, Brooks directs shoppers to ID.me’s help center.

A few claims to ignore: some aggregators say military spouses and dependents qualify, that GovX is an official route, and that codes "reset January 1." Brooks’ official page states none of these — it lists only Military, Nurse, and First responder, verifies via ID.me, and uses a rolling 12-month window. Sports Medicine Professionals are listed separately for a 40% offer on Brooks’ ID.me store page.
koa-military-discount: The honest math matters here. On a representative two-night stay at a ~$50/night daily rate ($100), a participating campground’s 10% military discount lands you at about $90 — free to use and with no membership fee. A location that posts 20% gets you to about $80. But if your dates flex to Sunday through Thursday, KOA’s public Mid-Week Savings takes 20% off each night outright, and KOA Rewards members layer an additional 10% on top (roughly 28% off) — the one reliably combinable public path, and it beats the 10% military rate.

KOA uses no third-party verifier — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute — for the military discount. Verification is manual at the campground: you show a valid service ID at arrival (or, per KOA’s deals page, by text the day of arrival). Because each campground is independently operated, the exact ID accepted and the eligible groups are set locally, so call ahead if you’re unsure.

KOA Rewards is a separate decision, not a military benefit. It costs $39/yr, gives anyone 10% off daily registration rates at 500+ North America locations plus points toward free nights, and typically pays for itself after about four paid nights. It keeps saving you money on trips where no military rate is offered — but it excludes weekly, monthly, and seasonal rates and generally can’t be stacked with the military discount.

If you have base access, price the nearest on-base military Famcamp first. These on-base RV parks are separate from KOA, frequently run around $20–$35/night, and are tax-advantaged — often materially cheaper than any KOA path. Beware coupon aggregators advertising flat "20% / 30% / 50% off KOA military" codes: there is no national KOA military promo code, and those sites routinely conflate the paid KOA Rewards 10% (open to anyone) with a military benefit.
thule-military-discount: Thule uses SheerID on thule.com: choose Military, First Responder, or Student, submit basic info, and SheerID verifies your status online — usually instantly. You then get a one-time discount code for checkout. SheerID’s military category typically covers active-duty, veterans, reserve/retirees, and immediate family, though the exact sub-groups follow SheerID’s standard rules, so confirm your status at the form.

The 15% figure is current but has moved before: Thule and SheerID launched the program at 30% in April 2023 (covering carriers, kids’ gear, RV products, and packs/bags/luggage) and have since reduced it to 15%. Some listicles still cite the old 30% — that’s the launch promo, not the live rate. Coupon-blog claims of "Verify with ID.me" or a GovX Thule storefront appear to be copied templates: the verified on-site provider is SheerID, and no ID.me flow or GovX Thule storefront was confirmed this pass.

The most important nuance for a big-ticket buyer is the retailer substitute. Thule enforces minimum-advertised-price and rarely deep-discounts direct, so the deepest reseller codes are at REI and Backcountry, not thule.com. An REI Co-op member 20%-off-one-full-price-item coupon (when live) beats the 15%, and the $30 lifetime membership pays for itself on one big-ticket carrier. The two don’t combine, so use whichever is lower.

There’s also Thule Pro — a separate, application-reviewed membership for industry professionals, influencers, athletes, and VIPs (not general military). Approval takes 5–7 business days, accounts are valid for the calendar year and must be reactivated annually, and all Pro orders are final. It can run deeper than 15% for those who qualify, but it isn’t a military channel.
brilliant-earth-military-discount: Brilliant Earth verifies military, medical, first-responder, and teacher status through ID.me, and students through Student Beans. You verify once, receive a single-use promo code, and apply it at cart. There’s no GovX, WeSalute, or SheerID military checkout for the jewelry itself — ID.me and Student Beans are the two verification paths.

Because the perk is a fixed, low-dollar gift, it’s almost never the best way to save on a real Brilliant Earth purchase. On a $3,000 engagement ring, a free pair of silver studs is a rounding error. The genuine max-savings paths are the live public promo, a cashback portal, and — above all — choosing lab-grown over natural diamonds, which is often 30–50%+ lower on the stone for a similar look and is the single biggest cost lever at Brilliant Earth.

Mind the stacking landmine: the ID.me free-studs offer “cannot be applied or combined with other offers available on site,” and ID.me-gated codes typically break cashback tracking, so “ID.me studs + Rakuten” usually does not both pay. The lab-vs-natural choice is a product decision, not a code, so it layers for free with whichever single savings path you pick. Free shipping and free returns apply to everyone.
cheesecake-factory-military-discount: How verification works: it doesn’t — there is no military verification flow because there is no military discount. The Cheesecake Factory has no partnership with any verification platform, and the chain did not appear on the major verified Veterans Day 2025 free-meal lists either.

The one "stack" that always works: gift cards are a payment method, not a discount — so a discounted CardCash or Sam’s Club card legitimately layers under any member promo, including half-price Cheesecake Day slices and the free birthday slice. Paying for the gift cards with a dining- or warehouse-category credit card adds its normal earn on top.

The honest math on a $75 dine-in check for two: a 7.8%-off resale gift card brings it to about $69.15; the Sam’s Club multipack to $71.98; and during the historical bonus windows, $75 in gift cards effectively bought $90 of dining across two visits (about 17–30% back depending on increments). That’s more than most real military discounts at other chains.

Know the channel rules before you order: gift cards cannot pay on DoorDash or any third-party pickup/delivery, the seasonal Bonus Card doesn’t combine with other offers and expires, and there is no promo-code field on a restaurant check — which is why every coupon-site "code" for dine-in is noise by construction.
renewal-by-andersen-military-discount: Verification runs through SheerID’s Audience Network — an instant, secure check of military, first-responder, or educator status that doesn’t require a membership or subscription. Alternatively, you can show proof of service directly to your consultant during the in-home appointment. Either way it’s the same single offer: you can’t claim the $300 twice, and it’s one discount per job.

The stacking rule is what makes this offer unusual: most military discounts exclude sale prices, but Renewal by Andersen states the $300 applies after all other discounts. The rotating public seasonal promos (historically of the "% off windows and doors plus additional dollars off with a 4+ unit minimum" variety) move far more money on a five-figure project than the flat $300 — so the play is to book during a live promo window and add the $300 on top. Those promo figures and expirations rotate constantly and are not military-specific; verify the live offer before counting on it.

Two debunks worth knowing. First, coupon aggregators list "up to 25% off" codes for Renewal by Andersen — but the company doesn’t sell online and doesn’t use checkout promo codes, so any "code" is marketing, not a redeemable coupon; the only military-specific, primary-sourced figure is the flat $300. Second, GovX re-lists the same $300 military/first-responder offer as a lead form — it is not a separate or larger discount, so going through GovX adds no value over the brand’s own page.
wonderworks-military-discount: Verification is entirely in person: a WonderWorks staff member checks your military ID at the admissions counter. There is no third-party digital verification (no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass) and no online account. Because the discount is applied at the counter, buying online in advance won’t attach it — present ID at the door.

Stacking is limited: the CenterEdge web store states coupons/discounts are "not valid for any other discount or promotional ticket," so the $2 online code cannot be combined with the Armed Forces Week, resident, or any other promo. The Armed Forces Week free admission is standalone and redeemed at the door with ID; the Pigeon Forge in-store ID discount is standalone at the box office; and reseller tickets are pre-discounted and likewise can’t be combined with the $2 code.

On the baseline of one adult Orlando All Access ticket ($37.99 at the gate, ~$40.46 with ~6.5% FL tax): an eligible service member during Armed Forces Week pays $0; a guest that week pays $34.99; the Pigeon Forge in-store ID discount lands around $34.99 at that location; the universal $2 online code makes it $35.99; and a third-party reseller (Undercover Tourist, GoCity, Groupon, FunEx) often runs ~$24–$32 year-round, usually the cheapest path when there’s no military event.
meta-quest-military-discount: The confusion is understandable: aggregator and coupon pages titled "Meta Quest Government & Military Discounts" imply Meta grants a military discount. It does not. A GovX "Meta Quest" storefront exists, but GovX is an independent marketplace you buy from instead of Meta.com — it is not a Meta offer, and its current-generation prices often sit near retail, so compare its live net price before assuming it beats Meta’s own refurbished store or a public sale. There is also a well-known mix-up on ID.me: the store named "Quest" there is Quest Diagnostics health testing, not Meta Quest VR.

Meta’s only self-serve discount is the Education program: 10% off for currently enrolled students and employees of accredited US educational institutions, verified by a .edu email (Meta reserves the right to require proof of enrollment). It is strictly non-combinable, excludes tax and shipping, and is capped at one Quest device and one Ray-Ban Meta eyewear per year. Alumni are excluded. Because it cannot stack, it typically loses to a deep public sale and to Meta’s Certified Refurbished pricing.

For a service member buying new, the best military-specific path is the military Exchange: AAFES (shopmyexchange.com) and the Navy Exchange (mynavyexchange.com) both stock Quest 3 and 3S and sell them tax-free, and the Exchanges price-match. On a Quest 3 512GB the tax-free win is roughly $48 — real money, but smaller than what refurbished or a live sale usually saves. Exchange access follows the usual rules: active, retired, Guard, Reserve, and dependents in store; honorably discharged veterans online via the Veterans Online Shopping Benefit.

The dependable best value is Meta Certified Refurbished (meta.com/refurbished): Quest 3 and 3S units that are inspected, tested, and cleaned, carry the same one-year limited warranty as new, and are typically 20–30% under MSRP. They are already discounted, so they generally do not accept further codes. And around Black Friday/Cyber Monday and spring events, public retailer deals and gift-card bundles from Best Buy, Amazon, and Walmart are open to everyone and are frequently the deepest prices of all. Prices here reflect Meta’s April 19, 2026 MSRP increase (Quest 3 512GB at $599.99).
heatwave-military-discount: Heat Wave Visual uses VerifyPass to confirm eligibility. You verify your status — military/veteran, first responder, or government — and receive a single-use code to apply at checkout. Verification is per purchase: the code is one-time, and you re-verify on the brand’s page for each new order, so do not expect a standing account discount.

The 20% is a single flat tier across all covered groups — there is no separate percentage for active duty versus veterans, first responders, or government employees. Note there is no medical/nurse, teacher, or student tier; VerifyPass lists only the military/veteran and first-responder/government groups for this brand.

Heat Wave Visual also links a separate GovX ID route, and its products are additionally sold through the GovX marketplace. If you already use GovX, price-check the specific SKU there against the VerifyPass price — it is a substitute, not a stack, and the exact GovX percentage is not confirmed from primary sources.

Coupon aggregators advertise inflated Heat Wave Visual codes of 25%, 40%, 50%, even 75% off. None of these is verifiable on the brand’s own site; the only brand-confirmed discount is the 20% VerifyPass offer plus a newsletter-signup code (reported around 10%, unconfirmed). Free shipping applies to all U.S. orders with no minimum, regardless of which path you use.
ritfit-military-discount: RitFit uses VerifyPass, a third-party verification service — not ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute. You confirm your status once, and VerifyPass issues a unique code tied to your eligibility. RitFit’s own pages describe the process but do not state a percentage or a re-verification interval, so check VerifyPass for how long a code stays valid. If a code fails to apply, RitFit’s FAQ says to email support@ritfitsports.com with your order number and a screenshot of the code (2–3 business days to resolve); phone support is 888-818-9660, Mon–Fri.

Because RitFit runs frequent public sitewide sales, a standing clearance (“Big Sale”) collection, and a first-order newsletter code, the member discount is often not the cheapest path. A live sale price can beat, and cannot be stacked on top of, the VerifyPass code — Shopify checkout takes one code per order. The deepest cuts on big-ticket racks and home-gym packages typically land during the Black Friday collection and seasonal sitewide events, which are open to everyone.

Two RitFit-specific extras are worth knowing. First, RitFit sells heavily on Amazon (the RITFIT LLC storefront), where the VerifyPass code does not apply — there you rely on Amazon’s own clip coupons and sale events, so compare the Amazon total against RitFit’s live site price. Second, RitFit runs a separate program that provides free fitness products to individuals with disabilities; it’s application-based (contact 888-818-9660 or support@ritfitsports.com) and is not a discount you combine with a cart.
lululemon-military-discount: lululemon uses SheerID to confirm eligibility. You click "Get Verified," sign in to — or create — a lululemon account, and submit your information and military or first-responder status. Verification may be instantaneous (up to about 20 minutes); if it can’t be confirmed automatically, SheerID compares your uploaded documents against your form entries, so enter your name exactly as it appears on your documents.

You’ll get a confirmation email from SheerID, after which the discount is active on your account. Your verified status is good for four years — after that, lululemon asks you to verify again — and there’s no limit on how many times you use it in between. Spouses and dependents of active personnel must each complete their own verification.

One detail worth noting: lululemon names "reservist" among eligible groups but does not separately list National Guard. Guard members are most likely covered, but because the official page doesn’t enumerate them, confirm through the SheerID form rather than assuming. For verification problems — including denials and renewals — lululemon directs members to SheerID support; for other questions, to lululemon’s contact page.
world-market-military-discount: The confusion comes from coupon sites that advertise a standing “World Market military discount 25%” as if it’s always available. It isn’t: the 25% is a seasonal, in-store Veterans Day promotion (alcohol excluded), and the 20% is a separate historical veteran offer. There is no online military verification at World Market, so the Veterans Day event is verified the old-fashioned way — a physical military ID at the register.

Because the percentages, dates, and any online component shift year to year, the honest move is to verify the current-year Veterans Day terms about two weeks before Nov 11 rather than assume last year’s deal. The military promo is generally one coupon per transaction and not combinable with other codes.

For everyday value, lean on the free Rewards program. The welcome offer, member coupons, and 10% off store pickup work online and in store without any military status, and they stack on sale prices per program terms. Time bigger buys to the Veterans Day event or public sale windows like Memorial Day and Black Friday, which are often the best public pricing of the year.
papa-johns-military-discount: All the math below uses one baseline: a realistic $25 online order (a large specialty pizza plus a side), with delivery fees and taxes excluded since they apply to every path similarly.

The debunk matters because the fake codes are specific. Coupon and military sites headline a Papa John’s "military discount" with codes like VETS50, MAHALO50, or MILITARY30, or a flat "25–50% off for military." Corporate Papa John’s has no national military program. MAHALO50 is a general 50%-off code, not a military benefit; VETS50 is expired/invalid; and military30 is a local Navy MWR partnership code tied to specific bases, not a sitewide offer. Any page telling you to "use the Papa John’s military code at checkout" is asserting something Papa John’s doesn’t publish.

The truthful maximum-savings play: for almost anyone, stacking a current public promo code or app deal (40–50% off) with Papa Rewards beats a discretionary military discount. On the $25 baseline, a 40–50% public deal lands you around $12.50–$15.00 and still earns Papa Rewards points, versus roughly $17.50 for a 30% MWR code if one is even live for your store. If you order regularly, enroll in Papa Rewards and let 75-point $10 rewards compound.

Where a local store does honor a military discount, verification is simply showing a military ID in person — there is no confirmed national SheerID or ID.me military checkout. If you’re uncertain whether your store honors one, call the franchise rather than relying on a scraped code.
rooms-to-go-military-discount: All the math below uses one baseline: a $1,499 living-room set (a sofa + loveseat or a sectional), a realistic big-ticket order where financing and tax actually move the decision. Sales tax on this cart is material (roughly $90–$150 at 6–10%) and applies to every Rooms To Go path equally; there is no tax-free channel.

The nuance that trips people up. Rooms To Go markets sales named for military holidays — most notably the "Veterans Day Furniture Sale." That naming is exactly what makes shoppers assume there’s a military discount. There isn’t: the sale is public, open to everyone, with no military ID and no service-member rate. ID.me confirms Rooms To Go offers no military discount, so the honest read is "great public sale, not a military benefit."

The codes are fabricated. Coupon sites push "military unlock" codes — e.g. a 30%-off or 35%-off code framed as a way for service members to save. Rooms To Go publishes no standing sitewide code; its deals are event-based, and these codes are unverified and are not military offers. Rakuten also pays No Cash Back on roomstogo.com, so there is no portal layer to add.

What actually saves you money. Financing (the RTG card’s 50 months at $875+) is a cash-flow tool — it avoids interest, but it doesn’t cut the sticker, and it generally won’t combine with coupon savings. The real price mover is timing a seasonal sale. And if a genuine verified military percentage matters to you, cross-shop Ashley Furniture (5% via SheerID, as of July 8, 2026) — about $75 on a $1,499-equivalent set — before you commit to Rooms To Go.
igloo-military-discount: Igloo runs no ID-verified military discount, so there is nothing to verify on its site. ID.me’s own store page states plainly that it is "not aware that Igloo Coolers offers Military discounts," which is why the scraped ID.me and "COMEBACK15" codes floating around coupon sites fail at checkout. We deliberately omit those percentages here because repeating them would imply an offer Igloo does not actually run.

First Responder Friday is Igloo’s only first-responder recognition on its own site, and it is a monthly sweepstakes — you nominate a first responder (or are nominated) and one winner per month receives up to $500 to spend at Igloocoolers.com. It is a genuine program, but it is a lottery-style giveaway, not a percentage anyone can redeem.

GovX is the one verified member channel. It is a third-party identity-verification marketplace that gives the military and first-responder communities access to member pricing from many brands. You create a free account, verify once with GovX ID, and shop participating storefronts — Igloo among them. Because that pricing is login-gated and sits on a separate storefront, treat GovX as a route to check and compare against the live Igloo sale rather than an always-on discount.

For most shoppers the public levers win: Igloo runs frequent sitewide and clearance sales (routinely 30–50% off) that are usually deeper than any claimed "military %," a newsletter welcome offer (10% off a first order), and an outlet with prior-season and blemished models well below retail. If you have exchange privileges, Igloo is commonly stocked at AAFES/NEX, where purchases are tax-free and price-matching is often possible — frequently the best total-savings path on a larger cooler.
hydro-flask-military-discount: The mechanics matter here, because this is not a checkout-code discount. Hydro Flask runs its military offer inside its Pro program: you create a free hydroflask.com account, apply at the Pro Deal application under the Military category, and SheerID verifies your status once. From then on the 20% rides on your logged-in account. That gated, account-based checkout is also why portal cashback likely won’t track on pro-discounted orders — standard portal behavior — so treat "20% + Rakuten" as non-stacking.

A number worth correcting: Military Markdown advertises "Save 25%" on Hydro Flask for service members. The figure published by SheerID — the actual verification provider — is 20%. Coupon sites also imply the discount stacks with sale prices and codes; Hydro Flask publishes no such promise, and pro-style programs typically apply off MSRP. Don’t bank on a number or a stack the brand hasn’t stated.

The real decision is 20% vs. the public sale. On a $100 drinkware order, the military discount lands you at $80. But when a bottle sits in a 30%-off event, the public price plus Rakuten’s 3% cashback (as of July 14, 2026) lands around $67.90 — and that path stacks cleanly because automatic sale pricing with no code entered is the portal-safe pattern. Full price: take the 20%. Deeper-than-20% sale: take the sale.

Two more layers: GovX hosts a Hydro Flask Pro Deal brand page that routes verified GovX members to the same offer — same economics, handy if you’re already GovX-verified. And House of Hydro Rewards, Hydro Flask’s free points program, earns points on hydroflask.com purchases — join before buying either way, though whether points accrue on pro-discounted orders isn’t confirmed in its terms.
monster-jam-military-discount: Aggregators claim a flat "Monster Jam military discount" — some say "up to 40%" via ID.me, "up to 50%" via GovX. Those percentages are the marketplaces’ site-wide maximums across all brands, not a confirmed Monster Jam rate, so don’t treat them as Monster Jam’s number. What is actually verified: a venue box-office rate (up to ~$10/ticket at the Broadmoor World Arena example), a GovX listing whose amount is only shown after verified login, and an ID.me "discount and/or cash back" listing with no published figure. The public "VAAXMJ – save up to 25%" code seen on Monster Jam social posts is a limited-time public promo open to anyone, not a military offer.

The four channels verify separately. ITT/MWR checks your military ID in person; GovX verifies through its own account system (military, veteran, first responder, law enforcement); ID.me verifies your status once and reuses it across partner offers; VetTix verifies service/veteran status at signup. None of these is a permanent Monster Jam entitlement — offers appear per event and can lapse. Ticketmaster, when it hosts a Monster Jam date, does not run its own military percentage; any military ticket type comes from the venue box office.

Two practical cautions apply across every paid path: discounted inventory is not sold the day of the event, and venue/AXS ticketing links frequently won’t load on government or military networks — so buy ahead on personal wi-fi or cellular data. The discounts also don’t stack: you pick one discounted price type, and the military/box-office rate and public codes don’t combine.

The smartest sequence: check your base ITT/MWR office first (often the deepest cut plus fee savings), compare GovX or ID.me against any live public code, and watch VetTix for free seats in your city. If you’re bringing kids, Monster Jam frequently runs public kids-ticket and free-pit-party deals worth stacking into the family math.
michaels-military-discount: The discount is delivered through Michaels Rewards, so the practical first step is creating that free account and verifying once. Verification is handled by SheerID — most checks are instant, though SheerID may occasionally request additional documentation. After verification, the 15% is attached to your Rewards account and applies automatically online and in store; Michaels does not publish a re-verification cadence, so don’t assume it’s permanent.

Michaels frames eligibility broadly as "military members and their immediate family" and does not break it into active duty, veteran, retiree, Guard/Reserve, spouse, or dependent. In practice, whether your specific status qualifies is decided by SheerID’s military verification, not spelled out on Michaels’ page — so the honest answer for any subgroup is "confirm it during verification."

Watch the exclusions: the 15% covers sale items but not clearance, custom framing, gift cards, classes and events, cut-to-order fabric, balloons, third-party-seller items, or most craft-technology machines (Cricut, Silhouette, Glowforge, Brother, Creality, 3Doodler) and several branded goods (Lego, Pokémon cards, and more). It’s also limited to one military discount per product and one per day. Because Michaels’ page geo-serves content and renders parts via JavaScript, re-check the current U.S. exclusion list at checkout.
insta360-military-discount: All the math below uses one baseline: the Insta360 X5 360° action camera at its $549.99 list price on store.insta360.com. Insta360 is a sale-timing brand — flagships typically hold price even during campaigns and get their value as free accessory bundles (roughly $50–$150 of bundle value), while last-generation models like the X4 and ONE X2 take the real cuts: observed campaign discounts put X4-class cameras around $349–$429, and the 2026 Memorial Day campaign listed savings up to $200 on select models.

Rule 1 — there is no identity discount to stack. Any "military code + sale" advice for Insta360 is fiction. Rule 2 — campaign prices are the floor: Insta360’s campaign terms treat promo codes as non-combinable with campaign and bundle pricing in general, and the $10 sign-up code applies to regular-price orders (verify the code’s own terms at receipt). Rule 3 — the one true stack is Trade-Up: trade-in value for an older camera applies before payment, effectively combining with whatever price is live.

Be cautious of coupon aggregators. WorthEPenny publishes an "Insta360 Military & Veteran Discounts" page, hotdeals claims a "20% student discount," and other sites list 25–55%-off codes — none of which Insta360, ID.me, SheerID, or Student Beans confirms. On July 14, 2026 the official Student Beans US listing carried no percentage offer at all — just free shipping over $129 and the $10 sign-up code. Treat any "Insta360 military code" as fabricated.

Two more honest notes for military shoppers. Cashback portals are a non-factor here: US portals show no meaningful rate for insta360.com (a UK portal listed about 1%), so there’s no cashback to protect — buy wherever the sticker price is lowest, including Amazon, B&H, or a Best Buy open-box unit. And the Exchange isn’t a workaround: no Insta360 listings surfaced at shopmyexchange.com or mynavyexchange.com as of July 14, 2026, so don’t count on the tax-free route for this brand.
west-marine-military-discount: The “West Marine military discount” you’ll see quoted around the web — usually “10% off, year-round, verified by ID.me,” sometimes paired with a code like “BOATUS15” — isn’t confirmed by a single West Marine source. No official page states a military discount, a percentage, or an ID.me military-verification flow. West Marine does appear on ID.me Shop, but only as an open, everyone-eligible cash-back store titled “Discounts and Cash Back for Everyone.” That’s a cash-back marketplace listing, not a military-gated discount, and it verifies nothing about military status.

The real West Marine savings rhythm is public sales plus loyalty. West Advantage Rewards has a free Silver tier (1 point per $1; $5 certificates at 500 points) and a $25/yr Gold tier that earns points 4× faster and bundles a full-year BoatUS membership with towing benefits — worth it for boaters who’d buy BoatUS anyway. Layer a cash-back portal on top (roughly 2%–8% depending on portal as of July 15, 2026), but choose either the portal cash back or an off-portal promo code, since combining them commonly voids the cash back.

The one genuine military lever in this ecosystem sits with West Marine’s partner, BoatUS: active-duty service members can claim a free 1-year BoatUS membership (via GEICO Military) at BoatUS.com/Military, plus half-price dues and 10% off water towing for active/Reserve/Guard. That’s a BoatUS benefit, not a West Marine discount — but for a service member who boats, it’s the highest-value move, and it stacks nicely with a West Marine sitewide sale and free West Advantage Rewards on the actual purchase.
wyndham-military-discount: The two paths use different baselines, which is why directories that flatten this to a single “20% military discount” are misleading. The guaranteed number is at least 15% off the Standard Rate via code SML; the up to 20% figure is the ID.me Best Available Rate offer, and Wyndham states it may be less than 20% off at some properties. So the smart move is to price both for your exact dates and take the lower final number.

Verification differs by path. The SML rate needs only a military ID at check-in. The Rewards perks and the ID.me rate require completing Wyndham’s “Confirm Military Status” step, which is powered by ID.me; a dedicated military member-services line (855-464-5739) supports the process, and WeSalute also lists a Wyndham offer.

Both military rates must be booked on direct channels (Wyndham sites and app, brand sites, the toll-free line, on-site, or traditional travel agents) — not third-party OTAs — and neither combines with other discounts. You can still earn Wyndham Rewards points on a qualifying military-rate stay, which layers loyalty value on top of the discounted rate. Verifying once banks auto-GOLD and the 3,000-point bonus, which offset future stays.
great-wolf-lodge-military-discount: Great Wolf Lodge verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. You verify on your chosen lodge’s Howling Heroes page by clicking the ID.me button, then sign in to or create a free ID.me account and confirm your eligible group. The brand’s page does not state how often ID.me re-verification is required — that cadence is governed by ID.me, not Great Wolf Lodge.

Because the percentage off varies by date and the offer can’t be stacked with other deals, it’s worth comparing the Howlin’ Heroes rate against Great Wolf Lodge’s public sales for your dates — such as the Early Saver Deal (book 60+ days ahead) or multi-night offers — and booking whichever is lower.

Booking is online only. Great Wolf Lodge’s official offer page describes booking through the lodge page plus ID.me; it does not state an in-person or front-desk redemption path, though you may be asked to show proof of eligibility at check-in.
floor-and-decor-military-discount: The policy, from the brand’s own Help Center: Floor & Decor honors military members "through occasional in-store military discount events" and points readers to its email list — the same page gives the everyday answer as a Low Price Promise (a verified lower price on the same product will be honored). Its coupons FAQ is equally plain: everyday low prices, no coupon program. That makes the aggregator claims — a "50% Floor & Decor military discount," codes like SAVE30 and URAF30, "30–60% off" — fabricated by definition. Store staff answering shopper questions have said the same: no military discount, a low-price promise for everyone.

The event history is real but modest: the brand’s own email campaigns (archived by Milled) document a limited-time 10% military discount in the November 2025 Veterans Day window, at least once capped at $200 off, with a "last chance" reminder closing the window; the emails thanked "active duty, retired military, and veterans." Military-appreciation sends have also appeared around May. Per-event terms are never published outside the email, so subscribe if your project can wait for a window.

The cap math is what matters on big tickets. On a 500 sq ft LVP job ($1,495 at $2.99/sq ft), a 10% event saves $149.50 — but on a whole-house 2,000 sq ft job (~$5,980), Lowe’s uncapped 10% is worth $598, Home Depot caps at $400/yr, and F&D’s event-style cap was $200. The bigger the job, the more Lowe’s wins — unless Floor & Decor’s sticker price on the comparable SKU is already 10%+ lower, which its everyday-low-price model sometimes delivers. Price the actual SKUs both ways, and mind the substitutes’ exclusions (sale/clearance items and certain commodities don’t take the 10%).

At Floor & Decor itself, the biggest lever isn’t a discount at all: shopping the tier below. The brand’s own How to Save page shows 20+ mil rigid-core vinyl from $1.99/sq ft — choosing $1.99 over $2.99 on 500 sq ft saves $500, more than any military offer discussed here — and every category has a clearance section. Layer a targeted card-linked offer if your Bank of America or Chase offer wallet happens to carry the recurring 5–10%-back F&D offer (caps ~$79–$100, community-tracked, YMMV), and trade pros can add PRO Premier Rewards points (~1% back). One caution: the store card’s deferred-interest financing charges interest retroactively from the purchase date if you don’t pay in full — treat it as a payment tool, never a savings path.
quad-lock-military-discount: Verification is manual and human, not an instant identity service. You send documentation to Support, they review it, and they issue a one-off code. There is no ID.me/GovX/SheerID account and no stated re-verification cadence — you simply request a code when you are ready to buy. Because it is discretionary, the value of the code is whatever Support quotes you, which is why we do not print a percentage here.

Watch out for the "10%–25% military discount" circulating on aggregator sites. Quad Lock’s official article states no percentage and only says "Military personnel"; it does not enumerate veterans, retirees, spouses, or dependents. That "10–25%" figure appears conflated with Quad Lock’s public 10% newsletter code — anyone can get that code by signing up with their email, and it is not a military benefit.

Quad Lock almost never discounts sitewide, so timing usually beats verification. Its signature event is Black Friday: in 2025 it ran 30% off sitewide (roughly Nov 13–Dec 2), the deepest and most reliable cut of the year, and it needs no ID. If Black Friday is live, that sale beats any code; if not, the free 10% newsletter code is the fastest guaranteed markdown, and it is worth emailing Support for a military code to compare. Because checkout takes one code per order, these paths are mutually exclusive — pick the single best price.
prana-military-discount: Verification is handled by ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA and the IRS. You create a free ID.me account once, verify your community, and the 20% applies to eligible full-price items at prana.com checkout; ID.me may periodically ask you to re-verify under its own policies. If auto-verification fails, ID.me offers a document-upload fallback.

One thing to watch: some coupon aggregators and AI summaries claim a "30% military discount" at prAna. That figure is unverified and incorrect — the ID.me store page and prAna’s own affiliate feed both state 20%. The "40% off" numbers you may see are either prAna’s public sales (select styles, open to everyone) or the profession-gated prAna Pro program — neither is a blanket military rate. The legitimate path is ID.me verification at checkout, not a scraped "military code."

Two more paths worth knowing: prAna runs a separate closed storefront on the GovX marketplace, worth a price-check for discounted past-season inventory, and a prAna Pro program with deeper (unpublished) pricing — but Pro is application-only for industry professionals such as yoga and climbing instructors and guides, not a military route. Neither stacks with the ID.me 20%, sales, or cashback.
burlington-military-discount: Burlington is a classic off-price retailer. Its buyers estimate a full-price "comparable value" and sell below it, and the deepest value sits in clearance and markdowns (items from ~$3.49). There is no published coupon mechanism and no ID-gated program, so there is simply no place to apply a military discount — the savings are structural to the pricing, not unlocked by status.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites that advertise a Burlington "military promo code" or a "30% off" code, or that tell you to "show a valid military ID at checkout for a discount." No official Burlington channel publishes a promo-code system or an in-store military discount, and some of the same aggregator pages simultaneously admit there is no official military program. We treat those savings claims as coupon-farm content, not fact.

The free Burlington Loyalty program is a perks program, not a percentage off: it adds extended receipt-free returns, early access to deals, and a $5 bonus on completed layaways. It is open to all shoppers and carries no price cut, but no cost or downside either.

For frequent shoppers who pay their cards in full, the Burlington Credit Card is the only structural price lever. It earns 5% back as Rewards points (100 points = $5) on card purchases and periodically opens with a time-boxed percent-off-first-purchase offer — a 20% opener with a stated 7/6/26–7/19/26 window was live at research time, but the percentage and window change, so confirm the current offer before counting on it.
disney-cruise-military-discount: Disney does not use a third-party verification service for the military rate. There is no online status check and no account requirement beyond a normal Disney booking — eligibility is confirmed in person at pier check-in. The eligible service member (or a spouse with a valid, active military ID) must be sailing in the stateroom. Verification is per booking, not a persistent "verify once" status.

Because Disney publishes no percentage, the dollar savings vary by ship, date, and stateroom category. Aggregator claims of "20%–35% off" are not stated by Disney and are not represented here. The select-sailing list changes over time, so check the live page for current eligible dates before booking.

The 2026 $250 onboard credit is a flat, separate benefit honoring America’s 250th anniversary. It auto-appears on the stateroom account for shipboard services, merchandise, food and beverage, or Port Adventures, and is the one offer Disney explicitly allows to be combined with the Special US Military Rate.
alo-military-discount: ID.me confirms the absence directly: its Alo military page reads, "We are not aware of Alo Yoga offering Military community discounts." The Alo store page on ID.me lists no military, nurse, responder, teacher, government, medical, student, or alumni deal — every "Does Alo Yoga offer a ___ discount?" link resolves to the same "we are not aware" answer.

The "up to 40% off" you may see is not Alo’s. "Special savings of up to 40% off for Military, Veterans, Nurses, Teachers, and more" is boilerplate ID.me promotes its browser-extension network with on every store page. It is not an Alo offer, and it should never be cited as Alo’s military discount.

What Alo actually runs is unrelated to military service. The Pro Program gives certified yoga, fitness, and Pilates instructors 25% off full-price items, verified through SheerID with applications reviewed by Alo, usable at aloyoga.com and US store locations only. Students can verify through Student Beans for a separate discount whose rate varies (and rises during back-to-school promos). Neither is tied to military status.

If you’re a service member, your real ways to save at Alo are the everyday Sale section, the free ALO Access rewards program, and — only if you also independently qualify — the Pro Program (as a certified instructor) or Student Beans (as an enrolled student). Several other activewear brands do run verified military discounts via ID.me or GovX, which are better destinations if a military rate is what you need.
eotech-military-discount: EOTECH uses GovX and ExpertVoice to verify eligibility — there is no self-serve code on eotechinc.com. GovX confirms military, first-responder, or law-enforcement status via a free account and sells through a separate GovX storefront. ExpertVoice verifies military membership (including veterans and spouses) for its deeper, personal-use pricing. A separate Industry Discount Program is an application-gated route for qualified FFL/LE/industry professionals with quantity limits, not a general veteran benefit.

On a baseline EXPS3 (MSRP around $729), the routes diverge sharply: ExpertVoice can land it as low as roughly $290–$450 for eligible personal-use buyers who accept the caps and no-resale terms, while GovX lands nearer $583–$656 at ~10–20% but with no caps. Both replace public codes — there is no stacking and no cashback on top of either.

Two things to ignore and one substitute to watch: coupon-site "military codes" are not real, and "GovX up to 50% off" is a platform-wide maximum, not EOTECH’s specific rate. Because EOTECH enforces MAP, the public substitute is a retailer sale — dealers like OpticsPlanet have run "up to 30% off" on select optics — worth comparing when you are not using ExpertVoice. If the exchange stocks your model, the tax-free path is a bonus, but verify stock first.
jcpenney-military-discount: How verification works: there’s nothing to verify for retail purchases — no provider, no register process. For Portraits, verification is simply showing a physical Military ID in studio; no account, code lookup, or online verification exists, and the studio associate applies the package pricing.

The honest math on a $200 apparel/home cart: the current extra-25% coupon plus TopCashback’s 2% lands around $147 net — roughly $53 saved, or 2.5× what a typical 10% military discount would give — with no verification at all. JCPenney’s own stacking rule: one % or $ off coupon first, then rewards, then free shipping; two percent-off codes never combine.

The Portraits package is genuinely generous for a military family session: free session fees (regularly $14.99 a person), a free 8x10 (regularly $19.99), the digital album at $129.99 instead of $179.99, 50% off wall art, and $6.99 standard prints — easily $65+ of value on a typical session. It doesn’t combine with other Portraits offers, and it runs through December 31, 2026.

The military-holiday record, labeled as history: a Veterans Day "Extra 30% Off" email on November 11, 2025; stale Military.com listings of older extra-5% military windows around Veterans Day and Memorial Day; and a one-week 10% first-responder in-store discount in October 2023. Expect something each November — promise nothing.
bandh-military-discount: B&H sells most gear at manufacturer-set (MAP) prices and does not issue blanket percentage-off coupons, which is why a "military %" was never the play here. Aggregator pages advertising "B&H military discount 25% with code" or "23% off military" are fabricated — there is no such code or program.

The Payboo card is the real "discount." It reimburses the sales tax B&H collects, applied instantly at checkout, so you effectively pay no tax in a sales-tax state — on big-ticket gear that easily beats any hypothetical military percentage. It stacks on top of a sale or price-matched price, but gives no benefit in the no-sales-tax states (DE, MT, NH, OR) or on tax-exempt items and gift cards. It is a standard credit product, so pay it in full to keep the tax saving real.

Beyond Payboo, use B&H price match (match a lower competitor price, then reimburse its tax), the B&H Used department for the same gear below new, free expedited shipping over $49, and B&H Rewards points. B&H’s military-facing activity is the charitable Veterans Portrait Project — free portraits for veterans and active duty — which is a goodwill event, not a purchase discount.
hellofresh-military-discount: The Hero Discount is verified through ID.me or GovX. You confirm your eligibility once; the provider validates your status and the discount auto-applies at checkout. The current official page shows only ID.me and GovX — despite some listings claiming SheerID, that path is not confirmed this pass, so don’t rely on it.

The offer is structured as a time-limited subscription discount: 55% off box 1 plus 15% off for the next 51 weeks, expiring 380 days after purchase, after which boxes revert to full price. It is not combinable with other promotions, codes, or gift cards, and it excludes premiums, upgrades, taxes, and shipping.

Because HelloFresh controls the program and can change it at any time, treat the numbers here as a starting point and confirm the current terms on HelloFresh’s official Hero Discounts page before you subscribe.
nordstrom-rack-military-discount: All the math below uses one baseline: a $150 Rack cart (a pair of shoes plus two clothing items at Rack markdown prices), pre-tax. There is no tax-free or military channel to price in — every real saving here is a layer open to all shoppers.

The debunk. "Nordstrom Rack military discount" pages invent a flat percentage — WorthEPenny, Living Tricky, and Military Markdown variously cite "20%," "15%," or "50% off" for service members. Those figures conflict with each other and appear on no Nordstrom or Nordstrom Rack property. ID.me Shop’s own Nordstrom Rack page states it is "not aware that Nordstrom Rack offers Military discounts," and there is no military verification flow at Rack. Treat every "Nordstrom Rack military code" as fabricated.

The 2026 loyalty change that actually matters. As of June 3, 2026, Nordy Club members no longer earn points on Nordstrom Rack or NordstromRack.com purchases; points are earned at full-line Nordstrom only. In its place, the Nordstrom credit card now gives an instant 5% off every Rack purchase (except gift cards), and Nordstrom Notes remain redeemable at Rack. That card 5% is the durable everyday lever at Rack now.

So what wins? If you hold a Nordstrom card, the instant 5% is the reliable win on the $150 cart (about $142.50). Buying online without the card, Rakuten’s 2% (as of July 8, 2026) is the simplest layer — check whether the card and portal both track before counting on the stack. And for maximum depth, a Clear the Rack event’s extra markdown on clearance beats any flat 2–5% every time.
spectrum-military-discount: Spectrum does not use ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or any third-party military-status verifier for a consumer discount on its own service — because there is no such discount to gate. For SCRA benefits, "verification" means submitting your military orders or deployment letter directly to Spectrum via the SCRA Disconnection Request Form or to customer service. "Spectrum Authorized Retailer" listings on ID.me Shop are operated by third-party resellers, not Charter Spectrum; any "verified" discount there is the retailer’s offer, not an official Spectrum military discount.

The mobile suspension benefit lets a deployed service member (proof of 90+ days, or a PCS to a no-coverage area) pause Spectrum Mobile with no service fees and keep the same number on reinstatement. The home-service benefit lets you cancel and reserve your phone number for up to three years, with reconnection/activation fees waived when you return (install/equipment charges still apply).

For a low-cost internet option, Spectrum Internet Assist runs about $25/mo (up to 30/4 Mbps), or $15/mo with an added qualifier, for households on NSLP, CEP of NSLP, or SSI (including seniors 65+ on SSI) — income-based, not military. If a status-based military discount matters, some Spectrum Mobile competitors like T-Mobile and Verizon advertise military plan discounts via SheerID/ID.me; verify each on its own site.
busch-gardens-military-discount: The program is verified entirely through ID.me.
