You create or sign in to a free ID.me account and confirm your military or veteran status once; veterans upload an accepted document (DD214, NGB 22, VA Eligibility letter, VHIC/VIC, or a Veteran-endorsed driver’s license, among others). There is no coupon code. Because document review can take a few days, register ahead of your visit rather than at the gate.

The distinction between active duty and veterans is where aggregators get it wrong. Active-duty members (plus drilling reservists and National Guard) get the year-round free ticket; veterans get 50% off year-round and free admission only during seasonal windows. Military retirees, inactive/standby reserve members, Merchant Marine, and DoD civilians are explicitly excluded from the active-duty free ticket — a widely copied error to avoid.

For extra guests, always price the 50% military ticket against Busch Gardens’ public online advance ticket and Fun Card deals — the public sale frequently undercuts the military rate. The same Waves of Honor structure applies at Busch Gardens Williamsburg; confirm the current veteran offer on the Williamsburg page.
salomon-military-discount: Verification is handled by Salomon/Amer Sports through the Amer Sports Pro Club, not by a third-party instant-verification service like ID.me or GovX. You register either with an invitation code or by applying with a supporting document that proves your eligibility. Approval is a manual review and is not instant. Membership privileges are valid for one year; you must re-confirm eligibility to renew, and renewal instructions are sent about one month before expiration.

One important trade-off: signing up for the Pro Club cancels your access to Salomon’s S/PLUS loyalty program unless you register the Pro Club with a different email address. Pro Club pricing is described as "preferred pricing" with a yearly spending allowance rather than a guaranteed flat 20% on every item, so confirm the actual applied rate after approval.

The military discount works online only — it does not apply at the Salomon outlet or retail stores. For excluded or in-a-hurry purchases, the Salomon outlet ("up to 40% off" last season’s styles) is open to everyone with no verification. Students have a separate 15% SheerID discount; law enforcement and firefighters use the same Pro Club path as military.
hard-rock-military-discount: Verification is in person — there is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID portal. You present a physical military ID at check-in for the Seminole room rates, or a military ID, DD-214, or "Veteran"-designated state ID at the Player’s Club to enroll in the Atlantic City Veterans Program.

Program enrollment and rates are per-property, and a benefit at one Hard Rock does not carry to another. Military room rates are booked as their own package rather than stacked with public promo codes, and the Atlantic City benefits are non-transferable and cannot be combined with other offers.

Because the query set is dominated by property-specific searches (Orlando, Las Vegas, San Diego, Biloxi, Bristol, and franchised cafes), always confirm on the individual location’s promotions page; a military offer may or may not exist there and is not guaranteed.
sunglass-hut-military-discount: The military discount is verified through ID.me, a third-party identity service — you need a free ID.me account. Online, verification happens at the cart page; in store, a dedicated ID.me link is used. Sunglass Hut does not state how long a verification lasts or whether re-verification is required for repeat purchases, so don’t assume a one-time, permanent verification beyond ID.me’s own terms. For ID.me wallet issues, Sunglass Hut directs users to ID.me Support (help@id.me, live chat, or 866-775-4363).

The catch is the exclusion list. The 15% can’t be combined with other codes, markdowns, new launches, limited editions, or gift cards, and it excludes a specific roster of brands (Chanel, Dior, Oliver Peoples, Alain Mikli, Maui Jim, Prada, Prada Linea Rossa, Miu Miu, Cartier, Brunello Cucinelli, Persol, Moncler) plus selected limited editions, exclusive styles, and collaborations. Because Sunglass Hut runs frequent public promos (e.g., 20% off selected styles, 50% off a second pair) that also can’t be stacked, compare which single offer saves more on the exact frame you want.

Note the scope of eligibility. Sunglass Hut names Active Duty, Retirees, Veterans, Military Spouses, and Military Family Members for the military offer — it does not separately name Reserve/National Guard or dependents, so ID.me verification is the deciding factor for those. First responders, medical workers, teachers, government employees, and students are eligible for 15% too, but through their own separate ID.me (or UNiDAYS) offers, not this military discount.
extra-space-storage-military-discount: The published military benefit is thin but real: 5% off the monthly rate for active service members at "select facilities near military bases." Availability, verification, and stacking are all decided at the facility level, so treat "5% everywhere" as false and confirm with the specific store. There is no national online military code and no third-party verification portal for this discount.

On a representative $150/month 10x10 unit rented for 12 months (about $1,800 before tax and fees), the math favors the move-in special for shorter stays: a single free month is worth about $150, while the recurring 5% saves only about $90 a year. For very long stays the recurring 5% eventually overtakes one free month. The best case is to reserve the unit online for the lower rate, then ask the base-area manager to apply both the move-in promo and the 5% where the store allows it.

Where Extra Space refuses to combine, CubeSmart is worth pricing: its site states its 5% active-military discount applies "in addition to any other specials or promotions," an explicit stack that Extra Space does not guarantee. Self-storage rent is not sold through GovX, the military exchanges, ExpertVoice, or cashback portals, so those channels do not apply here.
bombas-military-discount: The debunk matters here because the fabricated claims are everywhere. WorthEPenny advertises "20% Off Bombas Military & Veteran Discounts," Coupert claims "up to 20%," OrangeOffer claims "70% OFF," and several sites recycle "Bombas offers 10%–25% to military… verify with a valid military ID" or "20% site-wide verified with Troop ID." None of it is real: Troop ID is ID.me’s pre-2013 branding, and ID.me’s own Bombas page says it isn’t aware of any Bombas military discount. Bombas’ help center, checked July 4, 2026, confirms no military discount of any kind.

The real first-order play is COMFORT20 — 20% off for first-time customers, confirmed in Bombas’ help center and on the site banner. Know the stacking rules: one discount code per order, but a gift card CAN be used together with a discount code. And pick code or cashback, not both — TopCashback’s Bombas terms void cashback when you use a code not listed on the portal. At the rates checked July 4, 2026, the 20% code beats every cashback path on a first order ($108.00 versus $117.45 on a $135 12-pack).

On repeat orders, the built-in pack pricing is the quiet workhorse: 4-packs run roughly 8–10% under per-pair pricing and 12-packs roughly 19–20% (a $135 12-pack versus $168 unbundled). Pack prices aren’t codes, so they stack safely with any cashback portal — compare rates before each order, because the leader changes. Historically, the deepest total was late November: 25% off sitewide in 2025, on top of pack pricing.

No adjacent military channel exists either: shopmyexchange.com returns no Bombas listings, no active Bombas ExpertVoice store was found, and there’s no first responder, nurse, teacher, or student program. The brand’s military connection is genuine but charitable — Bombas has donated socks to homeless veterans since 2016, including 100,000+ pairs in fall 2023 with Veterans United and VA.
traeger-military-discount: Traeger uses ID.me on traeger.com: you verify your military, nurse, first-responder, or teacher status once through ID.me (free account), and qualifying items discount automatically in your cart. Traeger support states the discount is offered to all active duty, veterans, reservists, and retirees of the U.S. military, as well as their spouses and dependents. It’s online only (not valid in stores) and limited to US and Canada residents. Traeger "reserves the right to change product eligibility, discount and/or prices at any given time without prior notice."

The most important nuance is the "up to 20%" wording. It applies to select grills, so some models get less than the full 20% — grilling forums report the discount "only knocks off a small amount on some grills." Verify the exact model in your cart. MEATER products are excluded entirely, and only limited accessories, sauces, and rubs are included.

For a big-ticket buyer, the tax-free exchange path matters. Traeger models like the Pro 780, Pro 575, and Texas Elite 34 are stocked tax-free with free shipping at shopmyexchange.com (AAFES) and mynavyexchange.com (Navy Exchange), and are MILITARY STAR card eligible. On a ~$1,000 grill, the ~8% sales tax saved can beat a small ID.me percentage — and if your model isn’t in the 20% "select" set, the tax-free price often wins. The exchange is a separate channel, so you use one route or the other, not both.

A few aggregator claims to ignore: the "up to 40% Traeger military discount" traces to ID.me Shop’s marketplace-wide storefront banner, not Traeger’s grill offer; the ID.me landing page shop.id.me/discounts/traeger/military currently reads "We’re not aware that Traeger Grills offers Military discounts," which is a stale auto-generated template that Traeger’s own live offer contradicts; Ace Hardware typically excludes Traeger from its discretionary 10% military discount; and no Traeger GovX storefront was found this pass. Traeger’s own site is authoritative — the discount does exist.
comcast-military-discount: Comcast and Xfinity are the same company: Xfinity is Comcast’s consumer brand for Internet, Mobile, and TV. When you see "Comcast military discount" on aggregator or editorial pages, it is describing the Xfinity offer. That is why this page routes you to our dedicated Xfinity Military & Veteran Discount page for the exact benefits, who qualifies, and how to redeem — rather than duplicating it here.

The most important caveat carries over from the Xfinity offer: the perks are a benefits package layered on a paid Xfinity Internet subscription, not a standalone coupon. There is no percentage or dollar-amount military discount to combine with anything. Verification happens by signing in at xfinity.com/military and confirming your status, which Xfinity’s support documentation says is processed through SheerID; the offer page itself does not name the provider and sends status questions to 1-833-231-6446.

Beyond the Xfinity service offer, Comcast the parent runs Internet Essentials — low-cost broadband for as low as $14.95/month. Comcast states it connects military families to the internet, but it is a needs-based program (income/assistance eligibility), not a military benefit, and it is a separate service tier from the Xfinity military perks. For a lower-income household it is often the cheapest connectivity path, period, so check it first if cost is the constraint.

Comcast owns NBCUniversal, so its offers reach beyond Internet. Eligible military customers not already getting Peacock through Diamond Rewards can subscribe to Peacock for $3.99/month for a year, and active service members, retirees, and military spouses can get discounted Universal Destinations park tickets, vacation packages, and resort stays through a separate NBCUniversal program (verify through the park’s own military channel). And if you want a per-line bill discount rather than a bundled-perks model — or Xfinity Internet isn’t available at your address — it is worth comparing the military mobile offers from Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile.
mgm-military-discount: The Military & Veterans Program launched in July 2017 and extends MGM Rewards. Eligible groups are active duty, National Guard, Reserve, retired military, veterans, and spouses of eligible military personnel. Verification is entirely in person: either at check-in for the room rate, or at an MGM Rewards desk for the MVP card and Pearl status. Accepted proof includes an active-duty, dependent, retiree, or reserve military ID, a VA ID card, a DD-214, or a state ID with a veteran designation.

MGM does not use ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute for this program — online verification via ID.me is Caesars’ mechanic, not MGM’s. Because MGM’s military rate is a plain online-booked rate with no verification gate, a cashback portal generally tracks normally and a card-linked offer triggers on folio spend, so the military rate can stack with both in a way that ID.me-gated competitor rates often cannot.

The durable win is the auto-Pearl status. Pearl is the second of five MGM Rewards tiers and normally requires about 20,000 tier credits; MVP enrollees skip straight to it. Free self-parking alone can outrun a one-time 10% on a short stay, and the 10% Slot Dollars bonus and non-expiring points compound across repeat visits.
cold-stone-military-discount: The reason there is no single answer is structural: Cold Stone locations are franchisee-owned and operated, and company references confirm each franchise owner sets its own discounts, sales, and promotions. That is why a military courtesy might be about 10% at one store, higher at another, and absent at a third.

Verification, where a courtesy exists, is manual: a staff member checks a military ID. There is no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or integrated WeSalute verification for Cold Stone, and WeSalute itself notes its Cold Stone listing is outside its Partner Coalition and can’t be guaranteed.

For a reliable deal, lean on the rewards program rather than a discount. My Cold Stone Club’s sign-up bonus and points work at participating locations no matter which store you visit. Layer in public coupons or BOGO promos from the app, email, or Groupon when they exist, and time a visit to a Veterans Day promo where your local store participates.
bpn-military-discount: The verification partner is ID.me — the same service used by the VA and the IRS. Click "Apply Discount" on BPN’s military page, sign in or verify, and a one-time 15% code applies at checkout; on future orders you sign in to ID.me at checkout again for a fresh application. There is no GovX storefront, SheerID flow, or WeSalute offer for BPN, no ExpertVoice pro deal, and no evidence BPN is stocked at the exchange — ID.me is the only identity route.

BPN’s no-stacking rules come from its own help center, verbatim: "BPN does not allow discount stacking. Currently, our site only accepts one applied discount per order." The military 15% is also blocked outright if any cart item is a subscription item, and sale periods like July 4 and Black Friday are ineligible for extra discounts — Black Friday 2023 turned the military and first-responder discounts off entirely because the sale ran deeper. Any "military + code" combo you see advertised is impossible by policy.

That policy is why timing matters more than verifying. As of July 13, 2026, BPN’s Summer Sale 2026 has every product at 30% off — "our deepest discount ever," per BPN, with no published end date — and a 25%-off-all-new-subscriptions promo is running alongside it. Both beat 15%. On the $109.98 two-tub Whey Protein baseline cart, the sale saves $32.99 and a new subscription $27.50, versus $16.50 for the military discount. The 15% is the genuine everyday floor for quiet, non-sale weeks and one-time orders; BPN’s standard recurring subscription rate has historically been 10%.

Ignore the aggregator noise: coupon sites advertise "BPN military discounts up to 35% off" and codes like WELCOMEBPN or SAVE25 — none of that is the military discount. The verified military rate is exactly 15% via ID.me; the bigger numbers are BPN’s public sale and subscription promos relabeled. The claim that SMS subscribers get an extra 5% stacked onto the subscription rate contradicts BPN’s published one-discount rule and appears on no BPN-owned page. And since BPN has no cashback rate at any monitored portal (as of July 13, 2026), there’s no Rakuten-style layer to hunt for either.
etsy-military-discount: Etsy runs no verification program (no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID) because there is no platform discount to unlock. If a seller offers a military discount, they set their own — usually informal — proof requirement. The searchable "Military Discount" and "Veteran Discount" pages on etsy.com simply surface listings that shops chose to tag; they are product search results, not a corporate program.

Be cautious of aggregator claims. One circulating page states that "a 30% price reduction is granted on Etsy orders... via etsy.com, the Etsy mobile app, or Etsy’s participating retail locations." That is fabricated — Etsy has no retail locations and no platform military discount. We deliberately omit any Etsy-wide percentage because none exists.

The reliable move is direct: open the shop’s page, use "Message seller," and politely ask for a military/veteran coupon before buying. Success is high with small makers but entirely at the seller’s discretion. On top of any shop coupon or public Etsy sale event, layer a cashback portal when it has a live Etsy rate and pay with a rewards card for a couple more percent.
saks-military-discount: We checked where a real offer would show: ID.me’s Saks Fifth Avenue and Saks OFF 5TH pages both indicate no military program, and there’s no SheerID or GovX gate on saks.com. The "50% off military at OFF 5TH" claim lives only on coupon aggregators and is contradicted by ID.me, so we flag it as false rather than repeat it.

The real savings are public. Saks and OFF 5TH run a frequent sale/clearance calendar (OFF 5TH is the outlet channel with the lowest prices on the same designers), periodic email/first-order sign-up codes, and the free SaksFirst loyalty program (plus the Store Card) for points and shipping perks.

The practical plan: shop the sale or OFF 5TH for the base price, add a current sign-up code, put purchases on SaksFirst for points, and route through a cashback portal. That public stack is the best a service member can do at Saks — there’s no military rate to add on top.
vivint-military-discount: Vivint routes military benefits through ID.me on its site and honors GovX verification for the GovX-specific offer. There is no online "military coupon field" — verification unlocks the phone offer, which you complete with a sales rep. Because the deal is finalized on a call, confirm the credit value and the promo code at the time you call; partner bundles change month to month.

The military offer and the standard public promo overlap. Free professional installation is already the public default, so the military add-on is really the monitoring-months credit — don’t assume you get "double free install." The historically cited GovX bundle is free install plus the first four months of monitoring waived (roughly $180 of that ~$399 value on a $44.99/mo plan), but the exact terms are set at the call.

For active-duty members, the deployed-member contract policy is the other real benefit. It changes cancellation and relocation terms rather than the price, and relief typically requires documentation (orders) and covers suspension or cancellation rather than a refund. Read the Military Policy PDF and get the terms in writing. Coupon sites advertising "Vivint military discount 30% off" fabricate a figure — there is no published flat military percentage.
truewerk-military-discount: TRUEWERK runs verification through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA and many major retailers. At checkout you click the green ID.me button (if it’s not visible, choose "Check out as guest" and it appears at the top of checkout), sign in or create a free account, and verify your group; the 15% then auto-applies to qualified products. How often ID.me asks you to re-verify at TRUEWERK is not stated. One quirk: loyalty points earned while checking out as a guest take about 40 days to post to your account.

The honest math on a first order: TRUEWERK’s public welcome offer — 15% off for joining its email or SMS list — is exactly the same size as the military discount, and welcome codes need no verification. Since nothing combines, use whichever is less friction on order one, then verify with ID.me for every order after that, where the one-time welcome code can’t follow you. Repeat buyers can also bank rewards points (1 point per $1; 10 points = $1) and redeem 100–400 points ($10–$40) on a later $50+ order — points can’t share a transaction with a promo code, so redeem them on a code-free order.

One thing to watch: coupon sites advertise "30% off" and even "40% off" TRUEWERK codes. TRUEWERK’s own help center lists exactly three consumer mechanisms — the 15% welcome offer, the 15% ID.me discount, and rewards points — plus occasional limited-time promotions. No verified evidence supports an evergreen 20–40% public code. When a genuine limited-time site promo runs deeper than 15%, take it instead of the military discount; they can’t be combined.

There’s no side door for this brand: no TRUEWERK GovX storefront, no exchange (AAFES/NEX) listing, and no ExpertVoice military store was found as of July 14, 2026. Cashback through Rakuten was listed at roughly 2–3% — a rounding error, and adding a non-portal coupon code can void it. The ID.me 15% at truewerk.com is the program.
deer-valley-resort-military-discount: Deer Valley uses SheerID to confirm military status during online checkout, and honorably discharged veterans are explicitly told SheerID verification is required before a Military Season Pass is issued. SheerID alone is not sufficient at the mountain: every military ticket and pass must be issued in person at a Deer Valley ticket window, where each pass holder shows a current, valid military photo ID.

Tickets and passes are non-transferable and can only be issued to the verified eligible guest — someone else cannot pick them up. There is one ticket per designated day, per current military ID. For questions or to purchase by phone, the Deer Valley Ticket Office is reachable at 435-645-6626 (the Nov 2025 press release also lists 435-645-6625).

A separate program is worth knowing about but should not be confused with the resort discount: the Grand Hyatt Deer Valley “Salute to Service” program lets service-member lodging guests buy tickets up to 75% off the window rate, plus lodging, spa, and food/beverage discounts — but that is a partner hotel program with its own eligibility list, available only to guests staying at that property. It is not Deer Valley’s own ~25% ticket discount.

One accuracy note: coupon and aggregator pages circulate inflated or vague claims about Deer Valley military discounts. Only the two figures Deer Valley itself publishes — the “approximate 25%” in its press release and the $189 military lift ticket on its military page — are treated as fact here, and the $189 is tied to the 25/26 season, not encoded as an evergreen price.
nine-line-military-discount: Nine Line uses ID.me ("Powered by ID.ME"). You verify your military, first-responder, medical, or teacher credential through ID.me; the re-verification cadence is set by ID.me. Verification support runs through ID.me, and order support through Nine Line.

The 20% applies to non-sale items only and generally will not stack on already-discounted or clearance items or with the roughly 10% email-signup code. Free shipping over $70 is automatic and independent of any code.

Nine Line is also listed on GovX as a separate marketplace channel, and repeat buyers can earn points through Nine Line Rewards / the Patriots Club. Aggregator "25%/40%/50% off" codes are unverified scrapes — the repeatable discount is 20% off non-sale items via ID.me.
gymreapers-military-discount: Gymreapers uses a third-party verification provider to confirm eligibility. The brand’s official discount-page URL and its GovX brand listing both point to GovX ID, though one secondary source describes the flow as VerifyPass — so confirm the provider shown on the live page. Verification is real-time and secure, and a free provider account is required; re-verification follows the provider’s standard policy.

The key mechanic is stacking. On Shopify direct-to-consumer brands like Gymreapers, the cart generally accepts one code, so the verified 10% does not combine with a public promo code. Because Gymreapers runs frequent sitewide codes, the smart move is to compare: on full-price gear take the verified 10%, and when a live sitewide code is 10% or more, take that instead. On a $99.99 order the 10% saves $10.

A note on scope: the discount applies to eligible gear, and the brand states that "select gear and apparel" is excluded, directing shoppers to its FAQ for the exception list. Core lifting gear like belts and wraps is typically included, but confirm the item qualifies before checkout. Coupon aggregators floating "20–50% off military" figures are not supported by any primary source — the only verified military rate is 10%.
disney-plus-military-discount: Verification is handled entirely by The Exchange’s existing shopper-authorization system, not by ID.me or SheerID. To reach the offer you must have a valid, current ShopMyExchange.com account, which AAFES grants to authorized patrons — active duty, retirees, Guard/Reserve, and honorably discharged veterans who verify status through the VA’s online process. Once you have an Exchange account, no additional Disney-side military verification is described.

The "military families" wording in Disney’s press release does not override Exchange access rules: the standard online Veterans benefit does not automatically extend online access to a veteran’s family members, so spouse/dependent eligibility depends on whether that person holds their own authorized ShopMyExchange account. Confirm this at ShopMyExchange.com.

Disney has changed Disney+ Premium pricing repeatedly, so this guide deliberately states the 25% figure rather than a dollar amount — pull live pricing from ShopMyExchange or disneyplus.com at the time you subscribe.
chase-sapphire-reserve-military: The math is why this matters: the June 2025 relaunch made the Sapphire Reserve the most expensive mainstream travel card — $795 a year plus $195 per authorized user — yet an MLA-covered servicemember or military spouse reportedly holds it for $0 while keeping every benefit. The waiver never touches the card’s earnings: the welcome offer, 8x points on Chase Travel, 4x on flights and hotels booked direct, 3x on dining, the $300 annual travel credit, up to $500 a year in The Edit hotel credits, $300 in dining credits, $300 in StubHub credits, DoorDash and Lyft perks, Apple TV+ and Apple Music, airport lounge access (Chase Sapphire Lounges plus 1,300+ Priority Pass lounges), and the $120 Global Entry/TSA PreCheck/NEXUS credit all work normally on a fee-waived card. Many credits are split into six-month caps and several are limited-time partner deals — the fee may be $0, but the credits still take management to collect.

Which law applies comes down to one variable: the account-open date. Open the Reserve while you’re a covered borrower — active duty, Guard/Reserve on Title 10/32 orders over 30 days, or a DEERS-enrolled spouse or dependent — and the MLA route applies: Chase screens the application against Department of Defense records (credit cards came under the MLA rule on October 3, 2017) and the fee is reportedly zeroed automatically, no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX involved at any point. Held the card before you activated? File an SCRA request — the secure-message SCRA dropdown is fastest, or call 1-877-469-0110 — with electronic copies of your orders. Federal law caps pre-service interest at 6% with the excess forgiven; Chase is consistently reported to go further, to 4% APR plus waived or credited fees, through active duty and up to one year after. Two conflations to avoid: the MLA waiver needs no request, and the SCRA channel is only for pre-service accounts.

Two more facts shape the smart play. First, MLA coverage is per person — so a married military couple can each open their own fee-waived Reserve as primary cardholders (widely reported in military-finance communities), each earning their own welcome offer; and the reported waiver is card-agnostic across Chase’s personal lineup, so the $95 Sapphire Preferred and co-brand cards are reported to sit at $0 too while you’re covered. Second, coverage ends with your covered-borrower status: separated members report Chase re-checking MLA records and reinstating the fee within roughly one to two years (spouses report verification letters 6–9 months out), so never plan around a grace period. Before coverage lapses, decide whether the credits genuinely out-earn $795 for you — if not, product-change to the $95 Sapphire Preferred or a no-fee Freedom card; your Ultimate Rewards points survive the downgrade. American Express runs the same $0 play on its $895 Platinum and, unlike Chase, publishes the policy openly — see the Amex Platinum military guide for the other free premium card.
zumiez-military-discount: Zumiez’s own Deals page is unusually blunt: it says the company "does not offer coupons or promo codes but does have incredible deals," that it never posts codes to coupon sites, and that codes you find there "are not real." Because there is no code of any kind, there is no military code — and there is nothing to stack. Sale and clearance pricing is simply the item’s marked-down price at checkout, applied automatically.

No verification provider lists Zumiez either. Searches of ID.me, GovX, and SheerID (plus WeSalute and VerifyPass) turn up no Zumiez brand page, so there is no military, veteran, first-responder, teacher, nurse, student, or government status to verify. Aggregator claims of a "10% off for active duty and veterans" or a "DD-214 at checkout" process are not supported by any Zumiez source — treat them as fabricated.

The strongest real move for eligible shoppers is brand substitution at the military Exchange. ShopMyExchange (Army/Air Force), NEX (Navy), and MCX (Marines) carry many of the same action-sports brands Zumiez sells — Vans, Nike SB, and similar — tax-free, with member pricing. The Exchange verifies military and veteran status at account creation, so verification is handled there, not by Zumiez. It won’t stock Zumiez-exclusive labels, but for mainstream brands it’s savings Zumiez can’t match.

If the brand you want isn’t at the Exchange, the honest Zumiez stack is: shop sale/clearance, take the email free-shipping offer online, add a cashback portal (Rakuten/TopCashback) if the live rate is worth it, and — if you shop Zumiez often — join the free Stash for long-term reward value. Points buy merchandise, limited products, sweepstakes entries, and experiences, not dollars off your cart.
galls-military-discount: Here’s the debunk. Coupon and aggregator pages assert a flat "up to 10%–25% military discount," a "military ID at galls.com" gate, and stackable "military codes." None is verified. Galls uses no military identity verification — the profession dropdown on the 15% signup form literally offers "Civilian" as an option, so it’s a self-declared marketing code, not a service-gated discount. The "up to 25%" figure is the public sitewide sale, available to everyone, not a military rate.

The structural limits matter. Galls’ own offer-details page states "Limit one promotion code per order" and "Offer cannot be combined with any other offers, discounts or services." So the 15% code can’t stack on the sitewide sale or any other code — and because that sale is often 20–25% and needs no code, it frequently beats the 15%. Take whichever is lower, never both.

One more distinction: Galls does require credential verification to purchase restricted items (e.g., items marked POLICE/SHERIFF) — you email a department ID to id@galls.com, provide a letter of authorization, or ship to your agency. That gate controls what you can buy, not a discount. And since Galls competes with GovX, there’s no Galls GovX storefront and no tax-free exchange channel to compare.
halo-collar-military-discount: Coupon aggregators headline a "Halo Collar military discount — 50% OFF" or "35% off military," but no such official military offer exists. One aggregator states plainly that a military personnel discount is not available at Halo Collar. The "military" codes those sites advertise are ordinary public codes — anyone can use them — with exaggerated percentages. The genuine current discount is the on-site sale ($524 for the Halo Collar 5), and you should verify any code at checkout rather than trust the number in a listicle.

The real cost story is the subscription, not the sticker. Halo’s GPS fence requires an ongoing Pack Membership (from $9.99/month) to activate and maintain GPS and cellular data — the fence won’t function without it. Hardware deals never touch this recurring fee, so the plan tier you choose, paid month after month, is the bigger lifetime cost. Coupon pages omit this entirely; budgeting for the membership is the honest advice for any service member weighing a Halo Collar.

For the best real price, take the standing on-site sale as your baseline, then decide between a promo code and cashback — usually an either/or, since coupon-code orders commonly void or reduce Rakuten-style portal cashback. If the sale price is already applied, a code-free order through a portal (verify the live rate) is often the cleaner saving. If you have two dogs, the on-site 2-pack bundle ($998 for two, with an extra $50 for buying two collars) beats buying singles. Watch Black Friday and Cyber Monday for the deepest annual public markdowns — none of which is military-gated.
swarovski-military-discount: The evidence for "no current discount" comes from the verification provider itself. ID.me’s Swarovski US pages state plainly, "We’re not aware that Swarovski US offers Military discounts," and the same for first responders. Coupon aggregators still push a current 10%–25% military discount and a "select the Military and First Responder Discount at checkout, verify via SheerID/ID.me" flow — but that flow existed and has been discontinued, and the often-repeated 10% figure traces to a one-time 2019 in-store Veterans Day weekend. Treat any current "military %" claim as expired.

The best everyday path is the free Swarovski Club. Joining unlocks a 10% welcome code on your first online order and a 20% reward in your birthday month, plus early sale access and free-shipping perks. Both the welcome and birthday codes apply to full-price items only — so you choose the code or an already-reduced sale item, not both. For frequent buyers, the paid Crystal Society (about $55/year) adds free shipping on every order, an annual gift, and complimentary repairs.

On top of a code, a cashback portal can add roughly 4–8% back (about 8% at the time of writing, elevated from a 4% base). Because cashback is paid by the portal rather than Swarovski, it often layers on top of an on-site code — but the elevated rate’s terms note it "cannot be combined with most other offers," so treat stacking as uncertain and confirm at click-through. Free shipping kicks in at $150+ without any membership, and note that "Swarovski" listings on GovX are third-party resellers, not an official discount.
aura-military-discount: Aura verifies eligibility through its Military.com partnership, not a standalone provider like ID.me or SheerID. You provide the information Military.com’s flow requests to confirm active-duty, veteran, or dependent status, then you’re routed into the discounted Aura signup. Because it’s a subscription tied to your Aura account, expect eligibility to attach to that account rather than be re-verified at every renewal — confirm current terms at signup.

The exact discounted percentage is not settled across Aura’s own pages: the help center states up to 52% off, the military landing page currently advertises up to 68% off, and the 2022 Military Appreciation Month launch was 50% off the Family plan. Aura’s military landing page shows pricing as placeholders to automated fetches, so treat the discounted price as display-at-checkout and confirm the live number before you buy. We cite up to 52% as the conservative verified floor.

The single deepest published deal for the military community is actually the WeSalute partner offer — up to 75% off Aura’s online-safety plans for WeSalute members — not the direct 52%. The two routes are mutually exclusive, so price the WeSalute offer including current membership dues to know when it truly beats the direct offer. For everyone, annual billing (already about 30% under monthly), the universal 14-day free trial with no credit card, and the 60-day money-back guarantee on annual plans are the baseline saves.
home-depot-military-discount: The discount is everyday and year-round. The Home Depot expanded it from a holidays-only veteran benefit to an everyday benefit for veterans, active duty, and spouses in December 2021, and its May 1, 2025 investor-relations release describes it as a "10% military discount on full-priced, non-appliance merchandise." Older pages that say veterans only get the discount on patriotic holidays (Memorial Day, July 4th, Veterans Day) are outdated.

Verification and redemption are app/account based. According to military-benefit publications, The Home Depot uses the third-party verifier SheerID during a one-time enrollment; your verified status is then saved to your Home Depot account. For in-store use you present a virtual ID QR code generated live in the app — screenshots and printouts are reported not to work, and a paper DD-214 or physical ID is reported to no longer be accepted at the register. Because Home Depot’s own military FAQ is JavaScript-rendered and didn’t return its terms to our fetch, we present the provider name and these mechanics as commonly reported and link to the official page to confirm.

Two caveats worth planning around. First, appliances are excluded from the 10% — but eligible military shoppers can buy many appliances tax-free through the separate Military Exchange program at ShopMyExchange.com or myNavyExchange.com, confirmed in Home Depot’s 2025 release. Second, military.com and The Military Wallet consistently report a $400 maximum annual discount (about the first $4,000 of eligible spend per calendar year); that cap is not confirmed on any Home Depot page we could read, so verify it before relying on it — and if you hit it, a comparable everyday 10% military discount at Lowe’s is a useful alternative.
petsmart-military-discount: Verification is in person at the point of service, not through any third-party platform. PetSmart does not use ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute for these discounts — ID.me’s own site confirms it is not aware of a PetSmart military discount, so any "verify with ID.me at PetSmart checkout" claim is inaccurate. For grooming, you show a military ID (expired accepted) or a DD214 to a salon associate; for PetsHotel, government-issued ID to a Services associate. A free Treats Rewards membership is required for grooming. There’s no annual re-verification because there’s no account-linked status — you present ID each time.

The two offers have distinct rules. Grooming is Tuesdays only, requires Treats Rewards, and covers grooming services and add-ons but excludes merchandise and all other services. PetsHotel is 10% off any overnight stay, one discount per stay, and excludes add-ons, Doggie Day Camp, and Bundle Packages. The PetsHotel first-responder tier is state/local only — federal law enforcement (Border Patrol, CIA, DEA, FEMA, FBI, NSA) is explicitly excluded. Seniors 65+ qualify for both.

Since there’s no merchandise discount, the ways military families save on products are the same as for everyone: the free Treats Rewards program earns points on every purchase and gives free standard shipping over $49 (valid to military APO/FPO addresses), and Autoship saves 35% on a first order (up to $20) and 5% on recurring orders. PetSmart has historically promoted elevated Treats points around Veterans Day — treat that as seasonal and re-check each November rather than as an evergreen offer.
progressive-military-discount: There is no third-party verification provider (no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute) because there is no Progressive military program to gate. In Louisiana, verification is documentary and state-defined: you complete the Louisiana Application Form for Military Discount and provide supporting documentation (military orders for active duty; a commander’s letter for National Guard), submitted to your agent or insurer, per Louisiana Department of Insurance Bulletin 2023-04. The form and proof requirements have been revised more than once, so confirm the current version with the LDI or Progressive.

The scope is narrow and worth repeating: the 25% is Louisiana-only and applies to liability premium (per regulatory summaries), not the whole policy. Veterans and retirees are not covered by the mandate — the law only offers insurers an optional tax credit to extend it to retirees and 50%+-disabled veterans, and Progressive has not published whether it does. Because it’s a state mandate, a Louisiana resident can claim the same 25% at any LA-licensed insurer, so shop the post-discount rate rather than assuming Progressive is cheapest.

Outside Louisiana, the ways to save are Progressive’s standard, everyone-eligible discounts: multi-policy bundling, multi-car, continuous insurance, the Snapshot safe-driver program, good/distant student, homeowner, online-quote, paperless, pay-in-full, and automatic payment. Aggregator sources say Progressive offers comprehensive-only coverage for stored vehicles during deployment and won’t penalize deployment-related lapses — we could not confirm that on Progressive’s own site, so verify it directly. For an actual military price break nationwide, USAA (military/eligible family only) and GEICO publish military-specific discounts worth comparing. Note also Progressive’s Keys to Progress is a veteran vehicle giveaway, not an insurance discount.
tarte-military-discount: Tarte’s discount is verified through SheerID, a third-party identity service. You submit your details on Tarte’s Special Offers page; SheerID confirms eligibility and may ask for documentation if it can’t auto-verify. Approved members receive a unique, one-time-use code, refreshed by email at the start of each month — it is not a permanent account discount.

The military tier sits alongside the same 40% offer for first responders, medical professionals, K-12 teachers, and professional makeup artists, plus a 20% tier for students. All run through SheerID under the same terms, so if you qualify for more than one, pick whichever verifies fastest.

Because the code is fully standalone, there is no stacking game to play. At 40% it is typically deeper than Tarte’s public sales (which historically run around 25–30% during Friends & Family or Cyber Weekend), so for verified shoppers the military code is the single best path on virtually any eligible cart.
peacock-military-discount: Peacock uses SheerID to confirm military eligibility. At peacocktv.com/military you are redirected to SheerID and asked for your first name, last name, date of birth, and branch of service; SheerID checks this against authoritative military data. On success you receive a one-time promo code (valid 30 days) to apply to a new or existing Peacock account. For verification problems, Peacock links to SheerID’s military FAQ.

Peacock requires annual verification. To keep the discounted rate beyond 12 months you must re-verify your eligibility through SheerID; otherwise the plan renews at the full $10.99/month (or then-current) rate plus tax. The voucher code is one-time use, limited to one per person and per email account, and is void once redeemed or expired.

One thing to watch: several coupon and aggregator pages still advertise Peacock military pricing of $3.99/mo, $2.99/mo, or "$4/mo savings." Those figures are outdated — they reflect older promotional pricing. Peacock’s own military page and offer terms state $6.99/month for 12 months (a $10.99/month retail value), which is the only rate we quote.
discovery-plus-military-discount: discovery+ ran its military discount from around 2021 until it closed to new subscribers on June 1, 2023. The offer was 40% off the Ad-Lite (ad-supported) plan — $4.99/month down to $2.99/month — and eligibility was checked through SheerID using your name, email, date of birth, military status, and branch of service. It applied to the Ad-Lite tier only, never the Ad-Free tier, and could not be combined with other promotions. All of that is now historical: there is no active verification flow for new members.

Grandfathering is narrow. Members who were enrolled before June 1, 2023 keep their discounted rate, but only while they remain continuously subscribed and still eligible. Cancel once and the rate is gone for good — it cannot be reinstated. discovery+ can also raise grandfathered pricing with at least 30 days’ notice, so even continuously subscribed members are not locked to $2.99 forever. The exact current grandfathered price after subsequent standard increases is not publicly itemized.

Because discovery+ is a direct-to-consumer subscription, there is nothing to "stack." It is not sold through GovX or a military exchange, and streaming subscriptions generally are not on cashback portals, so the usual portal-and-code stacking does not apply. The genuine levers are the plan you pick and any perk you already have: the annual Ad-Lite plan ($59.99/year) beats monthly by roughly two months of cost, the 7-day free trial covers a short-term binge, and a qualifying carrier bundle (Verizon’s +play has historically included discovery+) can replace paying discovery+ directly. Much of the discovery+ library also lives inside Max, so if you already subscribe to Max, paying for both is redundant for many viewers.

If your goal is simply a streaming service with a real, standing military discount rather than discovery+ specifically, cross-shop the competition: Paramount+ offers verified military 50% off any plan for life through SheerID, and Peacock and Disney+ (through the military Exchange) also run military offers. Those are the strongest current streaming options for service members.
margaritaville-cruise-military-discount: Verification is through GovX, the military and government marketplace, which verifies active-duty and former military, first responders, medical personnel, educators, and government employees with a free account. You must be a verified GovX member at the time of booking, and hero staterooms are booked online after verification — either starting from the Heroes Sail Free page on margaritavilleatsea.com or from the Margaritaville at Sea Cruises page on GovX, which routes to the same offer.

The honest math: the fare is genuinely $0 for guests one and two, but shoppers report taxes, fees, and port expenses of roughly $110–$140 per person depending on itinerary, and gratuities run $18 per person per day per community reports — so a "free" 4-night cruise for two realistically costs a few hundred dollars out of pocket before drinks and extras. No official flat tax/fee number is published; any site quoting one exact figure for all sailings is overreaching. Budget those costs on top of every option, because they are never waived.

Heroes Sail Free launched in 2022 as an industry-first program with GovX and has welcomed over 100,000 heroes since. It expanded fleet-wide for 2024–2025 and was later re-scoped to Interior staterooms on Islander and Paradise; current marketing frames free hero sailings on select 2–7-night itineraries through 2026, with the 20%-off promos running year-round. Because the scope has moved repeatedly, treat the ships, cabin categories, and dates as check-before-you-book details.

There is no stacking game here: the free hero fare is the deal, and the 20% fallback applies to best available retail rates rather than layering on other codes. No cashback-portal path was verified for Margaritaville at Sea bookings as of July 14, 2026. If nobody in your party is GovX-verifiable, watch the line’s public flash fares — it has historically run aggressive $49–$179 guest-fare promos.
beats-military-discount: There is no Beats military discount to stack — the military-relevant discount lives at Apple (ID.me) or GovX, not on Beats.com. Apple’s 10% military discount covers most Apple products and accessories and, since Beats is sold through Apple, is the cleanest "official" military route; it has its own eligibility and exclusion rules and generally doesn’t stack with other Apple promotions. GovX member pricing is a separate channel you buy from directly, so nothing stacks across the two.

Be careful with aggregator claims. Some sites advertise a "25% in-store military discount (show military ID)" and a "40% off code GUETTAMIXR" for military. Neither is a published Beats military benefit — GUETTAMIXR is a general promotional code, and no 25% military term appears on Beats’ site. Knoji and aggregator Q&A threads consistently report "no official Beats military discount," pointing users to Apple’s store or retailer sales — which corroborates the finding.

The routing is simple. If a public sale is live, buy the sale — Beats headphones discount deeply and often, usually beating 10%. If no sale is live and you want a verified military route, use Apple’s 10% via ID.me, or take GovX if its member price is lower. If you have Exchange access, tax-free at the Exchange can beat a 10% civilian-priced order. Compare all of them on the day.
evenflo-military-discount: Evenflo’s discount is delivered as a promo code after you verify through ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. The military tier sits alongside parallel Community Heroes groups — first responders, healthcare workers, teachers, and students — that receive the same 20%.

One honest wrinkle: Evenflo’s own site disagrees with itself on the number. Its group offer pages (military, first-responder, student, healthcare) advertise 20% OFF, while its Promotions summary tile says members "receive a 15% discount." We treat 20% as the advertised offer-page value, but the code issued in the ID.me widget is the tiebreaker — confirm it before relying on a number.

Evenflo runs no public coupon codes and is not listed on cashback portals like Rakuten or TopCashback, so the ID.me 20% is effectively the savings path on evenflo.com. If you’re flexible on model, Evenflo’s Outlet runs up to 50% off closeout/overstock SKUs, and exchange-eligible shoppers can buy Evenflo car seats tax-free at AAFES or the Navy Exchange — a strong route on big-ticket seats.
honda-military-discount: The $500 is applied by Honda Financial Services, not the dealer directly: on a purchase it reduces your down payment, and on a lease it reduces the capitalized cost before your payment or total-due-at-signing is calculated. It only applies when you finance or lease through HFS and receive HFS credit approval — a cash buyer or someone using outside financing does not get the $500.

Verification is entirely document-based at the dealership, with no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or online verification code involved. Active-duty and Ready Reserve members show a Leave and Earnings Statement (LES) or DFAS confirmation form. Veterans show a DFAS RAS confirmation, DD-214, or Certificate of Release/Discharge. Spouses show a Military ID plus a copy of their spouse’s LES. Gold Star family members show a Report of Casualty (DD-1300), a completed Gold Star Lapel Button application (DD-3), or other official Gold Star documentation.

Only one $500 Military Appreciation Certificate applies per vehicle, and it combines with other Honda Financial Services programs except the Zero Due at Signing Lease program — worth checking against whatever other HFS incentive you’re considering before you sign. Honda also runs a separate $500 College Graduate Bonus through HFS; it is a different program with its own eligibility, and whether it can stack with the Military offer on the same vehicle for the same buyer is not confirmed.

A note on accuracy: individual Honda dealer pages phrase this offer differently — some call it "$500 off" or a "military discount," and some still display an older "valid through 3/31/2026" window. The program itself is Honda Financial Services’ national offer, it is a flat $500 (never a percentage of MSRP), and the current verified HFS text extends the window through March 31, 2027.
playstation-military-discount: Every credible source confirms there is no official PlayStation military discount, so the whole page hinges on channels, not an identity code. The Exchange is a closed, tax-free channel: on a $549.99 PS5 Slim Disc Edition, waiving roughly 6–10% sales tax is about $33–$55, and Exchange stickers are frequently below civilian MSRP on top of that. Nothing from PlayStation.com and no cashback portal stacks on an Exchange order — the value is tax-free plus free shipping.

For digital, the cleanest stack is a discounted PlayStation Store gift card plus a PS Store sale: you buy the wallet funds at 10–15% off, redeem them to your PlayStation account, and then buy a sale-priced game or PS Plus term. Because the “discount” is on the funding instrument rather than the checkout, it layers on top of whatever sale price PlayStation is already running.

Two common false claims to avoid. First, the Sony Electronics up-to-15% ID.me offer is a different Sony division (electronics.sony.com) and is not confirmed to cover any PlayStation SKU — do not present it as a PS5 or PS Plus benefit. Second, GOVX lists a member-gated “PlayStation Store” storefront, but GOVX’s standard discount excludes gift-card purchases and PS Store codes function as gift cards, so any headline percentage may not apply; verify after a GovX ID login before relying on it.

PlayStation’s real “sale seasons” are public, not military: Days of Play (spring/summer) and Black Friday/Holiday deliver the deepest PS Store markdowns and hardware bundles for everyone. There is no PlayStation Veterans Day or Memorial Day military promotion — the benefit path for service members is the tax-free Exchange and discounted gift cards, not a holiday percentage.
office-depot-military-discount: Office Depot uses two different verification paths. In store, a cashier checks your physical military, dependent, or veteran ID at checkout — no app or account required. Online, officedepot.com routes verification through ID.me; once verified, the online offer is delivered as 25% back in Bonus Rewards rather than an instant discount.

One thing to watch: coupon aggregators sometimes list a flat "25% off Office Depot military discount." The verified everyday in-store figure is 20% off regular-price purchases. The 25% figures you may see elsewhere are either the online Bonus-Rewards mechanic (25% back, not off) or the historical Veterans Day in-store boost — don’t treat either as an everyday 25%-off rate.

The everyday 20% in-store program was announced June 14, 2021 by The ODP Corporation, Office Depot’s parent company, via its corporate newsroom, and it remains the durable official source for the 20% figure and eligible groups. Because the live officedepot.com military-offer page renders as a JavaScript shell (its offer body doesn’t appear in a plain fetch of the HTML), the exact current exclusion list should be confirmed against the rendered page or in store before you assume every regular-price item qualifies.
carnival-cruise-military-discount: The military rate is priced per sailing, not as a published discount percentage. That means there is no single "X% off" figure to quote honestly — some marketing sources advertise "up to 40-50% off," but that framing comes from third-party cruise-deal agencies and membership marketing (like WeSalute), not from a fixed Carnival rate. Always compare the actual priced military fare against the public promo for your specific sailing and cabin before booking.

Verification here works differently than most retail military discounts: there is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID gate on the fare itself. Instead, Carnival verifies eligibility by document submission after you book — you upload or fax a DD214/DD256, an LES with the Social Security number redacted, or enlistment/discharge papers plus a photo ID, within a strict 24-72 hour window depending on how close your sailing is. Missing that window is reportedly the most common way travelers lose the rate.

Onboard credit commonly accompanies military bookings, and editorial and travel-agency sources report tiers roughly in the range of $50 for shorter cruises up to $250 for longer ones. Carnival’s own help-center page did not render its full terms on fetch, so treat those specific dollar tiers as commonly reported rather than guaranteed, and confirm the current offer at booking.

Twice a year — historically around May (Military Appreciation Month) and November (Veterans Day) — Carnival has run promotions extending the military rate to additional cabins beyond the military member’s own. These windows are typical seasonal patterns rather than a guaranteed annual commitment, so confirm current dates before planning a group booking around them.
autozone/law-enforcement: AutoZone stores are company-operated, not franchised — which is worth knowing because a common aggregator claim says the first-responder discount is "up to the owner of the franchise." There are no franchise owners, and no official first-responder program for one to opt into. What individual store managers occasionally do at the register as a courtesy is discretion, not policy, and it isn’t something to count on.

The GovX path works because gift cards are a payment method, not a coupon. Buy AutoZone gift cards at 5% off through GovX (denominations $5–$250, $25 minimum), then spend them like cash — including on an online order that also uses a public promo code. AutoZone publishes no restriction on paying promo orders with gift cards, though its gift-card terms don’t address the combination explicitly either way.

Because there’s no LE program at AutoZone itself, the public savings machinery matters more than anywhere else: sitewide promo codes (open to all, typically ship-to-home only), free AutoZone Rewards credits on every purchase, rebates, and the clearance section. When a 20%-off code is live and your order qualifies, that public deal outsaves every identity-gated route — pay with discounted gift cards and you stack the two.
kfc-military-discount: KFC is a heavily franchised fast-food brand, and franchised chains rarely run a published, national military rate. We checked KFC.com, the KFC app, and KFC’s newsroom and found no service-member offer, and KFC appears on no verified Veterans Day free-meal list (Military.com, Veteran.com). The most a service member can realistically expect is a discretionary, location-by-location courtesy that some franchisees may choose to honor at the register — never a guaranteed rate.

Be cautious of coupon and aggregator pages that advertise a "10-25%" KFC military discount for "active duty, veterans, and immediate family." No primary source supports any percentage, eligibility list, or online-redemption mechanism — so we omit the figure rather than repeat an offer that does not exist. Separately, the only "GovX KFC" result is the KFC Yum! Center in Louisville, an event-ticket venue discount, not a discount on KFC restaurant food.

The genuine best savings path for everyone — service member or not — is KFC Rewards layered on the current app deals. KFC Rewards earns 10 points per $1 on online orders placed through a Rewards account on the KFC app or KFC.com, and members redeem points for free food from the rotating Secret Recipe Vault. Because Rewards is online-only, in-store counter purchases neither earn nor redeem points, and any franchise "courtesy" discount would be a separate in-store cash-register event outside Rewards entirely.

One structural exception exists for those with base access: KFC operates in some AAFES Exchange food courts, and on-base food-court purchases carry no sales tax. That tax-free price is the only true "military" saving on KFC food, and it comes from where you buy, not from any KFC discount program.
universal-studios-california-military-di: The online military ticket is a single, ID.me-gated price rather than a code you layer on a promo ticket, and it is not combinable with other offers. The genuinely better deal for most eligible members is buying through a base MWR/ITT ticket office, where Universal sells discounted 1-Day General Admission and a 12-Month Military Pass at prices that typically beat the $4 online cut. The online and on-base channels are alternatives, not a stack.

Because the $4 and $20 online amounts are flat, they do not scale with Universal’s date-based gate price (roughly $109–$189 for a 1-Day General Admission depending on the visit date), so on high-priced peak days the percentage saved is small. Before buying the $4 online ticket with no base access, it is worth comparing Universal’s public multi-day or promotional tickets, which frequently beat a $4 cut on a per-visit basis.

Watch out for aggregator claims of a "$3 off" gate discount or an evergreen "buy a day, get a day free" military promo. Universal’s official Hollywood page publishes a flat $4-per-person online discount on 1-Day GA and Express and $20 per pass on the Neighbor or Silver pass — no $3 figure and no standing buy-one-get-one. A "buy a day, get a day free" title appears on the ID.me store listing and may run seasonally; treat it as a possible limited promo to verify at the ID.me-gated checkout, not a standing benefit.

This guide covers Universal Studios Hollywood in California only. Universal Orlando Resort runs a structurally different, ITT-only program (the 2026 Military Freedom Pass) — none of its terms apply in California, and vice-versa.
six-flags-fiesta-texas-military-discount: Six Flags uses ID.me to verify military and first-responder status for online tickets — you log in when prompted after selecting your admission, and the $35 price applies. The rate is rejected at the gate if it was not pre-purchased online, so plan ahead. Free-admission Military Appreciation Days are handled differently: they are verified in person by showing a valid military ID at the front gate.

The single best path depends on timing. Visiting over Memorial Day weekend? The free-admission Military Appreciation Days win outright — nothing beats free. Any other day? The $35 ID.me ticket is the everyday winner, and it also beats most public online single-day deals. If you will visit two or more times a year, price a Season Pass on a public sale instead, since the per-visit cost usually drops below repeated single-day tickets.

Watch the disambiguation: this page is about Six Flags Fiesta Texas in San Antonio, not Six Flags Over Texas in Arlington. The two parks publish separate military ticket pages and separate Appreciation-Days dates, so always confirm you are on the Fiesta Texas page before buying.
columbia-military-discount: Columbia verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. The percentage is confirmed at 10% on the ID.me Shop store page; Columbia’s own discount page describes the program and eligibility but does not publish the number — it’s revealed after you verify with ID.me at checkout. You verify once through ID.me; Columbia does not state how often you must re-confirm, so don’t assume a one-time, permanent verification.

The 10% sits alongside parallel ID.me communities for first responders (police, firefighters, EMTs, 911 dispatchers), teachers (classroom teachers, principals, school staff, college faculty), and students (enrolled at accredited US/Canada institutions). A nurse/medical or government-employee program is not listed among Columbia’s ID.me offers, so we don’t assert one. ID.me’s military definition also excludes civilian military employees, less-than-honorable discharges, non-U.S. military, and the Coast Guard Auxiliary.

A couple of cautions: the discount can’t be combined with any other offer or sale, doesn’t apply to gift cards, taxes, or shipping, and discounted purchases don’t earn Columbia Greater Rewards — so on a big sitewide sale, compare which path saves more. An in-store 10% is reported by some aggregators but isn’t confirmed in Columbia’s official sources (the flow described is online only), and a higher 20% Veterans-period promo reported in past years is not currently confirmed — check Columbia.com around Veterans Day for any active promo.
pxg-military-discount: Verification runs through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many retailers. You click "Verify with ID.me" on PXG’s Heroes page, select your group, and submit the documents ID.me requests for your category (for example a military ID, a retired ID or pension statement, an EMT/paramedic or firefighter certification, or a law-enforcement ID). Once ID.me confirms your status, your PXG Heroes account unlocks the discount.

Be careful with the number you may have seen elsewhere: PXG’s current Heroes landing page and its ID.me listing both state 20%. A 2022 PXG blog post advertised "up to 50% off select clubs and apparel" for first responders — that was a past promotion and is not the current evergreen rate, so don’t expect anything above 20% today. PXG also advertises separate "New Lower Pricing" on certain Heroes clubs without a fixed percentage; check the current club prices directly.

PXG does not publish how often ID.me re-verification is required, so don’t assume it’s permanent — ID.me credentials can expire and require periodic re-verification on ID.me’s own terms. For help, PXG directs members to ID.me support or to call 1.844.PLAY.PXG.
raising-canes-military-discount: The Hero Discount is best understood as a location-discretionary courtesy, not a corporate program. Cane’s PR references a "Hero Discount Program," but no official terms page defines it, and reporting consistently notes it "may vary by location." Shoppers report it is hit-or-miss: some stores apply ~10% readily, others say they don’t offer it. Carry a valid military or service ID, mention it at the register, and treat a "no" as store-specific rather than a policy you can appeal.

Because the Hero Discount is verbal and in-store only, there is no way to use it online — no code to enter on the app, website, or a delivery platform, and no third-party verification. That also means it does not stack in any online channel. In person, assume one discount per order: Cane’s publishes no stacking policy, so do not count on combining it with Caniac Club rewards or a public BOGO promo. Confirm at the counter if it matters to you.

The free Caniac Club is the most reliable way to save. It gives a free birthday drink and an anniversary/holiday buy-one-get-one Box Combo — and on a two-combo order, that BOGO beats a flat 10%. The old welcome free Box Combo was removed in August 2024 and the sign-up free Box in April 2026, so the birthday and anniversary rewards are now the core value. Most rewards redeem in-store.
wingstop-military-discount: The debunk, with dates: coupon aggregators currently claim a Wingstop US military discount of 15% (Coupert), 20% (military-discount.com), 50% (Valuecom, "first responder"), even 60% (OrangeOffer) — mutually contradictory and confirmed by zero official sources. The code WSCARES is marketed as "25% off military" and "30% off students" interchangeably — no official Wingstop source ties it to any identity discount. And the "show a valid photocard ID, NHS staff eligible" terms pasted into US pages are lifted from the separately operated UK Wingstop (a Blue Light Card partner run by franchisee Lemon Pepper Holdings) — they don’t apply at US locations.

The Veterans Day record is worth knowing because aggregators recycle it: the "free combo with military ID" promo dates to November 11, 2013 at participating San Antonio-area stores, and a Memorial Day free-meal gesture covered two Tri-Cities, WA franchise locations on May 25, 2015. Nationally, Wingstop ran no Veterans Day offer in 2024 (absent from the VA’s official list) or 2025 (absent from Brand Eating’s and Military.com’s lists — corporate marked the day with a veteran-employee podcast episode instead). Community reports of single franchises doing their own thing (a Hope Mills, NC store offering veterans 50% off around Veterans Day; Houston-area stores giving free combos) are real but store-level — call ahead.

The verified savings path is open to everyone: Club Wingstop is free and pays a 5-piece boneless-wings reward on signup (with a $5+ purchase, 14-day expiry), earns 10 points per $1 with redemptions from 150 points, and unlocks member boneless by-the-piece pricing on Mondays and Tuesdays. Order direct — Wingstop’s own terms state most offers don’t work on third-party marketplaces and that DoorDash/Uber Eats prices "may be higher." One structural note: every Wingstop offer carries "may not be combined with any other offers or promotions," so plan one offer per transaction.

Ruled-out paths, so you don’t chase them: no GovX listing, no cashback-portal merchant page (CashbackMonitor showed no Wingstop store as of July 4, 2026), no exchange or pro-deal channel for restaurant food, and no advertised gift-card bonus windows. If you want free wings on November 11 specifically, go where the verified offer is: Buffalo Wild Wings gave veterans and active-duty service members 10 free boneless wings and fries on Veterans Day 2025, dine-in with valid ID.
casio-military-discount: Casio verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. You click the ID.me button on Casio’s military-discount page, verify once, and a single-use coupon is issued — limited to one per customer per 30 days. Re-verify for a new code. The discount works only on casio.com/us and gshock.casio.com/us, not on third-party retailers.

The exclusions are what make Casio’s program distinctive. The 10% doesn’t apply to sale or outlet items, doesn’t apply to any item priced over $999.99, and never applies to shipping or tax. Because sale/outlet items are excluded, the code is best on new full-price releases — during a seasonal G-Shock sale, the sale price and the code are effectively either/or.

A separate channel exists for tactical and pro buyers: GovX (and Casio’s "Project Peacekeeper" pro-deal program) offers military and government pricing on the G-Shock line. It doesn’t stack with the ID.me code, so compare it model-by-model. And if you have base-exchange access, AAFES/NEX sells tax-free — which can beat a 10% civilian-priced order once tax is factored in.
youtube-tv-military-veteran: How the Base Plan discount works: verify once through ID.me on YouTube TV’s hosted offer page, then sign up for the Base Plan through the offer. You’re billed $67.99/mo for the first 12 months instead of ~$82.99 — $15/mo off, $180 over the year. It applies to the Base Plan and is not combinable with other coupons or new-subscriber intro promos, so it’s a substitute for those deals, not a stack.

The existing-subscriber path trips people up. If you already pay for YouTube TV, the rate isn’t applied to your live subscription automatically. The reliable route is to cancel your current plan’s auto-renewal, complete ID.me verification on the offer page, and then re-subscribe through the offer so the $67.99/mo rate attaches to your account. Skipping the cancel step is the most common reason the discount doesn’t show up.

The 12-month cliff is the most important fine print. The $67.99 rate is promotional and lasts your first 12 months; at month 12 it reverts to the standard ~$82.99/mo automatically. Treat the offer as a one-year saving and set a calendar reminder near month 11 to reassess — downgrade, pause, or compare alternatives — so you’re never surprised by the full-price renewal.

NFL Sunday Ticket is a separate decision. Its military offer is far deeper than the Base Plan discount in absolute dollars: $198 for the 2026 season (every out-of-market Sunday afternoon game), or $240 if you add the RedZone channel (+$42), available through Jan 10, 2027. It’s priced and redeemed on its own — not folded into the Base Plan rate — so only add it if you actually follow an out-of-market team.
dolly-parton-stampede-military-discount: The military rate is confirmed on the Stampede’s own FAQ, which directs guests to call for pricing. Two box-office numbers apply: Pigeon Forge (865) 453-4400 and Branson (417) 336-3000. You can also buy at the gate with a military ID. There is no online military checkout.

Eligibility skews to active-duty (active-duty ID is commonly required); veterans’ eligibility varies by location and show, so confirm when you call. The rate may not apply to every show or date. The commonly cited ~$10 adult / ~$4 child savings come from aggregators, not a published Stampede rate card, so treat them as a ballpark and verify by phone.

To pay the least, call the specific location with your ID ready, ask exactly what the military rate is for your show and date, and compare it against area military-appreciation promotions (e.g., Pigeon Forge/Branson "Celebrate Freedom" windows) — then book whichever is cheaper.
subway-military-discount: Because Subway restaurants are independently owned and operated, there is no company-wide military discount to point to. What you get depends entirely on the individual owner. Community and editorial reports put the typical franchise discount around 10% with a valid military ID, and it may be a little more generous at stores in military towns or on base — but it is never a promise. Confirm at the register before you order, and do not assume it carries between locations.

The genuinely best routine savings come from Subway’s app. Join MVP Rewards (free) to earn 10 points per $1, with 400 points redeemable for $2 in Subway Cash and a 250-point bonus for joining. On top of that, Subway pushes rotating public promo codes — buy-one-get-one or discounted-Footlong deals — that regularly beat a 10% counter discount and are available to everyone. Those app codes are typically one per order and exclude melts and premium subs, and a cashier-applied military discount and an app code usually cannot both apply to the same order, so take whichever total is cheaper. MVP points, however, still earn either way.

If you are on or visiting a military installation, use the Subway inside the AAFES/NEXCOM exchange food court. Exchange restaurants are sales-tax-free for authorized installation visitors, which quietly beats an off-base 10% in most states, and live app deals still apply where the operator participates.

On Veterans Day (Nov 11), many participating locations have historically given active-duty members and veterans a free 6-inch sub or 10% off, dine-in, with proof of service. This is a participating-location gesture, not a corporate program, so call ahead. And ignore the coupon-aggregator pages advertising a "50-70% off Subway military discount" or viral posts claiming "all locations are giving 25% to all veterans today" — those figures are fabricated or unverified.
uber-military-discount: Uber publishes only general new-rider offers and the paid Uber One membership — there is no military-specific pricing anywhere on its own surfaces. So the honest starting point is that a service member should not chase a "military code": you will only find expired or generic public codes, or fabricated ones. The most-repeated fake, a "$10 + 15% off Uber military discount, verify via SheerID," does not exist; Uber uses no SheerID rider fare checkout.

For most people the real standing saver is Uber One at $9.99/month or $96/year, with a 4-week free trial for eligible first-timers. It gives 6% back on rides in Uber One credits, automatic surge savings, and on Uber Eats a $0 delivery fee plus up to 10% off eligible orders — worth it if you ride or order often enough to cover the fee. New riders should take the public 30%-off-first-ride promo (up to $8) once.

There is a small ID.me involvement, but it is easily overstated. The ID.me Shop lists an Uber cash-back of up to $2.50 per rider trip — a rebate, not a fare discount — and it is available to every verified ID.me group, not just military. Separately, veteran drivers can display a military-affiliation badge after verifying through ID.me; that is a recognition feature for drivers, not a rider or driver discount.

The largest real dollar benefit for the military community is a VA program, not an Uber consumer discount. Under VHA-Uber Health Connect, beneficiary-travel-eligible veterans (for example a service-connected rating of 30% or more, travel for a service-connected condition, a VA pension, or income under the maximum annual pension rate) who are ambulatory and have a common-carrier beneficiary-travel consult can get free rides to and from VA medical appointments, arranged by VA staff through Uber Health. Ask your VA Beneficiary Travel point of contact — you cannot book it yourself as a promo.
cavenders-military-discount: Cavender’s (Cavender Stores L.P., Tyler, TX) is a near-constant discounter: a site-wide "new markdowns up to 50% off" banner and a dedicated clearance section run year-round across boots, clothing, hats, and work gear. For most shoppers that clearance is the deepest reliable saving — it beats the unverified "10% military" and needs no ID — with the important caveat that Cavender’s promotional-exclusion brands (Ariat, Lucchese, Old Gringo, Stetson, Resistol, Timberland PRO, Yeti, and others) never mark down through promotions.

The free My Cavender’s Rewards program layers on top for everyone: points on qualifying purchases, member-only offers, free shipping, early sale access, and receipt-free returns. Rewards are non-combinable with other discounts by default, so a member offer generally won’t stack on clearance — but it’s free to join and can shave a bit off full-price items. Cavender’s also posts occasional manufacturer mail-in rebates on qualifying boot brands, independent of its own promotions.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites that invent a Cavender’s "military discount." Specific false claims we found and corrected include "SOLIS10 = 30% off for military" (a scraped/influencer code, not a military offer), "up to 80% off military" (fabricated), and "10% off online with a military ID via ID.me/SheerID" (false — neither provider has a Cavender’s military offer, and there is no online military verification at checkout). The "Thank You Veterans" page is also frequently miscited as a discount when it is a Veterans Day charity donation.

If you want a specific national brand that Cavender’s carries — especially a work-boot maker — check whether that brand runs its own verified military discount (ID.me or GovX) and price it as a substitute; that can beat anything Cavender’s offers.
