goodr-military-discount: ExpertVoice is the only identity-verified route to a goodr discount, and usually the deepest. These are auto-applied with no code and no verification, so during a sale the public price beats every "military code" for everyone. goodr’s terms are explicit that a promo "cannot be combined with any other promotions or codes," so a scraped newsletter code and the live auto-sale are mutually exclusive.

Between goodr’s sales, the standout verified-military route is Scheels, which stocks goodr and gives verified military members a 5% everyday discount storewide. You verify once via ID.me inside your MySCHEELS account, and the 5% applies to goodr items online and in-store. Be cautious of coupon sites advertising a specific "goodr military discount" percentage. goodr publishes no brand-run military rate, so those figures — and the codes floating on aggregators — are unverified generic sitewide codes, not military offers. We route eligible readers to ExpertVoice and Scheels instead, the two routes that actually verify military status.
vessel-golf-military-discount: Vessel’s discount is powered by ID.me, the same free identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. Verify once and your eligibility links to your ID.me account, so future Vessel purchases — and discounts at other ID.me partners — go faster. At Vessel checkout the "Verify with ID.me" link sits right under the Order Summary.

If ID.me doesn’t auto-verify you, Vessel’s help center accepts a DD-214, a veteran designation on your driver’s license or state ID, a .mil email, or active-duty orders/LES — or third-party verification via ID.me/SheerID — and then emails you a unique one-time discount code. That code is single-use, good for one order.

Because the 20% can’t be stacked, the only time another path wins is when a specific bag is already marked down deeper than 20% in a public sale; compare the sale price against the military price and take whichever is lower.
kings-dominion-military-discount: The year-round online discount is gated by ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. After you select your ticket or pass on the Kings Dominion military discounts page, an ID.me login prompt confirms your military, veteran, or first-responder status before checkout. Verifying once links your eligibility to your ID.me account and is reused across other ID.me partners.

For most single visitors, the smartest move is a quick price comparison rather than an automatic assumption that the military rate is cheapest. Because the discount explicitly cannot be stacked on a sale, you pick either the military ticket or a public sale ticket — whichever is lower that day. When a public flash sale drops below $40 (as it did at $35 through July 31, 2026), the public ticket wins and needs no verification. Sale windows and prices are volatile and seasonal, so re-check the current public price before deciding.

For repeat visitors, the real value is concentrated in the 2026 Military Gold Pass at $89 plus fees. It covers unlimited 2026 visits, free parking, and Halloween Haunt, and it undercuts the regular Gold Pass (around $105). It generally pays off after roughly two visits and is the best overall path for anyone planning more than a single trip.

GovX is an alternative marketplace channel that sells Kings Dominion military and government tickets using its own verification if you prefer it over ID.me.
state-and-liberty-military-discount: State & Liberty verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA and many major retailers. You verify your military status once with ID.me; on future orders you sign in again to reapply the discount. Re-verification frequency is set by ID.me, not the brand — don’t assume verification is permanent. For problems, contact State & Liberty at support@stateandliberty.com or 734-757-3534, or ID.me help for verification issues.

Two things sweeten the deal. Free shipping applies on orders of $150 or more — easy to hit at these price points. And for every $500 spent using a military ID code through ID.me, State & Liberty donates a dress shirt to the SEAL Future Foundation. The only legitimate stack is payment-side: a flat cash-back credit card earns its usual ~2% on top of the discounted total.

One thing to watch: coupon aggregators advertise "25%, 40%, even 45% off State & Liberty" codes and claim students get 15%. None of that is supported by a primary source. The brand’s own FAQ says it does not run sales; its only public codes are the bulk dress-shirt codes STATEANDLIB3 (3 shirts) and STATEANDLIB5 (5+ shirts), whose percentage isn’t published. ID.me — the authoritative source — lists Military 15%, First Responders 10%, Students 10%.
ups-military-discount: Be careful of a common mix-up: "The UPS Store" (theupsstore.com — the independently owned retail print, ship, and notary franchise) is a different business from UPS the shipping carrier (ups.com). The keyword "ups military discount" is searched by people meaning either one, and nearly every aggregator conflates the two. This guide covers The UPS Store and clears up the carrier confusion.

The UPS Store’s own membership-discount page lists only AAA and AARP — there is no military program to verify. That means there is no military verification at The UPS Store: no ID.me and no SheerID. Do not trust any site telling you to "verify with ID.me for 50% off The UPS Store"; that offer does not exist. Coupon and aggregator pages repeat "$75 off," "50% off via ID.me," "up to 40% military," or "10–25% military discount" — none are supported by a primary source. The "40%" figure is lifted from UPS the carrier’s expired air-shipping code, and the "$15,000 / 50% off" figure is a franchise-purchase incentive for veterans who want to buy a store, not a shopper discount.

Separately, UPS the carrier historically ran a "VETERAN" promo code (20% off Ground, 40% off Air) on ups.com, but its published terms expired December 31, 2021 and the code no longer appears on ups.com. Independent checks through late 2025 found no active veteran shipping discount, so treat that offer as historical and discontinued — and note it never applied at The UPS Store retail counters anyway.

Even without a military discount, there are honest ways to lower what you pay. For printing, use the public 20% coupon or AAA’s up-to-30% on-demand print rate. For shipping, compare — The UPS Store adds a retail markup over ups.com rates, so ship directly on ups.com, or use USPS for APO/FPO (reduced military rates plus a free Military Care Kit). If you already hold AAA or AARP, always show the card, and it is worth a polite ask at your local, independently owned store for an owner-discretion courtesy discount.
penske-truck-rental-military-veteran: Penske’s military discount is a straightforward rate cut: reserve a truck online, apply promo code MILITARY for 15% off, and show a valid military or veteran ID at pickup. The percentage comes off the time-and-mileage base rate, not the taxes, fees, or optional coverage, and it cannot be combined with other promotions — so compare it against any standard online deal Penske is running before you lock it in.

The WeSalute+ route is the alternative for members: book online using your WeSalute+ ID and bring the WeSalute+ card to pickup. It carries the same 15% but is strictly an online booking — Penske will not apply it by phone, chat, or at a location. With either path the in-person ID check at pickup is what finalizes the discount, so don’t leave home without it.

For a military move specifically, the dedicated call center (1-844-4TROOPS) is the differentiator. A personally procured move (PPM/DITY) is reimbursable by the Department of Defense when you keep your paperwork, so the rental discount stacks with a reimbursement you claim through your transportation office. Shoppers weighing options should cross-quote Budget Truck (20% with code USMIO for those traveling on orders) and U-Haul (no rate discount, but a free month of storage) to see which is cheapest for the specific move.
coach-outlet-military-discount: The "no" is well documented. ID.me’s Coach Outlet military page states it is not aware of any military discount, and its store page shows only affiliate cash-back offers — no verified checkout percentage for any community, military or otherwise. Coach’s own promotions page lists sitewide sales, Coach Insider, and text sign-up perks, with no military offer anywhere. Aggregator claims of "10–25% off" or a "50% military code" have no Coach source behind them.

The storefront itself changed: as of July 7, 2026, www.coachoutlet.com 301-redirects to www.coach.com/shop/outlet. Nothing was lost — the Outlet assortment, with its built-in markdowns (32–52% off comparable value on items we checked, clearance to 60%), now lives as a section of coach.com. Rakuten still runs a dedicated Coach Outlet store page paying 2% cash back, so start tracked clicks there.

The genuinely military-only angle is the Exchange. Coach handbags at shopmyexchange.com sell at Exchange special-value prices with zero sales tax — a corroborated example priced a bag at $149 against a $295 comparable value. Authorized patrons include active duty, retirees, Guard/Reserve, dependents, and all honorably discharged veterans online via the Veterans Online Shopping Benefit. On a $199 outlet bag with ~7% tax, the Exchange path saved about $64 in our comparison.

In stores, the only military-ID discounts ever reported are mall-run events — outlet malls like Tanger have advertised "extra 10% off with military ID today" at Coach Outlet locations. Those are mall promotions, sporadic and store-specific, not a Coach policy, so call ahead rather than counting on one.
disney-world-military-discount: Disney does not use a third-party verification service (no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute) for this promotion. Verification is in person via a valid and active U.S. Military ID, checked at the point of purchase, again when the ticket is first activated at a park ticket window (which the Eligible Service Member or spouse must do), and at hotel check-in for the room offer. There is no online account flow.

Salute tickets are flat promotional prices rather than a percentage. Buying at a base ticket office or Shades of Green avoids sales tax (tickets bought at park windows add tax), and actual base prices may be lower than Disney’s published prices. You can also add a specially-priced Memory Maker (Disney PhotoPass) for $98, max 2 per eligible member or spouse, purchasable only at park ticket windows.

The room offer runs 15%–30% off depending on resort tier and season and can be combined only with the 2026 Kids Dining Plan Offer. Because these offers renew annually with new dates and pricing, re-check Disney’s official pages before you book — and note that Walt Disney World (Florida) is distinct from Disneyland (California), which runs its own military offers.
kids-foot-locker-military-discount: Kids Foot Locker uses SheerID, a third-party verification service — not ID.me. You submit your name, branch, and current military status; SheerID confirms eligibility (often within minutes, up to about 20 minutes if documents are reviewed). You’re limited to four verifications on a rolling 30-day basis, each capped at $100 in discount.

The 10% military discount cannot be combined with other offers or promo codes and does not apply to prior purchases — you choose the military discount or a coupon code, not both. When an item is on a deep sale or clearance, the sale price often beats 10% off retail, so compare the two before checking out.

A separate 15% rate runs through Veterans Advantage (now WeSalute), a paid membership program. It also cannot be combined with other offers and excludes gift cards, team orders, and open or prior orders — so it only wins outright for heavy repeat Foot Locker-family shoppers who already hold the membership.
disney-plus-hulu-bundle-military-discoun: The Disney Bundle carries a built-in discount (~45–47% off standalone pricing), which is why stacking the two individual military discounts usually cannot beat it. The standard Duo bundle (both With Ads) is about $12.99/mo and the Duo Premium bundle (both No Ads) is about $19.99/mo, as of July 13, 2026 — and no military discount applies to either. The individual military route only pulls ahead in the narrow ad-free-Disney+/OK-with-Hulu-ads case.

Both military offers are gated entirely by The Exchange (AAFES). You need a valid, current ShopMyExchange.com account as an authorized Exchange shopper. Neither offer uses ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute — a recurring "40% off / $5.99 Hulu via SheerID" claim is unverified and conflates Hulu with other services; the only primary-sourced Hulu military figure is 25% off Hulu (With Ads) via The Exchange.

Watch the myths. Several aggregators and AI summaries claim you get a military discount "on the bundle," or that "the 25% Disney+ discount carries into the bundle on the Disney+ portion." Neither is true. Both official offers state the discount cannot be combined with the Disney Bundle — the moment you are on a bundle SKU, no military pricing applies to any part of it.

One practical note reported by shoppers: once you are on the standard bundle you cannot retroactively apply either military discount — you would have to cancel and re-subscribe to the individual services through The Exchange. And the Disney+ Exchange offer is limited to new or eligible-returning subscribers, so long-time Disney+ holders may be ineligible without cancelling first. Confirm the exact mechanics on ShopMyExchange.com.
madewell-military-discount: Madewell’s discount is powered by SheerID, an identity-verification service tied to your free Madewell Insider account. You verify once, may be asked to upload documentation of your status, and approval lasts one calendar year — after which you re-verify. This is not a permanent enrollment; treat it as an annual renewal.

A common myth is that Madewell runs an ID.me military discount. It does not. Madewell’s own Community Heroes page and its checkout use SheerID, and ID.me’s store page explicitly states it is not aware that Madewell offers a military discount. There is also no GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass route — SheerID is the path.

The military tier sits alongside parallel Community Heroes segments for first responders and medical professionals, all at the same 15%. Teachers and college students get their own separate 15% tier verified by school ID through SheerID. These are one-per-person identity discounts — the same 15%, not additive.

Because the 15% is non-combinable, the smart move depends on your cart. Buying full-price jeans with old denim to recycle? The $20 Do Well trade-in edges 15% (on a $128 pair: $108.00 vs $108.80). Buying anything else full-price? Use the 15%. And if a deep public sale (often 25–40% off) is live, that markdown can beat 15% on its own.
bmw-military-discount: This is a per-model dollar incentive, not a fixed percentage or a self-serve coupon. BMW publishes the $500–$5,000 range, and the example amounts shown on its program page as of June 23, 2026 included the 3 Series up to $2,500, the X5 up to $4,000, the i4 up to $3,000, and the iX up to $5,000. BMW does not publish a complete per-model table and the figures change over time, so treat those examples as a snapshot and confirm your model’s current amount with a BMW Center.

Verification runs through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many retailers. You verify the segment that matches your status, then the lead form generates a Customer ID and offer code emailed to you. The dealer step is where the incentive is actually applied — there is no in-person-only path, and BMW does not state how often ID.me re-verification is required, so don’t assume it’s permanent.

Two things to know on stacking and alternatives. The incentive combines with most BMW offers and campaigns but not the Corporate Sales Program. Separately, USAA members may have their own BMW vehicle savings offer (reported up to $2,000), but that is documented on BMW dealer pages rather than the core program page — confirm its current amount, eligibility, and whether it stacks with USAA and a BMW Center before relying on it.
vrbo-military-discount: Coupon and aggregator pages fabricate a Vrbo military program — WorthEPenny advertises "up to 25% off Vrbo military" and CouponCabin shows rotating "10% / 19% off" banners — but there is no verified Vrbo platform military code or percentage. The genuine "10% Discount for Military" phrases that appear on some vrbo.com listings are individual host offers written into their own listing titles, not a Vrbo-wide program.

Because pricing is host-controlled, the reliable levers are structural. Host weekly and monthly length-of-stay discounts (often 10-25% for a week, and Vrbo recommends around 45% for a month) apply automatically to longer stays, and dynamic off-season pricing can run 20-40% below peak. Both are open to everyone and frequently beat any bare military ask — so the smartest move is usually to book a full week off-peak and then also message the host for a military rate.

ID.me does list Vrbo, but only for cashback paid to your ID.me wallet — a third-party rebate, not a discount Vrbo applies. It is roughly 5.75% back with a $50 cap as of July 12, 2026 (confirm the live rate, since portal rates move). Vrbo’s own One Key program layers separately: Silver earns 1% and Gold/Platinum 2% OneKeyCash on eligible bookings, redeemable 1:1 at checkout on eligible Pay Now rentals.
safeway-military-discount: What officially exists is Safeway’s community & profession discount program. On safeway.com/grocery-discounts, Safeway invites eligible groups to verify their status — through SheerID, inside a free Safeway for U account — to "Get exclusive, limited time offers," "Earn Points and redeem rewards," and "Clip deals to save more." The FAQ lists military and veterans among the verifiable groups: anyone currently serving or who "at one time" worked for the U.S. Armed Services qualifies. What Safeway never states is an amount. There is no percentage anywhere on the page, which is why this guide won’t quote one.

The "10% Safeway military discount" you’ll find on aggregator sites traces to two real but limited programs. Safeway’s Denver division (Colorado, Nebraska, New Mexico, Wyoming, South Dakota) ran 10% off groceries for active-duty, reserve, and retired military with ID on the first Saturday of each month from 2020 to 2023 — taken "at the end of the bill, after all savings," with the usual exclusions (prescriptions, alcohol, tobacco, gift cards, lottery, fuel). The Denver-area deal tracker that documented it now files it under "Expired." Separately, some regions and stores have run one-day ~10% military discounts around Veterans Day in past years; shoppers report participation varied store to store, and no chain-wide 2025 offer was verified. Treat every in-store percentage claim as historical and YMMV — call your local store.

All the math on this page uses one baseline: a $150 weekly grocery run at a Safeway store. The free Safeway for U program is the real everyday engine — member prices, personalized clipped deals, and Points typically take $10–$20 off that cart, varying by basket. SheerID military verification adds unpublished member offers on top; it costs nothing, so unlock it, but treat it as a bonus rather than a percentage. For eligible readers, the commissary is the genuine military grocery discount: DeCA sells at cost plus a 5% surcharge, with claimed average savings around 25% including the surcharge — roughly $110–$125 for a comparable basket, and manufacturer coupons are accepted there. Since 2020, in-store commissary access extends beyond active duty, retirees, and Guard/Reserve families to veterans with service-connected disabilities, Purple Heart recipients, former POWs, and registered VA caregivers.

Stacking rules, for what they’re worth: the historical 10% stacked on top of everything — per the Denver-division terms it came after all savings, including sale prices and coupons — so if a regional or Veterans Day percentage ever reappears, expect the same mechanic but confirm in-store. SheerID status offers live inside Safeway for U and combine with member prices the way any clipped deal does. There is no promo-code layer: Safeway promo codes are online delivery/pickup offers (often first-order only), not identity discounts. And the commissary is a substitute channel — no Safeway coupons or loyalty apply there.
harley-davidson-military-discount: Harley-Davidson routes its military offer through ID.me, the same free identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. You verify your military or first-responder status once, receive an H-D Hero offer code, and bring it to a participating dealership. ID.me is the sole named verification partner — there is no confirmed GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute route for the corporate offer.

The key detail is the "+": the military $500 "Customer Cash+" is built to stack on top of public H-D Customer/Hero Cash offers, so during a live public promo the combined take can be much larger. Harley-Davidson has run up to $1,500 "Hero Cash" on select touring models during past summer events (historical, not current). The $500 cash and the $250 P&A credit remain either/or, and the $100 Riding Academy discount is a separate offer.

Because Harley-Davidson controls the amount, the eligible model list, and the offer window (the current motorcycle-cash window runs through August 31, 2026), treat the numbers here as a starting point and confirm the current terms on Harley-Davidson’s official military page before you buy.
doona-military-discount: There is no verification path because there is no program: Doona’s own US support and promotions page lists free shipping over $75, Klarna, and collection promos — but no military or hero discount, and no ID.me/GovX/SheerID flow. Any "Doona military discount" you see advertised is not supported by Doona’s site.

Coupon aggregators advertising a "35OFF" 35% code or "first responder 30–40% off" (WorthEPenny, valuecom, Knoji) are not verifiable on Doona’s site, and parents repeatedly report those codes not working — consistent with there being no such program. Any hero discount on Doona products comes from a third-party retailer (like Albee Baby’s Heroes program), applied to that retailer’s stock, not from Doona — and because Doona is MAP-priced, retailer Heroes programs frequently exclude it.

The reliable way to save is timing an authorized-retailer sale event. Retailers run Doona sale events (historically around $100 off) and Black Friday/Cyber Monday deals; a baby registry can add completion discounts on remaining items; and if you have Exchange access and Doona is stocked, tax-free pricing can be the best net cost. Because Doona rarely discounts, waiting for a sanctioned sale is usually the difference-maker.
dtlr-military-discount: Coupon and aggregator pages titled "DTLR military discount — 40% / 70% off" are recycling public promo codes (like the "PANTS" 40% code) and clearance depth, not any military program. DTLR has no military discount — ID.me, the natural host for one, confirms it does not exist. A single third-party blurb about "10% off at a DTLR in Orange Park, Florida with valid ID" is an unverified single-store claim, not a chain policy, and should never be presented as DTLR’s discount.

The honest maximum-savings play is a substitute retailer. On a representative $120 sneaker order, Finish Line’s 20% in-store military discount brings it to about $96, and Foot Locker or Nike’s 10% via SheerID brings it to about $108 — real, verifiable military discounts DTLR does not match. You buy from that retailer instead of DTLR; nothing stacks across stores.

If the shoe is DTLR-exclusive or already marked down, DTLR’s own public sale and clearance prices (up to ~50% off Nike and ~70% clearance) usually beat a 10-20% military discount outright, with no verification. On a plain, no-code order you can also layer free Trendsetter points (1 point per $1) and ID.me Shop’s ~1.5% cashback — but note that cashback is a rebate open to all shoppers, not a military benefit, and it commonly voids when you enter a promo code.
tampa-zoo-military-discount: Verification is simple: ZooTampa checks a valid military ID at the front-gate ticket windows. It does not use ID.me, GovX, or SheerID, and there’s no online verification portal — bring a current DoD/military ID, and bring your dependents with you for the summer offer. Don’t let a coupon site sell you a paid "discount code" when active-duty entry is free this summer.

The year-round discount deserves a caveat: the $4-off-per-ticket figure (up to four tickets, for active duty, retirees, and veterans) is reported by Military.com, not itemized on a ZooTampa terms page, so verify the current amount at the window before paying. For reference, gate rack general admission is $51.95 for adults (12+) and $41.95 for children (3–11), and buying online saves $5 per guest for everyone.

Stacking is straightforward because the offers replace paid admission rather than combining: the summer free-admission offer is the discount, the $5-online savings applies to online purchases (not to a gate military discount), and memberships are a separate purchase. For a family of four at gate rack ($187.80), the summer active-duty offer takes that to $0; the reported military gate discount saves about $16; buying online saves $20. Repeat visitors can also weigh a membership (tiers from roughly $134–$294/year with unlimited admission through the end of 2026 plus free parking), which pays off in about two visits.
safelite-military-discount: You apply the code yourself at booking, and Safelite verifies your eligibility at the time of your appointment. Safelite does not name a verification provider and does not list which documents it accepts — and it does not use ID.me, GovX, or SheerID for this discount (ID.me’s own page states it is not aware Safelite offers a military discount and lists only cash back). So bring whatever proof of status you have to your appointment, and contact Safelite directly if you’re unsure what qualifies.

The most important limits are the exclusions. The 10% is valid on any product or service except recalibration, and it can’t be applied to insurance claims or deductibles. Since most windshield work is covered by auto insurance — and Safelite files the claim for you — the discount really only helps when you’re paying out of pocket. It also won’t stack with Safelite’s public coupons ($45 off replacement, $15 off repair), so if one of those saves more than 10% on your job, use that instead — but you can’t use both.

A note on eligibility and codes: Safelite says only "members of the military" without breaking out active duty, veterans, retirees, or Guard/Reserve, and it doesn’t address spouses or dependents — so confirm your specific status with Safelite. And be skeptical of coupon-site codes like "MIL70," "MIL25," or "75% off" — none of those appear on any Safelite official page; the real, confirmed code is 10THANKYOU10 for 10%.
siriusxm-military-discount: The military discount is a durable floor, not the absolute cheapest price. Because it is 25% off the then-current rate rather than a locked dollar amount, if SiriusXM raises its standard rates (it did on February 24, 2026) your 25%-off price rises with them. The discount is durable; the base price is not.

SiriusXM verifies eligibility through SheerID, the partner that hosts SiriusXM’s "Exclusive Military Offer" and runs the student check. You confirm your military status once — SiriusXM’s page notes it is "subject to review of any required documentation." There is no confirmed ID.me route for the military tier despite aggregator claims; the named partner is SheerID, and a GovX SiriusXM storefront exists as an alternate door to the same class of offer.

Debunk the aggregator noise: there is no verified "75% off" or "$1-for-life" military code. The "75%" figures are conflations of the student $4/mo streaming deal or of ordinary new-subscriber and retention promos — not a military offer. A separate Student Streaming Platinum plan ($1 for 3 months, then $4/mo via SheerID, for enrolled 18+ students) is confirmed, but a standalone first-responder or nurse rate is not confirmed on SiriusXM’s official offers hub this pass, and the teacher discount is reported discontinued.
travis-mathew-military-discount: TravisMathew is a golf and lifestyle apparel brand under Topgolf Callaway Brands. Unlike some sibling brands, it runs no verified military discount on its own website: there is no ID.me or SheerID option at checkout, and the brand explicitly states it does not issue discount coupons or codes. The only exception is a single one-time 20% code you receive for signing up for the newsletter, applied to your first online order.

The one military-specific channel is GovX, an identity-verification marketplace that gives the military and first-responder communities access to member pricing from many brands. You create a free account, verify your status once with GovX ID, then shop the TravisMathew storefront on GovX. Because it is a closed marketplace, TravisMathew does not publish that member percentage publicly — you see the price only after you verify, and you cannot add a travismathew.com code on top of a GovX order.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites that advertise a specific TravisMathew "military discount" of 10% to 25%. TravisMathew publishes no brand-run military rate, and the GovX marketplace does not post a public fixed percentage, so those figures are unverified aggregator estimates rather than real terms. It is also easy to confuse this with Callaway Golf’s program: Callaway runs a separate ~15% ID.me military discount, but that does not extend to travismathew.com.

Even without a brand-run military discount, there are honest ways to save on TravisMathew: use the one-time 20% first-order newsletter code, join the free TM Rewards program for free shipping and returns, shop the Sale and outlet collections where public markdowns often beat GovX member pricing, and — for verified military — compare the GovX marketplace price against any live sale before paying full price.
midas-military-discount: There is no third-party verification provider for a Midas military discount — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass, and no GovX storefront for Midas. Where a shop offers the discount, verification is showing a valid military or veteran ID at the counter. Because it’s franchise-run, both the amount and who qualifies (veterans only? spouses? Guard and Reserve?) are decided shop by shop and are not guaranteed anywhere.

The seasonal promos are the only Midas-corporate military offers on record: 15% off tire and auto-repair services from Nov 1-30, 2024 for Active Duty, Retirees, and Veterans, and 10% off during May’s Military Appreciation Month — both only at participating shops, meaning individual franchises can opt out. Treat both as historical: confirm with your shop each May and November rather than assuming a repeat.

For the math on a representative $500 brake-pad-and-rotor job: a discretionary 10% military discount saves ~$50, and the historical 15% Veterans Day promo would save ~$75 — but a public Midas brake special can cut more than either, which is why checking midas.com/coupons.aspx for your location first is the honest default. If a big repair is looming, it’s also worth cross-shopping chains with clearer programs — Firestone Complete Auto Care, for example, has historically offered a year-round in-store military discount — and getting quotes from more than one shop.
gm-military-discount: GM validates eligibility through ID.me. You create or log in to an ID.me account at gmmilitaryappreciation.com and confirm your military status; once validated, you can request an Authorization Number (the "Go Code"). It is the Authorization Number — not your ID.me login itself — that the dealer needs, and it expires 90 days after issuance. You may request up to two per year. GM also conducts periodic audits and may request documentation (military ID, a marriage license for a sponsored spouse, title or registration) to confirm eligibility, so keep your supporting records.

At the dealer, the program works as a price, not a coupon: bring your Authorization Number before delivery and present a copy of your driver’s license showing the ZIP Code and Date of Birth used to obtain the number, which must match. The dealer then applies the program price below MSRP to your eligible new vehicle. Because participation is voluntary, not every GM dealer honors the program — call ahead. If you buy with cash or a loan, plan to keep the vehicle at least six months, and note it must be for personal, non-commercial use.

One thing to watch: many coupon, dealer, and aggregator pages assert specifics that GM’s own sources do not publish — a flat "$500 additional" allowance, stacking with Customer Cash and Loyalty Cash, SiriusXM/OnStar perks, or guaranteed Corvette eligibility. GM’s Rules and the GM Financial Vehicle Purchase Program page publish no dollar figure, list no combinable incentives, and guarantee no specific model; they say only that the offer is "not available with some other offers" and that the eligible-vehicle list "may change at any time." Treat those specific claims as unverified and confirm the real, model-specific number with a participating dealer.
sherwin-williams-military-discount: Verification is intentionally simple: there is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID step, no account to create, and no promo code. You just show a valid military ID at a Sherwin-Williams retail paint store, and the associate applies 15% off list price on eligible items. That simplicity is also the limit — the discount is confirmed only for in-store, personal retail purchases; there is no verified online redemption path.

The 15% is Sherwin-Williams’ standing military rate, separate from the everyday PaintPerks Preferred Customer discount, which is 10% and open to any shopper who joins that program (not a military-specific benefit). Some listings conflate the two or understate the military rate as 10% — the official military rate is 15%, not 10%.

Each May, Sherwin-Williams has a recurring history of adding an extra 10% off paints & stains for Military Appreciation Month, on top of the everyday 15%. This is documented as a historical, recurring pattern rather than a guaranteed annual term, so it is worth confirming the exact dates and scope directly with your local store as May approaches.

The discount is not combinable with other coupons, percent-off promotions, or special-price programs — but Sherwin-Williams’ terms guarantee you the better of the two: "sale pricing or other offers that result in greater savings will supersede this offer." In practice, compare any live public sale to the 15% (or 15%+10% in May) and take whichever is deeper.
coursera-military-discount: Coursera’s official discounts and offers page lists financial aid and public promotions (such as 20% off Coursera Plus Annual and 40% off three months of monthly Plus) — and names no military or veteran rate. The military benefit does not live on coursera.org at all; it lives with Coursera’s nonprofit partners, which is why service members repeatedly ask on Coursera’s community forums where the "free military courses" are and cannot find a login toggle for them.

The single best path for almost every eligible service member is not a discount — it is free access through a partner. Veterans Transition Support (VTS) advertises 12 months of no-cost, full-catalog access (certificates and specializations) for veterans, active duty, reservists, National Guard, and military spouses, with year-round enrollment. The USO Pathfinder Transition Program provides a Coursera license to pick one entry-level Professional Certificate, and Hire Heroes USA arranges Coursera access alongside 1:1 transition coaching. ACT Now Education runs an application-based free-Coursera portal. A free 12-month catalog or a free certificate beats any percentage discount, so a partner program is the first thing to check.

Be cautious of coupon and affiliate blogs that headline a "Coursera Military Discount — 40% OFF." That is false framing: the 40% is a public promo (40% off three months of monthly Coursera Plus, open to everyone) that these sites relabel as "military." Coursera publishes no military percentage and no military promo code — several of those same pages even admit in their body text that Coursera does not offer a military discount directly. The real, verifiable military benefit is free access through the nonprofit partners, which is worth far more than 40% off.

If you do not qualify for a partner program, anyone can use Coursera’s own routes: apply for financial aid on a specific certificate page (free certificate access to that course if approved, verified per course rather than by military status), or audit most courses free for the lectures and readings without the certificate. And if you simply want the whole catalog and must pay, the best available price is Coursera Plus Annual during a public 20%–40% promo (Black Friday is historically the deepest) — there is no better "military" price than the public one. The baseline used throughout this guide is 12 months of Coursera access plus one Google Professional Certificate, benchmarked against Coursera Plus Annual’s $399 list price.
aimpoint-military-discount: Aimpoint’s program — also branded the "Government Purchase Program" — is a gated store, not a stackable code. You create an account, select your eligibility category, and upload one supporting document; a human reviews it (stated turnaround: by the next business day) before your discounted catalog unlocks. Aimpoint uses its own in-house verification, not a third-party service like ID.me or SheerID.

Eligibility is broad: active, civilian, and retired law enforcement; federal agency agents, civilians, and retirees; active-duty, reserve, National Guard, and veteran military; fire and EMS; and private security and security contractors. The current program page caps purchases at 5 optics per calendar year (up from 2 at the May 2025 launch of the individual-officer version) and states that program optics are not for resale.

Be cautious of coupon and aggregator sites that advertise a specific Aimpoint "10%–25% military discount" or a percentage-off code. Aimpoint publishes no such figure — the value is only visible after your credentials are approved — so any specific percentage you see on a coupon site is unverified. We deliberately omit it here.

Separately, GovX operates an Aimpoint storefront (govx.com/m/809/aimpoint) with member pricing that is also hidden until you register for a free GovX ID. Treat GovX as a substitute channel, not a stack — you cannot add a brand code or a cashback portal on top of its pricing. The Veterans Canteen Service (VCS) PatriotStores also carry Aimpoint tax-free for eligible VA patrons, which matters on a roughly $986 optic where sales tax is real money.
camping-world-military-discount: The Hero Program is Camping World’s military-specific RV lever. Its discount is a fixed dollar amount off the advertised price of a new RV, tiered by RV type — Class A Diesel $2,000, Class A Gas $1,500, Camper Van $1,000, Class C and Fifth Wheel $750 each, and Travel Trailer, Pop-Up, Truck Camper, and Small Trailer between $300 and $500. Because it is a dollar figure rather than a percentage, RV buyers should negotiate the advertised price first and then apply the Hero certificate on top.

For everyday retail, the 5% military discount applies to select items year-round at Camping World locations, for active duty, retirees, veterans, and Reserve/National Guard. But the bigger retail lever is a Good Sam membership: ~$30–$39/year for 10% off most retail. Camping World’s own RVers guide says Good Sam savings stack on top of the military discount, so an in-store service member who joins Good Sam lands around 15% off — beating the 5% alone and paying for the membership on roughly $300–$400 of purchases. (This stacking is stated on the brand blog, not the terms page, so confirm the exact combined rate at the register.)

Verification is per-purchase and in person: request a Hero Discount Certificate online, then present it with one accepted physical ID document at the register each time you buy. There is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID account and no saved digital status. Coupon sites overstate this offer — "75% off" and "up to $100 off" claims are ordinary seasonal coupons, not a military benefit, and there is no verified military promo code.

For online gear orders, the reliable route is different: layer a Good Sam membership with the best cashback portal that day (Rakuten was 3% as of July 13, 2026; some portals ran up to ~6%). Cashback portals track campingworld.com orders and cannot be earned on an in-store purchase, so they are the online counterpart to the in-store ID discount.
black-diamond-military-discount: Black Diamond uses SheerID (not ID.me) for the Community Professional tier — ID.me’s own page confirms Black Diamond does not use ID.me for military verification. You verify your military, first-responder, teacher, or student status through SheerID; if instant checks fail, you upload documentation. Approval can be instant or take up to 5–10 business days, and Pro accounts auto-subscribe you to BD email marketing.

The Pro discount does not stack. Pro pricing can’t be combined with public promo codes, Pro members don’t qualify for BD Rewards, and GovX is a closed marketplace where you can’t add a BD code or a cashback portal on top. Cashback portals such as Rakuten (~3% on a May 2026 listing) generally void on coupon or identity-verified checkouts, so treat cashback as usable only on a plain, no-code BD.com order.

Ignore the flat "10%/15%/20%/25% Black Diamond military discount" figures on coupon aggregators — none of that is on Black Diamond’s site, and the old /content/military-discount/ URL now soft-404s to the homepage. The only first-party military value is Pro-Deal pricing, whose exact depth Black Diamond does not disclose. For a single purchase, GovX and Full Send Deals frequently beat the hassle of Pro enrollment.
rhoback-military-discount: Rhoback uses ID.me, a third-party identity-verification provider, for its military, veteran, and first-responder discount. You sign in or create a free ID.me account and verify your status through their system at checkout — there’s no need to send Rhoback photos or scans of a government ID. ID.me periodically requires re-verification per its own policies; Rhoback’s page does not state a re-verification cadence.

Ignore the coupon aggregators advertising “30% off” or “35% off” Rhoback codes — those are generic, seasonal, or unverified sitewide claims, not the military benefit. The verified military/first-responder discount is 15%, applied through ID.me at checkout; there is no special “military promo code.” If you see one live in your cart, treat it as unverified until it actually applies.

Rhoback’s offer page is silent on stacking, so the safe assumption is that the 15% does not combine with sales or other promo codes — ID.me checkout discounts typically occupy the single discount-code slot. Separately, GovX lists a handful of co-branded Rhoback collab items (e.g., Rhoback x Barstool Golf) for verified members, but that’s a different channel from the direct 15% and not the full Rhoback catalog.
carowinds-military-discount: Carowinds uses ID.me. You pick your tickets first; the ID.me login prompt appears after product selection. If you already have an ID.me account, verification is just a login; if not, you create one free and verify your military or first-responder status once. The brand doesn’t publish a re-verification interval — expect an ID.me login on each purchase.

The honest math for two adults on a summer Saturday: the ID.me military tickets run about $74 total versus $78 for public advance tickets and $160 at the gate. The everyday military edge over buying early online is roughly $2 a person — the program’s real value is the up-to-6-ticket mechanic, the $105 Military Gold Pass, and the free Military Days window.

The Military Gold Pass is the quiet winner for repeat visitors: $105 versus $110 for the public Gold Pass online ($160 gate), with unlimited season visits at Carowinds and every East Coast Six Flags park, free parking, and 10% off food and merchandise. It pays for itself versus ~$37–39 tickets in about three visits.

Watch out for aggregator spin: "10–25% off Carowinds military discount" claims are fabricated — Carowinds publishes no percentage, only fixed date-based prices. Local editorial coverage says the park has historically added military windows near July 4 and Veterans Day, but Carowinds has published nothing beyond the May 22–25, 2026 Military Days — don’t plan around unconfirmed dates. There is also no cashback path: Rakuten lists Six Flags as "No Cash Back" (as of July 7, 2026).
journeys-military-discount: Verification is handled by ID.me, a third-party identity-verification service. In-store, an associate helps you scan a QR code that launches the ID.me flow; you can also verify through ID.me directly. ID.me confirms military status using a .mil email or by uploading qualifying documentation. Each successful verification can produce up to 3 codes per month; each code is one-time use and expires 7 days after creation.

Because codes are generated through ID.me, Journeys cannot send a replacement or fix a broken code — code issues go to help.id.me. The Journeys page does not state how often you must re-verify beyond the per-code and monthly mechanics.

Journeys’ help page nudges members toward the in-store flow for "the smoothest experience," but explicitly confirms the code can be used online at checkout. If a code doesn’t apply, confirm it hasn’t expired (7-day window) or already been used (one-time use), then contact help.id.me. Journeys also runs a separate student discount through Student Beans and UNiDAYS — that is not the ID.me military offer.
helix-military-discount: Helix verifies eligibility through VerifyPass. You create or sign into a free VerifyPass account, confirm your status once, and receive a one-time code to paste at checkout. Verification is per-code and one-time rather than a permanent account discount, and each code is limited to one per order and one per day. Support runs through Helix customer service and VerifyPass help resources.

The mechanic that defines this offer is that the specialty code is engineered to beat, not add to, the public sale. Helix states the discount "fluctuates" so it always offers at least as much savings as any promotion running at the time — which is exactly why it is an either/or with the public sale rather than a stack. When a public Helix sale ties the specialty percentage and throws in free Dream Pillows the code does not, the public offer is the better deal on the same price.

Ignore stale and third-party figures. Some aggregators still quote a fixed "15%" or a flat "25%" as the Helix military discount; the current verified rate is 30% and it moves. The only legitimate military route is your own VerifyPass-verified one-time code. A separate WeSalute+ partner offer (25%, full-price only) exists but only makes sense if you already pay for WeSalute+ membership.

Standard Helix terms apply on any path: a 100-Night Sleep Trial (30-night minimum before a return; free return pickup; up to two returns per household), free U.S. shipping, and a 10-year limited warranty (15-year on Helix Plus and Luxe). Some Helix marketing references a 120-night trial, so confirm the current trial length at purchase.
regal-military-veteran: The headline savings — up to 30% off box-office price — come from WeSalute+, a paid membership (formerly Veterans Advantage). WeSalute+ members order discounted Regal tickets through WeSalute’s entertainment partner, Working Advantage, and receive them as e-tickets or mailed tickets. Because these are pre-purchased partner tickets, all sales are final, so buy only what you plan to use.

GovX is the second online route. After a free GovX ID verification, eligible military, veterans, and first responders can buy discounted Regal Cinemas tickets directly from GovX. It is the better fit if you want free verification or you qualify as a first responder rather than through a paid membership.

Separately, many Regal theatres honor a military discount at the box office with a valid Military ID, Veteran ID, or DD214. This in-person discount is set locally, so the amount and availability vary by theatre — confirm with your Regal before you go. Whichever route you choose, the free Regal Crown Club, Value Tuesdays, and member concession deals are loyalty perks that stack on top of normal pricing and are not the military discount itself.
walmart-military-discount: Walmart’s military commitment is employment and philanthropy, not retail discounts. Its corporate veterans page covers hiring (500,000+ veterans and spouses hired since 2013), the Military Family Promise, veteran-owned supplier spend, and giving — but no consumer discount is mentioned. So the honest answer for a shopper looking for a "Walmart military discount" is that there isn’t one.

The one official, military-relevant lever is Walmart+ Assist. Walmart’s help article lists the full set of qualifying government-assistance programs — including SNAP, WIC, Medicaid, SSI, TANF, and the VA "Veterans and Survivors Pension Benefit" — and states that applicants must complete the SheerID process to determine eligibility, that not all programs qualify, and that membership stays verified for one year with an annual eligibility re-check. The discount is 50% off Walmart+: $49/year or $6.47/month versus the standard $98/year.

Two claims to watch. First, aggregator and "military discount" blogs frequently state that Walmart gives veterans 10% off on Veterans Day via SheerID — but no Walmart.com or corporate.walmart.com page confirms a 10% Veterans Day discount or any SheerID-gated Veterans Day offer; Walmart’s "Veterans Day Deals" pages are ordinary public sale pages open to all shoppers. Treat the 10% figure as unverified. Second, the well-known Walmart "10% discount" is the associate (employee) discount card on general merchandise and produce — an employment benefit, not a customer military discount, and the two should not be conflated.
alaska-airlines-military-discount: There is no online verification portal for Alaska’s active-duty benefits — verification is in person with a valid military ID (airport counter, gate, onboard, lounge) or by phone for the special fare. Dependents 10+ must present a white Uniformed Services Dependent ID marked "active," and additional documentation may be required if a dependent’s name differs from the service member’s. For the pet cargo discount, a common access card and PCS orders within 60 days of report date are required at tender. The WeSalute+ 5% fare is gated by a paid WeSalute+ membership (open to active duty, retirees, Guard, Reserve, veterans, and family) and redeemed through WeSalute’s booking portal, not alaskaair.com — no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID is used.

On amounts: Alaska does not publish a percentage for its active-duty special fare (it’s quoted by phone), so we don’t state one. The clearest quantified benefits are up to 5 free checked bags on orders (often the highest-value perk), 15% off inflight food, a $35 lounge day pass versus the standard $65, and the 5% base-fare discount via WeSalute+. Note a stale figure floating around: a 2024 newsroom post said the lounge pass was $30, but two live Alaska pages show $35 as current.

Watch the exclusions. The active-duty special fare excludes retirees and TDY travel and follows all standard fare rules; the WeSalute 5% excludes Saver fares, select First Class, codeshares, taxes/airport fees, and award travel, can’t be combined with other promotions, and doesn’t serve Prudhoe Bay, AK — though it can apply on top of Alaska’s sale prices. Because WeSalute+ is a paid membership, weigh its cost against your expected savings (it also bundles 1,400+ non-airline offers). For comparison, Delta, United, American, and Southwest also waive checked-bag fees for active-duty on orders, and United and JetBlue likewise offer 5% via WeSalute — so Alaska is competitive but not uniquely generous on fares.
ifit-military-discount: NordicTrack uses GovX ID to confirm current or former military status. Verification is instant; you receive a single-use code, and you can log back into GovX for a new code on future orders (one code per user, limit one per day). There is no ID.me or SheerID path, and no verification path for ProForm or the iFIT app because neither offers a military discount.

The 5% is an equipment-order discount, not a subscription discount. The iFIT app membership — $39/mo or $396/yr for iFIT Pro — is billed separately and has no military pricing. Most new NordicTrack machines include a free iFIT period, so factor that in before paying for the app.

NordicTrack also runs separate Medical Professional and Educator discount programs on its own gated pages. Those are distinct appreciation offers, not the military discount, and they do not change the fact that ProForm and the iFIT subscription carry no military rate.

Because NordicTrack machines carry deep, frequent seasonal markdowns (New Year, Memorial Day, July 4, Veterans Day, Black Friday), the public sale price usually beats 5% off full sticker, and GovX single-use codes generally can’t stack on already-discounted items. Compare the live sale price against 5% off full price and take the lower.
saks-fifth-avenue-military-discount: Verification is not applicable here: Saks uses no military verification provider because it has no military discount to verify against. That puts Saks in the same no-military-discount department-store cluster as its luxury peers — full-price retailers whose savings levers are promotions and loyalty, not identity-based discounts.

For the math, take a representative $500 order. Rakuten’s base ~2% returns about $10; an elevated 10x/10% Rakuten day returns about $50; a 20–40% seasonal markdown saves $100–$200; and a gift-card-with-purchase event (historically around a $75 gift card on $150+) is effectively ~15% back. None of these depend on military status — choose the biggest single lever, and remember a non-Rakuten coupon code can void the portal cashback.

Two passive layers stack on top of whatever you do: SaksFirst/Saks cardholders earn 2–6 points per dollar (2,500 points auto-convert to a $25 SaksFirst gift card; smaller balances forfeit January 1), and Amex Platinum’s enrollment-required Saks credit is worth up to $50 twice a year — a card benefit, not a Saks discount. Finally, Saks’s 7-day price adjustment quietly captures a post-purchase markdown if your item drops in price and is still in stock in the same color.
hurricane-harbor-military-discount: Because the discount cannot stack, the military rate is not automatically the cheapest — when a public online sale drops the daily ticket below the military daily, buy the public one. You pick one price, not two.

Verification is handled by ID.me: you verify once, then log in during checkout each time. There is no front-gate verification — everything is online. Support for verification issues goes through ID.me; ticketing questions go to Six Flags guest services.

Six Flags now operates the former Cedar Fair water parks too, so exact pricing and pass names vary by location. The dollar figures here ($20 daily / $80 Gold Pass) are the Splashtown example — always price your specific park’s page.
bobs-furniture-military-discount: s uses no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute military flow. Any verification is manual and at the store

s is its own machinery.
