Various sites variously claim a Rough Country military discount of 5%, 10%, or 30% — but these figures contradict one another, cite no official source, and could not be confirmed against anything Rough Country publishes. Treat them as unreliable. Note also that some third-party GovX storefront sellers list Rough Country-branded products at a discount; that is the seller’s discount, not a Rough Country program.

The savings that are real are open to everyone: the Rough Country Sale section (ongoing category deals on lift kits, bed covers, steps, and shocks), free sitewide shipping on eligible orders (which meaningfully lowers cost on heavy suspension parts), and Affirm financing at checkout to spread payments. If a verified military discount is the priority, off-road retailers such as ExtremeTerrain and Quadratec publish their own military/first-responder programs worth comparing. And Rough Country does support the military community another way — it sponsors Operation ReConnect, whose annual custom-Jeep raffle (at operationreconnect.org) funds free vacations for veteran families; that’s a fundraiser, not a purchase discount.
peter-millar-military-discount: Peter Millar is a no-military-route brand with a myth problem. Coupon aggregators fabricate offers for it: military.hotdeals.com claims "PMCART24 allows military members to receive 50% off," and WorthEPenny advertises a "10% military discount for in-store purchases with valid military ID." Neither appears in any primary source — petermillar.com publishes no such program, and ID.me explicitly says it isn’t aware of one. Treat every flat-percentage "Peter Millar military discount" claim as invented until the brand itself says otherwise.

The GovX situation deserves the distinction most sites miss: GovX does not carry Peter Millar as a brand. What it carries is a handful of Peter Millar x Barstool Golf collaboration pieces, sold through Barstool Sports’ GovX shop at member pricing. If one of those specific golf pieces is what you want, a free GovX account (military, veterans, first responders, and government per GovX’s rules) is worth checking first. But GovX is a substitute channel, not a stack — no promo codes or cashback portals apply there, and its collab inventory is narrow.

For everything else, the real "military discount" is the one open to everyone: buy last-season colors and styles in the end-of-season, semi-annual, or Black Friday windows — routinely 30% or more off — and click through a cashback portal first. On a $250 cart (say a ~$115 performance polo plus a ~$135 quarter-zip), a 30% markdown plus ~2% cashback lands around $170–$175, saving roughly $75–$80. Buying full price today, the portal alone is all there is: ~$5–$8 back at 2–3% (rates as of July 14, 2026). The portal play is safe here precisely because no code is involved — Peter Millar’s Conditions of Sale allow only one promo code per order anyway, applying the single greatest discount, and codes may not work on sale items.

Two more honest angles: department-store carriers like Nordstrom and Dillard’s stock Peter Millar and sometimes mark it down deeper than the brand’s own site, so price-check both before you buy. And mind the returns fine print — discounted styles purchased through promotions may be final sale per the Conditions of Sale, so confirm the current language before committing to a deep-sale piece. No military-specific promotion has been found in any Veterans Day or Memorial Day window checked, so don’t hold out for one.
hydrojug-military-discount: HydroJug verifies eligibility through GovX ID, which confirms your status against its military, first-responder, and government databases. You create a free GovX account once, pick your community group on HydroJug’s Hero Discount page, and verification typically takes under 60 seconds. HydroJug then grants lifetime access — no re-verification required, per the official page — which is unusually generous next to brands that make you re-verify every year. Verification support runs through GovX.

One thing to watch: aggregator and coupon pages variously claim the HydroJug military discount is “10–25%,” “up to 15%,” or verified “through SheerID.” None of that comes from HydroJug. The official page names GovX ID — not SheerID — and publishes no percentage at all. The honest answer to “how much is it?” is: an exclusive code whose amount is shown after you verify.

The full-price-only rule does real work here. HydroJug’s page is explicit that the hero discount cannot be combined with other promotions or sale pricing, and coupon trackers report that public promos and site sales run regularly. That means the hero code and a public sale are competing options, not a stack: on full-price gear, verify and use your code; on marked-down gear, the sale price wins by rule, because the hero code is barred on markdowns.

Two more angles worth knowing. HydroJug also has a brand page on the GovX marketplace (govx.com), where member pricing sits behind the GovX login — it’s a substitute for the brand-site code, not something you can combine with it, but worth a comparison check once you’re verified. And the same one-time GovX ID verification unlocks discounts at hundreds of other brands, so the 60-second signup pays beyond HydroJug.
crutchfield-military-discount: Crutchfield’s discount is powered by ID.me. You verify your military, veteran, or family status once, receive an offer code, and enter it at checkout under "Apply Gift/Reward Card or Offer Code" → "Offer Code." The confirmed value is a flat $25 off a $250+ order — not a percentage — which works out to roughly 6% on a $400 cart and about 10% only at exactly the $250 floor. Coupon sites that advertise "10% off almost everything," "20%," or "25%" military codes are overstating it; the flat $25 with a long exclusion list is the real offer.

The exclusion list is the catch. The code does nothing on Apple, Bose, Denon, Klipsch, LG, Samsung, Sony, Sonos "and others," nor on digital imaging, pro audio, drones, prepaid installation/programming services, gift cards, or Outlet items — and it’s not combinable with any other offer. So the code only shines on a qualifying, non-excluded item bought at (or near) full price for $250 or more.

Because Crutchfield is a MAP-priced specialty retailer, its own tools frequently save more than the $25. The Outlet / Scratch & Dent channel sells open-box and closeout gear at a discount that still carries the full manufacturer’s warranty, Crutchfield’s Money-Back Guarantee, and 60-day returns — and usually beats the flat $25 (the code can’t be used there anyway). Crutchfield also price-matches Amazon, B&H, BestBuy.com, Sonic Electronix, and manufacturer prices, and refunds the difference if its own price drops within 60 days. Crutchfield Rewards (free, ~2% back, points never expire) and free lifetime US-based tech support round out the value.

For the premium brands the military code excludes — Sony, Bose, Samsung, Sonos, Apple — the strongest play is often the tax-free military exchange (shopmyexchange.com / mynavyexchange.com), which can beat a $25 flat code once sales tax is counted. All honorably discharged veterans can shop the exchanges online; active duty, retirees, and certain disabled veterans also have in-store privileges. As always, if a public seasonal sale is deeper than $25, take the sale — the code won’t stack with it.
weathertech-military-discount: WeatherTech uses no military-verification provider — no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute — because it offers no military discount to verify against. If you already have an ID.me or GovX account, it will not produce a WeatherTech product discount. ID.me’s own WeatherTech page says it is "not aware that Weathertech offers Military discounts."

Watch for two name collisions that are not WeatherTech product discounts. First, GovX sells discounted event tickets for "WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca" — that is a stadium naming-rights sponsorship, not a discount on WeatherTech auto products. Second, "3Wliners" is a different aftermarket floor-liner brand that runs its own first-responder program — it is not WeatherTech.

The legitimate way to save is built into WeatherTech’s own checkout: spend $100+ for 50% off Ground Shipping, or $250+ for free Ground Shipping to the 48 contiguous states, with no code needed. WeatherTech also offers Affirm financing (a budgeting option, not a discount) and accepts official WeatherTech Gift Cards online, by phone, and in its Factory Stores.
sweetwater-military-discount: Sweetwater is the Fort Wayne, Indiana musical-instrument and pro-audio retailer, and its pricing model is everyday MAP (minimum advertised price) plus a personal Sales Engineer relationship rather than sitewide coupon codes. Because of that, there is no "military discount" lever to pull: the genuine best path for a service member is the same as for any savvy buyer — call a Sales Engineer and negotiate off MAP before you check out. Guitar and audio forums report that around 10% off is fairly easy, roughly 7% is typical, and long-time high-spend customers occasionally see up to about 20%. Treat those as YMMV community signal, not policy.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites that advertise a specific "Sweetwater military discount" percentage or a checkout code. The most common is a "JOLLY 30% off for military" code, alongside "15%," "20%," and "up to 50%" claims. None of these is published or confirmed by Sweetwater — the terms these aggregators cite ("cannot combine, excludes sale items, online only, subject to change") are generic boilerplate, not a Sweetwater offer. Sweetwater rarely issues sitewide percentage codes at all, so treat every "Sweetwater military code" from a coupon site as fabricated until it appears on sweetwater.com.

When you are flexible on the exact unit or cosmetics, the DealZone (open-box, demo, B-stock, used, price drops, and call-in savings) is often the cheapest route of all — advertised up to 83% off on some gear, with the free 2-year "Total Confidence Coverage" warranty still included. Stock is unpredictable and changes daily, so a specific model may or may not be listed the day you look. Memorial Day and Black Friday/Cyber Monday are the public sale events that move the most open-box inventory; there is no dedicated, verified military-only holiday promotion.

For a large purchase, the Sweetwater Card adds value: 0% APR financing tiers (for example, 48 months on $499+ and shorter same-as-cash terms on smaller amounts), 5% back in Bonus Bucks on $99+ orders, and a $50 credit for new cardholders. The catch is that Bonus Bucks load only after your items ship and expire 60 days later, so the reward is future store credit rather than an instant discount — worth it only if you will spend the credit in time. Financing tiers change, so confirm the current terms when you apply.
ecoflow-military-discount: EcoFlow’s discount runs through ID.me, the identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. You verify your group membership once; on future orders you simply sign in to ID.me and apply the discount code at checkout. ID.me states it does not share or sell your data, and you can delete your account at any time.

On a big-ticket item, the standing 5% is real but rarely the deepest savings. On a roughly $1,000 power-station order, the 5% saves about $50 — while EcoFlow’s seasonal events (Outdoor Sale, Prime Day, Black Friday) have historically run 30–50% off, and the Certified Refurbished store often beats 5% on the same model. Third-party retailer deals at Amazon, Costco, and Walmart sometimes beat EcoFlow-direct pricing too. The 5% wins when nothing is on sale and you’re buying new at MSRP.

There are extra layers worth knowing: EcoFlow’s corporate purchase program offers up to 10% off bulk multi-unit orders, and signup EcoCredits (roughly $35 in credit), Refer-a-Friend, and Trade-In are account-level programs that generally sit under whichever price path wins. One caution on aggregator claims: EcoFlow’s own program is 5% via ID.me — "GovX EcoFlow" offers you may see are typically third-party reseller listings, not EcoFlow’s own store.
Because EcoFlow controls the program and its sale calendar, treat the numbers here as a starting point and confirm the current offer on the official discount-program page before you buy.
leupold-military-discount: The core fact: Leupold’s military/veteran/law-enforcement benefit is the VIP Program, an application-gated pro-deal channel — not a public percentage coupon. Its own VIP page publishes no percentage; VIP pricing is disclosed only after verified enrollment. Any confident "Leupold military discount of 10%–25%" from aggregator sites should be treated as unverified.

How verification works: Leupold runs its own VIP enrollment. You register, select your category, and upload documentation — Military ID for active duty, DD Form 214 or Military ID for veterans, an LE ID for law enforcement, or a valid US federal government email for federal employees. Approved VIP pricing is valid for one year and is personal or duty use only; reselling or buying on behalf of others forfeits access.

The rules are strict. Annual caps are hard — 3 riflescopes or red dots, 6 observation optics, and 6 accessories per calendar year — and the program is in-stock and online only, with no unit or department purchases. Public promo codes do not stack on a VIP order; the VIP price is a closed-channel deal.

Where else to look: Leupold Tactical is also listed on ExpertVoice, a separate pro-deal platform with its own eligibility. And because a live public code (such as a seasonal 20% off) can occasionally match the VIP price on a single scope, it’s always worth comparing your VIP price to the current public code and authorized-dealer sales (OpticsPlanet, Scheels, Bass Pro/Cabela’s) before ordering.
budget-military-discount: Verification is handled by WeSalute, not by ID.me, GovX, or SheerID. You enroll in the paid WeSalute+ tier and verify your military status; WeSalute issues a secure WeSalute+ ID so you don’t share your military ID directly with each merchant, and provides the Budget BCD number used to apply the rate. Treat WeSalute+ as an ongoing paid membership and confirm its current cost before relying on it.

The headline rate is a maximum. Budget publishes only "up to 35%" (with a stated minimum of 5% in Canada), and the actual savings vary by location, dates, and car class. Because Budget also runs public "up to 35% off" promotions, it’s worth comparing the military rate against current public deals on budget.com before booking.

WeSalute’s Budget offer page notes the up-to-35% Pay Now promotion is "valid until June 30, 2026," while Budget’s own page frames the discount as ongoing — re-verify the headline percentage and validity after that date. Combinability language differs between Budget and WeSalute, so confirm at checkout.
transparent-labs-military-discount: The verification partner is GovX, not ID.me — worth spelling out because Transparent Labs does appear on ID.me Shop, but only with affiliate offers (like free shipping over $99), not an ID.me-verified discount. The real program lives on the brand’s own military page: real-time GovX ID verification, then a single-use 15% code per visit, capped at one code per day. If you skip the code at checkout, you pay full price — nothing is account-applied.

The honest comparison for repeat buyers: the GovX 15% beats the evergreen Subscribe & Save 10%, but the subscription adds guaranteed free shipping and zero re-verification. On a $110 cart the spread is about $5.50 an order — disciplined buyers can pull a fresh GovX code every order, while hands-off buyers may prefer the subscription. Whether the GovX code applies on top of subscription pricing is unstated by the brand, so don’t plan on combining them.

The cashback trap: TopCashback paid 10% on Transparent Labs orders as of July 7, 2026, but its terms void cashback when you use a coupon code not listed on its site — and the GovX code isn’t. So it’s 15% instant or ~10% rebate, never both. One portal-listed exception worth testing on a first-ever subscription order: the SUBSCRIBE15 code (15% off a first subscription order, listed on TopCashback as of July 7, 2026) should coexist with cashback precisely because it’s portal-listed — verify it applies at your checkout before counting on it.

And the calendar beats the code once a year: Black Friday 2025 was 25% off all supplements (subscribers automatically included) plus a free bundle on $149+ orders, per the brand’s own blog — historically the year’s best window, no verification needed. Aggregator claims of a "41%" or "20%" military discount are fabricated or unverified; the brand’s own figure is 15%.
brunt-military-discount: BRUNT routes its military discount through ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. At checkout you click the ID.me button, verify your eligibility once, and ID.me confirms your status to unlock the 10% instantly. There is no confirmed GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute path for BRUNT — ID.me is the named partner.

The make-or-break fact is BRUNT’s own rule: "our system allows for one discount code per order." The ID.me 10% is that one discount, so on a first order you should compare it against a $10-off welcome code or a live sale — if a code or sale saves more than 10%, use that instead, because they do not combine.

One clarification on first responders: ID.me Shop’s separate cashback marketplace says it is "not aware" that BRUNT offers a first-responder discount, but BRUNT’s own Help Center explicitly lists first responders for the 10%. Treat BRUNT’s Help Center as authoritative, and confirm the 10% applies at checkout before completing your order.
nordvpn-military-discount: Verification runs through GoCertify (gocertify.me), not the ID.me or SheerID services most military discounts use. GoCertify verifies your military employment in-browser — accepted documents are an armed-forces ID or a Guard/Reserve ID — and issues a single-use discount code; support runs through GoCertify, not NordVPN. One eligibility wrinkle: the offer’s headline says "Veterans and Military Personnel," but the FAQ’s accepted-document list names only current armed-forces and Guard/Reserve IDs, so veteran acceptance isn’t clearly documented — try verifying, but don’t count on it.

The competing path matters more than usual here. Rakuten’s NordVPN store page lists 98% cashback for new customers (as of July 14, 2026, listed as "previously 20%"), which reduces a roughly $94 two-year Basic plan to about $2 net after the payout. But Rakuten’s terms void cashback when you use a coupon code that isn’t listed on Rakuten — and the GoCertify military code is exactly that. Pick one: for new customers while the elevated rate is live, cashback wins decisively; for renewals (cashback is first-sign-up-only) or if you’d rather skip portals, the military 15% is the play. Deal-forum shoppers report the Rakuten rate fluctuating between roughly 97% and 100% over 2026 — a signal the elevated rate recurs, not a promise it’s live on any given day.

Ignore the coupon-site noise. Pages advertising an "83% off NordVPN military code" and similar stacked-percentage claims are just restating the public promo — the only verified official military mechanic is GoCertify’s extra 15% on top of the standing promo, and nothing verified supports a standalone military coupon code that works without GoCertify verification.

One caveat applies to every path: NordVPN’s pricing is intro-term pricing. A two-year Basic plan runs roughly $83–$94 upfront at current promo rates (NordVPN’s own pricing page blocks automated checks, so spot-check the live price), and every plan renews at a much higher standard rate after the first term. Whether the military code can be re-used at renewal is not stated — buy the longest term you’ll actually use and set a calendar reminder before auto-renewal.
planet-fitness-military-veteran: Planet Fitness publicly lists two main membership types. The Classic membership starts at $15/month plus taxes and fees and gives unlimited access to your home club. The PF Black Card starts at $24.99/month plus taxes and fees and adds access to any of 2,700+ locations, a free guest every visit, premium app workouts, PF Perks partner offers, and select Black Card spa amenities at participating locations.

Watch the fine print: memberships may include a 12-month commitment, a $49 annual fee may apply, state and local taxes may apply, and prices, services, and perks vary by location because clubs are independently owned and operated. The everyday local join offer in the online flow — for example a reduced startup fee or a no-commitment promotion — is often a bigger saving than a military rate would be, so it is worth comparing first.

Even without a national military discount, military families have several legitimate ways to save: check the local join offer in the online club flow, ask the home club about any local military or community promotion, use referral savings (Planet Fitness says members can earn a free month per friend who joins, up to 3 months a year), review PF Perks after joining, and use the free High School Summer Pass for teens ages 14–19 through August 31 at participating locations. None of these is a military benefit, but each can lower the real cost of belonging.
tommy-hilfiger-military-discount: Tommy Hilfiger’s discount is powered by ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. You verify your status once, and ID.me issues a discount code. It routes you to a third-party (ID.me) site with its own privacy terms. The code is single-use and capped at one per week on Tommy.com — it is not a permanent account-level discount.

The military tier sits alongside parallel ID.me communities for first responders, nurses, medical providers, teachers, and students, all at the same 15%. Choose "Online" or "In-Store" when you verify; the in-store code works at Tommy Hilfiger stores in the US, Puerto Rico, Guam, and Canada, but not at department stores or Clearance stores.

Because the 15% may not be combined with any other promotion, it frequently loses to Tommy Hilfiger’s own public offers. First-time buyers usually do better with the 20%-off-first-order newsletter/Club signup, and sale shoppers often do better stacking the public SAVE15 code on already-marked-down styles (Tommy Hilfiger runs End-of-Season sales up to 70% off). Aggregators list scraped "Tommy Hilfiger military promo codes" — there is no public military code; the only verified military mechanic is the ID.me 15% issued to you after verification.
kalahari-military-discount: The Heroes rate is a rate plan, not a stackable coupon: you book it with code HEROES, then prove eligibility with a physical ID at the front desk. If your ID doesn’t validate at the desk, the resort can adjust you to the standard rate. There is no third-party verifier — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute — unlike competitor Great Wolf Lodge, which uses ID.me for its up-to-40% military rate.

Because Kalahari’s rate plans are mutually exclusive, the smartest move is to price-check Heroes against Book Early & Save every time. If you can prepay and commit two to four weeks out and don’t need to cancel, the non-refundable Book Early rate (~15–20%) usually beats the 10% Heroes rate. If you need flexibility or are booking last-minute, Heroes is the refundable military rate. They don’t combine, so pick one.

A word on the aggregators: coupon sites headline a “20%,” “30%,” or even “70%” Kalahari military discount. None is verified. The actual brand-published benefit is 10% off the Best Available Rate (VA up to 15%) on an overnight stay via code HEROES — there is no secret online military code beyond HEROES.

Keep the math honest: the discount applies to the room rate only. The mandatory ~$39.99/night resort fee and taxes are never discounted by any rate plan, and waterpark admission is already bundled with an overnight room, so there’s no need to buy day passes on top of a stay.
zenni-military-discount: Zenni’s discount is powered by ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. You verify your status once through ID.me and can reuse that verification on future Zenni orders. ID.me can detect fraudulent use across accounts and reserves the right to revoke access for abuse.

Zenni uses ID.me only for status verification — not GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute. Some coupon aggregators imply a stackable Zenni "military code" or a GovX path; neither is how it works. There is no coupon to paste: the 10% is applied only through ID.me verification, and it overrides any other code rather than stacking on it.

Because the 10% overrides sale pricing, the honest math is an either/or. On a full-price order, verify with ID.me for the 10%. But when a sitewide or clearance sale deeper than 10% is live, take the sale price — the discount would replace it and leave money on the table. And if you just want the cheapest possible pair, start from Zenni’s lowest-priced frames ($6.95+), where 10% off a $20 order is only about $2.

Zenni also runs an identical 10% program for first responders and medical workers — police, firefighters, EMTs, nurses, and other medical personnel — through the same ID.me flow. Because Zenni controls the terms and can change them at any time, treat the numbers here as a starting point and confirm the current offer on Zenni’s official military discount page before you buy.
green-chef-military-discount: Green Chef, an organic meal-kit brand owned by HelloFresh, verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. You authenticate once, ID.me confirms your military affiliation, and Green Chef issues the discounted subscription. Some checkout flows have historically used SheerID instead, so follow the verification option shown that day. Re-verification may be requested periodically per the provider’s policy.

On the number: the headline first-box percentage is a customer-acquisition lever, not a fixed veteran benefit. It moves with Green Chef’s public new-customer promo, which is why aggregator claims of 60%, 65%, or 70% are inflated or stale. We state the as-shown 55% first box plus a 15% tail and flag that the figure at verification is what actually applies.

Because Green Chef is online-only, there is no in-store, Exchange, or commissary channel. The only legitimate way to stretch the deal further is a cashback portal (Rakuten has listed a flat first-order cashback), which sits outside the code and can pay on top. Staying subscribed captures the 15% ongoing tail, which outlasts most one-time public offers.
alamo-military-discount: The core fact: Alamo confirms discounted government and military rates but publishes no percentage. Its government pages describe "discounted rates for federal government employees and military personnel at over 550 car rental locations worldwide" and split them into Official/TDY and Leisure lanes — but no dollar figure or percentage appears on any Alamo military or government page. That makes the channel and the rate bucket, not a single headline number, the thing that matters.

Two lanes, two kinds of proof. The Official/TDY rate is for government business and requires official orders or a government-issued travel card; it’s booked at airport-serving locations and bundles unlimited mileage (CONUS/Canada), damage and 3rd-party liability protection, and a full tank at pickup — often the best total value on duty travel. The Leisure rate is for personal trips and needs only a valid military or government ID at the counter. A veteran with no orders uses the leisure lane.

Why the "%" and code claims keep circulating. Aggregators and military-listing sites confidently quote Alamo "military discounts" of 20-25% and repeat the GOVRNR customer number. None of those percentages come from Alamo. GOVRNR is real — it pre-loads the government/military leisure rate via a Military.com "Redeem Online" deep link — but it is not published on alamo.com, so we present it as a working-but-unofficial contract number and tell you to verify the price it returns.

Where the real savings are. Because the military rate isn’t guaranteed to be cheapest, the discipline is to price the same car and date across several buckets: the leisure government rate, the separate GovX marketplace listing, a prepaid "Pay Now" rate (USAA cites "up to 35%" for prepaying — a prepay figure, not a military percentage), and the free Alamo Insiders 5% off the base rate. If you have a Costco or USAA membership, add those quotes too — they’re frequently competitive and can waive the additional-driver fee. The cheapest bucket flips week to week; take the lowest total on your exact reservation.
doordash-military-discount: DashPass is a fee-waiver subscription, not an order discount: on eligible orders it drops the delivery fee to $0 and reduces the service fee, and it adds 5% back in credits on Pickup. The benefits are identical whether you buy it standard ($9.99/month or $96/year), through GovX, or via a partner — so the only question is which source is cheapest for you. Because it saves money only when you order enough to clear the fees it waives, DashPass is worth it at roughly 2+ orders a month and not below that.

GovX is a free, closed verification marketplace for the military, first-responder, and government communities. You create a GovX account, verify once with GovX ID, and claim the DoorDash offer — a one-time link that sets DashPass at $72 for 13 months. It is the genuine "military" route, but it is not available to accounts with an active DashPass, is US and Puerto Rico only, and auto-renews at the full $96/year after month 13, so set a reminder to cancel or re-shop.

For many service members the cheapest path is not GovX at all. Eligible Chase cards — Sapphire Reserve/Preferred, Freedom/Slate, and most co-brands — include complimentary DashPass, and the Sapphire cards layer monthly DoorDash credits on top ($5/month dining plus two $10/month non-restaurant promos on Reserve). Eligible T-Mobile customers get 12 months of DashPass free. Because you can only hold one DashPass source at a time, take the free one if you have it before paying anyone.

Be cautious of coupon and "military discount" aggregators advertising "up to 60% off," a "15% off / $5 off $15 military offer via SheerID," or generic "military promo codes." None of these is verified on a DoorDash, GovX, ID.me, or SheerID primary source. The in-app "Offers" tab shows merchant-funded promos available to everyone, not a military tier. Students have a separate, real route: a 50%-off (or sometimes free) Student DashPass verified through SheerID — but that is a student benefit, not a military one.
cardo-military-discount: Cardo verifies eligibility through ID.me, a third-party identity service. You need a free ID.me account; Cardo says verification is nearly instant and returns a coupon code you paste at checkout. Re-verification cadence and code expiry aren’t stated on the page, so assume you may need to re-verify for future orders. On the baseline PACKTALK EDGE single unit ($439.95 list), 20% brings it to about $351.96.

The offer is strictly non-stacking. Cardo limits it to "products which are not discounted already," so it can’t ride on top of a sale, bundle, or clearance price, and "new products are excluded from all promotions" — currently the flagship PACKTALK PRO while it’s still new. There’s one coupon field at checkout, so you use the ID.me code or a sale price, not both.

That makes the best move situational. For a current full-price unit — the PACKTALK EDGE, Neo, Freecom 4X, or Spirit HD — the 20% ID.me code is the clear winner. But when Cardo runs a Black Friday / Cyber Monday site sale or a two-unit DUO bundle, the sale or per-unit price frequently beats the 20% code, and you can’t combine them — so compare and take the lower. Ignore aggregator "25/30/40% military code" claims: the only verified rate is 20%.
disney-on-ice-military-discount: Disney On Ice is a Feld Entertainment touring production, and tickets sell through Ticketmaster and arena box offices. Because there is no first-party program, the military benefit is delivered as ongoing per-market GovX and FEVO offers rather than a national holiday sale — a 2019 Military.com listing for one market cited "up to $4 off per ticket" plus reduced service fees, redeemed by phone or concierge.

The military paths are substitutes, not stacks: a GovX, FEVO, or ID.me military price is its own transaction and cannot be combined with a public promo code or a group rate. On multi-ticket orders the real edge of the online military offer is its service-fee reduction, since those fees scale with the number of tickets.

Because exact GovX and ID.me amounts are not disclosed on their landing pages and terms vary by show, treat the figures here as historical context and confirm the current offer at click-through before you buy.
dollywood-military-discount: Online, Dollywood uses ID.me to confirm military status before you can buy discounted tickets or passes, and you also sign in to or create a My Dollywood account to complete the purchase. In person, a Dollywood or Splash Country ticket-window host checks your physical military ID instead of using ID.me. For stays, you present your military ID at check-in. Dollywood does not state an ID.me re-verification frequency; ID.me’s own policy governs how often you re-verify.

Because Dollywood publishes set military prices rather than a percentage, you can’t quote a single "% off" for tickets — and any flat percentage you see on coupon sites (5%, 26%, and 30% have all appeared) is not supported by Dollywood’s official source. Compare the published military price against general-public promotions, which are sometimes lower and open to everyone.

The military program is sponsored by Humana. First responders, teachers, and other public employees are not part of the military offer, but Dollywood runs a separate "Public Employee Appreciation Days" program that has included some of those groups — verify it separately if you also qualify there.
jd-sports-military-discount: JD Sports US does not use ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute to gate a military discount — ID.me appears only for member cash back (Retro up to 1.5%, Sale Items up to 1.0%), which is available to all ID.me members and is not a military discount. Any in-store military discount would be verified the old-fashioned way: by showing a physical ID to the cashier at a participating store. There is no account, online enrollment, or re-verification confirmed for a JD Sports military discount.

Where the "10%" comes from matters. That figure — plus the eligible-group list (active/veteran/retired/Reserve/Guard/spouse/dependents) and the accepted-ID list (DD214, VFW, American Legion, VetRewards, VA ID) — traces to military-discount aggregators, not to any JD Sports page. The one primary confirmation is a single Tanger outlet store advertising "Military Offer 10% off purchase — must show military ID." That’s real but location-specific; whether the offer is chain-wide is unverified, and aggregators even report that federal civilian employees don’t qualify. Treat all of it as store-dependent and unconfirmed until the store tells you otherwise.

For the everyday, confirmed ways to save, JD STATUS (the free US rewards program) and seasonal sales/coupons are open to everyone, and ID.me members can stack cash back. But if a guaranteed military discount on the same sneakers matters, the better-documented options are sister-market Foot Locker — which offers a 10% military discount online and in-store, verified via SheerID (four verifications per rolling 30 days, $100 max per verification) — and Finish Line (owned by JD Sports), which reports a 10% in-store military discount at participating stores.
danner-military-discount: How verification works: there is none on danner.com itself. ExpertVoice verifies your service status once at account creation and gates pricing behind login, with personal-use and no-resale terms. The Exchange verifies via your military status or the VA’s veteran verification (all honorably discharged veterans can shop online). GovX runs its own membership verification for current and former military, first responders, law enforcement, healthcare, and government employees.

The one confirmed stack: Danner’s pro-deal article states the Danner Member free-shipping-over-$50 benefit "can be applied in addition to your exclusive discount" on ExpertVoice orders. Everything else is channel-exclusive — ExpertVoice is a gated storefront rather than a code, GovX is a closed marketplace, and Exchange pricing (plus MILITARY STAR card promotions) lives entirely on the Exchange side.

One thing to watch: coupon aggregators invent Danner military programs that do not exist — "10% off with SheerID," "up to 60% off," even a "70% first responder discount." Danner’s own support page names exactly two routes, ExpertVoice and AAFES, and publishes no percentage. Treat every "Danner military code" as fabricated.

The honest math on a $180 pair of duty boots: the Exchange’s tax-free checkout saves roughly $12.60 at a 7% state rate before any Exchange pricing edge, an unpublished ExpertVoice pro-deal price may beat that (check it first — it stacks with member free shipping), and a clearance or retailer markdown of 30–50% beats every gated channel whenever your model qualifies.
fleet-feet-military-discount: The confirmed benefit — on the Augusta franchise’s Military & Law Enforcement Personal Rewards page — is 10% off full-priced items with a valid Military, EMS, or Peace Officer ID at the time of purchase, not combinable with other discounts. That structure (in-store, ID-verified, full-price-only) is typical of the chain, but each Fleet Feet is independently operated, so the exact terms and who qualifies can differ at your local store.

Because the discount excludes sale merchandise and can’t be combined, it’s an either/or against the clearance price rather than a stack. On a $140 full-price shoe the 10% saves $14 ($126); a last-season colorway is frequently $30–$50 off, which usually beats it. The one loyalty lever that layers on is Fleet Feet Rewards, whose points generally accrue regardless.

On verification: in-store is a simple ID check at the register with no third-party account. Any online path uses SheerID, but availability depends on the store or promo running it — Fleet Feet’s corporate site doesn’t confirm a national online offer, so confirm at checkout before relying on it.
carvana-military-discount: Carvana runs no military-verification program (ID.me, GovX, or SheerID) because there is no military discount to unlock. Directory listings and coupon aggregators that imply a "Carvana military discount" of some percentage are not describing an official offer — any "code" is either a general public promo or nonexistent.

The biggest savings variable is financing, not the car price. A lower APR from a military-friendly credit union stacks against any car price and typically saves hundreds to thousands over the loan versus a subprime or dealer-arranged rate. Get pre-approved from Navy Federal, USAA, or PenFed first, then bring that offer to Carvana.

Two more protections matter. The Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) can cap the interest rate at 6% on qualifying pre-service debt and adds other protections — but it attaches to the loan through your lender, not to Carvana. And for deployed or remote buyers, Carvana’s fully online process paired with a military Power of Attorney lets someone complete the purchase on your behalf.
midway-usa-military-discount: MidwayUSA’s "no military discount" answer is a deliberate business policy, not a gap. Its own Help pages and multiple corroborating Q&A sites repeat the same explanation: Mr. Potterfield is an Air Force veteran, but he believes the best strategy is to offer every customer the same low price. So the honest starting point for a service member is that there is no military rate to unlock — and no verification partner to check one.

The free MidwayUSA Rewards program is the closest thing to a standing saving. You get a 250-point join bonus, earn Reward Points on purchases, and redeem them as Reward Coupons on future orders. It is earn-and-redeem rather than a checkout percentage, so its value compounds for repeat buyers rather than cutting one order. Points expire 12 months after your last purchase, and the exact points-to-dollar conversion is set on midwayusa.com/rewards.

On top of Rewards, layer email/text sign-up coupons and shop Sale & Clearance (up to ~75% off select gear) — and time big buys to public holiday events. MidwayUSA ran a Veterans Day sale up to ~60% off with free shipping over $100 in November 2025, but that is a public event open to everyone, not a military-gated offer. A cashback portal can add a few percent on eligible items, but firearms, ammunition, and hazmat categories are commonly excluded and a promo code can void the cashback, so verify the live rate first.

For firearms and ammunition, expect no coupon, no cashback, and no meaningful stack — compare MidwayUSA’s flat price against Brownells, Palmetto State Armory, OpticsPlanet, Cabela’s/Bass Pro, and Sportsman’s Warehouse, some of which carry military or first-responder discounts on select categories. And do not confuse MidwayUSA the retailer with the USS Midway Museum in San Diego, which offers military admission benefits and is a separate organization.
budget-truck-rental-military-veteran: Budget Truck’s military offer is a 20% rate cut for U.S. military personnel traveling with orders, applied with promo code USMIO at online checkout. The discount comes off the time and mileage of the Best Available Rate, not the taxes, fees, surcharges, or optional products such as damage waivers and refueling — and it cannot be combined with any other discount, coupon, promotion, or commercial rate. A 24-hour advance reservation is required, and availability and blackout dates apply, so book early during PCS season.

There is a second path worth knowing: Budget Truck, through parent Avis Budget Group, has a longstanding partnership with WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage), so WeSalute+ members can claim savings that way instead. Some booking paths may also verify military status through ID.me. Because Budget does not spell out every eligible group, reservists, retirees, veterans, and family members should confirm eligibility rather than assume the 20% applies automatically.

As with any military move, the rental discount is only part of the savings. A personally procured move (PPM/DITY) is reimbursable through your transportation office when you keep receipts and weight tickets, so the out-of-pocket truck cost may come back to you. Shoppers comparing brands should cross-quote Penske (15% with code MILITARY, sometimes up to 20%) and U-Haul (no rate discount, but a free month of storage) to find the cheapest option for the specific route and dates.
govx-discount-code: GovX is the largest online marketplace exclusively for the military and government community — over 1,000 brands and more than 6.7 million pre-verified members. The savings mechanic is verification, not coupons: when you verify through GovX ID, the system generates a single-use code unique to you and to that store, applied in the promo box at checkout. You’re limited to one code per 24 hours, and an unused code is re-issued rather than added to — GovX doesn’t hand out pre-made batches, which is exactly why a code copied from a coupon aggregator won’t work.

How much you save is set by each brand, but GovX’s marketplace listing rules put a floor under it: merchants must offer category minimums of roughly 25% on apparel, footwear, food, health, and tactical gear, 15% on tech, electronics, and medical, 30% on eyewear and jewelry, and about 20% on most other goods — and many brands go higher. Those percentages are merchant listing floors, not a universal member coupon, so check the specific offer. On GovX.com you generate a code and are redirected to the brand’s own site to buy; a code generated directly on a brand’s site delivers the same discount without the marketplace referral.

Verification is free. GovX ID confirms eligibility against Department of Defense databases, a work or organization email, or a document upload, and most checks complete in about a minute. GovX makes its money from a 15% referral commission paid by merchants — not from members — so there’s no fee to join, verify, or generate codes.

Two honest caveats. First, GovX codes generally don’t stack with other promo codes, so when a brand runs a deep sitewide sale, the public sale can beat the member price — compare every time and take the lower. Second, GovX ID is one of several competing verification services: some brands use ID.me or SheerID instead, occasionally with a better discount. If a brand doesn’t show a GovX ID button, check which verifier it runs before assuming there’s no service discount.
anytime-fitness-military-discount: The honest core fact: Anytime Fitness’s FAQ says it does offer a military discount, but immediately qualifies that "it is up to each location to opt-in to offer the discount." That single sentence is why no national rate can be quoted — the discount genuinely exists, but it lives at the individual franchise, not at corporate.

Why the "10–25%" claims keep circulating. Aggregators and military-discount listicles generalize across many clubs into a tidy percentage range. That range is a third-party estimate, not an Anytime Fitness figure. Some members report no military discount at their club; others report waived enrollment fees — which is exactly what "opt-in per location" produces.

How verification works. There is no central ID.me or GovX program. You present a military ID or discharge paperwork at the club when you sign up, and the club applies whatever discount it has opted into. Because the rate is local, the smartest single step is to call your specific club before signing anything.

Where the bigger wins often are. Ask the club to waive the one-time joining and key-fob fees — frequently a larger save than the monthly percentage. Explore HSA/FSA reimbursement (a Letter of Medical Necessity, via a Dr. B $15 consult) to pay dues pre-tax. And if you have base access, the free on-base gym may beat any club rate — reserve Anytime Fitness for when you need 24/7 hours or nationwide club access.
uber-eats-military-discount: There is no military verification at Uber Eats — no ID.me or SheerID military step at checkout, and no GovX Uber One offer this pass. The only verification in play is student status for the $4.99/mo student plan (18+ student verification, typically handled by SheerID) and simply holding the eligible Amex card, where the credit auto-applies to Uber One paid on that card with no separate enrollment.

You hold one Uber One membership at a time — student, standard, Amex-credited, and employer-provided are sources for the same membership, not stackable add-ons, so pick the cheapest single source. The one genuinely additive value is the Amex $15/mo Uber Cash, a payment credit (not a discount) that layers on top of your actual order. A first-order promo can pair with the free trial once, but it’s open to everyone and isn’t a military tier.

On a $30 delivery order that carries roughly $8–$12 in fees on a non-member account, Uber One drops the per-order cost to about $27–$32 by zeroing the delivery fee and taking up to 10% off — the trade-off is the membership price. At around 2+ orders a month a membership typically pays for itself; below that, pay the fees or use an in-app offer. If you hold an eligible Amex Platinum or Centurion, the membership is effectively free and the Uber Cash is pure upside — the cheapest path by far.
trek-military-discount: Coupon and aggregator pages float claims that Trek runs an official service-member program — one headlines "Trek Military Discounts, $7,100 Off," and a search aggregator asserts "Trek Bikes provides a 10% discount to verified military personnel through ID.me at checkout." Both are false or unverified: trekbikes.com publishes no military discount and uses no ID.me gate, and the "$7,100" is the value of an unrelated clearance roundup, not a military benefit. Treat any such claim as inaccurate unless Trek itself publishes it.

The dealer reality is more modest and entirely local. Independent Trek shops set their own policies — some give ~10% off parts and accessories to active and retired military with an ID at the register, a few offer ~5% off a bike, and some fold in first responders and teachers — but this is dealer discretion, not a Trek corporate policy, and it can be withdrawn at any time. Crucially, Minimum Advertised Price rules stop dealers from advertising or selling current-year bikes below MSRP/MAP, so even the shops that do offer a military courtesy usually cap it at parts, accessories, and service. Prior-year bikes are exempt from MAP — which is exactly why clearance is where the real markdowns live.

The honest best-savings path for a service member isn’t a "military discount" at all. Trek’s own Sale & Clearance section (prior-year closeouts) and Red Barn Refresh certified pre-owned program deliver real 20-40% savings with the warranty retained — a 151-point inspection, a limited lifetime frame warranty transferred to the new owner, one year of free service, and a 30-day return. If you’re brand-flexible and want a genuine military percentage, Specialized’s 15-30% ID.me discount is the single best service-member deal in the category, and Trek has no equivalent.

Finally, two disambiguations that trip people up. Trek Travel — a separate Trek business unit that runs guided cycling vacations — does offer a real 10% military/first-responder discount, but through GovX and on trips, not on bikes or gear at trekbikes.com. And the "Redfeather Outdoors - Trek" listing on GovX is a snowshoe brand unrelated to Trek Bicycle. Trek and its independent dealers control any courtesy discount and can change or withdraw it at any time, so call ahead and never assume a number.
ebay-military-discount: eBay uses no military verification of its own. The only military-tagged offer, ID.me Shop’s cash back (reported at up to ~2%), is verified by ID.me through your ID.me account and applies at the ID.me Shop portal level, not at eBay checkout — and portal rates change. The exchange path (ShopMyExchange) is verified separately by AAFES/ID.me for eligible service members and honorably discharged veterans; that’s a different benefit, not an eBay one.

The single best structural saving on eBay is Certified Refurbished. These items come with a free 2-year Allstate (SquareTrade) warranty — 100% parts and labor, no deductible — and usually cost well under new; other refurbished grades (Excellent, Very Good, Good, Certified Open Box) carry a 1-year Allstate warranty. On any listing you can also send a “Make an Offer,” apply a seller coupon, or use a live eBay site-wide coupon, and a cashback portal rebates a percentage of whatever you actually pay — so those effectively stack with the portal.

Two stale claims to ignore: eBay Bucks was discontinued April 2, 2024, so any advice to “earn Bucks” is out of date, and the flat “10%” or “up to 25%” eBay military discounts on coupon sites are fabricated — eBay publishes no such offer. For a comparable new item, price-check the tax-free military exchange; once sales tax is added to an eBay cart, ShopMyExchange/NEX frequently wins.
anakeesta-military-discount: Anakeesta’s military discount is confirmed on the park’s own FAQ, which offers "10% Active/Retired Military Discount for ID Holder and Immediate Family" on single-day admission tickets "when purchased on-site at 576 Parkway in Gatlinburg." Because the discount lives at the booth, eligibility is checked visually — there is no third-party verification provider and no online code.

The same policy makes clear the discount is non-combinable: "No other discounts can be combined including but not limited to AAA, Military, and Local," and "Discounts cannot be used for online purchases, annual passes, adventure add-ons, or in park purchases." So you pick a single best discount per order, and you cannot layer the military 10% on top of the advance online saving or a reseller price.

Anakeesta has historically run a deeper 25% Memorial Day weekend discount for active and retired service members and their immediate family (with an honor-guard ceremony). That’s a seasonal event, not the everyday rate — re-check the park’s site around Memorial Day. Because Anakeesta controls the terms and can change them at any time, confirm the current offer at the booth before you buy.
merrell-military-discount: Merrell’s discount is powered by ID.me, the same identity-verification service used by the VA, the IRS, and dozens of major retailers. On merrell.com you click "ID.me Discounts" in your cart, choose your group (Military, First Responder, Nurse, Teacher, or Student), and verify once through ID.me. Verifying links your eligibility to your ID.me account, so future Merrell purchases — and discounts at other ID.me partners — go faster.

The reason to slow down before checking out is that Merrell is a heavy discounter. It runs near-constant public sales (for example, an "up to 40% off select styles" event and a separate "Moab Sale" at up to 50% off), and those sale prices are pre-marked on the site. Because the 20% ID.me code does not stack on marked-down items, a 30–50% public sale frequently gives a lower final price than the verified discount. Treat the 20% as the easy, everyday route on full-price items, and compare it against whatever sale is live.

For those who qualify, the single deepest documented flat rate is the WeSalute (Veterans Advantage) exclusive Merrell store at 40% off. But it is not the free public discount: it requires a paid WeSalute+ membership, all sales are final, purchases are personal/immediate-family use only, US shipping only, and it is capped at 12 products per year. It also cannot be combined with Merrell’s public military discount. Do not conflate the paid WeSalute+ 40% with the free ID.me 20% — some listicles blur the two.

Merrell also lists "Merrell" and "Merrell Work & Tactical" storefronts on the GovX marketplace and a brand store on ExpertVoice (Wolverine ProDeal). These are separate, closed programs with their own verification, and their pricing is gated behind login. Merrell and Wolverine Worldwide control every program and can re-verify eligibility or change or end any offer at any time, so confirm the current terms at the source before you buy.
nordictrack-military-discount: NordicTrack’s discount is powered by GovX ID. Verification is real-time; once approved you receive a single-use code with a limit of one code per user per order. To buy again later, you re-authenticate through GovX ID to pull a fresh single-use code. Nothing about the process is permanent — the codes are single-use and the terms are controlled by NordicTrack and GovX.

The military tier sits alongside parallel GovX programs for first responders (police, firefighters), medical personnel (EMT, paramedic, RN, NP, PA, hospital staff), educators, and government employees — all at the same 5% rate. The GovX "marketplace" link for NordicTrack is the verifier, not a separate storefront: it routes you back to NordicTrack.com with your 5% code.

Watch two traps. First, many coupon aggregators claim a "10% military discount" — that figure is stale and unsupported; NordicTrack’s own military, discount-program, medical, and law-enforcement pages all state 5% off your entire order (verified July 13, 2026). Second, NordicTrack allows only one promo code per order, so the 5% GovX code and a public code cannot both be applied. The automatic sale markdown is not a code, so a single 5% code can usually sit on top of it — confirm at checkout.

If you have base or exchange access, price-check shopmyexchange.com or your NEX first — tax-free pricing can beat a 5% code — and compare warehouse-club bundles (Costco, Sam’s Club) with their member cashback and longer return windows before you buy.
buckle-military-discount: SheerID checks your military credentials on Buckle’s behalf. Online, you click the "Military Discount" link on the shopping-bag page and complete a one-time verification; if you’re not instantly approved, you can upload documentation showing your name, a date of birth or discharge/retire date, and a clear military affiliation (black out sensitive info first). Buckle and SheerID state the data is used only for that verification and then purged. In store, you simply present a valid military ID.

The valuable, true nuance that coupon pages bury is that the 10% includes sale merchandise — Buckle’s own page says "entire merchandise purchase – regular and sale." So the "skip your discount during a sale" trap that applies at most retailers doesn’t apply here: a $60 sale item drops to about $54 with the 10% on top.

What’s not confirmed: aggregators float "40% off" Buckle codes and claim the military 10% freely stacks with the Buckle Credit Card’s first-purchase 10% or with public promo codes. Buckle’s page doesn’t confirm those stacks and notes "some exclusions may apply," so don’t assume them — compute each path on its own. The free Buckle Rewards program (editorial: 1 point per $1, 300 points = $10, free shipping over $150 for members) is a separate compounding layer; confirm current tiers on buckle.com.

Bottom line: verify once for the 10%, then shop the Sale section, because Buckle unusually lets the military discount ride on top of clearance. If you’re not verified and want a small portal-safe layer, Rakuten shows 2% cash back (as of July 8, 2026) on a no-code order — though identity-verified checkouts commonly break cashback tracking.
kifaru-military-discount: A page-source scan of kifaru.net on July 18, 2026 found no military-discount page (the expected /pages/military-discount 404s) and no GovX, ID.me, SheerID, WeSalute, or VerifyPass string anywhere on the storefront. So any claim that you "verify with GovX ID at checkout" is not supported by the brand’s own site.

Because there’s no automated program, the reported discount is handled manually and discretionarily by a Kifaru representative who reviews proof of service you provide directly, then issues a personal code. Availability, eligibility, and the amount can vary and are not guaranteed by any published policy — treat the reported rate as a starting point to confirm, not a fact.

On a $500 regular-price cart, the only guaranteed, verifiable savings are the Closeout collection (deepest markdowns on listed SKUs) and the annual Black Friday sale (historically up to ~20% on select items). If you’re eligible, ask Kifaru directly before paying full price. The used market on Rokslide and Hunt Talk classifieds is often 20–40% below retail because the gear is durable and holds value.
champs-military-discount: Champs Sports verifies eligibility through SheerID. The Champs-branded SheerID FAQ says you’ll "only need to be successfully verified once, then the military discount can be applied to future purchases" — but don’t treat that as permanent, since the four-verifications-per-30-days cap implies re-verification can recur. Documentation is technically optional but practically required; without acceptable proof, verification can’t complete. SheerID says it doesn’t sell, rent, or store uploaded documents. For verification problems, SheerID’s support is customerservice@sheerid.com, and verification is online-only — there’s no phone path.

The caps are the thing to plan around: 10% off, but a $100 maximum discount per verification, and only four verifications on a rolling 30-day window. It also can’t be combined with other offers or applied to previous purchases, and Champs notes "some product exclusions apply" without listing them publicly — so confirm at checkout whether your specific item qualifies.

One eligibility nuance worth repeating: Champs’ help center names veterans, National Guard, and reservists, while an older Champs SheerID FAQ page uses narrower "Active and Retired… and their eligible dependents" language. The help center is the more current, authoritative list, but the live SheerID gate at checkout ultimately decides who passes — so veterans, Guard, and reservists should just run the SheerID form to confirm. And if a military family member is also a student, Champs’ separate Student Beans offer (20% off $99+) may beat 10% on a given order; the sibling banner Foot Locker (same parent) runs a comparable SheerID military discount worth comparing too.
bruce-bolt-military-discount: The whole “BRUCE BOLT military discount” conversation online is built on fabricated framing. Coupon aggregators (WorthEPenny, Knoji, SimplyCodes and others) claim “military members take 35% off with code magnus30,” “10% off with LOTT,” or a “25% military discount.” None of it is military-gated — magnus30 and LOTT are ordinary athlete/influencer codes open to anyone, and BRUCE BOLT’s own FAQ, checked July 15, 2026, confirms no military program of any kind and no verification provider.

The real savings are public and boring. The biggest lever is buying the patriotic line during a seasonal sale — the Patriot “Standard Issue / Military” Premium Pro short-cuff gloves were $53 vs. a $75 compare-at price (about 29% off) on the verification date. On a first, full-price order, the email/SMS welcome offer helps (its exact percentage isn’t published, and it can’t stack on a live sale — take whichever is deeper, usually the sale). BRUCE BOLT allows one discount code per order and won’t let you add a code on top of a promotional offer, though a gift card can be combined with one code.

BOLT Nation is a two-tier membership: SELECT is free, PRO is $50/yr. PRO adds 15% off full-price apparel, hats, and personalized gear, recurring store credits, free shipping on $30+, and early access — but gloves are not on the 15% list, so PRO does nothing for a glove-only shopper and only pays off if you buy a lot of apparel. If you specifically want a real military discount on gear, you’ll have to buy a different brand that runs an actual GovX or ID.me program — BRUCE BOLT is not one.
ikea-military-discount: There is no third-party portal for most IKEA store offers — you present a valid military or veteran ID (or proof of status) at the register along with your scanned IKEA Family number, and an IKEA Family membership (free) is required to receive the discount. The one clear exception is IKEA Norfolk’s "Capture the Flag" offer, which is verified through SheerID. No IKEA source reviewed indicates ID.me or GovX for military offers. Because each promotion is store- and date-specific, verification is effectively per offer / per purchase — there is no persistent "verified once" military status across IKEA.

When an offer runs, the exclusions are consistent across IKEA’s store terms: it’s in-store only (not online, not on previous purchases), and it doesn’t apply to services (delivery, assembly, Click & Collect, kitchen planning), gift cards, IKEA credit-card payments, the Kitchen Event offer, or the Restaurant/Bistro/Swedish Food Market. The discount is applied before tax, shipping, and handling. Whether it stacks with general sales isn’t clearly stated — confirm at the register.

The everyday savings path open to everyone, including the military community, is IKEA Family (free) — member prices on select products, a points-based rewards program, a free hot beverage in store, and extended returns. Beyond that, watch for recurring Veterans Day / store-event offers (often November), and if you’re a Norfolk-area or NATO-relocating family, the "Capture the Flag" program is purpose-built for incoming military families. Some other home and big-box retailers run standing or seasonal military discounts worth comparing.
outdoor-research-military-discount: The aggregator claim of a standing "up to 10–25%" Outdoor Research military discount is a conflation of two very different, real things. There is no evergreen first-party military rate on outdoorresearch.com — ID.me’s own Outdoor Research military page even states it is "not aware that Outdoor Research offers Military discounts." The "10–25%" figure mashes together the seasonal Veterans Day 25% promo (a one-week offer for veterans and retirees) with the Pro Program (active-duty and reserve only, discount unpublished). Treat any "Outdoor Research military promo code" outside the Veterans Day window as fabricated.

The Pro Program is the deepest route when you qualify. OR lists Military under its "Government" category alongside Fire, Fish & Wildlife, Land Management, and Law Enforcement; you apply with an LES, active military ID, or a recent paystub, and approval is discretionary. But OR intentionally publishes no percentage — some styles stay full-price even for Pros, purchases are personal-use only (no resale or gifting), a charity donation is required on every order, and accounts renew annually. In-store Pro pricing is available only at OR’s Seattle location. If your category is not listed, OR points to its partners ExpertVoice and Outdoor Prolink for similar access under different rules.

For veterans the year-round math is different. The Veterans Day 25% is full-price-only and cannot stack — so during any 30%+ public sale, the sale price beats it. Outside November, the GovX marketplace (govx.com/m/1171) lists select Outdoor Research styles for verified members at up to ~40% off, but it is a closed storefront with no brand code or cashback stack. And because Outdoor Research is not carried by the military exchange (Bass Pro is the Exchange’s outdoor-gear provider), there is no tax-free exchange channel to compete.

The upshot: active-duty and reservists should apply to the Pro Program; veterans and retirees should use GovX or wait for a public sale year-round, and the 25% ID.me promo only during the November Veterans Day window. And whenever a 30%+ sale is live, skip the identity routes and buy the public sale price — it’s open to everyone and the 25% can’t combine anyway.
turo-military-discount: Coupon and aggregator pages (WorthEPenny, Knoji, HotDeals, Groupon, wethrift, valuecom) advertise a "Turo military discount" and first-time codes like WIN35, TURO50, or a flat 50% off — but there is no Turo military program, and these scraped codes are unverified, frequently expired, and often fabricated. TikTok and how-to posts framing "how to add the military discount on Turo" reflect confusion, not a real feature: there is no military-discount field. Do not present any "military code" as real.

The verified guest savings are real and stackable. The 10% non-refundable discount is automatic and host-locked — it applies whenever you book 4+ days out and pick the non-refundable rate, and hosts cannot change or opt out of it (it replaced the old early-bird discount on Nov 6, 2024). Host-set weekly and monthly duration discounts are the biggest lever on longer trips; Turo recommends around 45% off the daily rate for monthly trips, which also carry $0 trip fee in most markets. If a trip qualifies for multiple discounts, Turo applies them one after another — duration first, then the 10% non-refundable — sequentially, not additively.

The comparison Turo cannot win on a short standard rental is the traditional-agency military rate. On a representative $300 3-day base price, the 10% non-refundable discount brings the base to $270, and adding a $25 first-trip referral credit brings it to about $245 — but Turo then layers a trip fee, guest protection, and tax on top. A traditional agency’s published military identity discount (Hertz 25% off pay-later base; USAA up to 25%) is a real, verifiable rate with simpler all-in pricing that often beats a discounted Turo total on a short leisure rental. Use Turo when its host duration discounts or unique-vehicle inventory win; use the agency military rate when you want a guaranteed identity discount.
oreilly-military-discount: Reilly associate at the counter, repeated each transaction. No account is required for the discount, though a free O
Rewards (1 point per $1; 150 points → a $5 reward that expires in 90 days) and use O
rhone-military-discount: Rhone uses ID.me to confirm eligibility. You create or sign in to a free ID.me account, prove your status once (uploading service documentation if prompted), and ID.me returns a single-use discount code for checkout; re-verification is periodic per ID.me’s standard cycle. Verification problems go through ID.me’s help center; discount and order questions go through Rhone’s Help Center.

A note on the numbers you’ll see elsewhere: several coupon aggregators show a "20% Rhone military discount," and coupon sites advertise "35-40% off" codes. The verification provider’s own catalog states 15% for military and every community group — treat the 20% figure as unverified. The 25-40% numbers are Rhone’s public sitewide sale windows, open to everyone and generally not stackable with the ID.me code; those codes expire and routinely fail out of season.

Rhone also has a brand page on GovX as an alternate military/government verification route. The GovX discount value wasn’t directly readable at verification time, so if you already use GovX, confirm the actual percentage at redemption before choosing it over the ID.me 15%.
5-11-tactical-military-discount: 5.11 uses ID.me at its own checkout: you verify your community once — military, responder, nurse, teacher, government, student, or alumni — and the discount applies to qualifying items. Re-verification can be required periodically per ID.me’s rules, and the community percentage rotates with promotions and seasons.

GovX is a separate verification and marketplace: a distinct account with its own proof-of-service review and its own checkout at member-only, per-item pricing. Aggregators quote "up to 30%," but the savings are SKU-specific rather than a flat rate, and a strong public sale can sometimes beat the GovX price. GovX and ID.me are mutually exclusive routes — you pick one checkout.

A third channel is the military Exchange: 5.11 is carried tax-free at AAFES/NEX for shoppers with military privileges, independent of ID.me and GovX. Because 5.11 controls the terms and the ID.me percentage rotates, treat the numbers here as a starting point and confirm the live offer at checkout before you buy.
vitamin-shoppe-military-discount: There is no online military verification at The Vitamin Shoppe — no ID.me, and no SheerID for military. Verification is simply presenting a valid military ID in store on Mondays. Healthy Awards is a standard free loyalty signup with no service requirement, so it’s available to everyone, not just military shoppers.

Coupon aggregators claim an online Vitamin Shoppe "military discount code" and headline figures like "25% off military" as if they’re an everyday online offer. That’s misleading. The real program is Military Mondays — 20% off, in store only, on Mondays, with a military ID. The 25% figure is a historical Veterans Day (Nov 11, 2024) in-store promotion, not a standing rate, and any "military promo code" for the website is unverified.

The best military move is simple: shop in a store on a Monday for the 20%. If you must buy online, stack a portal-safe sitewide code with Healthy Awards points and ~2% Rakuten cashback, or use Auto Delivery for supplements you reorder. Around Veterans Day, watch for the deeper in-store promotion the brand has historically run.
audible-military-discount: Audible is a monthly audiobook subscription, not a checkout cart, so there is no cashback portal, GovX marketplace, or coupon-stacking play the way there is for physical goods. Its meaningful savings are its public promos, and none of them is military-specific. The standard credit plan, Premium Plus, lists at $14.95/month or $149.50/year for 12 credits — the annual plan works out to about $12.46/month, roughly 17% under paying monthly. A lower-priced Standard plan is $8.99/month, and a 24-credit annual Premium Plus plan is $229.50/year.

The best year-one value for many people is the Prime-member offer: new Audible customers who are Amazon Prime members can get 3 months free plus a $20 Audible credit on the Standard plan, which then renews at $8.99/month. It’s open to all Prime members, not just military, and a current cycle ends July 15, 2026. It can’t be combined with the standard 30-day free trial and isn’t available to existing or currently-trialing members. Because the promo runs in cycles, confirm the live offer and end date before relying on it.

Be cautious of coupon and military-info aggregators that advertise a specific Audible "military discount" percentage. Audible does not publish a brand-run military rate, so those figures are unverified and often copied between audiobook brands. We deliberately omit the circulating number here because repeating it would imply an offer Audible does not run. The real ID.me military audiobook discount those sites reference is for Audiobooks.com — a separate competitor listed on ID.me Shop — which they conflate with Audible; confirm its current percentage at ID.me before switching platforms.

Even without a military discount, service members have honest ways to listen for less. Libby (OverDrive) and Hoopla give thousands of free audiobooks with a public library card, and the DoD MWR Digital Library offers free audiobooks to the military community. Audible also runs recurring public promos — "$0.99/month for 3 months," "2 credits for the price of 1," and extended free trials — that beat any invented military percentage. Libro.fm is a subscription alternative that supports local bookstores and occasionally runs new-member promos.
dell-military-discount: Dell verifies eligibility through SheerID, a third-party verification service. You start verification from your Dell account’s membership section — not at general checkout: open the military discount program, click Verify, and complete the SheerID form, uploading documents if SheerID requests them. Verification is usually almost instant; if SheerID needs to review documents manually, it typically takes about 20 minutes in the U.S.

For verification problems (pending or failed), Dell directs you to SheerID’s Help Center. For discount or purchase issues on Dell.com after you’re verified, Dell directs you to its sales team via Contact Us.

Two things to watch. First, many aggregators present a flat "10% off" — Dell’s own page says "Save up to 10% extra," so treat 10% as a ceiling that varies by product, not a guaranteed rate. Second, some aggregators claim Reserve/National Guard members, spouses, dependents, and Gold Star families are eligible. Dell’s official Heroes page does not state this — it lists only active-duty, veterans, and retirees — so don’t assume those groups qualify without checking through SheerID.
golden-corral-military-discount: How verification works: it mostly doesn’t — and that’s unusual in the right direction. Golden Corral runs no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID program, and its corporate press releases state military identification is not required for the free Military Appreciation Night meal. For everyday courtesy discounts at participating franchises, a physical military/veteran/VA ID at the register is the norm.

The event’s scale is why it matters: nearly 6.7 million free meals served since 2001, with 185,000+ meals in 2024 alone — and more than $20.5 million raised in-restaurant for Disabled American Veterans along the way. DAV volunteers are stationed in restaurants from late October through the event (from October 27 in 2025).

The honest everyday math on an illustrative $25 dinner check: a franchise courtesy discount (if honored) lands at $20–22.50; the Rewards app’s $5-off-$25 signup offer hits $20 on the first qualifying visit; and ongoing Rewards return roughly $2.50 per visit in future credit. Points accrue "after all discounts and before tax and gratuity," so a register discount and Rewards points do work together.

Watch out for the lookalike-site network: goldencorralmenus.com, golden-corral.us, and similar fansites present the "10–20% everyday military discount" as a standard national program, extend it to "immediate family," claim ID requirements for the free meal, and "confirm" unannounced event dates. None of them are Golden Corral, and corporate’s own pages say otherwise on every point.
bronx-zoo-military-discount: There is no third-party verification service here — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute. WCS self-verifies: you enter the promo code when booking, and staff check your military ID at the entrance. The four codes are MILITARYBZ (active duty), VETERANBZ (veteran), and MILITARYBZDEP / VETERANBZDEP for dependents using the discount without the member present, which requires an Active Dependent Card. Because it’s ID-at-the-gate, the reservation alone isn’t proof — keep your credential on you.

The structure is member-free plus 50% off up to 3 guests, and it can’t be stacked with any other discount or promotion. On the baseline military family of four (1 active-duty member + spouse + 2 children 3–12) buying Bronx Zoo Admission, the full-price base flex cart is about $132.80; the code drops it to roughly $47.30 — the member free, three guests at half price. It’s the best deal every day except Wednesday, when basic Limited Admission is already free for everyone (reservations open Mondays at 5pm).

One caveat worth knowing: an older WCS press release said the military discount was “on-site only,” but the current bronxzoo.com FAQ supersedes it, providing the promo codes explicitly for advance online reservations. WCS also is not a documented Blue Star Museums participant and doesn’t mention the program — it runs its own year-round military discount instead. Bronx Zoo Admission uses flex pricing, so the base rate climbs on peak dates; the military math still holds (member always free, guests always 50%), but the dollar figures move.
birch-aquarium-military-discount: There is no third-party verification — no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID. You apply the MILITARY code yourself when buying online, and staff verify a current U.S. military ID at the entrance. Buy in advance: the code is not applied at the gate, and buying online already saves $5 off the walk-up price (adult admission is $34.95 online vs. $39.95 at the gate).

The $3 code is real but small, so compare it against the two bigger levers before checkout. First, Birch's discounts page says most base ticket offices (ITT/MWR) sell discounted Birch tickets — if you have base access, check your office's price first. Second, Birch advertises "save up to $20" on select low-demand online dates/times; because the military code can't be combined with other discounts, a discounted date can beat it outright — price both and take the lower.

On free admission: Birch is not listed as a Blue Star Museums participant on its own discounts page or the San Diego Museum Council's listing, so its published military benefit is the $3-off code — not free summer admission. Separately, the needs-based Museums for All program offers $3 admission for up to 4 people with an EBT or California WIC card, and groups of 10+ auto-discount to $31.95 adult / $26.95 child.
