Because Rogue does not post a percentage, the smart move is to verify ahead of time and capture the live price when the window opens.

GovX is the other verified military channel. Rogue (via its Rogue Origin storefront) lists on GovX, a closed marketplace that verifies military members, veterans, retirees, reserves, first responders, and government employees through GovX ID. It’s a members-only rate you can’t combine with a Rogue code, so the right approach is to compare the GovX net price against roguefitness.com for your exact item before buying.

Where the real savings often are: free shipping. On heavy iron — racks, rowers, bulk plates — freight is a major cost, and Rogue’s rotating free-shipping promos ("3 Ships Free," functional-trainer free-ship, select-item free-ship) frequently save more than any coupon. Always check the live shipping-promotions page. For government and unit purchases, Rogue’s GSA contract applies — but that’s procurement, not a personal discount. And ignore the coupon-site "70% off" and stacked promo codes: those are aggregator fabrications, not Rogue offers.
groove-life-military-discount: Groove Life uses ID.me for verification. You register once with ID.me, verify your group affiliation, and the discount auto-applies at Groove Life checkout. This is identity verification, not a permanent stored status on Groove Life — you verify through ID.me at checkout each time.

Separate from the brand’s own military discount, Groove Life products are also sold through a GovX marketplace storefront for military and government shoppers (reported at ~15%). GovX is a closed marketplace, not a code on groovelife.com — you can’t add a groovelife.com code or the ID.me discount to a GovX order, so compare its net price and return terms instead.

The military tier sits alongside parallel ID.me offers for nurses, medical providers, first responders, and teachers, each reported at 15%. These are mutually exclusive with the military offer — one promotion per order.
dicks-military-discount: The single most important fact: DICK’S has no military or veteran discount. Many aggregators (operationmilitarykids, usmilitary.com, themilitarywallet, worthepenny, and others) state or imply DICK’S "gives service members and veterans a 10% military discount." No DICK’S primary source supports that. The only DICK’S-published ID.me offer is for nurses, medical providers, and hospital employees — treat any "DICK’S military discount" claim as unverified store-by-store manager discretion, not company policy.

How the nurse/medical/hospital offer actually works: you verify with ID.me, generate a single-use 10%-off promo code, and paste it at checkout, where it auto-applies to the single highest-priced eligible item in your cart. A new code is available roughly every two weeks (the page also describes it as one eligible product twice every thirty days), each code expires within about two weeks, and it cannot be combined with other offers or discounts. It is online only and cannot be used in store. None of this is available for military status.

Because there is no military discount, the best moves for a military shopper at DICK’S are the same savers open to everyone: join the free ScoreCard loyalty program (earn 1 point per $1, a $10 reward per 300 points), use DICK’S Best Price Guarantee, grab the first-time text sign-up offer ($20 off $100+, exclusions apply), and shop seasonal sales — Veterans Day and Memorial Day weekends often bring sitewide promos open to all. ScoreCard is not a military benefit and is not required to use the ID.me program.
vuori-military-veteran: GOVX is an identity-verification marketplace that gives the military and first-responder communities access to member pricing from many brands. You create a free account, verify your status once with GovX ID, and then shop participating storefronts. Vuori has a storefront on GOVX, but the products and prices listed there rotate — so the Vuori section may be well-stocked, limited, or temporarily empty depending on when you visit. Treat GOVX as the route to check rather than a fixed, always-on discount.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites that advertise a specific Vuori "military discount" percentage or a checkout code. Vuori does not publish a brand-run military rate, so those figures are unverified and the codes often do not work. We deliberately omit the circulating number here because repeating it would imply an offer Vuori does not actually run.

It is easy to confuse Vuori’s V1 Community program with a military discount, but they are different. V1 Community gives certified, actively practicing fitness professionals — yoga, Pilates, barre, and spin instructors, personal trainers, strength and conditioning coaches, studio owners, and collegiate athletes and coaches — 40% off full-priced items, up to $2,000 in savings per membership year, on Vuori.com and in Vuori stores. It is a professional program with its own eligibility, not a benefit for military service or veteran status.

Even without a brand-run military discount, there are honest ways to save on Vuori: sign up for Vuori email and text updates for a welcome offer on your first order, shop the Final Sale / markdown section on vuoriclothing.com, watch for seasonal sale events, and use Vuori’s free shipping and free returns to size right and avoid extra costs. None of these is a military benefit, but each can lower what you actually pay.
turbotax-military-discount: Verification happens inside the TurboTax Online product while you prepare your return — there is no separate signup with a third-party verifier like ID.me, SheerID, or GovX, and no promo code. You enter your DFAS-issued military W-2 and confirm your rank/pay grade (E-1–E-9); TurboTax applies the discount automatically at filing. An account is required. The official source does not state a re-verification cadence; in practice you verify each tax year when you file. If the discount doesn’t apply, the likely cause is rank/product ineligibility (officer, warrant officer, Guard, or use of Desktop/Experts) — contact TurboTax Support.

The scope is narrow and worth repeating: enlisted E-1–E-9 only, on TurboTax Online only. Unlike some offers, this makes your military state taxes free too, not just federal. But it does not extend to officers, warrant officers, veterans, retirees, or (per the official page) National Guard, and it will not apply if you start in TurboTax Desktop or a TurboTax Experts/Live product — a common reason the discount fails to appear.

If you don’t qualify here, two other free routes exist for a broader military audience: MilTax, the Department of Defense’s free tax software and support via Military OneSource (militaryonesource.mil), and IRS Free File for taxpayers under an income threshold (irs.gov). Confirm current eligibility on those official sites. Comparing H&R Block and TaxSlayer’s own military offers is also worthwhile before you file.
costco-military-discount: The recurring SERP error this page corrects: many aggregator and "military discount" pages list a "Costco military discount" and sometimes quote specific figures ($20/$30/$40 Shop Card, "save $60"). Those dollar figures track Costco’s general new-member promo, which is not gated by military status. Treating the Shop Card as a military benefit is inaccurate — only the general new-member promo is confirmed on Costco’s official pages.

There is no military verification because there is no military discount to gate. Neither the Join page nor the military-family-savings page asks for military credentials or offers a military-only rate. The only eligibility check tied to the promo is whether you are a genuinely new member (or have not held any Costco membership in the last 18 months), plus enrolling in auto-renewal on a qualifying card.

Watch the naming overlap: "Gold Star Member" is Costco’s basic membership tier and has nothing to do with Gold Star military families. Do not conflate the two — the Gold Star tier carries no military benefit.

Where military members do get true warehouse-style savings: on-base commissaries and military exchanges (AAFES, NEX, MCX) offer military-only pricing. Off base, the honest move at Costco is to take the general new-member Shop Card promo, and for heavy spenders, weigh the Executive Membership’s 2% annual reward against the higher fee.
owala-military-discount: Owala uses VerifyPass to confirm eligibility. You submit your information through VerifyPass on Owala’s military discount page; once your military or veteran status is verified, Owala emails you a unique, single-use discount code to apply at checkout. Account creation specifics, accepted documents, and re-verification cadence are not detailed on Owala’s own page, so we don’t describe verification as permanent or "verify once." If automatic verification fails, the standard path is VerifyPass support or Owala customer service.

Because the code is one-time and can’t be combined with other offers, compare it against Owala’s seasonal site-wide sales (e.g., its "Birthday Bash"), which can occasionally beat 10%. Owala also runs separate one-time discounts for healthcare/medical workers (15%) and first responders through VerifyPass — if you also qualify under one of those communities, compare which single-use code is larger.

Note that some third-party retailers sell Owala drinkware and may run their own military pricing (e.g., a Keurig/WeSalute "30% off Owala drinkware" offer). Those are the retailer’s terms, not Owala’s program, and are governed separately.
tommy-bahama-military-discount: GovX is an identity-verification marketplace that gives the military and first-responder communities access to member pricing from many brands. You create a free account, verify your status once with GovX ID, and then shop participating storefronts. Tommy Bahama has a storefront on GovX (govx.com/site/brands/1323/tommy-bahama), but it is a closed marketplace — there is no brand code or cashback portal to stack on top, and on current-season goods the price often lands near retail. Treat GovX as a price to check per item rather than a fixed, always-on discount, and compare it against the live public code before buying.

Be cautious of coupon and deal sites that advertise a specific Tommy Bahama "military discount" percentage — figures like "20–25% off military" are unverified. Those numbers are really Tommy Bahama’s public promo codes, which are open to everyone, not a military-gated rate. Likewise, the ID.me Shop "store" listing for Tommy Bahama is cashback through the ID.me browser extension (an affiliate rebate), not a Tommy Bahama-granted military code. We deliberately omit the circulating "military %" here because repeating it would imply an offer Tommy Bahama does not actually run.

The one place a genuine military price appears in person is at certain outlet malls. A Tommy Bahama Tanger outlet advertises an "extra 10% off" for military shoppers who present a military ID at the register, stacked on top of the outlet’s already-reduced prices. This is location-specific and in-store only — it does not work on tommybahama.com — and it is valid at that mall through Dec 31, 2026, so confirm it is still running before you go. Full-line Tommy Bahama stores have no standing military discount.

Even without a brand-run military discount, there are honest ways to save on Tommy Bahama: use the strongest live public code (a "$50 off $100" threshold code or a sitewide percentage up to ~25%, one per order), shop the Final Sale / outlet clearance for your size, take free shipping at $100 or more, and — if you are near a Tommy Bahama Tanger outlet — stack the in-store military 10% on the outlet markdown. Best public-code windows tend to be around July 4, Labor Day, and Black Friday / Cyber Monday.
quality-inn-military-discount: Quality Inn is a Choice Hotels brand, so its military benefit is the umbrella Choice Privileges military program that runs across all Choice brands (Comfort, Sleep Inn, Clarion, Econo Lodge, and more). There is no brand-specific Quality Inn military rate — you select the Choice "Military/Veterans" rate at booking, and it varies by property and date because hotels price by availability rather than a fixed percentage.

The most reliable win is the free limited-time Gold Elite status. Because it is status and not a rate, it stacks on top of whatever rate you book — adding bonus points, late checkout, and a welcome gift on every stay while active. The rate discounts, by contrast, are mutually exclusive: the military leisure rate, WeSalute’s 15%, Pay Now & Save, and the public member rate cannot be combined, so the smart move is to price-check all of them and book the single lowest.

Two facts trip travelers up. First, you must be a Choice Privileges member and book direct on choicehotels.com or the Choice app — booking through an OTA like Expedia or Booking.com forfeits the rate, your status, and your points, and it is the single most common way people lose the benefit. Second, the old "Lifetime" Gold status was downgraded to a limited-time benefit in early 2025 and the former 2,500-point sign-up bonus appears to have been removed, so ignore any page still promising Lifetime Gold or guaranteed bonus points and confirm the current terms on Choice’s live page.
sleep-number-military-discount: Sleep Number routes its military discount through SheerID: you verify your service status once and receive a code for the additional 5%. There is no ID.me, GovX, or WeSalute path for Sleep Number’s military offer — SheerID is the named partner, and ID.me’s own store page states it has no Sleep Number offer. Coupon sites claiming a flat "10% via ID.me" or "20% off military" are conflating time-boxed holiday campaigns (Veterans Day 2025 ran 10%) or the separate teacher channel; the standing everyday figure is 5%.

The counterintuitive move is the tax angle. On a big-ticket, taxable mattress, sales tax (~7% here) is larger than the 5% discount — and the Exchange (AAFES/NEX) carries Sleep Number smart beds (p6, i8, iLE, pSE have all appeared) tax-free, with price-matching to Sleep Number’s sale and free shipping over $49. For an Exchange-eligible buyer, skipping the tax usually beats the 5%.

Stacking is unresolved from primary sources: several report the 5% "cannot be combined with another promo or holiday sale," while Sleep Number’s own wording is "additional 5% off your entire purchase," which implies it comes off the displayed price. Because the brand is almost always on sale, confirm at checkout which reading applies to your cart, and take whichever single path is lowest.
microsoft-office-military-discount: Which store you buy from decides your price. For the Microsoft 365 subscription, the only military discount is the Family "Military Appreciation Edition," and it lives at the Exchange. Microsoft frames it as 30% off estimated retail at $99.99/year and sends each branch to its Exchange to complete the purchase. Because it’s a separate Exchange SKU, there’s no Microsoft.com coupon to enter and nothing to stack on top.

The Microsoft Store 10% is a different offer for different products. It covers "select products" — Surface, laptops, tablets and other hardware — for active, former, and retired military and their families. Its terms exclude subscriptions, apps, and services, which is why it can’t be used on Microsoft 365, and it "may not be combined with any other offer." Use it for a device, not for the software subscription.

Don’t use the Home Use Program — it’s gone. Forums still circulate advice to "get 30% off Office through the Home Use Program with your .mil email." That’s outdated: HUP was replaced by the Workplace Discount Program, which requires a participating employer’s work email. A plain .mil address does not automatically qualify, so treat "use HUP" as debunked.

If you’re a student or teacher, check Microsoft’s education pricing instead — it’s a separate eligibility that is often far cheaper than either military offer. And around Black Friday or back-to-school, compare public Microsoft Store hardware promos against the 10% military discount, since the 10% can’t be combined with other offers.
hertz-military-discount: Hertz does not gate these offers behind a third-party verification service — there’s no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX checkpoint for the standard military leisure CDP. Instead, the discount code (CDP) is pre-populated when you use the official booking link, and Hertz states you may be asked to provide proof that you qualify for the military CDP when you collect your rental (for example, official government or military ID). The WeSalute+ route is different: it requires an active WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage) membership, and the up-to-25% discount books under CDP 1264103.

There is no single “Hertz military CDP.” Hertz’s own pages surface more than one code — the Government & Military leisure booking link, Military Brands CDP 2306779, and WeSalute+ CDP 1264103 — and the relationship between them isn’t explained on-page. Because each offer caps savings differently (“up to 20%” vs. “up to 25%”), the best rate can vary by booking, so it’s worth pricing the same dates and location under each code you’re eligible for.

Watch the difference between leisure and duty travel. The leisure discount gives military members a reduced personal-travel rate. Official government travel (TDY) is a separate contracted program where the CDP is pre-populated and a $5/day GARS fee is added per the U.S. Government Car Rental Agreement — that’s duty-travel pricing, not a personal discount.
mcdonalds-military-discount: s ownership model: the vast majority of U.S. restaurants are independently owned and operated. Any military courtesy — its amount, its terms, whether it exists at all — is decided by the local owner and varies store to store and season to season. Community reports say a small courtesy (around a free coffee or a modest discount) is most likely near a base or VA hospital, but it is unadvertised and never something to count on. We deliberately do not quote a percentage, because McDonald
s uses no third-party verifier — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass — for military status. Any check happens at the register, at the cashier

sorel-military-discount: SOREL uses no military verification of its own because it runs no US military discount. If you use a retailer substitute, that retailer runs its own verification — REI Co-op, for example, verifies military status through its own program. SOREL’s parent Columbia uses ID.me, but only for Columbia-brand purchases on columbia.com.

The genuine savings on SOREL boots are structural. SOREL’s end-of-winter clearance frequently takes signature boots like the Caribou 30% or more off list, and a public email-signup code plus a cashback portal can layer on top of a sitewide sale. During a deep markdown, that public price usually beats any small identity discount elsewhere.

One claim to ignore: aggregator pages advertising a US "SOREL military discount — 15% + extra 10%" are miscrediting the UK GoCertify offer to US shoppers. US SOREL has no first-party military discount, and Columbia’s 10% is for Columbia products only — don’t assume it transfers to SOREL.
wendys-military-discount: s offer plus WendyMail coupons flow to your email and app. WeSalute covers active-duty members, retirees, National Guard and Reserve, veterans, and their families — Wendy

gunmag-warehouse-military-discount: There is no military verification at GunMag Warehouse because there is no verified military program — its FAQ does not document one, and no GovX, ID.me, or SheerID integration is advertised on-site. The only "verification" is signing up for the newsletter to receive the public welcome code. Aggregator claims of a flat "16% off military," a "$7.99 military discount," or "30% off with code GunMag" are inconsistent, frequently expired, and unconfirmed by the brand.

For a service member, the honest maximum-savings path is public: shop the sale/clearance section first (that’s where the deep discounts are, up to ~70% off select items), add the 10% newsletter welcome code on a first order over $100, and hit the free-shipping threshold (around $250, contiguous 48 states) or buy items flagged "Free Shipping." Layer a cashback card or portal on top of whatever price you reach. For large quantities, a bulk/wholesale quote can beat per-unit retail.

One compliance note that coupon pages ignore: federal law and state policy restrict who can buy certain magazines and where they can ship — state magazine-capacity bans can block an order regardless of any discount. And while GunMag Warehouse isn’t a listed GovX brand, many of the individual brands it carries offer their own verified military discounts directly, which can be worth checking brand-by-brand.
fred-meyer-military-discount: Fred Meyer requires enrollment for the discount to apply — its page notes that “Customers currently enrolled in the Military Discount will see their savings at the time they place the order.” Editorial sources report the online enrollment verifies military and veteran status through SheerID; in store, staff can verify a valid military or veteran ID at the customer-service desk. Once enrolled, the discount links to your Fred Meyer Rewards account, so you don’t re-verify every trip.

This is also the honest correction to the widespread “Kroger 10% military discount” reputation. Kroger’s corporate “Honoring Our Heroes” page is a veteran-hiring and USO-partnership page with no storewide percentage — the recurring 10% is a banner-level program on one day a month, and Fred Meyer (a Kroger division serving the Pacific Northwest) is one of the banners that actually runs it.

For everyday grocery savings the bigger lever is the free Fred Meyer Rewards card (sale prices, personalized digital coupons, and fuel points), which covers the name-brand groceries the 10% excludes. And if you’re commissary-eligible, the tax-free commissary (at cost plus a 5% surcharge) usually beats even the 10% on name-brand groceries.
sephora-military-discount: Sephora has no military-verification step because it offers no military discount. ID.me’s Sephora page confirms ID.me does not currently verify military status for any Sephora offer. If a third-party site asks you to "verify for a Sephora military discount," treat it as unaffiliated and unverified.

The real, primary-source-backed way to save is Beauty Insider: earn 1 point per $1 on eligible purchases and redeem in the Rewards Bazaar, with a birthday gift and free standard shipping; higher VIB ($350 annual spend) and Rouge ($1,000 annual spend) tiers add early access and event invites. Public promo codes and the periodic Sephora Savings Event (tiered % off by Beauty Insider tier — a member benefit, not a military one) round out the options.

Separately, authorized military shoppers can buy Sephora gift cards through the Exchange (AAFES) at shopmyexchange.com. GovX also lists a Sephora gift-card affiliate page. These are gift-card channels, not a Sephora-operated discount on merchandise. Ulta Beauty likewise has no published military discount, so military shoppers seeking discounted prestige beauty often use the Exchange/AAFES assortment directly.
tidewe-military-discount: TideWe uses GovX ID. Registration is free; GovX verifies affiliation through DoD databases, email verification, or document upload, usually in real time. Support runs through support.govx.com, and re-verification follows GovX’s periodic schedule.

GovX ID issues a single-use discount code; standard GovX integrations apply one code per order and commonly exclude sale/clearance items — so the 15% usually will not stack on Flash Sale pricing. TideWe’s member "subscribe 10% off" and member-exclusive pricing are separate account perks, an alternative rather than a guaranteed stack.

Aggregators advertise "TideWe 70% off," "17% off," and generic "military codes." Those are recycled public sale claims, not a special military rate — the only verified military mechanic is the 15% GovX ID code on TideWe’s own military page.
halara-military-discount: Verification is handled by Beans iD, a third-party identity and eligibility verifier similar in function to ID.me or SheerID. You create or verify an account, prove your military status, and receive a discount code. Re-verification cadence and code reuse follow Beans iD’s terms — keep the code for your session and re-verify if it expires. Halara’s store also appears on ID.me Shop.

The single caution to watch is the offer’s currency: the most recent published terms carried an expiration of 12/31/2025, so the live status must be re-confirmed on Halara’s own site before you count on the 15%. Coupon aggregators advertising "20%," "25%," or "50% off" military are repackaging generic sitewide sale figures — no primary source supports a military rate above 15%.

Because the military code applies to full-price items only, it and Halara’s frequent sitewide sales are effectively mutually exclusive: you pick one, never both. When your item is on sale, take the public sale price and, if Halara is live on a cashback portal such as Rakuten or TopCashback, add that on top — that route typically beats the 15% military discount.
santas-village-military-discount: The two offers work through opposite channels, so match the mechanic to the park. In East Dundee, Illinois, the whole transaction happens at the ticket gate: show your Military ID, DD214, Veteran ID, or vet-designated license, enter free, and buy up to four family tickets at $29.99 each (+tax) on the spot — the offer isn’t sold online. In Jefferson, New Hampshire, it’s the reverse: you buy the $46 "Military (with ID)" admission online for a Summertime or Holly Jolly Halloween date, then show your military ID at the park entrance. Neither park uses a verification platform — no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID accounts, no pre-registration — so verification is per-visit by nature.

The savings gap between the parks is an order of magnitude. For a family of four (one service member or veteran, a spouse, and two kids ages 4+), the IL gate offer prices out at $0 + 3 × $29.99 = $89.97 + tax — roughly $82 + tax saved against four regular $42.99 tickets. The NH rate saves $4 per qualifying ticket (8%), and because the park publishes only a "Military (with ID)" rate, whether it extends beyond the ID holder is unstated — a family of four could pay $184–$196.

Watch the seasonal wall at the New Hampshire park: its military rate applies only to Summertime and Holly Jolly Halloween tickets. The park states plainly that it does not discount FEASTival, Christmastime, or New Year’s Eve admission — counterintuitive for a Christmas park, but that’s the published policy. It also states it has no coupon codes for admission at all, and Illinois prohibits combining discounts park-wide, so there is no stacking layer at either park.

One correction worth knowing: Military.com’s listing for the Illinois park still quotes family tickets at $24.99 — the park’s own page says $29.99 as of July 14, 2026. Most aggregator pages also never say which Santa’s Village they mean. One more lead for ticketed events: donated Santa’s Village tickets have appeared on Vet Tix at least once historically — which park and whether it recurs is unverified, so treat it as worth a look at vettix.org before you buy, not a benefit to plan around.
culvers-military-discount: s is a franchise system, and the chain states plainly that military perks are set restaurant-by-restaurant: “Select restaurants offer military discounts… Reach out to your local Culver

Be cautious of aggregator sites that assert a chain-wide “daily heroes discount — 10% off entire checks” or “everyday perks of 15% or more.” No official Culver’s source documents any such national program, and Culver’s corporate explicitly states discounts are franchise-by-franchise. The reported “25% Delicious Rewards sign-up coupon” appears only in aggregator summaries and is not in Culver’s official press release, so treat it as unverified. Treat the 10% as a possible local offer to confirm by phone, never as a guarantee.

The one guaranteed, nationwide value is the free Delicious Rewards loyalty program. You earn 10 points per $1, get birthday and half-birthday rewards, and receive targeted surprise offers — join through the app, at culvers.com/earn, or by giving your phone number at checkout. It is not a military-verification program, but it is the dependable everyday value that applies at every location, discount or not.

On the calendar, Veterans Day (November 11) is the main military window: many locations hand out a free single-scoop sundae with a military or veteran ID and run veteran fundraisers, though corporate has not confirmed a chain-wide free offer. In May 2025, Culver’s of Manitowoc ran a 10% Armed Forces Day discount for active-duty across all branches — a single-location example, not a national promo. There is no Culver’s presence on GovX, at military exchanges, or through cashback portals, so those routes are ruled out.
holland-america-military-discount: The benefit is part of Holland America’s Community Appreciation program, which extends the same US$100 onboard credit per stateroom to healthcare workers, first responders, medical professionals, active and retired teachers, and AARP members across 500+ itineraries. The military version covers U.S. and Canadian active-duty, retired, and veteran members, verified through SheerID — not ID.me. You submit your status via the "Verify Your Status" link on the offer page; once approved, the benefit can be applied to a new booking. Holland America’s FAQ recommends verifying before you book, and it does not state how long a verification stays valid, so re-verify if prompted on a later booking.

Know what the credit is — and isn’t. It is spending money on your stateroom account, capped at one credit per stateroom: two veterans sharing a cabin still get $100 total. It is non-refundable and non-transferable, has no cash value, expires when the cruise ends, and cannot pay casino charges, gratuities, or specified fees. It never reduces the fare itself. Military-travel agencies and aggregators market "Holland America military rates" and "up to X% off" claims, but Holland America’s own pages describe exactly one military benefit: this $100-per-stateroom onboard credit. Any percentage-off "HAL military rate" is agency sale-fare marketing, not an official military program.

On stacking, Holland America is silent where sister line Princess is explicit. The credit applies to a new booking at whatever eligible fare you book — so fare shopping (wave-season and public sales) is where the real money is — but the terms do not say whether it combines with other promotional onboard credit, including the separate Carnival Corporation shareholder benefit ($100 on a 7-day sailing for holders of 100+ CCL shares, claimed via Stockperks at least 3 weeks before departure, on sailings through December 31, 2026). Treat a military-plus-shareholder double-post as a bonus to confirm on your reservation, not a promise. Shoppers on cruise forums report getting the military credit applied alongside other onboard credit, but that’s community-reported — check the line items on your own booking confirmation.

If your household is line-flexible, run the comparison: Princess (same parent company) pays $50–$250 onboard credit per qualified passenger — up to two per booking — and states its credit is combinable with other onboard-credit offers, which makes it richer than Holland America’s flat $100 per stateroom for two-veteran cabins. If military verification doesn’t fit your household, the AARP, teacher, and healthcare versions of the Holland America offer carry the same $100 value.
kuiu-military-discount: KUIU’s program is straightforward: a flat 10% off, every day, verified through GovX (GOVX ID) rather than a code. You start verification from KUIU’s cart/checkout or the "Military/First Responders" link in your account menu, then sign in to or create a GovX account to get verified before you order. GovX stores the verification on your GOVX ID, and because it’s tied to your KUIU account, the discount reapplies on future logins. KUIU doesn’t publish how often re-verification is required, so treat it as periodic rather than permanent.

On who qualifies, KUIU’s own help article names active-duty military, veterans, and active first responders, while its program-page meta and GovX store listing add retirees "and their dependents." Reserve, National Guard, and military spouses aren’t spelled out on KUIU’s pages, but they fall inside GovX’s broader Military and Military-Family groups, so they’re verifiable at checkout — the honest framing is "GovX can verify you; confirm it applies before ordering." First responders are included, but this program does not cover teachers, nurses/medical, or government employees; KUIU has separate ID.me landing pages for some of those audiences, but their terms aren’t confirmed on KUIU’s own site.

The limits matter for planning a purchase. The 10% can’t be combined with any other promotion or discount, so during a KUIU sale you’ll want to compare the sale price against the member discount rather than expecting them to stack. It also excludes select New Releases, third-party gear, outlet/clearance items, previous purchases, and Gift Certificates. And despite KUIU running brick-and-mortar stores, the company only states the discount as online at KUIU.com — an aggregator’s "in store" claim isn’t confirmed by KUIU, so don’t count on in-store use without asking the store.
mercedes-military-discount: US savings run through TrueCar’s military verification, which is backed by ID.me/GovX — there is no ID.me military checkout on mbusa.com itself. A dealer "Mercedes-Benz Military Program" web page is a lead form that funnels you to TrueCar (or MAS) plus whatever public MBUSA lease/APR offer is live, not a separate guaranteed discount. Take the TrueCar certificate to a participating dealer and confirm the current Military Bonus Cash on the exact model you want.

The TrueCar Military Bonus Cash generally stacks on TrueCar member pricing and the month’s public MBUSA lease or finance incentive, and a verified purchase adds the Military Appreciation Package (Auto Repair Reimbursement of 20% of a repair up to $500, and Auto Deductible Reimbursement up to $500, each twice a year for two years). Because bonus-cash amounts and eligible models rotate monthly, treat "up to $5,500" as a current ceiling on select models rather than a fixed figure on your car.

For those stationed overseas, Military AutoSource is its own closed channel — you take the MAS package rather than stacking a stateside dealer discount or TrueCar bonus on it — and its tax-free element is frequently the single biggest saving (roughly 7% sales tax on a $50,000 car is about $3,500 avoided). Confirm current Mercedes availability through MAS before relying on it. The Sam’s Club and Amex auto-buying programs are public, non-military perks listed only so you can compare — they’re an either/or with TrueCar Military.
michael-kors-military-discount: The Michael Kors military discount is verified in person: you show a valid U.S. military ID (or comparable documentation) to the sales associate at checkout, and the discount ties to your KORSVIP account email. Michael Kors does not publish an ID.me or SheerID online military offer, so there is no digital "verify once, shop online" flow for this discount. Several aggregators frame the 10% as an online code applied through ID.me — that is not what Michael Kors publishes, and you should not rely on it.

Because the discount is not combinable, you choose the 10% or a public promo code — never both. Michael Kors runs deep, near-constant public sales (recently a 25% off KORSVIP code and an extra 40% off already-reduced styles), so on most handbag purchases a live sale beats the 10%. The one benefit that is always additive online is KORSVIP itself — free shipping and returns, points, and a birthday reward layer on regardless of any sale.

The 10% also excludes a big chunk of the catalog: watches, jewelry, fragrance, eyewear, Access smartwatches, MK Collection, dust bags, Rain & Stain Protector, charitable products, and gift cards. Handbags, wallets, and most accessories and apparel qualify. For Michael Kors eyewear and sunglasses specifically — which the in-store discount excludes — GOVX lists Michael Kors and Michael Kors Eyewear as marketplace storefronts with member pricing, a separate route worth checking.

For the lowest absolute price, the Michael Kors Outlet is a separate, much cheaper channel (outlet-exclusive handbags often run $130–160, with Memorial Day and Black Friday markdowns up to roughly 80% off). Eligible veterans can also shop the military exchanges (shopmyexchange.com, mynavyexchange.com) online tax-free, where MK fragrance, watches, and some handbags are commonly stocked — price-check first, since stock of any specific item is not guaranteed.
skechers-military-discount: Skechers verifies eligibility through ID.me. You create or sign in to a free ID.me account, confirm your community (military, first responder, healthcare, teacher, or student), and Skechers issues an instant, single-use coupon code per purchase.

Unlike most apparel and footwear brands, Skechers explicitly allows its community discount to combine with most site promotions and to apply on sale/clearance styles, not just regular-priced items. That stackability is the real value here — verify once, then apply the 10% on top of whatever promotion (like a BOGO or percent-off sitewide sale) is currently live.

Debunking the "20%" myth directly: some aggregator sites describe a flat 20% Skechers military discount, and some imply it works in physical stores. Neither is accurate. Skechers’ official terms confirm the military/first-responder/healthcare/teacher/student benefit is an additional 10%, and it is online only — "not valid at Skechers store locations." The 20% figure belongs to the separate, public email/SMS signup offer that has nothing to do with military status.

One stacking limit to know: the 10% cannot combine with other "stackable offers," meaning you cannot chain two ID.me community discounts (for example, military plus teacher) on a single order — only one 10% applies per purchase.
all-clad-military-discount: The math below uses one baseline: an All-Clad D3 Stainless 10-piece cookware set (~$700 MSRP on all-clad.com). All-Clad publishes no fixed dollar prices for its sale events, so the figures are the ceilings the brand and editorial coverage state (“up to 70% off”).

All-Clad is a premium brand that competes on periodic deep-discount sales, not audience discounts — the archetype where the real savings live in the factory/seconds channel. The Factory Seconds (“VIP”) Sale online and the in-person Factory Sale in Washington, PA both reach up to ~70% off MSRP on cosmetically imperfect or overstock cookware.

For authorized shoppers, the Navy Exchange is a separate channel: no code stacking, but inherently tax-free, which typically wins on pristine new goods once you factor in the ~6–9% sales tax you’d otherwise pay. If you want new (not seconds) at a discount without exchange access, a retailer sale at Sur La Table, Williams-Sonoma, Amazon, Costco, or Macy’s is the fallback.

On all-clad.com itself, percent-off codes cannot be combined with other percent-off codes (one per order), but they do stack with free-shipping promotions — and certain products are excluded. None of this is military-gated.
solo-stove-military-discount: Solo Stove verifies eligibility through VerifyPass, a third-party service. You submit your details once, VerifyPass confirms your military or professional status (usually instantly), and you receive a one-time code to paste at checkout under "+ discount." There is no confirmed ID.me, GovX, or SheerID verification for the first-party discount — VerifyPass is the named partner. (ID.me and GovX exist for Solo Stove only as a separate cashback portal and a separate marketplace, respectively.)

The offer is a flat dollar amount and non-combinable: $20 (military) or $15 (healthcare, first responders, government, teachers) off orders of $100+, with a one-time code that won’t stack with any other promotional code. Because Solo Stove is on sale most of the year and its sales are often deeper than the flat code, compare the public sale price against the code and use the lower one. hershey-park-military-discount: Coupon aggregators headline figures like "up to 40% off Hersheypark military," "$20 off," and "up to 25%." The "40% off + free parking" figure belongs to the historical May Military Appreciation Weekend, a limited-time event whose exact dates and terms are set each spring. The "up to 40%" (GovX) and "up to 25%" (WeSalute) figures come from third-party ticket marketplaces, not from Hersheypark directly. These platforms run their own military/first-responder identity verification and set their own live pricing, which can move — always confirm the current price on the platform itself before buying.

Hersheypark’s FAQ deliberately frames the advance online ticket as the best baseline price, meaning the military "discount" often competes with — and sometimes loses to — the general online deal. Compare all channels (GovX, WeSalute, base ticket office, seasonal ID.me) against the plain online price before you buy, since the winner shifts by season and ticket type.
starz-military-discount: There is no verification partner because there is no discount to unlock: Starz uses no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute military flow. Some aggregators claim a "50% military discount" or list "Starz military promo codes," but those are false or generic public coupons mislabeled as military — the recurring public intro promo is what those codes actually reflect, and it’s available to anyone.

The genuine levers are all public. Starz frequently runs multi-month intro promos at a steep discount to list price; the annual plan lowers the effective monthly rate for year-round viewers; and buying Starz as an add-on through Amazon Prime Video Channels, Hulu, or Roku is billed by that platform and sometimes promo-priced. For a single series, binge-and-cancel keeps you to about one month of list price.

If military-specific streaming savings matter to you, they exist elsewhere: Disney+ and Hulu via The Exchange (AAFES), and Paramount+ via SheerID, are documented military streaming deals. Starz is not among them — so treat any "Starz military" offer you see as an unverified public coupon.
oncloud-military-discount: On verifies eligibility exclusively through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. One thing to watch: coupon and aggregator pages headline "On Cloud military discount — up to 50% off" or "60% off with promo code." That is false framing. On’s military discount is a flat 15% via ID.me and cannot stack with any sale; the "up to 50/60%" figures are generic clearance and coupon-site noise, not a military rate. The only legitimate code is the single-use one ID.me issues after you verify. Some listings also still show a 10% figure — that is stale; the current stated offer is 15%.

kane-footwear-military-discount: Kane uses GovX ID to verify military, first-responder, teacher, and healthcare status. kings-island-military-discount: This is Kings Island (Mason, Ohio) — a Six Flags / former Cedar Fair park now hosted at sixflags.com/kingsisland (the old visitkingsisland.com URLs redirect there). It is not Kings Dominion (Doswell, VA), which runs a separate program.

spirit-military-discount: What happened: Spirit filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on November 18, 2024, emerged in March 2025, then filed a second Chapter 11 on August 29, 2025. That reorganization collapsed, and on May 2, 2026 Spirit ceased all flight operations — "all flights have been cancelled, and customer service is no longer available" — entering a court-supervised orderly wind-down with its assets up for auction. Its web presence followed: the former support and customer-service pages, including the military-benefits article, now redirect to spiritrestructuring.com, the wind-down site.

How the benefit used to work (historical record, not a current offer): active-duty members selected "Active Duty U.S. Military Personnel" during booking and verified through ID.me, or showed a military ID at the airport. Each qualifying traveler got two free checked bags and a free carry-on (plus a free personal item), and accompanying spouses and children added their free bags with an agent at the ticket counter. Complimentary priority boarding required presenting a military ID at the gate. Spirit had expanded the benefit to spouses and children in May 2024 — the program died with the airline two years later.

If you hold an unused Spirit ticket: do not go to the airport, and don’t wait on hold — customer service is closed. Dispute the charge with your credit-card issuer for undelivered service, and watch the bankruptcy wind-down (the Spirit Aviation Holdings case) for consumer claim instructions; refunds route through the case, not spirit.com. Spirit offers no rebooking help, and the DOT-coordinated discounted rescue fares that other carriers offered stranded passengers in May 2026 have ended.

For military travelers booking now, the landscape is actually solid: the DOT customer-service dashboard records every listed airline’s commitment to at least one free standard carry-on and at least two free standard checked bags for service members and their accompanying spouse and children with a valid military ID. Frontier — the closest ultra-low-cost substitute for Spirit — waives bag fees (including oversize/overweight on those bags) for active duty. American, Delta, and United publish allowances of roughly 2–3 free bags on personal travel and up to 5 heavier bags on orders. Because these waivers are fee waivers rather than fare discounts, they layer on any fare, including sale fares — so compare total trip cost (fare + fees) rather than hunting for a military fare code, which essentially no U.S. airline offers.
hot-topic-military-discount: The near-identical "Hot Topic offers a 10% military discount — call 1-800-892-8674" text on WorthEPenny, SemperSave, RetailSalute, and Groupon is not sourced to any live official Hot Topic page, and ID.me explicitly says no military offer exists. Hot Topic did post a discretionary 10%-off Veterans Day gesture in past years, so the phone benefit may be a legacy/manager’s-discretion holdover — but it is not documented policy, and terms could vary by rep, store, or date. We do not publish "10% military discount" as fact.

Hot Topic Rewards is a free, tiered loyalty program: Silver earns 1x, Gold 1.2x, and Platinum 1.5x points per $1 of subtotal, 100 points converts to a $5 reward, and there is a $5 birthday reward with a 45-day redemption window. Points earn on your subtotal and stack with sales and codes, so it is always worth leaving on under whatever else you use.

Hot Cash is a cyclical earn-and-redeem coupon. You earn a coupon on qualifying spend (tiers from $15 off $30 up to $75 off $150), then redeem it in a separate window. The key rule: Hot Cash is not combinable with other offers or codes at redemption, but you can earn it while applying other discounts. So the play is to use a code now, earn Hot Cash, and redeem it on its own on a later order.

On a realistic $60 Hot Topic cart, a live sitewide code (~20% off, ~$48) plus free Rewards points and an earned Hot Cash coupon beats the rumored standalone 10% (~$54). Clearance (up to ~50% off, ~$30) is the deepest single-item cut, though codes usually will not stack on it. Free shipping kicks in at $75, so consolidating orders helps, and a cashback portal may add a little on top if its rate is verified and it does not conflict with your promo code.
sony-military-discount: Sony verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA, the IRS, and many major retailers. You create a free ID.me account, verify your service status (uploading documentation if prompted), and then confirm at Sony’s checkout with the "Verify with ID.me" button. Verification is per transaction, so you’ll confirm again on future orders, but you don’t re-upload documents each time once your ID.me status is established. Sony does not use GovX or SheerID for this offer.

The strongest feature of the offer is that the group discount stacks on the current sale price on eligible items — so buying eligible Sony electronics during a sale (Black Friday and Cyber Monday are deepest) means the up-to-10% comes off the already-reduced price. It generally cannot be combined with other promo codes or coupons, and per-item eligibility gates everything: non-eligible SKUs show the regular price with no discount.

Two things to watch. First, many coupon and aggregator pages advertise an "up to 15%" Sony military discount. That figure is not confirmed on Sony’s or ID.me’s primary listing, which says up to 10% — treat 10% as the verified ceiling and 15% as unconfirmed. Second, the discount is for Sony electronics only: PlayStation Direct has no official military discount on consoles, games, or PlayStation Plus. For PlayStation, the levers are seasonal PS Store sales and discounted gift cards, not a military rate.
silencerco-military-discount: SilencerCo runs its own SPEQ credential verification through participating SPEQ dealers and the SPEQ portal (speq.silencerco.com) — not a third-party ID wallet like ID.me or SheerID, and not a GovX marketplace checkout. You submit proof of status; a dealer reviews it (one authorized dealer states “typically within 48 business hours”); federal employees can verify via a .gov/.mil email or agency letterhead with personal details redacted. Because pricing is confidential, your discounted number is delivered privately after approval, and you place the order through the SPEQ dealer — not directly through the distributor.

On the baseline SilencerCo Omega 36M (MSRP $1,187; roughly $993 street at Silencer Shop), SPEQ is the lowest new-can price for a verified buyer. Shooters on forums report concrete SPEQ figures — an Omega around $782, for example — but SPEQ pricing is confidential and standardized, so treat those as unverified signal, not published prices; verify your actual number after credentialing. There is no coupon, cashback, or public code that stacks on top of a SPEQ price.

The 2026 regulatory change is the bigger story for every buyer: under H.R.1 (signed July 2025), the federal suppressor tax stamp dropped from $200 to $0 effective January 1, 2026 — “the tax went away, the paperwork did not.” You still file an ATF Form 4, get fingerprinted, pass a background check, transfer through an FFL/SOT dealer, and wait for ATF approval before taking possession. If you don’t qualify for SPEQ, the public play is street price plus the current free $250 SilencerCo webstore credit (buy and submit Form 4 by August 15, 2026). Whether that credit can also apply to a SPEQ order isn’t confirmed — treat it as either/or and compare SPEQ against ($993 − $250).
cox-military-discount: Cox routes its military, first-responder, teacher, medical, and government offer through GOVX ID. You create a free GOVX account, verify your group affiliation once, and GOVX confirms your status before sending you to Cox to sign up. There is no confirmed ID.me, SheerID, or WeSalute route for Cox — GOVX is the named partner. Coupon and "military discount" aggregators variously claim Cox gives a "$5–$10/month military discount," "up to 20% off with military promo codes," and an "up to $200" prepaid Mastercard. crate-and-barrel-military-discount: The "no" is documented on the brand’s own site: the coupons page enumerates every discount program Crate & Barrel runs — registry completion, the professional Trade Program, the new-mover offer, refer-a-friend — and a military discount is not among them, alongside the brand’s own statement that it has "no active coupons at this time." No primary source supports any of it — there is no Crate & Barrel offer on ID.me Shop or GovX, and no verification button at checkout.

What actually works: seasonal sale depth plus the store card. On a $500 full-price cart, a realistic 30% sale takes you to $350, and paying with the Crate & Barrel Visa returns another $35 in Reward Dollars — about $185 of combined benefit, with sales peaking at 50–60% off around Memorial Day, July 4, and Black Friday. verizon-military-discount: The single most important thing to understand: the $10/$25/$20 figures are a discount per account, not per line. Verizon’s marketing "$25/line" headline reflects the resulting plan price with Auto Pay, paper-free billing and 4 lines — not the discount amount. The fixed-dollar amounts apply to current Unlimited plans; "most other advertised plans" instead get 15% off the plan’s account access charges.

Verizon verifies eligibility through ID.me. You create a free ID.me account and confirm your status; ID.me may require a validating document such as a military ID, orders, or a DD-214 for Gold Star next of kin. The person registering must be both the military/Gold Star member and the Verizon Account Owner or Account Manager. Military members, veterans and first responders can also register in a Verizon Company Store.

There’s no annual renewal — Verizon states eligible service members generally keep the military discount for life, though Verizon may occasionally re-verify status. The Fios discount lasts as long as you keep a qualifying home internet plan and verified ID.me status.

You can stack more savings on top: bundling Verizon mobile with Fios adds an extra $15/mo through the Mobile + Home Discount, a separate $5/mo discount is available on Fios Digital Voice or Home Device Advisor, and the military discount combines with the Auto Pay + paper-free billing discount. The current structure is the $10/$25/$20 per-account tiered amount on current Unlimited plans, with 15% applying only to most other advertised plans — both confirmed on Verizon’s own support page.
united-airlines-military-discount: The most important thing to get right is that United runs two distinct 5% discounts that aggregators often collapse into one. United’s own Active-Duty Military Leisure Discount is verified inside your MileagePlus profile and is framed as active-duty only — there is no third-party verifier and no code, and eligible flights simply show the discount applied at search. The separate WeSalute+ 5% covers a much broader group (veterans, retirees, Guard/Reserve, and immediate family) but requires a paid WeSalute+ membership and a personal Travel Code entered at booking.

The practical takeaway: if you’re active duty, use United’s free MileagePlus verification first — it’s a real 5% with no membership fee. If you’re a veteran or family member, your path to a United fare discount is the paid WeSalute+ membership, so weigh its cost against how often you fly. Both discounts let you still earn MileagePlus miles on the discounted fare.

On the airport perks: United’s page says active military don’t pay fees for "up to five checked bags, depending on your type of travel," can board with the pre-boarding group, and can visit a United Club when space is available. The exact bag count by travel type isn’t numerically stated on United’s own page — the widely cited "5 on orders / 3 personal, 70 lbs each" split comes from WeSalute and military.com, so confirm your allowance at check-in. Reserves and National Guard get these airport benefits when traveling on active orders.

United also runs a military pet program for transport on current orders between Honolulu (HNL) and Guam (GUM), and a separate United Vacations discount of up to $150 per reservation (3% off the hotel portion) on flight-and-hotel packages for active-duty and veteran personnel, requested by email. None of these benefits use ID.me or SheerID; the fare discounts use MileagePlus or WeSalute, and the airport perks use your military ID.
kitchenaid-military-discount: SheerID confirms your military, veteran, or first-responder status tied to your KitchenAid account. You select the Military (or First Responder) option in My Account and authenticate through SheerID; if you get a SheerID success email, sign out and back in to refresh your verified status. Verification is per-account, and the discount then applies to eligible major-appliance orders.

The scope matters. The discount covers major appliances — refrigerators, ranges, cooktops, wall ovens, microwaves, dishwashers, hoods, beverage and wine centers, ice makers, and compactors — and excludes refurbished models. It does not stack with public sale pricing; KitchenAid’s terms state it combines only with the Delivery & Haul-Away offer. Free delivery on major appliances $399+ is a shipping benefit, not a stack conflict.

Coupon sites advertise flat "KitchenAid military promo codes" and specific percentages like "15% off with code." That’s misleading: the discount is not a code — it’s an account-gated SheerID verification, and the percentage is not published anywhere on the brand page. The often-cited 15% comes from editorial roundups, not KitchenAid’s own terms — plausible but unconfirmed. A "military discount on a KitchenAid stand mixer" (a countertop product) is also not confirmed by the "all major appliances" language.

For the lowest price, verify via SheerID and then price it against the live public sale (and retailer prices at Lowe’s, Best Buy, Abt, and AJ Madison). On a big appliance event — Memorial Day, July 4, Labor Day, Black Friday — the public sale often wins and won’t combine, so take the lower. When no deep sale is live, the verified discount plus free delivery is your floor. coach-military-discount: There is no Coach military-verification flow, because there is no Coach military discount. eddie-bauer-military-discount: The widely-cited Eddie Bauer "10% military discount" is now stale aggregator content describing the pre-2026 program. ten-thousand-military-discount: Verification is handled by GovX ID — a third-party identity service for military and first responders. The 25% is a genuine, generous everyday discount — better than the 10–15% many apparel brands offer. It functions as its own discount and cannot be combined with another promo code in the same order. Packs, kits, and limited edition gear are excluded.

One correction worth flagging: some coupon and discount-directory pages claim a "10% Ten Thousand military discount via ID.me." That is not the brand’s program. firestone-military-discount: All the math below uses one baseline: a $300 service order before tax, in a high-tax state at ~9.5% sales tax (so the normal out-the-door price would be about $328.50). Tires are priced separately and the Veterans Day promo excludes them, so a service order is the cleanest way to compare the paths; for tire-only purchases, see the WeSalute "store cost +10%" note and the chooser.

The tax-free perk, worked out: on that $300 service order, waiving the ~9.5% sales tax saves about $28.50 on its own. Add the 10% off ($30) and the everyday path lands near $270 out the door — roughly $58.50 saved, an effective ~19.5% off the normal taxed price. The higher your state’s tax, the more the tax-free half is worth, and the harder a taxed 15% has to work to catch up.

Rule 1 — the paths don’t stack, so you’re choosing one. The everyday 10% + tax-free, WeSalute’s 15%, the Veterans Day +10% service promo, and any public coupon are alternatives, not layers. Don’t expect "10% + a coupon" or "10% + Veterans Day 10% = 20%"; pick the single path that nets the lowest out-the-door price.

Rule 2 — a taxed 15% can lose to a tax-free 10%. WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage) advertises 15% off service, but it’s a paid membership and the 15% is typically still taxed. On the $300 baseline that’s about $279 out the door — more than the everyday 10% + tax-free (~$270). WeSalute earns its keep mainly on tires, where "store cost +10%" can beat 10% off on a big set, so price both for a tire purchase.

Rule 3 — the Veterans Day promo is service only and time-boxed. Firestone has run an extra 10%-off-service promotion around Veterans Day that excludes tires and does NOT stack with the everyday 10% (so it isn’t 20%). It mainly helps with timing or if you can’t use the everyday path that day. The window rotates each year — confirm the current-year dates before counting on it.

Rule 4 — watch two myths. First, the everyday discount is in-store only: online tire buyers forfeit it, so book or claim it at the counter. Second, "NEW15" is not a 15% military code — it’s a general new-customer offer that coupon sites mislabel. Verify any code on Firestone’s own coupons page, and don’t skip your guaranteed in-store 10% + tax-free chasing it.
goodwill-military-discount: Facebook posts and aggregators circulate a flat "Goodwill offers a 10% military discount daily" as if it were a national policy — it is not. Some individual regions do run a daily or weekly military discount, but there is no company-wide Goodwill military discount, and the number, day, and eligibility differ by organization. Any page stating a single national Goodwill military percentage is wrong; the only accurate national statement is that it varies by your local Goodwill.

Verification is manual and in-person: you show a valid military ID (and, where required, proof of veteran or dependent status) to the cashier. There is no third-party verifier — Goodwill does not use ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass for this, and there is no account, code, or online enrollment. Because it’s discretionary and regional, acceptance and the exact ID accepted can vary store to store.

The verified regional map as of July 2026: Dallas 25% off (Thursdays, active duty and veterans), Southern California an additional 10% (Mondays, active and retired plus dependents), Columbia Willamette 10% (Tuesdays, veterans and active, excluding outlets), Heartland 10% (Fri–Sun, active, reserve and veteran plus spouses), Inland Northwest 20% on Veterans Day (excluding the outlet), and Omaha a combined military and first-responder discount day on the third Wednesday. Because these discounts generally don’t stack with the color-tag sale, take whichever single discount is deeper — often the public color tag.
carmax-military-discount: CarMax’s no-haggle model is the whole reason there is no military discount: the windshield price is set and identical for every buyer, so there is nothing for a service-member rate, code, or verification program to reduce. There is no CarMax page that lists a military offer because none exists — CarMax’s own articles and FAQ confirm the price "is the same price for everyone," and the ID.me CarMax page confirms ID.me runs no CarMax military offer.

Because the car price is fixed, the genuine military savings are levers off the sticker. The biggest is financing: buy the CarMax car but finance it through a military credit union rather than accepting a marked-up dealer loan. Navy Federal cuts its auto-loan APR by 0.25 percentage points for active-duty and retired members and runs a TrueCar-powered car-buying service; PenFed offers competitive member rates. The loan APR is independent of the car price, so this "stacks" in the sense that it lowers your total cost without touching the sticker. Trade-in credit is a second independent lever — CarMax’s instant online offer (carmax.com/value) applies directly to the purchase or can be taken as cash.

If you are flexible on where you buy — especially for a new car — TrueCar Military is the real military-exclusive path. It authenticates status through ID.me (military email, USAA membership, service record, or DD 214 / LES), offers upfront pricing on new or used cars, and advertises a Military Appreciation Package of repair and deductible reimbursements (commonly cited around $2,000–$4,000; verify the current figure). GovX’s auto discounts also run through TrueCar, not CarMax. TrueCar routes you to its own dealer network, so it and CarMax are mutually exclusive — you don’t get the package on a CarMax car.

Two more paths matter. SCRA is not a purchase discount: it caps interest at 6% on qualifying pre-service obligations and provides service-member protections on a CarMax Auto Finance account — you submit a copy of your orders to CAF — but it does not lower a car’s price or a new loan’s rate. And for those stationed overseas (OCONUS) 30+ days buying a new car, Military AutoSource / the Exchange offers a tax-free purchase with free shipping home — the single largest military-exclusive auto deal, but one that does not apply to a domestic used CarMax purchase. Finally, ignore every "CarMax military promo code" you see: WorthEPenny and MilitaryMarkdown both state there is no official CarMax military program even while surfacing junk coupon tiles.
cole-haan-military-discount: Cole Haan’s military benefit is an evergreen ID.me rate, not a dated holiday event — the 15% runs year-round rather than only around Veterans Day or Memorial Day. The same ID.me program extends the 15% to first responders, nurses and medical providers, hospital and government employees, and teachers.

A common myth is worth clearing up: several coupon and aggregator sites advertise a "20% Cole Haan military discount." That figure is actually the separate SheerID student/academic offer, which aggregators mislabel. Cole Haan’s own site sets the military discount at 15% via ID.me — treat any "20% military" or "25% military" claim as unverified.

The discount applies to the price shown at checkout, so in practice it may land on top of a marked-down sale price (standard ID.me behavior) — but Cole Haan does not explicitly confirm sale-item eligibility, and because you cannot also apply a promo code, a deep semi-annual or outlet sale often beats the 15% on its own.
lenovo-military-discount: Lenovo uses ID.me to confirm eligibility, and verification happens in the shopping cart — you select your group (Military/First Responder/Student/Senior), then verify with ID.me. An ID.me account is required (you can create one during checkout). ID.me may ask for documentation such as a military ID or service records to confirm status; the exact documents are determined by ID.me, not Lenovo. Lenovo’s pages do not state a re-verification interval for the military program, so do not assume permanent or one-time-only verification.

Because Lenovo does not publish the military percentage on a crawlable page and the rate shifts with promotions, we intentionally avoid asserting a number. Third-party sites cite 5% off, but that is not confirmed by Lenovo directly — the reliable path is to verify with ID.me in your cart and read the discounted total. The "up to an additional 7%" ceiling suggests possible tier variation.

If the discount doesn’t appear, confirm you completed ID.me verification (not just sign-in), check that your item isn’t a doorbuster/clearance exclusion, and re-apply any generated promo code. Note that Lenovo has also been listed as a WeSalute partner (a separate membership program) since 2018, and its verified discounts apply on top of Lenovo’s instant savings on eligible products.
streamlight-military-discount: You never verify with Streamlight — you verify with the channel. GovX ID checks military, first-responder, government, and education status in real time and unlocks member pricing after a free account; it covers seven groups including veterans and military family. ExpertVoice verifies military eligibility by .mil email or credential and approves accounts for personal-use pro pricing (program-wide, up to ~60% off MSRP across tactical brands). VCS and the exchanges gate on VA and exchange eligibility respectively.

About those coupon-site claims: aggregators variously advertise a "Streamlight military discount" of 10%, 25%, 40%, even 65% — as a code applied on Streamlight’s own site. That’s false on its face: Streamlight has no direct-to-consumer store, so there is nothing to enter a code into, and no primary Streamlight source publishes any military percentage. The figures contradict each other precisely because none comes from Streamlight.

For the math, take one ProTac HL-X (model 88065): dealer-listed MSRP is about $178.39, but the ordinary street price runs $97–$103 at Walmart, BrightGuy, and OpticsPlanet. Each verified channel is a closed store — you can’t stack a coupon or cashback portal on top — so the smart move is to compare three numbers: the retail sale price, the ExpertVoice or GovX member price if you’re verified, and the tax-free exchange/VCS price if you’re eligible.
olive-garden-military-discount: Olive Garden does not use a third-party verification service (no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute) and no online account is required. For the Veterans Day offer, staff confirm eligibility in person when you show proof of military service. Because acceptable proof can vary by location and manager discretion, call your local restaurant ahead if you’re unsure your ID will be accepted.

Be skeptical of any "Olive Garden everyday 10% military discount" you see on coupon sites — no primary source confirms it, and Olive Garden’s only "10%" is an unrelated discount on bulk gift-card purchases of $1,000 or more. The Veterans Day free entrée is effectively a 100% discount on one dish, but only on that one day and only for the veteran or active-duty diner.

The everyday ways to save are open to everyone: join the free eClub for email coupons, check the Specials page, and enjoy a complimentary dessert on your birthday when you dine in. Many casual-dining chains (e.g., Applebee’s) also run Veterans Day free-meal promotions worth comparing.
maui-jim-military-discount: Maui Jim routes its hero discount through ID.me. You create a free ID.me account and verify your eligibility (military, first responder, nurse/medical, teacher) once; ID.me confirms your status and issues a special code, up to twice every 12 months. GovX is a parallel verification route to the same 30%. There is no confirmed SheerID or WeSalute route for Maui Jim.

The 30% is non-combinable: Maui Jim’s own promo terms state ID.me purchases are "not eligible for" other promotions — so no public code, sale price, or cashback layers on top. On current styles the 30% is usually the deepest single discount, so the verified shopper should generally just take it; only reach for GovX Open Box, the tax-free Exchange (for prescription pairs), or a clearance style when the 30% doesn’t apply.
Maui Jim controls the program and can change it at any time, so confirm the current terms on the Mahalo to Heroes program page before you buy.
hims-military-discount: The program was real, and it made headlines: in September 2024, Hims & Hers announced compounded semaglutide GLP-1 injections at up to 50% off — as low as $99/month — for U.S. military, veterans, teachers, nurses, and first responders. Eligibility was verified through SheerID, which required documents like a DD214, dated ID, insurance card, official orders, or a paystub dated within 90 days (active-duty and reservist ID cards were not accepted, per Title 18 U.S.C. §701). Per the current promotion terms, that path is now closed: the Special Groups Discount is "no longer available to new members" as of April 10, 2025.

Grandfathered members keep the deal. If you completed SheerID verification on or before April 10, 2025, the legacy pricing — $1,188/year on an annual plan or $894 bi-annual, roughly $99/month — continues on eligible annual or bi-annual plans with low-dose compounded semaglutide. The full subscription is auto-charged once a provider prescribes, it auto-renews, and it isn’t combinable with public promo codes.

Be cautious of what aggregators still say. Many coupon pages and older press coverage continue to push "Hims military discount — $99/month GLP-1" as if it were claimable today, and some even label it an ID.me offer. Both claims are wrong: the program is closed to new members, and it was never an ID.me offer — ID.me Shop itself notes it is not aware that Hims offers military discounts. A service member signing up today gets standard pricing, full stop.

What actually saves money now: if you’re grandfathered, keep the legacy rate — it’s about 50% under standard. If you’re a new customer, use any public first-month intro promo, cross-shop other GLP-1 telehealth providers (Ro, LifeMD, Noom), and check whether TRICARE or your insurance covers a branded GLP-1 through your own provider — a copay is often the cheapest path of all. Remember that no discount guarantees a prescription; a provider must deem treatment clinically appropriate after an online consultation.
mlb-tv-military-discount: MLB.TV’s military discount is brokered entirely through GovX, an identity-verification marketplace used by many brands to serve the military and first-responder communities. You create a free GovX account, verify your status once, and buy the subscription at the member price. The official MLB military page exists mainly to route you to GovX — the actual purchase and verification happen there.

The discount covers the yearly all-teams package (~$97.50 after 35% off $149.99) and the yearly single-team package (roughly $78 after 35% off ~$119.99). The $29.99 monthly plan is not part of the offer. Beyond the core military groups, the GovX storefront that carries MLB.TV also verifies first responders, nurses and other medical workers, teachers, and government employees — verify your specific group at GovX checkout.

The timing nuance is the whole story. The GovX 35% is fixed against the regular $149.99 price and does not track MLB’s public in-season price ladder. MLB steps the public seasonal price down through the year — it was already $94.99 by July 12, 2026 — so late in the season simply buying direct at the public price can cost less than the military price. Buying in February–April, the GovX discount is the clear win; from about June onward, price-check the live public MLB.TV page against the live GovX price and take the lower.

MLB.TV moved to ESPN and launched there February 10, 2026. You can watch on the MLB App or the ESPN App, and US subscriptions include MLB Network 24/7, MiLB, Big Inning, and live audio. Coverage is out-of-market only — your local team’s games and nationally exclusive games are blacked out under standard MLB.TV policy.
nfl-ticket-military-discount: The hero tier uses ID.me; the student plan uses SheerID. You verify once through the provider inside the YouTube purchase flow. ID.me hero subscribers auto-renew at the discounted rate at the then-current season price unless cancelled — no re-verification action is required to keep the rate. The student plan does not auto-renew. Don’t assume the discount is permanent: YouTube can change terms and the season price resets annually.

The decision is simply which verified price you qualify for. Enrolled college students get the $119 Student Plan (SheerID); military, veterans, first responders, medical workers, and teachers get the $198 hero price (ID.me); everyone else new to Sunday Ticket can take the $240 new-user promo with no verification. Student and hero are mutually exclusive at checkout, and if you qualify for both, the Student Plan is cheaper ($119 < $198). RedZone is an add-on ($42 hero / ~$10 student), not a stack.

Watch the details on old and third-party claims. Some aggregator posts imply the discount is military-only — it’s not; it’s a hero tier that also covers first responders, medical, and teachers. Others still cite a DirecTV military discount — that offer no longer exists, because the rights moved to YouTube in 2023. And there’s no GovX, WeSalute, military exchange, or cashback path for this product — buying anywhere other than YouTube via ID.me/SheerID is not the official discount. Existing non-verified auto-renewals must be cancelled first, then re-purchased through the ID.me link to get the $198 rate.
boot-barn-military-discount: Boot Barn uses ID.me for online verification: you verify in the cart before checkout, and an ID.me account is required. ID.me lets members verify their community status once and reuse it across participating retailers, though ID.me may re-verify or require re-authentication at its discretion — so do not assume verification is permanent. For in-store purchases, eligibility is confirmed by showing proof of service or a qualifying ID at the register rather than through ID.me.

Boot Barn and ID.me explicitly confirm the discount for “all active and retired personnel.” Boot Barn does not individually name veterans, Reserve and National Guard members, spouses, or dependents on its page; those groups are part of ID.me’s standard military definitions and are likely eligible, but you should confirm your specific status through ID.me rather than assume it.

The discount applies to full-priced styles only and cannot be combined with other offers, previous purchases, or gift cards. Boot Barn also notes “exclusions apply; see cart for details,” and the exact additional exclusions are not published, so compare a sale price against 10% off the full price before you buy.
roborock-military-discount: Roborock verifies eligibility through ID.me, the same identity service used by the VA and many major retailers. You verify your community once on the Exclusive Offer page, receive a discount code, and enter it at Roborock’s checkout. ID.me may periodically re-verify your status under its own policies. For help, Roborock’s US support is available 24/7 at support@roborock.com or 1-855-960-4321.

Know the stacking rules before you count on a double-dip. The 10% arrives as a single discount code, and the checkout accepts one code per order — so it won’t combine with the 5% email-signup code or any other coupon. Sale prices are automatic markdowns rather than codes, but Roborock doesn’t state whether the 10% code applies on top of a sale price, so test it at checkout: if it applies, great; if not, you still have the larger discount. ID.me Shop cashback is different — it’s a rebate paid for clicking through shop.id.me (roughly 2%–4% depending on model, accessories excluded), so it layers on top of whatever price you pay.

Two things to watch. First, aggregator pages advertise "Roborock 30% off" or "60% off" military-flavored codes — those are generic sitewide or sale codes, routinely expired or fabricated, not a military benefit; the only verified military mechanic is the 10% ID.me code. Second, Roborock is sold at the Exchange (shopmyexchange.com), which is tax-free for authorized military shoppers — on a big-ticket vacuum, skipping ~6–9% sales tax can rival or beat the 10%.
seattle-aquarium-military-discount: For the $2 discount, verification is a simple military ID check at the gate — no online account or third-party provider. Because the discount is gate-only, it can’t be combined with online promos; you choose one channel.

For Blue Star Museums, eligibility is confirmed by presenting a valid military ID (CAC, DD Form 1173, DD Form 1173-1, or Next-Generation USID) at the gate during the program window. It covers currently serving members and up to five accompanying family members, and it replaces a paid ticket entirely rather than stacking on top of one.

Admission itself uses demand-based "plan-ahead" pricing — an adult ticket is around $33.95 regular but ranges roughly $23–$51 depending on the date and attendance.
