The WeSalute/BenefitHub offer is the source of most "Mint military discount" claims online. It lists deals such as "5GB for $10/mo" and device bundles for verified WeSalute+ members, but it is a standalone paid-membership marketplace deal — verification is of your WeSalute membership, not a Mint benefit — and it does not stack with Mint’s public new-customer promo. Because the membership costs about $120/yr, the offer nets worse than the free public promo unless you already pay for WeSalute+ for other reasons.

Be cautious of aggregators circulating a "GENIUS15" code for 15% off as a "military" saving. It is a general influencer/referral-style code, not a military discount, and no Mint primary source confirms it is currently active — so we do not assert it here.

Mint does grant one real military accommodation: it waives the 60-day phone-unlock waiting period for deployed military. Call Mint care at (800) 683-7392 to request an early unlock. It is a service accommodation, not a price discount, and it is a fact most coupon pages never mention.
skylight-military-discount: There is no verification because there is no military discount. Skylight has no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute military program, and it isn’t sold on GovX or through the military exchanges — so those channels don’t apply. The military-tagged “codes” circulating on coupon sites, like “OBSESSED,” are public codes anyone can try, and ID.me itself confirms Skylight has no military program.

Because there’s no identity discount, a service member saves exactly the way everyone else does — and the public paths are decent. The everyday plays are the $10 email welcome and the $20 referral (take the larger of the two when no better sale is live), and the deepest single discounts come from seasonal sitewide sales, with Black Friday and Cyber Monday the best windows of the year. Codes are generally one-per-order, so a sale price and a welcome/referral code typically can’t be stacked.

Watch the total cost of ownership. Skylight Plus is a $79/yr subscription that unlocks features like the photo screensaver, meal planner, and Magic Import. The core calendar or frame works without it, but some features are gated — so a “cheap” frame can cost more over time once you add the subscription. Factor Skylight Plus in when comparing a Skylight against a no-subscription alternative.
sun-home-saunas-military-discount: The GovX relationship here is verification-only: there is no Sun Home storefront on the GovX marketplace. You verify through the form on the brand’s military page, receive a personal single-use code, and spend it at sunhomesaunas.com. Each code covers one order, but the brand’s FAQ says you can return to the form and request a new code for each additional order with no stated limit.

The stacking terms are unusually shopper-friendly for this category. Most wellness brands force a choice between the military discount and the sale price; Sun Home’s published terms state that "site-wide seasonal sales (hard-marked discounts) may stack with one coupon code per order." The brand runs sales near-continuously around holidays — Memorial Day 2025 took up to $600 off select models, and a July 2026 "Black Friday in July" event marked the Equinox 2-Person down from $6,799 to $6,099 — so the realistic military price is usually sale price minus $300.

If you have a Health Savings Account or FSA, check the brand’s Truemed option before anything else: Sun Home states that paying with pre-tax dollars through Truemed delivers an effective 30–40% savings depending on your tax bracket — several times the value of the $300 code on a big-ticket sauna. Whether the $300 code can be applied to a Truemed order is not stated; ask support (info@sunhomesaunas.com) before assuming the two combine.

Two stale claims to ignore: coupon sites advertising a generic "$300 off Sun Home code" are describing select-item promo claims unrelated to the military program, and any page pointing to Sun Home’s old ID.me store ($200 off) is out of date — that listing has been delisted, and GovX is the only current verification route. Sun Home controls these terms and can change them at any time, so confirm the current offer on the official page before you buy.
sitka-military-discount: SITKA’s discount is delivered through its Pro Program rather than a sitewide coupon. You apply at sitkagear.com/military-discount, verify your military or first-responder status through GovX, and link your GovX credentials to your sitkagear.com account. Once SITKA approves the application, the Pro-tier discount auto-applies to eligible, in-stock items when you are logged in — there is no code to paste at checkout.

Because SITKA does not publish the exact rate on its public page, treat the widely reported ~40% figure as a community-reported estimate, not an official number. It comes from verified members over 2020–2025 and is consistent with SITKA’s Pro tier, but the only way to confirm your actual discount is to see it applied in your own approved account. The flat "10–25%" percentages and "20% off + free ship" claims on aggregator sites do not match how the benefit actually works.

The Pro discount has a clear boundary: it applies only to eligible, in-stock, full-price gear and does not apply to the Outlet/clearance section. For Outlet items, shoppers report that a separate GovX marketplace code can stack on the already-reduced Outlet price at guest checkout (Rokslide, Dec 2025) — but at least one member reported it did not work, so treat that as a community signal rather than a guaranteed path. Public Black Friday and Labor Day "Big Game" sales can reach up to about 50% off discontinued or seasonal stock with no verification needed.

The Pro benefit is a confidential, personal contract: it is personal-use only, reselling is prohibited, approval is discretionary, and membership can be revoked. SITKA is also not stocked at the military exchanges (AAFES/NEX), and cashback portals return a negligible ~0.04%, so for current full-price gear the approved Pro Program is the strongest savings path by a wide margin.
ulta-military-discount: Ulta does not run any military, veteran, first-responder, or government-employee verification. ID.me’s brand pages for Ulta state, for each group, "We are not aware of ULTA Beauty offering [Military / First Responders / Government Employees] community discounts." If a third-party site asks you to "verify for an Ulta military discount," treat it as unaffiliated and unverified.

The only consumer verification Ulta operates is for students, through SheerID — a completely separate program. Students who are Ulta Beauty Rewards members (16+, currently enrolled) confirm their details with SheerID; a successful verification lasts one year, but a coupon code is only issued when a limited-time student offer is live. This student path does not extend to military status.

The best evergreen way for military shoppers to save at Ulta is the free Ulta Beauty Rewards program, plus public coupons and seasonal events (summer sale, Buy More Save More, 21 Days of Beauty) that are open to all. If a verified military discount is the priority, some competing beauty brands do offer one via ID.me or SheerID — verify each brand’s current terms independently.
bonobos-military-discount: Bonobos’ military discount is powered by SheerID, an identity-verification service used by many retailers. You submit your name, military details, and an ID document; SheerID confirms your status — which can take a few hours up to a day or two — and emails a single-use 20% promo code. The code is per-issuance, so you re-verify or re-request for future orders as SheerID and Bonobos require; treat each code as one-time rather than a permanent account discount.

Watch the figures other sites quote. Some coupon pages show "15% off five orders per year" — that is a stale older term — and others show "25%," which conflates Bonobos’ separate refer-a-friend offer. The verified current military rate is 20%, confirmed against SheerID’s own Bonobos offer, SheerID’s military verify link, and Military.com on July 14, 2026.

The smartest play depends on your situation. On a first Bonobos order, the public 20% code (GETSTARTED20 / email signup) with free shipping ties the military rate with no verification, and a 25% referral link beats it. As a repeat customer buying full-price items, the SheerID military 20% is your lever. If your item is in the sale section (up to ~50% off), buy the markdown and let ~10% TopCashback ride — the military code is full-price-only and cannot stack with cashback anyway.
comptia-military-discount: CompTIA’s own "how to save on your IT certifications" guide lists five official money-saving paths — bundles, a student discount, 529 plans, employer reimbursement, and flash sales — and names no military or veteran rate. What CompTIA does offer service members is government/DoD account pricing (for people buying through a linked government-agency or contractor account, quote-based rather than self-serve) plus military career and funding resources that point you to the programs that actually pay for the exam.

The single best path for almost every eligible service member is not a discount at all — it is funding. Active-duty Army/Air Force Credentialing Assistance or Navy COOL typically covers the exam in full ($0 out of pocket); separated veterans use the GI Bill or VET TEC; and eligible military spouses use MyCAA (up to $4,000 toward approved training through an approved school). A free exam beats any percentage discount, so funding is the first thing to check.

Be cautious of coupon and affiliate blogs that claim CompTIA gives active duty, veterans, and military spouses "~50% off exam vouchers through the Academic Store, verified with ID.me." That is not supported by any CompTIA primary source. CompTIA’s academic/student discount is verified through SheerID, not ID.me, and it is gated on current student enrollment — not military status. The real ~40% path is the student discount, which a veteran enrolled in school can use as a student.

If you must pay cash and do not qualify for funding or the student rate, the reliable universal play is an authorized-reseller voucher (about 10–15% off) from Dion Training, Professor Messer, Total Seminars, or GetCertified4Less. Those vouchers are already discounted and bought outside the CompTIA Store, so you cannot add a CompTIA store promo on top. For reference, the baseline used throughout this guide is one CompTIA Security+ (SY0-701) voucher at $439 retail (raised from $425 on June 1, 2026).
best-western-military-discount: The rate is verified with a physical government or military ID at check-in — there is no online ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute gate on the Best Western government/military rate itself. Service Rewards (the free Gold-status enrollment) may ask you to confirm military or government status when you sign up. WeSalute lists Best Western as a travel partner, but that’s a separate paid membership, not the official rate.

Best Western rates are mutually exclusive: the government/military rate, the member rate, and AAA/AARP rates are separate rates, so you book exactly one — price-check them and pick the lowest. What does layer on top is your Gold Elite status and points, which apply to whatever eligible rate you book and earn the +10% bonus. That’s why enrolling in Service Rewards is worthwhile regardless of which rate wins.

Always book direct. Third-party and opaque bookings (Priceline, Hotwire, Expedia wholesale) don’t earn Best Western Rewards points or elite benefits and usually aren’t upgrade-eligible. Government per-diem rates may be intended for eligible or official travel at some properties, so confirm leisure eligibility when you book.
stihl-military-discount: STIHL Inc. sells exclusively through 11 U.S. distributors that supply independent authorized dealers, and pricing and promotions are set at the dealer level. That’s why there is no national military rate to publish and no online verification provider (no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute) — the company runs no national program. In store, a dealer offering a courtesy will simply eyeball a valid military or veteran ID.

The widely copied "10% off STIHL military discount" figure on coupon-aggregator sites is not an official STIHL program and should be treated as unverified. STIHL issues no consumer coupon codes, isn’t sold on Amazon, and tightly controls MSRP — so "stacking a STIHL military code with a sale" is not a real scenario. Any discount is a dealer-by-dealer variable, typically modest if offered at all.

The genuine best-savings paths are dealer seasonal promotions (spring for trimmers and blowers, late summer through fall for chainsaws), which often come as value-add bundles; 0% financing on qualifying big-ticket purchases, which defers cost rather than lowering price; and credit-card rewards, which stack on essentially any purchase. Buying in person from a dealer? Ask for a military courtesy. Buying online at MSRP? There’s no code — use 0% financing and card rewards, and shop the seasonal promos.
asics-military-discount: ASICS uses SheerID to confirm eligibility, and the discount is tied to your free OneASICS™ account. You select your community (Military), then verify online and/or in store — the two channels are verified separately. SheerID may ask for a work/school-issued email address or supporting documentation; verification is usually instant but can take longer if a document review is needed, and approval is communicated by email.

Your eligibility lasts one year, after which you re-verify with SheerID to renew. Completing verification requires consenting to ASICS marketing emails, though you can unsubscribe afterward without losing the discount. Participants may be verified under only one community at a time, so pick the one that fits you best.

A couple of things to watch. Several coupon and aggregator pages advertise “40% off” for ASICS — that figure is not supported by ASICS’s current official source and appears to trace to an older, time-limited 2020 healthcare-worker promotion; only up to 25% footwear / up to 30% apparel is confirmed on ASICS’s own pages. Some aggregators also claim ASICS verifies via ID.me or that in-store shoppers simply “show a military ID” — ASICS’s official pages name only SheerID and describe in-store redemption via an emailed QR code.
jeep-military-discount: Jeep verifies military status through SheerID, the same third-party verification service used across Stellantis brands (Ram, Chrysler, Dodge share the same $500 structure and provider on their own model lists). There are two entry points from the Jeep military-incentive page: a standard military verification button and a separate "disabled military" button for 100% Disabled Veterans.

Because this is a flat $500 allowance rather than a percentage, its dollar value doesn’t scale with the vehicle price the way a percent-off discount would. On a typical $40,000–$70,000 Wrangler or Grand Cherokee purchase, $500 is a modest add-on — the bigger lever is timing your purchase to Jeep’s largest live public incentive or APR/lease event and then stacking the $500 on top.

One thing to watch: some dealer sites and coupon/aggregator pages present the "$500 Jeep military discount" as if it applies broadly or as a percentage. It is a fixed $500 bonus-cash allowance tied to a specific, precise model list that changes by model year (for example, the 2026 Wrangler list excludes the 392 trim, and the 2025 Compass list excludes the Sport trim) — always verify the current list at jeep.com/incentives/military-incentive.html at the time of purchase.

If you’re stationed or deployed overseas, the $500 US bonus cash does not apply the same way — Jeep’s Military AutoSource program offers separate, tailored overseas pricing and benefits. Get a Military AutoSource quote and compare it against buying stateside.
pottery-barn-military-discount: Pottery Barn does not run a military-status verification flow (no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute military partnership) because there is no military discount to gate. ID.me Shop’s own Pottery Barn page states it is "not aware that Pottery Barn offers Military discounts." If Pottery Barn launches a future program, verification would most likely run through a third-party provider, but none is confirmed today.

The realistic ways to save are open to all shoppers: Key Rewards (a free, cross-brand loyalty program that also covers Williams Sonoma, West Elm, and Pottery Barn Kids), frequent sitewide sales and clearance, and the Pottery Barn credit card. Pottery Barn also offers free design services — not a discount, but it can reduce costly mistakes on furniture.

Service members who specifically want a confirmed home-goods military discount may look to retailers that do publish one; verify each independently before relying on it, as these programs change. Pottery Barn’s sister brands (West Elm, Williams Sonoma) follow the same no-military-discount pattern.
meow-wolf-military-discount: Verification is a physical ID check at entry — there is no ID.me, SheerID, or online-only verification wall. You can buy the discounted ticket online without uploading documents, but your military ID is checked at the door, and anyone who bought a discounted ticket without valid ID is charged full price on arrival. Denver’s page also accepts a VA card or DD Form 214 as proof. GovX offers a separate verified-marketplace route for some Meow Wolf tickets (notably Omega Mart in Las Vegas) with its own account-based verification — use one channel or the other, not both.

The discount is a distinct ticket type: you select it instead of a standard adult ticket, and it does not stack with resident, child, or senior pricing. It applies only to standard General Admission timed-entry tickets — not special events, concerts, the annual Portal Pass, or add-ons. If you also qualify for NM or NV resident pricing (or seasonal Denver CO resident pricing), price both and take whichever is lower; you can’t combine them.

Two honesty flags matter here. First, no official Meow Wolf page states the everyday discount’s value, so treat any specific "military price" you see on third-party blogs as unverified. Second, the dedicated promo pages for Denver, Las Vegas, and Grapevine have recently read "This offer is currently unavailable. Check back for updates." The general FAQ still lists military as an active discount category shown at checkout, but availability may be intermittent — run through checkout for your date before counting on it.
go-city-military-discount: Go City sells all-inclusive and Explorer sightseeing passes for 28+ cities worldwide, at a single all-in price with no separate sales tax added at checkout. Because it already bundles attractions at a discount, it declines to layer a military discount on top — its FAQ answers the military/senior discount question with a plain "Sorry, we don’t." There is no first-party verification flow (no ID.me, no SheerID) and no Go City military code to enter at checkout.

The only route branded "military" is GovX. Verify your status once through GovX ID (for military and first responders) and you get a unique code for an extra 6% off, redeemable on gocity.com, newyorkpass.com, londonpass.com, and parispass.com. It is real and reliable, but modest — and it cannot be used with any other promo code.

For a service member the GovX 6% is usually not the best deal. Rakuten pays 6.5% cash back on Go City pass purchases with no code and no membership (rate as of July 14, 2026), and a working public ~10% referral code frequently beats the GovX 6% outright. None of these stack: any code you enter voids the Rakuten cash back, and the GovX code is one-code-only. Rakuten also excludes Essential Passes, single tickets, gift cards, and app purchases, and pays only after your travel is completed. So the real decision is a one-of-three pick — best working public code, GovX 6%, or 6.5% cash back.

Be cautious of coupon and AI-answer sources that invent Go City "up to 50% off" and phantom "military" codes. The "up to 50%" is Go City’s own marketing comparison of pass price versus buying each attraction separately, not a code. Codes above ~10% (for example GOCITY10, TRIPLE20) are routinely rejected at Go City’s checkout, and ID.me shows only a generic site-wide banner with no Go City-specific verified code. Treat any "20%+ military code" as a red flag.
princess-cruises-military-discount: The benefit is fixed onboard credit, not a percentage off the fare — so any site marketing a "Princess military discount — up to 40–50% off" is describing sale fares or paid-membership marketing, not the military program. Princess’s own program pays $50 on cruises of 6 days or less, $100 on 7–13 days, and $250 on 14 days or more, per qualified passenger, guaranteed year-round on any eligible sailing. Up to two military members per booking each receive the full credit, so a qualifying couple on a 7-day sailing collects $200 in spending money regardless of what fare they booked.

Verification is a one-time event. U.S. personnel verify through SheerID, tied to a free Captain’s Circle account — once approved, the credit auto-applies to current bookings and attaches to all future ones, visible in Cruise Personalizer. Accepted proof includes a DD214 (or WD AGO / NAVPERS) plus current photo ID for veterans, or a military verification certificate for active duty. Canadian National Defense members use a PDF form by email, fax, or mail instead. Either way, apply no later than 14 days before departure; requests are handled within about 7 days. Questions go to Princess at 1-800-774-6237.

The stacking is what sets Princess apart. Its terms state the offer "is combinable with other Onboard Credit offers" and "combinable with most cruise fares" — so the right move is never to hunt for a special military rate, but to book the cheapest public fare you can find and let the credit follow you onto it. That combinability currently extends to the Carnival Corporation shareholder benefit: 100+ CCL shares adds $50–$250 more per stateroom (same length tiers, claimed through the Stockperks app at least 3 weeks before departure, currently offered on sailings through December 31, 2026). One honest caveat: Princess announced in June 2023 that the military and shareholder credits would stop combining, then reversed course — the rule has flipped before, so re-confirm when you book.

Know the fine print on spending it: the credit posts to your stateroom folio and covers things like specialty dining, the spa, shore excursions, and shops — but it cannot be used for casino credits or charges, and it’s non-refundable, so unused credit is forfeited. Princess doesn’t state whether it can pay crew appreciation (gratuities), so don’t plan on that without confirming onboard. The stated fare-side exclusion is "Travel Agent fares," a term Princess doesn’t define — if you book through an agent, ask them to confirm the military credit attaches rather than assuming either way.
chick-fil-a-military-discount: Chick-fil-A uses ID.me to identify and "from time-to-time honor" Chick-fil-A One members who belong to Community Helper groups — military, teachers, first responders and nurses. You start at chick-fil-a.com/community-helper-verify and are redirected to ID.me to validate your status; a Chick-fil-A One account is required to link the verification. Chick-fil-A states this gives members "an opportunity to be recognized and/or rewarded for their service" — it does not promise a specific or permanent discount, and it does not state a re-verification frequency.

Be cautious of the widely repeated "10% Chick-fil-A military discount." That figure is aggregator-sourced and location-dependent — it is not confirmed by Chick-fil-A and should never be treated as a brand-wide term. Similarly, claims that the app hands out "free food coupons for verified veterans on Veterans Day" appear only in social posts, not on any official Chick-fil-A page.

The everyday savings open to everyone are Chick-fil-A One rewards (earn points on qualifying purchases, redeem for free food) and receipt-survey free items at participating locations. The most reliable savings path is simply to ask your local Owner-Operator — many restaurants near bases run standing discounts — and to check participating locations near November 11 for Veterans Day meals.
google-fi-military-discount: Two different providers cover two different things at Google. SheerID verifies government/military employment for the OCONUS usage exception on Fi service (a policy exception, not a discount). ID.me verifies military status for the Google Store hardware discount (a different Google business). There is no verification path that produces a discount on your Fi monthly bill, because no such discount exists. Google can change or end any of these programs at any time.

The OCONUS exception is the entire reason many service members choose Fi: after SheerID verification, active-duty and State Dept members stationed abroad can use Fi’s international data up to 9 months without suspension, covering everyone on their group plan. It preserves data roaming only — international calling rates still apply — so don’t conflate it with free international calling.

If a lower monthly price is your priority and you’re flexible on carrier, the honest comparison is that T-Mobile, Verizon, and AT&T run genuine military plan discounts that Fi does not. If you don’t need Fi’s global feature set, one of them likely wins on price; if you value the OCONUS coverage, Fi’s value is the feature, not a discount.
nordstrom-military-discount: Nordstrom operates no military-status verification for a discount — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, or WeSalute flow exists on its site or in stores. Because there is no offer, there is nothing to verify. If you encounter a third-party site asking you to "verify military status for a Nordstrom discount," be cautious. Separately, ID.me Shop lists Nordstrom Rack as a cash-back store available to all ID.me members — that is a general shopping-portal cash-back perk, not a military discount.

Be skeptical of coupon-aggregator claims. Figures like "20% off," "15% off," or "50% off" for service members appear only on deal and affiliate sites, don’t trace to any Nordstrom primary source, and even contradict each other. The same applies to Nordstrom Rack, which has no published year-round military discount despite being an off-price channel.

The savings that are real are open to everyone: the free Nordy Club earns 1 point per $1, with 1,000 points converting to a $10 Nordstrom Note usable at Nordstrom and Nordstrom Rack (a Nordstrom credit/debit card earns at higher rates); regular markdowns and the signature mid-year Anniversary Sale; and the Nordstrom Rack off-price channel, where the Nordy Club also applies. Confirm current Nordy Club terms on the official page, since point ratios and Note values can change. For an actual verified military discount, several apparel and department retailers do run SheerID/ID.me offers worth comparing.
eos-military-discount: There is no verification partner because there is no discount to unlock: EōS uses no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute military flow, and no GovX gym storefront exists. A military ID works only as a standard government photo ID for check-in — never to trigger a rate. Any site telling you to "verify your military status for an EōS discount" is describing a program that does not exist.

The aggregator claims are not just unverified — they disagree with each other. One site advertises a 20% first-responder discount, another a 50% "military" code, another 10% off. Three different, uncited numbers, none confirmed by EōS. The only real levers are the public monthly enrollment promo and ACH billing, both open to everyone regardless of service. EōS’s own terms note that discounted enrollment offers and monthly rates are "valid at select locations only," so the public promo is location-gated and not stackable with a second promo.

Choose the right tier for how you will actually use the gym: the single-club "Will Do" plan (~$9.99/mo advertised) is cheapest if you only use one location, while the multi-club "Will Crush" (~$24.99/mo) is worth it only if you travel between clubs. It is also worth checking whether an employer or insurance fitness benefit (Active&Fit, Renew Active, One Pass) covers an EōS membership — eligibility there is by health plan, not by service.

Note on brand: "eos military discount" almost always means the gym (EōS Fitness). The skincare brand eos ("evolution of smooth") is a different company and likewise publishes no military discount — only general public promo codes.
